Incompatible yakıt comingling, asphalten: Commingling incompatible fuels forms heavy sludge through asphaltene flocculation; it clogs the purifiers and filters and causes a blackout through fuel starvation. A compatibility spot test and keeping new batches in a separate tank are the basic protection.
Tank içine deniz suyu girişi (sounding p: Seawater ingress into a tank (sounding pipe, vent, coil leak) or condensation creates a risk of both corrosion and, in MGO, microbial growth (diesel bug). Microbial contamination causes filter clogging and tank bottom corrosion; it is managed by biocide dosing and regular draining of water.
Yakıt ve yağ yönetimi, teknik bilgi kada: Fuel and oil management requires disciplined record-keeping and skeptical quality control as much as technical knowledge. For the Chief Engineer, the strongest defense is a provable chain of compliance: the sealed MARPOL sample, a correctly kept BDN and the changeover log. This discipline prevents both machinery damage costing millions of dollars and PSC detentions and fines.
Makine dairesinde yangının üç temel bile: In the engine room, the three basic components of a fire are present together: fuel (oil/fuel leaks), oxygen (forced ventilation) and an igniting hot surface (exhaust manifold ~400°C, turbine casing, steam pipes). Fuel spraying onto a hot surface from a crack in a high-pressure fuel line (HP fuel line) turns into a major fire within minutes.
Diğer riskler: kapalı alan (boş tank, ka: Other risks: oxygen deficiency or toxic gas (H2S, CO) inside enclosed spaces (empty tanks, boilers, crankcases), arcing/fire in electrical switchboards, mechanical entanglement in rotating equipment, and high noise/temperature. The Chief Engineer puts layered barriers (prevention, detection, containment, response) in place against each of these risks.
Makine dairesi A-class divisions (A-60/A: The engine room is enclosed by A-class divisions (A-60/A-30/A-0). Fire dampers and the skylight and ventilation closing (quick-closing) arrangements are there to cut off the air and smother the fire in the event of fire. Quick-closing valves (fuel/oil tank outlets) can be closed from outside the engine room (remotely, usually from the fire control station).
Detektörler fire detection panel'e (gene: Detectors are connected to the fire detection panel (usually with repeater indication on the bridge and in the ECR). Managing false alarms is important: repeated false alarms make personnel insensitive to the alarm (alarm fatigue). Dirty detectors, steam/oil mist and vibration cause false alarms; regular cleaning and calibration are carried out.
Bilge high-level alarm, makine dairesi s: The bilge high-level alarm is the early warning of engine room flooding (sea water pipe leak, cooler tube rupture, sea chest valve failure). The levels in the engine room bilge wells and the shaft tunnel are monitored. The alarm is tested and recorded in the PMS; an inoperative bilge alarm is a serious finding for PSC.
CO2 sistemi, makine dairesini tamamen ka: The CO2 system fills the whole engine room and smothers the fire by cutting off oxygen (usually a target concentration of 34%+). Before release: personnel out of the space (head count!), ventilation stopped, quick-closing valves closed, machinery stopped in sequence and doors/dampers closed. CO2 release is designed in two stages (pilot + main) and with a deliberate delay (pre-discharge alarm).
CO2 sistemi yıllık serbest olmayan testl: The CO2 system is checked by annual non-release tests (blow-through of the discharge lines, alarm test, time-delay test); cylinder weighing (weight/level check) and hydrostatic testing of the hoses are periodic. The system is kept in a locked room (CO2 room) to protect it against unintended manual or erroneous release.
Modern gemilerde high-pressure water mis: On modern ships, a high-pressure water mist system (HI-FOG etc.) is an alternative or supplement to total flooding; very fine water droplets provide both cooling and oxygen dilution, and it is safer than CO2 (personnel do not need to leave the space). Local application water spray covers high-risk points such as the top of the main engine, the purifiers and the boiler.
Fixed foam (boiler/oil-fired alanlar) ve: Layered protection is provided by fixed foam (boiler/oil-fired areas) and portable extinguishers (CO2, foam, dry powder). Fire main + emergency fire pump water must always be available at the hydrants and nozzles.
Emergency generator, ana güç kaybında (b: On loss of main power (black-out), the emergency generator starts automatically under SOLAS II-1 Reg. 43 and supplies vital services (emergency lighting, navigation, GMDSS, steering, fire pump, watertight doors) via the emergency switchboard. Automatic starting must be completed within 45 seconds.
Emergency generator haftalık çalıştırma: The emergency generator is given a weekly running test (usually on load) and a monthly black-out simulation; the fuel tank is kept full, the batteries charged and the starting air/system ready. Test records are evidence for PSC and class.
Emergency fire pump, makine dairesi yang: In an engine room fire (the main fire pump may be out of action), the emergency fire pump runs from an independent power source (emergency generator or separate diesel) and pressurizes the fire main. It is located outside the engine room and has an independent sea suction. It is tested weekly; priming, pressure and flow rate are verified.
Kaynak, taşlama, kesme gibi sıcak işler,: Hot work such as welding, grinding and cutting is a major source of fire in the engine room. A hot work permit requires gas-free measurement (LEL 0%, surroundings cleared of combustibles), a fire watch, extinguishers ready, isolation of nearby fuel/oil and the approval of the Master + Chief Engineer. The fire watch is maintained at the end of the job and for 1 hour afterwards.
Tank/kapalı alan içinde hot work için ek: Hot work inside a tank/enclosed space requires an additional double permit: hot work + enclosed space. Watch out for sparks and drops of hot metal falling to lower levels (e.g. onto oil in the bilge); the areas below are also cleaned and covered.
Dönen veya enerjili ekipman üzerinde bak: When maintenance is carried out on rotating or energized equipment, the energy source (electrical, hydraulic, pneumatic, steam) is physically locked and tagged under LOTO. This prevents unauthorized start-up. Each lock is unique and can be removed only by the person doing the job. Starting air is the most critical LOTO point while the main engine is being turned.
Boş yakıt tankı, kazan, krank karteri, s: Entry into enclosed spaces such as empty fuel tanks, boilers, crankcases, bilge wells and cofferdams is made under an enclosed space entry permit. Before entry, the atmosphere is measured: O2 20.9%, LEL 0%, toxic gases (H2S, CO) within safe limits. Continuous ventilation, a standby person (attendant), communications and a rescue plan are mandatory.
Oil mist alarmı veya sıcak yatak sonrası: Opening the crankcase after an oil mist alarm or a hot bearing carries a special risk: a sudden inflow of air (oxygen), a hot surface and atomized oil vapor can trigger a crankcase explosion. For this reason, after the engine is stopped, a cooling-down period of at least 15-30 minutes is allowed, the crankcase doors are opened slowly and from the side, and no one stands in line with a door being opened.
Makine dairesi dışından (köprü/fire stat: Emergency stops that can be activated from outside the engine room (bridge/fire station): remote stop of fuel/oil transfer pumps, separator/booster pump stop, ventilation fan stop and quick-closing valves. These arrangements cut off the fuel supply to a fire. All remote stops are tested periodically and must be clearly labeled.
Skylight, fire damper ve ventilation kap: The skylight, fire damper and ventilation closing arrangements are there to limit smoke/air in the event of fire. Regular greasing and function testing ensure that these mechanical arrangements work without rusting up or seizing.
Yakıt/yağ tankı çıkışlarındaki quick-clo: In a fire, the quick-closing valves on fuel/oil tank outlets are closed remotely to cut off the fire's fuel source. They are tested periodically; the spring/pneumatic trip mechanism and the valve movement are verified. A seized (non-closing) QCV means disaster in a fire.
ISM Code ve SOLAS gereği düzenli tatbika: Regular drills required by the ISM Code and SOLAS: fire drill (monthly), abandon ship, enclosed space entry & rescue (every 2 months), black-out / emergency generator (monthly), steering gear failure and oil spill (SOPEP). The Chief Engineer ensures that engine room scenarios are realistic and varied; after each drill, a debrief is held and improvements are recorded.
MSC.1/Circ.1432 kapsamında tüm yangın ko: Under MSC.1/Circ.1432, all fire protection equipment (detectors, CO2, fire pumps, portable extinguishers, BA sets, fire dampers) is placed on a maintenance/test schedule and entered in the PMS. These records are the primary evidence at the class annual survey and in a PSC inspection; a missing record is a deficiency.
Makine dairesi emniyeti, tek bir ekipman: Engine room safety is not about a single piece of equipment; it is the management of the continuous soundness of the prevention, detection, containment and response barriers. The Chief Engineer's task is to make sure that none of these barriers is taken out of service "temporarily" and that each of them has been tested in a provable way. A shortcut in safety is a price that is paid sooner or later.
MARPOL'ün tüm ekleri (I-VI) makine daire: All the annexes of MARPOL (I-VI) concern the engine room. In the USA, APPS makes keeping a false Oil Record Book a federal crime; seafarers can be given a "whistleblower" award (up to 50% of the fine). For this reason, a report by a single crew member can bring the company a fine of millions of dollars and a prison sentence for the responsible officer.
Baş Mühendis için temel ilke: \"kayıtla: The basic principle for the Chief Engineer: "the record must match reality exactly". A bypass line (magic pipe), manipulation of records or tricking the 15 ppm equipment is never acceptable. Even if equipment fails, correct recording and proper disposal (shore reception) are the only right course.
Baş Mühendis bu akışların her biri için: The Chief Engineer manages the correct equipment, the correct record book and the correct disposal route for each of these streams. Each stream has its own record book, and these are cross-checked during inspections.
OWS (genelde gravity coalescer + ikinci: The OWS (usually a gravity coalescer + second-stage filter) separates oil from bilge water. The discharge water is measured continuously by the 15 ppm Oil Content Meter (OCM/oil monitor); when 15 ppm is exceeded, the three-way valve automatically returns the water to the bilge tank (it cannot be pumped overboard). This is the core of the MEPC.107(49) standard.
OWS'in düzgün çalışması coalescer eleman: Proper OWS operation depends on cleaning the coalescer elements, calibrating the oil monitor and correctly managing emulsions. Detergents/cleaning chemicals create emulsions in bilge water; these emulsions reduce the separating efficiency of the OWS and keep triggering the alarm. For this reason, the use of detergents in the engine room is kept under control.
Baş Mühendis, OWS her çalıştırıldığında:: Every time the OWS is run, the Chief Engineer supervises the operator, matches the oil monitor record with the ORB, and verifies the overboard discharge time and the position. If the OWS is defective, the bilge water is delivered ashore; "bypass because of a defect" is never an option.
Sludge; purifier deşarjı, fuel/oil arıtm: Sludge is the oily waste from purifier discharges, fuel/oil treatment residues and drains. The generation rate is estimated at approximately 1-1.5% of fuel consumption (IMO sludge generation formula). The balance between sludge tank capacity and daily generation is monitored; sludge is burned in the incinerator or delivered to a shore reception facility.
Sludge ölçümü (sounding) düzenli yapılır: Sludge is sounded regularly and entered in the ORB under Code C/D. An imbalance between generation and disposal (e.g. very little shore disposal but a low tank level) raises suspicion of a "magic pipe" during inspections; the sludge balance must therefore be consistent and traceable.
Incinerator (IMO type-approved), sludge: The incinerator (IMO type-approved) burns sludge and solid waste. Its use is restricted in special areas and inside ports, and also under certain distance rules. The correct operating temperature (combustion chamber usually 850°C+), the difficulty of burning sludge with a high water content, and flue gas quality are managed. Incinerator running hours and the quantity burned are recorded.
ORB Part I (makine dairesi operasyonları: ORB Part I (machinery space operations) records every oily waste operation: ballasting/cleaning of fuel tanks, bilge water disposal, sludge disposal, bunkering, OWS use, accidental/exceptional discharge. Each entry is made with time, position, quantity and tank identification and is signed by the officer in charge; each page is signed by the Master.
Kayıtlar gerçek zamanlı, silinmeden (düz: Entries are made in real time, without erasures (corrections by a single line + initials) and completely. A complete, correct and up-to-date ORB is the first checkpoint of a PSC and USCG inspection. Gaps, late entries or a mismatch with reality are the most common causes of deficiencies and prosecutions.
Baş Mühendis, ORB kayıtlarını oil monito: The Chief Engineer cross-checks the ORB entries against the oil monitor log, sludge soundings, incinerator hours, shore disposal receipts and tank levels. All these records must be consistent. The Chief Engineer carries out this reconciliation personally before an inspection; if there is an inconsistency, it is disclosed and corrected rather than hidden.
BWM Convention, geminin ballast suyundak: The BWM Convention makes compliance with the D-2 biological standard mandatory to control invasive organisms in a ship's ballast water. Modern ships are fitted with a type-approved BWMS (UV, electrochlorination, ozone). The Chief Engineer manages the correct operation of the BWMS, sensor calibration and the recording of ballast operations in the BWRB (Ballast Water Record Book).
BWMS arızasında contingency measures (al: If the BWMS fails, contingency measures (alternative port, mid-ocean exchange to D-1 as a temporary measure, shore reception) and notification of the relevant port authority come into play. The USCG in the USA and some ports inspect BWMS compliance strictly and take samples.
Her ballast alımı, deşarjı, BWMS treatme: Every ballast uptake, discharge, BWMS treatment and failure is recorded in the BWRB. The entry includes time, position, quantity and treatment status. Like the ORB, this book is examined during inspections and must be consistent with reality.
SOx emisyonu doğrudan yakıt sülfürüne ba: SOx emissions depend directly on fuel sulfur; the global limit of 0.50% and the ECA limit of 0.10% apply (see the Fuel Management section). Ships with scrubbers use HSFO, but EGCS washwater must be kept within the pH, PAH and turbidity limits (MEPC guidelines) and monitored continuously. Some ports prohibit open-loop scrubber discharge.
NOx emisyonu motorun yanma sıcaklığına b: NOx emissions depend on the combustion temperature of the engine. For Tier III, SCR (Selective Catalytic Reduction — with urea/AdBlue) or EGR (Exhaust Gas Recirculation) is used. Every engine is certified with a NOx Technical File; the setting parameters (injection timing, nozzle, cam) must be kept within the range permitted by this file. Unauthorized "tuning" is a NOx violation.
EIAPP sertifikası ve onboard NOx verific: The EIAPP certificate and the onboard NOx verification procedure prove that the engine is in its certified condition. On the engine, the Chief Engineer uses only the components and settings permitted by the NOx Technical File.
MARPOL Annex IV, lağım suyu deşarjını dü: MARPOL Annex IV regulates the discharge of sewage: sewage treated in a type-approved STP (Sewage Treatment Plant) may be discharged to sea under certain conditions; untreated sewage may be discharged only more than 12 nm from land, with the ship en route and at a certain speed. The biological process (activated sludge) and disinfection performance of the STP are monitored.
Annex V, çöpün denize atılmasını çok büy: Annex V prohibits the discharge of garbage into the sea to a very large extent; plastics are strictly prohibited. Every disposal (ashore, incinerator, limited discharge to sea) is recorded under the Garbage Management Plan and in the Garbage Record Book. Engine room waste (oily rags, used filters, paint cans) is segregated into the correct category and landed ashore.
SEEMP (Ship Energy Efficiency Management: The SEEMP (Ship Energy Efficiency Management Plan) and the company's environmental management system (in some cases ISO 14001) continuously monitor and improve energy and waste performance. On the engine room side, the Chief Engineer is the data provider and implementer for these systems; trend reports are shared with the superintendent.
PSC ve vetting denetimlerinde çevre odak: Environmental focus points in PSC and vetting inspections: ORB/GRB/BWRB accuracy, 15 ppm alarm test, OWS function, sludge balance, incinerator records, scrubber washwater monitoring and sulfur compliance. Missing or inconsistent records are enough to get the ship detained and to damage the company's record. The Chief Engineer ensures that these records are always ready for inspection.
Çevre uyumluluğu, Baş Mühendis için tekn: For the Chief Engineer, environmental compliance is a test of honesty and discipline more than of technical knowledge. Equipment may fail and operations may become difficult, but correct recording and proper disposal are always the only legitimate course. A single false entry can destroy a career of many years and the company's reputation. A culture of transparent, traceable records that match reality exactly protects both the sea and the ship.
Her yedek parça, ekipmanın kritikliğine: Every spare part is classified according to the criticality of the equipment. A "critical spare" is a part whose failure would take the ship out of service (off-hire) or endanger safety: for example, main engine exhaust valves, fuel injectors, fuel pump plungers, T/C shaft bearings and generator crank bearings. These parts are always kept on board in at least the specified quantity.
İkinci kategori \"insurance spare\"dır —: The second category is "insurance spares" — parts that rarely fail but have a long lead time and cause serious off-hire if they fail (e.g. main engine cylinder cover, crankshaft bearing shell). The third category is "running spares/consumables": frequently replaced items such as gaskets, O-rings, filters, V-belts and gland packing. The Chief Engineer manages these three categories with separate stock strategies.
PSC ve klas surveyor, bu zorunlu yedekle: PSC and class surveyors check the physical presence of these mandatory spares and that they match their certificates. A missing mandatory spare is grounds for a "deficiency" and, in serious cases, for detention. The Chief Engineer manages this list in the inventory with a separate "do-not-use without replenishment" tag.
Her kalem için minimum (reorder point) v: A minimum (reorder point) and a maximum stock level are defined for each item. The minimum level is calculated allowing for the consumption rate, the lead time and the safety stock. The reorder point is determined by the formula: reorder point = (average daily consumption × lead time) + safety stock.
PMS/ERP yazılımı (AMOS, ShipManager, Sta: PMS/ERP software (AMOS, ShipManager, Star IPS, TM Master) monitors these levels automatically and generates warnings for items that fall below the minimum. The Chief Engineer reviews these warnings weekly and turns them into requisitions.
Yedekler, makine deposu (engine store) i: Spares are labeled in the engine store with a systematic bin/rack number. Each part must match its record in the PMS (part number, manufacturer, location). A wrong location record means the part cannot be found during an emergency breakdown and leads to unnecessary duplicate orders.
Yılda en az bir kez fiziksel sayım (stoc: A physical count (stock-take) is carried out at least once a year; the PMS record is compared with the actual stock and discrepancies are corrected. A count before a survey and before a handover is critical. Parts liable to corrode in a humid environment are stored in VCI (Volatile Corrosion Inhibitor) packaging with grease protection.
Requisition, parçanın tam tanımıyla hazı: A requisition is prepared with a full description of the part: maker, type/model, part number (drawing/position no.), quantity, justification and urgency code. A vague description ("gasket for pump") leads to wrong supply and delay; always use the maker's catalog position number.
Aciliyet kodlaması tipiktir: AOG/urgent: Typical urgency coding: AOG/urgent (risk of ship operations stopping), normal (for planned maintenance), routine (stock replenishment). The Chief Engineer limits urgent orders to those that are really critical; overuse of "urgent" means a loss of both money and credibility.
Sipariş, geminin sefer planına göre uygu: The order is routed to a suitable delivery port according to the ship's voyage plan. Spares are delivered through the ship's agent or by a forwarder; customs procedures (in-transit/under bond) and the delivery window must be synchronized with the voyage plan. A badly timed delivery means the part does not reach the ship in time.
Ağır/büyük parçalar (silindir kapağı, kr: For heavy/large parts (cylinder cover, crank bearing), drydock or a suitable port is planned; crane capacity and manifold/access preparations are assessed in advance. Consumables containing dangerous substances (chemicals, gas cylinders) require IMDG shipping documentation.
Makine yedek parça ve sarf bütçesi, gemi: The engine spare parts and consumables budget is a significant item of the ship's annual OPEX. The Chief Engineer spends within the annual budget approved by the company (Superintendent) and reports the actual vs budget variance monthly. Unplanned major breakdowns strain the budget; anticipating failures through predictive maintenance is therefore a direct cost saving.
Harcama kontrolünde \"total cost of owne: A "total cost of ownership" approach is fundamental to spending control: a cheap but low-quality (e.g. non-OEM) spare can turn out more expensive in the long run because of its short life and failure risk. The Chief Engineer sets the quality-cost balance according to equipment criticality.
Sarf malzemesi tüketimi (yağ, gres, kimy: Consumption of consumables (oil, grease, chemicals, filters) is monitored as a trend. An abnormal increase in consumption is a sign either of a hidden fault (e.g. an oil leak) or of undisciplined use. By reviewing the consumption log, the Chief Engineer both controls cost and catches hidden technical problems early.
Atık ve sona eren raf ömürlü kimyasallar: Managing waste and chemicals whose shelf life has expired (shelf-life expired) is also important for cost and for the environment. Old stock is used first on the FIFO (first-in-first-out) principle; chemicals past their shelf life are disposed of under MARPOL Annex V/the appropriate waste procedure.
Belirli ekipman ve donanım, periyodik se: Certain equipment and gear require periodic servicing and certification: fire extinguishers, liferafts, EEBDs, SCBA, lifting equipment (lifting gear/LOLER), pressure vessels, calibrated measuring instruments (gas detectors, OWS 15 ppm monitor). The Chief Engineer tracks in the PMS the certificate expiry dates of those items that belong to the engine department.
Süresi dolmuş bir servis sertifikası (ör: An expired service certificate (e.g. CO2 system service, lifting gear test) is both a PSC deficiency and a safety risk. Service windows are planned in advance according to the voyage plan and the ports where a suitable service provider is available.
Kritik parçaların (örn. krank yatağı, ex: Batch/serial number traceability is kept for critical parts (e.g. crank bearings, exhaust valves); this is needed for a maker recall or for the analysis of a recurring failure. The fitting date and running hours of the spare fitted and the condition of the part removed are recorded in the PMS work order.
Modern PMS sistemlerinde her work order,: In modern PMS systems, every work order automatically deducts (issues) the spare parts used from stock. This integration makes actual consumption traceable and reduces the margin for manual error. When a work order is closed, the Chief Engineer checks that parts consumption has been entered correctly; otherwise inventory reliability suffers.
Şirket merkezi (ofis) ile gemi arasında: Data synchronization (replication) between the company head office and the ship is carried out regularly; this lets the Superintendent see the ship's stock remotely and makes it possible to obtain the advantage of fleet-wide bulk purchasing (frame agreements).
Yedek parça veritabanının doğruluğu (mas: The accuracy of the spare parts database (master data quality) is the foundation of the whole system: wrong part numbers, missing maker information or duplicate records cause errors in both ordering and stock. The Chief Engineer and the engine team are responsible for entering the maker's spare list completely in the PMS when new equipment comes on board.
Tanker vetting (OCIMF SIRE 2.0) ve TMSA: In tanker vetting (OCIMF SIRE 2.0) and TMSA audits, the availability of critical spare parts, the effectiveness of the stock management system and the consistency of consumption records are questioned. The inspector may ask to see a random critical part physically; a mismatch between the PMS record and the actual stock results in an observation.
Klas survey öncesi, zorunlu (mandatory): Before a class survey, the mandatory spares list is verified by a physical count, and urgent replenishment is started for any missing items. Spare parts to be used during the survey (e.g. a new spindle/seat for an exhaust valve to be overhauled) are brought on board in advance; otherwise the survey is postponed and cost/off-hire increase.
Baş Mühendis değişiminde (handover), açı: At a change of Chief Engineer (handover), open requisitions, expected deliveries, critical stock status and actual budget spending are handed over in a written handover note. The incoming Chief Engineer takes over by comparing the physical stock with the PMS record; any discrepancies found are recorded at handover.
Bu süreklilik, geminin yedek parça güven: This continuity ensures that the reliability of the ship's spare parts does not depend on a single person. A well-kept inventory and a clear handover enable the new Chief Engineer to make the right decisions from day one.
Aşağıdaki kontrol listesi, Baş Mühendisi: The following checklist helps the Chief Engineer to stay systematic in spare parts and materials management:
Yedek parça ve malzeme yönetimi, geminin: Spare parts and materials management is an art of balance that requires protecting the ship's operational reliability and its cost-effectiveness at the same time. The Chief Engineer neither wastes capital by tying it up in excessive stock nor risks off-hire by leaving a critical part short. Systematic criticality analysis, a disciplined inventory and correctly timed supply are the technical basis of this balance.
Tipik bir ticari gemide makine departman: On a typical merchant ship, the engine department consists of the Chief Engineer (C/E), Second Engineer (2/E), Third Engineer (3/E), Fourth Engineer (4/E), Electro-Technical Officer (ETO/Electrician) and the engine ratings (Fitter, Motorman, Oiler, Wiper). The Chief Engineer reports directly to the Master and, ashore, to the Superintendent; within the department, the Second Engineer runs day-to-day operations.
İkinci Mühendis, bakım planlamasının ve: The Second Engineer is in practice responsible for maintenance planning and the organization of watches, and puts the Chief Engineer's strategic decisions into practice on the job. The ETO is responsible for automation, electrical and high-voltage systems and has a critical role on modern ships. Ratings report to a specific engineer and receive their work orders from that engineer.
Görev karmaşasını önlemek için Baş Mühen: To prevent confusion over tasks, the Chief Engineer uses a RACI matrix (Responsible, Accountable, Consulted, Informed). For example, in a bunkering operation the Chief Engineer may be Accountable, the Second Engineer Responsible and the Third Engineer Consulted on the soundings.
Bu matris, yeni binen personelin sorumlu: This matrix enables newly joined personnel to understand the limits of their responsibilities quickly and shows the maturity of the department's organization in inspections (vetting/PSC).
Modern gemilerin çoğu UMS (E0/AUT notati: Most modern ships are classed for UMS (E0/AUT notation); the engine room runs without a watch at night and alarms are relayed to the ECR and the bridge. The Duty Engineer is responsible through the call system (dead-man alarm, engineer's call). On ships with traditional watchkeeping, a 4-hour watch system (0000-0400, 0400-0800 etc.) is used.
Baş Mühendis, UMS'e geçiş öncesi günlük: Before switching to UMS, the Chief Engineer makes sure of the daily "rounds" discipline, that the alarm system has been tested and that the dead-man alarm is working. During maneuvering, port entry/departure and bad weather, the engine room is put on manual control (manned).
MLC 2006 ve STCW, yorgunluk (fatigue) yö: MLC 2006 and STCW make fatigue management mandatory: a minimum of 10 hours of rest in any 24 hours and a minimum of 77 hours in any 7 days. Rest may be divided into no more than two periods, one of which must be at least 6 hours uninterrupted.
Baş Mühendis, yoğun liman/bakım dönemler: During busy port/maintenance periods, the Chief Engineer monitors the rest hour records and prevents the risk of violations. Fatigue is the leading human factor in engine room accidents and must be managed deliberately.
Yeni binen her ekip üyesi, görevine başl: Every newly joined crew member goes through familiarization under the ISM Code before starting duties. The Chief Engineer, or a Second Engineer designated for the task, shows the emergency escape routes, fire stations, EEBD/SCBA locations, emergency stops and quick-closing valves, and the bilge and ballast system.
Familiarization checklist imzalanmadan p: Personnel are not put on an independent watch until the familiarization checklist has been signed. This process is especially critical in multinational crews with a language barrier and is supported by visual/hands-on instruction.
Genel tanıtımı, sorumlu olunacak ekipman: The general familiarization is followed by detailed familiarization with the equipment the person will be responsible for. For example, the Third Engineer is introduced to the generators, purifiers and boiler, and the ETO to the switchboard, PMS automation and high-voltage systems. Vendor manuals, P&ID diagrams and the notes of previous personnel are used.
Baş Mühendis, ekipman tanıtımının teorik: The Chief Engineer ensures that equipment familiarization includes practical elements (start/stop, alarm reset, normal parameters) besides theoretical knowledge; familiarization "on paper" is not accepted.
Baş Mühendis, her zabitin pratik yetkinl: The Chief Engineer assesses each officer's practical competence by observation: taking indicator cards, purifier overhaul, fuel changeover, paralleling and troubleshooting. TMSA Element 3 expects a documented competence assessment.
Eksik görülen alanlar için kişiye özel g: For areas found to be weak, an individual development plan (training need analysis) is drawn up. Strong performance is managed with a recommendation for promotion, weak performance with constructive feedback.
Sefer sonu veya periyodik appraisal form: End-of-voyage or periodic appraisal forms are entered into the company SMS and feed the promotion/re-employment decisions of the crewing department ashore. The Chief Engineer's fair, specific and development-oriented assessment directly affects team motivation.
Olumsuz değerlendirmeler somut örneklerl: Negative assessments must be backed by specific examples and must not be made personal. Feedback is given as soon as possible after the event, wherever possible.
Makine departmanı; black-out recovery, e: The engine department takes part in black-out recovery, engine room fire, flooding, steering gear failure and enclosed space rescue drills. The Chief Engineer plans and observes these drills and reports any deficiencies. Drills must be run with realistic scenarios and must not turn into a routine "form-filling" formality.
Her drill sonrası debrief yapılır: ne iy: A debrief is held after every drill: what went well, what needs improving, what deficiencies were identified. These outputs shape the scenario of the next drill.
Belirli ekipmanlar (MAN ES ME-C engine,: Certain equipment (MAN ES ME-C engine, Alfa Laval separator, high-voltage switchboard, BWMS) requires manufacturer training. The Chief Engineer tracks which personnel need which certificate and forwards requests for shore training to the Superintendent.
High-voltage (1 kV üstü) sistemler için: Under STCW, special training is mandatory for high-voltage (above 1 kV) systems. As new technologies (scrubber, LNG dual-fuel, methanol) come on board, training needs are updated.
Baş Mühendis, ekibinde \"just culture\": The Chief Engineer establishes a "just culture" in the team, that is, an environment where mistakes are reported honestly without punishment. Near-miss and unsafe condition reporting is encouraged; these reports are early warnings of major accidents.
Susturulan küçük hatalar, büyük kazaları: Small errors that are hushed up are the forerunners of major accidents. Most human-factor machinery accidents result from an accumulation of small abnormalities that were not reported in time.
Modern gemi ekipleri çok-uluslu ve çok-d: Modern ship crews are multinational and multilingual. The Chief Engineer makes sure that the common working language (usually English) is used clearly in safety-critical communication. Toolbox talks, permit-to-work briefings and drills are conducted in a way that everyone understands.
Kültürel duyarlılık ve adil davranış, ek: Cultural sensitivity and fair treatment directly affect team cohesion and therefore operational safety. A language barrier can prevent critical information from being passed on and lead to an accident.
Baş Mühendis, PMS'ten gelen iş emirlerin: The Chief Engineer distributes the work orders coming from the PMS according to the team's capacity. The workload must be balanced during busy voyage periods, port stays and before drydock; otherwise fatigue increases and maintenance quality falls.
Kritik görevler (örneğin exhaust valve o: Critical tasks (for example exhaust valve overhaul) are given to experienced officers and routine tasks to juniors; however, to give them a chance to learn, juniors are included in demanding tasks under the supervision of an experienced colleague.
Drydock döneminde iş yükü zirve yapar; B: During drydock the workload peaks; the Chief Engineer prioritizes the critical path jobs (shaft survey, tail-shaft draw, main engine overhaul) with a master plan and manages coordination with the shipyard team.
Baş Mühendis değişiminde detaylı bir han: At a change of Chief Engineer, a detailed handover report is prepared: main engine condition, open work orders, critical spare parts stock, survey schedule, outstanding problems and notes on crew competence. This continuity ensures that department performance is maintained independently of individuals.
Eksik handover, yeni gelen Baş Mühendis': An incomplete handover leaves the incoming Chief Engineer starting out with blind spots and lets preventable problems grow. The handover is made face to face, on board and in writing.
Aşağıdaki kontrol listesi, makine person: The following checklist summarizes the key elements of engine personnel management and should be reviewed in every voyage cycle.
Makine personelinin yönetimi, Baş Mühend: Managing engine personnel is the most visible reflection of the Chief Engineer's technical leadership. A well-managed team produces fewer accidents, higher maintenance quality and a stronger safety culture. The modern Chief Engineer is as much a mentor, planner and human resources manager as an engineer.
Sınıf sertifikası beş yıllık döngüde yen: The class certificate is renewed on a five-year cycle. The cycle includes the Annual Survey (every year, with a ±3-month window), the Intermediate Survey (between the 2nd and 3rd year) and the Special/Renewal Survey (5th year). Flag State certificates (Safety Construction, IOPP, IAPP, MARPOL) are also surveyed on a similar cycle.
Baş Mühendis, tüm sertifikaların geçerli: The Chief Engineer tracks the expiry dates of all certificates and the survey windows. An expired certificate keeps the ship from sailing; planning must therefore be proactive.
Modern gemilerin çoğu CMS programıyla yö: Most modern ships are managed under a CMS program: machinery items are surveyed in turn under a program spread over five years, so that each item is surveyed once every 5 years. This removes the burden of stopping all the machinery at once.
Onaylı Chief Engineer Survey (CHE) yetki: Where approved Chief Engineer Survey (CHE) authority exists, certain CMS items may be opened up, examined and reported on by the Chief Engineer; the surveyor confirms this. This authority is an important tool for survey economy.
Onaylı PMS scheme'i altında, makine bakı: Under an approved PMS scheme, machinery maintenance is accepted as evidence for class surveys. The Chief Engineer ensures that PMS records (work order, date, measurements, remarks, spare parts used) are complete and consistent with the actual situation on site.
PMS kayıtlarının \"kâğıt üstünde\" tutul: If PMS records are kept "on paper" while the work is not done on site and this is found at a survey, it leads to cancellation of the system's approval and serious consequences. Consistency between records and actual work on site is checked.
Baş Mühendis, sörvey öncesi şu kayıtları: Before a survey, the Chief Engineer keeps the following records ready: crank deflection measurements, exhaust valve overhaul, T/C overhaul, fuel injector pop test, safety device tests (overspeed, low LO pressure trip), boiler safety valve test and relief valve setting records.
Ayrıca ORB (Oil Record Book), OWS 15 ppm: In addition, the ORB (Oil Record Book), OWS 15 ppm alarm test, emergency generator/fire pump test records, bilge alarm tests and sentinel valve test records are primary evidence for surveys and PSC.
Special survey'de surveyor, belirli sili: At a special survey, the surveyor may ask for certain cylinders, pistons, bearings and exhaust valves to be opened up and examined. The Chief Engineer plans the opening-up work, takes the measurements (liner wear, ring gap, bearing clearance) and compares them with the class acceptance criteria.
Açma işlemleri yorucu ve zaman alıcıdır;: Opening-up work is tiring and time-consuming; it requires a good plan, the right tools, availability of spare parts and an experienced team. With CMS, this burden can be lightened by spreading it over the years.
Tail-shaft (pervane şaftı) survey'i, yağ: The tail-shaft (propeller shaft) survey is carried out every 5 years or at extended intervals, depending on the lubrication type and seal condition. On ships with an oil-lubricated stern tube and an approved seal system, the survey interval can be extended (Extended Tail Shaft Survey).
Şaft draw (çekme) gerektiren survey'lerd: In surveys requiring a shaft draw (withdrawal), wear-down measurement, seal renewal and NDT (non-destructive testing) are carried out. The Chief Engineer integrates this plan into the drydock master plan.
Bir sörveyde tespit edilen ve hemen gide: A deficiency found during a survey that cannot be rectified immediately is recorded as a "Condition of Class" (or Memorandum) and must be rectified by a set date. The Chief Engineer tracks open CoCs in a register and closes them before the due date.
Süresi geçen bir CoC, sertifikanın askıy: An overdue CoC can lead to suspension of the certificate. CoC management is therefore a critical part of survey preparation and is carried out in coordination with the technical office ashore.
Her bulgu için Baş Mühendis bir root cau: For each finding, the Chief Engineer draws up a root cause analysis and a corrective action plan. This aims not only to fix the problem but also to prevent it from recurring, and is entered into the company SMS.
Yedek parça temini gereken aksiyonlar iç: For actions that require spare parts, the ordering process is started; if a temporary repair is needed, class approval is obtained and a permanent solution is planned.
PSC denetiminde makine tarafında en sık: The most common engine-side findings in PSC inspections: ORB kept incorrectly/incompletely, OWS 15 ppm alarm failure, emergency generator not working, fire damper/quick-closing valve failure, bilge alarm disabled, and emergency fire pump starting problems.
Baş Mühendis, bu sık bulguları proaktif: The Chief Engineer checks these common findings proactively; before the PSC inspector boards, critical emergency equipment is tested and its records are updated. A detention is a serious financial and reputational loss for the company and the ship.
Paris ve Tokyo MoU'lar her yıl belirli b: The Paris and Tokyo MoUs run a concentrated inspection campaign (CIC) on a specific theme every year: for example MARPOL Annex VI, fire safety or stability. The Chief Engineer follows the annual CIC theme and prepares the ship specially in that area.
CIC döneminde ilgili alandaki ekipman, k: During a CIC, the equipment, records and personnel competence in the relevant area are questioned in detail; proactive preparation directly affects the inspection result.
Özellikle tankerlerde vetting (SIRE insp: Vetting (SIRE inspection) is critical, especially on tankers; a negative vetting leaves the ship out of charter. SIRE 2.0 is risk-based and focused on the human factor; the inspector directly questions the competence of the engine team (open questions, hardware/process/human element).
Baş Mühendis, makine dairesinin temizliğ: The Chief Engineer keeps the engine room clean and free of leaks and keeps labeling, the permit-to-work system and the consistency of the team's answers in good order. The visual order of the engine room sets the inspector's first impression.
Energy management, emisyon takibi (EEXI/: Energy management, emissions monitoring (EEXI/CII), critical equipment reliability and continuous improvement are the basic expectations of these elements and must be documented.
Sörvey ve trial öncesi Baş Mühendis bir: Before a survey or trial, the Chief Engineer prepares a test program: main engine safety trip tests, generator black-out/auto-start, emergency generator load test, steering gear changeover and fire pump remote start. The result of each test is recorded.
Testler sörvey günü değil, öncesinde yap: Tests are carried out before the survey day, not on it, so that any faults found can be rectified in time. An unexpected failure on survey day is a loss of both time and reputation.
Drydock veya büyük tamirat sonrası sea t: During the sea trial after drydock or a major repair, main engine load tests, gradual load increases, vibration measurements and performance verification are carried out. The Chief Engineer compares the results with the baseline and presents them to the class surveyor.
Trial verileri, gelecekteki performans i: Trial data form a reference point for future performance monitoring and are also used for EEXI/CII verification.
Survey preparation is a joint ship-shore task. The Chief Engineer coordinates the survey schedule, the required spare parts/service team and attendance planning with the Superintendent. Surveyor attendance is synchronized with the port call.
İyi bir koordinasyon; sörveyin gecikmede: Good coordination ensures that the survey is completed without delay, without missing evidence and without additional cost.
Aşağıdaki kontrol listesi, her sörvey ön: The following checklist summarizes the engine department's preparation before each survey.
Sörvey hazırlığı, Baş Mühendis'in planla: Survey preparation is a test of the Chief Engineer's planning discipline and culture of honest record-keeping. Proactive, documented preparation coordinated between ship and shore keeps the ship certified, clean in inspections and fit for charter. A survey should not be a last-minute rush but a discipline maintained continuously.
Teknik raporlama; günlük (noon report),: Technical reporting consists of daily (noon report), weekly (summary/issues), monthly (detailed technical) and event-based (defect/incident) layers. Each layer feeds a different level of decision-making: daily reports feed operational decisions, weekly reports tactical decisions and monthly reports strategic decisions.
Baş Mühendis bu döngüyü bir disiplin ola: The Chief Engineer runs this cycle as a discipline; late or incomplete reports lead to wrong decisions ashore and wasted resources. Reports are prepared in a standard format with correct data.
Raporların değeri, verinin doğruluğuyla: The value of reports is proportional to the accuracy of the data. Manipulated or "corrected" consumption data cause performance disputes, vetting problems and loss of trust. The Chief Engineer stays true to the raw data and reports anomalies with an explanation.
Özellikle yakıt tüketim ve performans ve: Fuel consumption and performance data in particular have legal consequences in charter party settlements and in EU MRV/IMO DCS reporting; accuracy is therefore vital.
Noon report, her gün öğlen (12:00 local/: The noon report gives, every day at noon (12:00 local/UTC), the ship's position, the distance covered in the last 24 hours, average speed, main engine rpm, slip, weather/sea conditions, fuel consumption (HFO/VLSFO, MGO, cylinder oil, system oil) and ROB.
Baş Mühendis, raporun makine tarafını (c: The Chief Engineer verifies the engine side of the report (consumption, RPM, ME load, generator running hours, ROB) on the basis of sounding and flowmeter data. Bridge and engine data must be consistent.
Noon report verileri, charterer'ın gemi: Noon report data are used by the charterer to assess the ship's performance (good weather speed/consumption warranty). Bad weather, current and fouling increase consumption; the Chief Engineer explains these factors in the report.
Performance dispute durumunda, doğru kay: In a performance dispute, correctly recorded weather data and engine parameters protect the ship from unjustified claims. The data are therefore kept complete and realistic.
Baş Mühendis, her bunker sonrası BDN mik: After every bunkering, the Chief Engineer compares the BDN quantity with the ship's tank measurements (sounding/ullage + temperature correction) and reports the difference. Regular ROB reconciliation ensures the accuracy of the consumption calculation and detects possible "short delivery" cases.
Yakıt tüketimi flowmeter (varsa) ve tank: Fuel consumption is cross-checked using the flowmeter (where fitted) and tank measurements. A persistent difference between the two methods calls for a check of the flowmeter calibration or an investigation into measurement error.
Cylinder oil feed rate (g/kWh) ve system: Cylinder oil feed rate (g/kWh) and system oil consumption are reported. An abnormal increase in cylinder oil consumption points to an over-lubrication setting, ring blow-by or liner wear. An increase in the system oil top-up quantity is an indicator of water/fuel ingress or leakage.
Baş Mühendis bu trendleri aylık raporda: The Chief Engineer plots these trends in the monthly report and explains any deviations. Oil consumption is not only a cost; it is also an important indicator of machinery health.
Aylık teknik rapor; tamamlanan ve gecikm: The monthly technical report contains completed and overdue PMS work orders, the condition of critical equipment, open defects and the plan for the coming period. This report enables the technical office ashore to monitor maintenance performance (overdue ratio, planned vs. corrective).
Baş Mühendis, gecikmiş kritik bakımları: The Chief Engineer explains overdue critical maintenance with its reasons (spare parts, weather, port) and presents a recovery plan. Transparency is the key to getting the right support from ashore.
SFOC, exhaust gas spread, T/C devri, sca: SFOC, exhaust gas spread, T/C rpm, scavenge air pressure and oil analysis results are presented as monthly trends. It is not a single day's data that is assessed, but the rolling average and the direction of the trend.
Trend bozulması (örn. SFOC'un sürekli ar: A deteriorating trend (e.g. a steady rise in SFOC) triggers joint diagnosis and intervention planning with experts ashore. This predictive approach prevents sudden failures and voyage disruption.
Bir arıza tespit edildiğinde Baş Mühendi: When a failure is detected, the Chief Engineer quickly prepares a defect report: equipment, description of the failure, probable root cause, operational impact (voyage/safety/environment), temporary measures taken, the proposed permanent solution, and spare parts/service needs.
Raporun netliği, karadaki kararın hızını: The clarity of the report determines how quickly a decision is made ashore. Instead of vague reports such as "engine defective", specific reports backed by measurements and photographs bring effective support.
Ana makine, şaft, kazan veya emniyet sis: Major failures affecting the main engine, shaft, boiler or safety systems must be reported to the classification society and, where required, to the insurer (H&M). The Chief Engineer coordinates this notification with the Master and the Superintendent.
Sınıf bildirimi yapılmayan majör hasar,: Major damage not reported to class puts certificate validity and the insurance claim at risk. Notification thresholds are therefore defined in the SMS and applied rigorously.
Baş Mühendis-Superintendent ilişkisi, ge: The Chief Engineer-Superintendent relationship is the backbone of the ship's technical management. Effective communication must be timely, clear, solution-oriented and documented. When reporting a problem, the Chief Engineer usually also offers a proposal/plan.
Acil konularda telefon/e-posta hızlı kul: For urgent matters, telephone/e-mail is used for speed, but decisions and approvals are confirmed in writing. This written trail is critical later for responsibility and continuity.
Liman tamiratı, servis ekibi attendance': Port repairs, service team attendance, spare parts logistics and drydock planning are a joint task of the Chief Engineer and the Superintendent. The Chief Engineer manages the reality on site; the Superintendent manages the budget and logistics resources.
İyi koordinasyon; tamiratın doğru limand: Good coordination ensures that repairs are carried out in the right port, with the right team and without delaying the ship. Poor coordination leads to off-hire and runaway costs.
IMO Data Collection System (DCS) ve EU M: The IMO Data Collection System (DCS) and EU MRV (Monitoring, Reporting, Verification) require verified reporting of annual fuel consumption and CO2 emission data. The Chief Engineer ensures that consumption data are collected in line with the approved monitoring plan.
2024'ten itibaren EU ETS, denizcilik emi: Since 2024, the EU ETS has covered shipping emissions; correct consumption/emissions data have a direct financial consequence for the calculation of allowances and for cost.
Oil Record Book (ORB Part I — machinery: The Oil Record Book (ORB Part I — machinery space) is the legal record of sludge and bilge management. The Chief Engineer ensures that ORB entries are correct, timely and consistent with operations.
ORB hataları PSC'de en sık ve en ciddi b: ORB errors are among the most frequent and most serious PSC findings; suspicion of a "magic pipe" can lead to criminal consequences. Legal records are the most sensitive part of technical reporting.
Tüm raporlar, e-postalar ve onaylar düze: All reports, e-mails and approvals are archived regularly. This archive is the body of evidence that protects the ship in survey, vetting, performance dispute and insurance processes. At a change of Chief Engineer, this archive is part of the handover.
Dijital raporlama platformları (vessel p: If digital reporting platforms (vessel performance, fleet management software) are used, data entry is done in a disciplined and timely manner.
Aşağıdaki kontrol listesi, teknik raporl: The following checklist summarizes the discipline of technical reporting and company communication.
Teknik raporlama, Baş Mühendis'in karada: Technical reporting is the bridge of trust that the Chief Engineer builds with management ashore. Correct, timely and honest data ensure the right maintenance decisions, fair charter settlements and legal compliance. The modern Chief Engineer must be as good a data manager and communicator as an engineer.
ISM Code Eleman 8, gemilerin olası acil: ISM Code Element 8 requires ships to identify potential emergencies, establish response procedures and hold regular drills. For machinery-related scenarios, the Chief Engineer ensures that these procedures are up to date, realistic and known by the team.
Acil durum prosedürleri muster list ile: Emergency procedures are integrated with the muster list; every crew member's duty in an emergency (e.g. fire team, engine team) is clearly defined. Procedures are reviewed periodically and updated with drill findings.
Acil anda Baş Mühendis hızlı durum değer: In an emergency, the Chief Engineer makes a rapid assessment of the situation: what has happened, what is at risk (people/ship/environment), what resources are available. Instead of panic, procedures internalized through training are applied.
Köprü ile sürekli iletişim kritiktir; Ka: Continuous communication with the bridge is critical; the Master's navigational decision (stopping, anchoring, moving away from the coast) and the Chief Engineer's technical response must be synchronized. The flow of information is two-way, not one-way.
Black-out, tüm ana jeneratörlerin elektr: A black-out is the loss of electrical power from all main generators; the main engine, steering, cooling and lighting stop. Under SOLAS, the emergency generator starts automatically and within 45 seconds supplies the essential services (emergency lighting, communications, emergency steering, navigation).
Dead ship; hiçbir güç olmadan, depolanmı: Dead ship means being able to restart the ship with no power available, using stored energy (starting air, emergency battery). IACS UR M requires the ability to recover from the dead ship condition without external assistance. The emergency air compressor (usually independently driven) is the key to this capability.
Recovery sırası: emergency generator → e: Recovery sequence: emergency generator → filling the main air receiver with the emergency air compressor → starting the first generator → energizing the main busbar → cooling/lubricating pumps → main engine restart. The Chief Engineer and the team must know this sequence by heart.
Seyir sırasında ana makinenin durması (e: A main engine stop (engine stop/trip) while under way is a serious emergency; it is especially critical in a narrow channel, in traffic or in bad weather. The Chief Engineer informs the bridge immediately and determines the cause of the trip (overspeed, low LO pressure, jacket water high temp, scavenge fire).
Slow-down ve shut-down sistemleri (auto: Slow-down and shut-down systems (auto slowdown) cut in to protect the ship. The Chief Engineer distinguishes whether the automatic protection is responding to a real hazard or to a sensor fault; if necessary, the override procedure is applied in a controlled way.
Baş Mühendis, arızanın türüne göre resta: Depending on the type of failure, the Chief Engineer assesses whether the engine can be restarted or needs repair. If there is a risk of crankcase explosion or suspected bearing damage, an uncontrolled restart can end in disaster; in that case the ship is stopped and anchoring/tug assistance is considered.
Tek silindiri devre dışı bırakarak (cut-: In some cases it is possible to proceed at reduced power (limp home) by cutting out one cylinder. This decision is taken in accordance with the manuals and class guidelines, in coordination with the bridge.
Dümen sistemi arızası, gemiyi manevra ka: A steering system failure deprives the ship of its ability to maneuver and creates a risk of collision/grounding. SOLAS requires main and auxiliary steering gear and remote/local control. When a failure occurs, an emergency steering order comes from the bridge to the engine room.
Baş Mühendis/makine ekibi, steering gear: In the steering gear room, the Chief Engineer/engine team applies the procedure for changing over to the standby pump, switching to local control and carrying out helm orders received by telephone/talker. This changeover is rehearsed in periodic drills (under SOLAS, it is tested before leaving port).
SOLAS, limandan ayrılmadan 12 saat içind: SOLAS requires the steering gear to be tested within 12 hours before leaving port and an emergency steering drill to be held every 3 months. The Chief Engineer ensures that these tests are carried out and recorded.
Drill'de helm order iletişimi, pompa cha: In the drill, helm order communication, pump changeover time and rudder response are measured. In a real failure, this rehearsal prevents loss.
Makine dairesi yangınları genellikle yük: Engine room fires usually start when a high-pressure fuel/oil leak comes into contact with a hot surface (exhaust, T/C, manifold). Early detection (fire detection, flame detectors) and rapid response (portable extinguishers, fire team) are critical.
Baş Mühendis, yangının boyutuna göre lok: Depending on the size of the fire, the Chief Engineer directs local firefighting or moves to the decision to withdraw all personnel from the engine room and use the fixed extinguishing system. Fuel quick-closing valves and pump stops cut the fire off from its fuel.
Lokal müdahale yetersizse, makine daires: If local firefighting is insufficient, the engine room is completely cleared of personnel, all openings are closed and the fixed extinguishing system is activated. With a CO2 total flooding system, the gas is not released until the head count has been fully confirmed — asphyxiation is a fatal risk.
Water mist / high-pressure water fog sis: Water mist / high-pressure water fog systems are more flexible than CO2 for local machinery fires (boiler front, purifier, ME) and safer for personnel. The Chief Engineer knows which system is used in which scenario.
Makine dairesinde su yükselmesi; sea che: A rising water level in the engine room may result from a sea chest/sea valve leak, a cooler tube rupture, shell plating damage or a burst pipe. The bilge high-level alarm gives early warning; the Chief Engineer quickly finds the source and isolates it.
Sea water tarafı kaçaklarda ilgili sea v: For leaks on the sea water side, the relevant sea valve is closed and the affected system is bypassed. If the water ingress exceeds the capacity of the pumps, the emergency bilge suction (usually connected to the main circulating pump, large diameter) is brought into use.
Emergency bilge suction valve, en büyük: The emergency bilge suction valve connects the largest-capacity pump directly to the engine room bilge so that water can be pumped out quickly. The Chief Engineer teaches the team where this valve is and how it works, and tests it periodically.
Su alma, geminin stabilitesini ve trim'i: Flooding affects the ship's stability and trim; the Chief Engineer reports the situation to the bridge immediately. If flooding cannot be brought under control, decisions including abandoning ship are taken together with the Master.
Baş Mühendis; black-out, engine room fir: The Chief Engineer plans and conducts black-out, engine room fire, flooding, emergency steering and enclosed space rescue drills. Drills are run with realistic scenarios and timed, and deficiencies are identified in the debrief.
Rutin \"kâğıt doldurma\" tatbikatı tehli: A routine "form-filling" drill is dangerous; it is of no use in a real emergency. Every drill must rehearse what the team will actually do and expose the weak points.
Acil durumda köprü (seyir kararı) ile ma: In an emergency, the bridge (navigational decisions) and the engine room (technical response) must be closely coordinated. The Chief Engineer clearly conveys the situation (remaining power, estimated restart time, maneuverability) to the Master; the Master in turn passes the navigational risk (anchor, tug, distance off the coast) to the engine room.
Ortak bir terminoloji ve iletişim disipl: A common terminology and communication discipline prevent misunderstanding at a critical moment. Radio/telephone communication is carried out by the closed-loop (repeat back and confirm) method.
Her acil durum ve drill, log book ve inc: Every emergency and drill is recorded in the log book and an incident report: what happened, what action was taken, what the outcome was, what lesson was learned. These records are used in class, insurance and company investigations and in future training.
Olay sonrası kök neden analizi ve düzelt: Post-incident root cause analysis and corrective action prevent the same emergency from recurring. Open and honest reporting is the foundation of a learning organization.
Aşağıdaki kontrol listesi, acil durum te: The following checklist summarizes preparedness for technical response in an emergency.
Acil durumda teknik müdahale, Baş Mühend: Technical response in an emergency is the moment of highest responsibility for the Chief Engineer. Success is the combination of technical knowledge, cool-headed decisions, rehearsed procedures and strong coordination with the bridge. The best response is the natural result of good preparation and continuous drills.
Yükleme öncesinde charterer veya termina: Before loading, the pre-stowage plan sent by the charterer or terminal operator is the Chief Officer's first checkpoint. On container ships it comes in bay-row-tier format, on bulk carriers as hold-by-hold tonnage and on tankers as a tank-by-tank parcel distribution. The plan is loaded into the stability/trim/strength software specific to the ship type (e.g. LoadMaster, BluePrint, Cargomax); bending moment, shear force, torsion (for container ships), draft at FP/AP/Mid, GM and list values are checked.
Final cargo plan, Birinci Zabit tarafınd: The final cargo plan is signed by the Chief Officer and submitted to the Master for approval. The approved plan is handed to the chief stevedore, the terminal and the duty officer. If there are last-minute changes to the plan (e.g. a trailer with ramp damage on a ro-ro, contaminated cargo on a tanker), the stability software is run again.
GM değerinin yükleme süresince intact st: The basic principle is that GM must not fall below the intact stability criteria during loading. The IMO 2008 IS Code sets minimum GM values according to ship type (≥0.15 m for general cargo, ≥0.15 m + correction for container ships, and for tankers calculated including the free surface of liquid cargo). Excessive GM, on the other hand, makes a "stiff" ship; short-period, violent rolling overloads the lashing forces and increases the risk of parametric rolling in container stacks.
Çok yumuşak GM ise \"tender\" gemi yarat: A GM that is too small makes a "tender" ship; the rolling period lengthens and the risk of listing increases. By keeping GM within the optimum range, the Chief Officer balances safety, passenger/crew comfort and cargo safety.
Yükleme yazılımı her loading kademesinde: At each loading stage, the loading software shows bending moment (longitudinal), shear force and, on container ships, torsion values. These values must be kept below 100% of the limit; above 85% an alarm is given and the loading sequence is revised.
Aşırı sagging (boğum çökmesi) durumu, ho: Excessive sagging results from loading heavy cargo in the midship holds + light cargo at the ends. Hogging is the opposite. Both lead to fatigue in the hull and, in the long term, to cracks. On bulk carriers, shear force can reach a critical level during "alternate hold" loading; it is therefore mandatory to keep to the CSR-approved sequence.
İdeal trim, gemi tipine ve hız profiline: The ideal trim varies with ship type and speed profile; on modern container ships, "trim optimization" software gives 2-5% fuel savings. The Chief Officer sets the arrival trim as requested by the charterer (usually even keel or slightly by the stern). List is kept below 0.5° wherever possible; otherwise lashing forces are not evenly distributed.
Hold hazırlığı; previous cargo'ya, sonra: Hold preparation is defined at 4 levels according to the previous cargo, the next cargo and the charter party terms: load-ready (sweepup), shovel-clean, grain-clean, hospital-clean. Grain charters require an NCB (National Cargo Bureau) inspection.
Hold hazırlığı; sweeping, washing (sea w: Hold preparation covers sweeping, washing (sea water + fresh water rinse), drying, paint touch-up, smell removal, bilge well cleaning and checking the hatch cover seals. The Chief Officer carries out the hold inspection personally and keeps a photo/video record.
Her gemi, klas onaylı bir Cargo Securing: Every ship must carry a class-approved Cargo Securing Manual. This manual contains the MSL (Maximum Securing Load) values of the lashing equipment, examples of lashing patterns and calculation methods. There are separate chapters for container, ro-ro, project cargo and heavy lift.
CSS Code Annex 13, \"Methods to assess t: CSS Code Annex 13 provides a practical calculation method in its chapter "Methods to assess the efficiency of securing arrangements for non-standardised cargoes". It shows mathematically that the transverse, longitudinal and vertical forces in Beaufort 9 conditions can be taken by the lashings.
Twist lock + lashing rod + turnbuckle ko: Twist lock + lashing rod + turnbuckle is the standard combination. Tier limits (usually a single lashing is not enough above tier 4 or 5), stowage on hatch covers, on-deck positions of heavy reefers and hatch cover lashing are under the Chief Officer's supervision. Lashing failure is the main cause of container losses (Maersk Essen 2021, ONE Apus 2020).
Ro-Ro'da trailer ve self-propelled units: On Ro-Ro ships, trailers and self-propelled units are secured to deck pad-eyes with webbing/chains at no fewer than 4 points. For heavy lift cargo (transformers, generators, crane structures etc.), a detailed lashing plan and engineering calculation are made (usually coordinated between the shipper and the 1/C). The plan requires the approval of the Master and class.
IMDG Code 9 ana sınıf + alt sınıf kullan: The IMDG Code uses 9 main classes + subclasses (1 explosives, 2 gases, 3 flammable liquids, 4 flammable solids, 5 oxidizing substances, 6 toxic substances, 7 radioactive material, 8 corrosives, 9 miscellaneous). The segregation table governs which classes may be stowed side by side, on top of each other or in adjacent holds.
Birinci Zabit; DG manifest, packing cert: The Chief Officer checks the DG manifest, packing certificate, CTU (Cargo Transport Unit) packing inspection, stowage position and emergency response (EmS) preparations. During DG loading, special PPE, fire hoses ready, a cordoned-off area and an authorized supervisor are mandatory.
Group A (sıvılaşabilir yükler — nickel o: Group A (cargoes that may liquefy — nickel ore, iron ore fines, bauxite fines): TML (Transportable Moisture Limit) tests, the Flow Moisture Point and the cargo declaration are critical. If the TML is exceeded, loading is refused; otherwise liquefaction causes the ship to capsize (MV Bulk Jupiter 2015).
Group B (kimyasal tehlike — DRI, sulphur: Group B (chemical hazard — DRI, sulfur, coal): risk of self-heating, off-gassing and CO emission. Hold ventilation, surface temperature monitoring, gas detection and the fixed CO2 system must be ready. Group C covers low-risk cargoes (cement, sand, salt).
BWM Convention, geminin ballast water'ın: To protect the ecosystem of the port where the ship discharges its ballast water, the BWM Convention makes compliance with the D-2 biological standard mandatory. Modern ships are fitted with an IMO type-approved BWMS (UV, electrochlorination, ozone etc.). The Chief Officer checks BWMS operation, the sampling port, the BWRB (Ballast Water Record Book) and SDC calibration.
Tankerlerde COW + ballast yönetimi paral: On tankers, COW and ballast management run in parallel; ballast changes between bunkering, loading and discharging operations are planned with a careful scenario. Incorrect ballast management leads to major risks such as listing, exceeding the bending moment limit or hold flooding.
Pre-arrival 72/24/12 saat öncesinden hol: In pre-arrival messages 72/24/12 hours before arrival, the hold/tank condition, the planned loading sequence, the number of cranes to be used, the ballast plan and bunkering requirements are passed to the terminal. Under ISGOTT, the Ship-Shore Safety Checklist must be completed on tankers after berthing and confirmed every watch.
Operasyon süresince Birinci Zabit (veya: Throughout the operation, the Chief Officer (or cargo officer) takes draft, list and trim readings at each stage; loading rate, ballast rate and ullage measurements are recorded. If a deviation is noticed, the operation is slowed down or stopped. Drips, spillage and hose/pipe leaks are monitored continuously; any marine pollution is reported immediately.
Mate's Receipt, yükün gemiye fiilen alın: The Mate's Receipt is the internal record documenting that the cargo has actually been received on board and its condition (apparent order and condition). The Bill of Lading is prepared from it. If the cargo is damaged or short, it is "claused"; otherwise a clean B/L is signed and the ship/company becomes responsible for that condition.
SOF, terminal/charterer ile birlikte tut: The SOF is the timeline of the operation, kept jointly with the terminal/charterer. If a dispute arises, demurrage is calculated from this document. The Chief Officer issues a Letter of Protest (LOP) whenever necessary: slow loading rate, equipment breakdown, weather delays, etc.
Bauxite yükü TML'in üzerinde yüklendi, V: The bauxite cargo was loaded above its TML, and the ship capsized off Vietnam. 18 dead. Lesson: do not trust the shipper's TML declaration blindly; carry out a can test and, if necessary, refuse to load.
Yanlış declared DG (calcium hypochlorite: Wrongly declared DG (calcium hypochlorite) started a fire in a hold, and 5 crew members died. Lesson: DG declarations are unreliable; CINS circulars must be followed, and mis-declared DG is an industry-wide hazard.
Birinci Zabit'in yük operasyonundaki baş: The Chief Officer's success in cargo operations comes from disciplined records, cross-checks and regulatory knowledge, which remain invisible "when everything goes well" but are the only line of defense "when something goes wrong".
Her gemi, klas/bayrak devleti onaylı bir: Every ship must carry a Stability Booklet and Loading Manual approved by class/the flag State. These documents contain the hydrostatic tables, cross curves (KN values), tank capacity tables, free surface moment values, allowable bending moment/shear force envelopes and the standard loading conditions (departure full load, arrival ballast etc.). By comparing the actual loading condition with these standard conditions, the Chief Officer continuously monitors the safety margin.
Loading instrument (LoadMaster, Cargomax: The loading instrument (LoadMaster, Cargomax, BluePrint etc.) is calibrated with these data and verified by class every year. Even if the instrument fails, the Chief Officer must be able to construct the GZ curve by hand from the hydrostatic tables and KN values; this competence may be questioned during a PSC inspection.
Intact stabilite, GZ (righting arm) eğri: Intact stability is verified by the GZ (righting arm) curve meeting the IS Code 2008 criteria: GZ ≥ 0.20 m at 30°, angle of maximum GZ ≥ 25° (preferably 30°), area from 0-30° ≥ 0.055 m·rad, area from 0-40° ≥ 0.090 m·rad and initial GM ≥ 0.15 m. The weather criterion (severe wind and rolling) measures the ship's resistance to capsizing under wind and rolling.
Çok yüksek GM, kısa ve sert yalpa periyo: A very high GM produces a short, violent rolling period (T = 2π·k/√(g·GM)). This increases the inertial forces on container stacks and lashing equipment and raises the risk of crew fatigue and injury. A stiff ship is uncomfortable and dangerous for cargo safety.
Birinci Zabit, ağır yükü mümkün olduğunc: The Chief Officer brings GM into a reasonable range by distributing heavy cargo as high as possible or by reducing double bottom ballast, while taking care not to go below the intact stability minimums.
Düşük GM, uzun ve yavaş yalpa periyodu v: A low GM gives a long, slow rolling period; although it may seem comfortable, a small off-center weight or the wind causes a permanent list, and resonance with the wave period can produce dangerous roll angles. A tender ship is very vulnerable to a sudden increase in free surface (e.g. tank rupture, hold flooding).
Trim, FP ve AP draftları arasındaki fark: Trim is the difference between the FP and AP drafts. The change of trim caused by adding/shifting a weight is calculated as trimming moment / MCTC (Moment to Change Trim 1 cm). At each loading stage, the Chief Officer predicts the forward/aft draft and compares it with actual observation (draft survey).
Even keel veya hafif by-stern trim genel: Even keel or a slight trim by the stern is generally preferred hydrodynamically. On modern ships, trim optimization software finds the trim giving the lowest resistance for a given speed and draft and saves 2-5% fuel.
List, transverse ağırlık dengesizliğinde: List results from transverse weight imbalance or from negative GM. Before correcting a list by ballast transfer, the Chief Officer first diagnoses the cause: unbalanced cargo, free surface or negative GM? A list caused by negative GM (loll) can get dangerously worse if ballast is taken on the wrong side.
Loading instrument, her kademede longitu: The loading instrument shows longitudinal bending moment and shear force at each stage as a percentage of the permissible envelope. Above 85% is the alarm zone; exceeding 100% means a risk of structural damage. On bulk carriers, during alternate hold loading, shear force peaks at the critical bulkhead positions; therefore only the approved sequence is followed.
Sagging (orta çökme) ve hogging (orta ka: Sagging and hogging create cyclic stresses in the hull and lead to fatigue cracks in the long term. The limits must be observed in port just as at sea; partly loaded intermediate conditions in particular may be overlooked.
Açık güverteli container gemilerinde tor: On open-deck container ships, the torsional moment is also monitored; diagonal weight distribution and quartering sea conditions increase torsion. In addition, tank top strength, hatch cover load and container stack/corner casting limits are part of the local strength check.
Kısmen dolu (slack) tanklardaki sıvının: The free surface of liquid in partially filled (slack) tanks moves the center of gravity as the ship rolls and virtually reduces GM. The free surface effect is proportional to the cube of the tank breadth; wide tanks are therefore the most dangerous. Wherever possible, the Chief Officer keeps tanks either full or empty ("pressed up" or "empty") to minimize the number of slack tanks.
Ballast değişimi veya yakıt transferinde: During ballast exchange or fuel transfer, the Chief Officer avoids having more than one wide tank slack at the same time and fills/empties the tanks one after another. This keeps both the free surface and the list/trim deviations during transfer under control.
Yanlış ballast yönetimi; aşırı shear for: Incorrect ballast management can create excessive shear force, a situation resembling hold flooding or a dangerous list. The ballast plan is therefore prepared in writing and shared with the duty officer.
BWM Convention, ballast suyunun aktarıla: To protect the ecosystem of the port to which ballast water is carried, the BWM Convention requires compliance with D-1 (ballast water exchange — in the open sea, >200 nm, >200 m depth) or D-2 (treatment — biological standard achieved with an approved BWMS). Most ships now carry a type-approved BWMS (UV, electrochlorination etc.) for D-2.
Birinci Zabit; BWMS operasyonunu, sampli: The Chief Officer checks BWMS operation, access to the sampling port and the accuracy of the Ballast Water Record Book (BWRB). In open-sea exchange operations, stability and strength are also checked for the intermediate conditions; the flow-through method is carried out by overflowing the tank.
Parametric rolling, baş/kıç dalgalarda g: Parametric rolling occurs in head or following waves when the change in the ship's waterline form periodically varies the roll restoring moment; it builds up rapidly, especially in head/following seas, when the wave period approaches half the roll period. On container ships it can cause sudden roll angles of 30-40° and the loss of many containers.
Birinci Zabit, weather routing ile birli: Together with weather routing, the Chief Officer coordinates with the Master the adjustment of GM to avoid resonance, speed/course alterations and lashing tightness. Awareness of the danger is the first defense.
Following ve quartering denizlerde dalga: In following and quartering seas, the righting arm temporarily decreases while a wave crest is amidships; there is a risk of broaching and loss of stability. MSC.1/Circ.1228 gives the Master practical guidance on choosing speed/course. The Chief Officer supports the management of these risks operationally through cargo distribution and the choice of GM.
SOLAS II-1, çarpışma/oturma sonrası bölm: SOLAS II-1 introduces the criterion attained subdivision index A ≥ required index R for watertight subdivision and damage stability after collision/grounding. The Chief Officer monitors the status of watertight doors/manholes and whether the loading condition is consistent with the damage control plan.
Damage Control Plan ve booklet, her su g: The Damage Control Plan and booklet show the floodability of each watertight compartment. In the event of damage, the Chief Officer makes cross-flooding and counter-ballasting decisions on the basis of this document.
GM, GZ veya strength değerleri limitlere: When GM, GZ or strength values approach their limits, the Chief Officer has the authority and the responsibility to stop the operation. "Charterer pressure" cannot override stability safety. Every decision to stop and its justification are recorded.
Stabilite ve trim kontrolü, Birinci Zabi: Stability and trim control is the Chief Officer's least forgiving responsibility: errors do not appear instantly but build up step by step, and usually become visible only at the worst moment. Written verification, cross-checks and regulatory knowledge at every stage are the ship's only real line of defense.
