Birinci Zabit, köprüüstü ile koordineli: In coordination with the bridge, the Chief Officer monitors weather forecasts (NAVTEX, weather routing services, GMDSS broadcasts, GRIB files) and identifies the heavy weather window in advance. A weather routing service gives advance warning (e.g. of tropical cyclones, deep low-pressure systems), so that preparations can be made safely in calm seas. Working on deck after the storm has arrived is a fatal risk.
Tahmindeki dalga yüksekliği, periyot, sw: The forecast wave height, period, swell direction and wind force are assessed together with the ship's loading condition (GM, freeboard). The Chief Officer checks with CSM calculations whether the existing lashing is adequate for the expected conditions.
Birinci Zabit, hazırlık durumunu ve risk: The Chief Officer reports the state of preparation and the risks to the Master. Decisions on altering course, reducing speed (slow steaming/heave-to), seeking shelter (port of refuge) or waiting are taken by the Master; the Chief Officer carries them out on deck. MSC.1/Circ.1228 recommends speed/course adjustments to avoid dangerous situations such as parametric/synchronous rolling and broaching.
Bulk ve genel kargo gemilerinde hatch co: On bulk carriers and general cargo ships, the hatch covers are the primary defense against water ingress. The Chief Officer verifies that all hatch covers are fully closed, the cleats are secured and the cross-joint/peripheral seals (rubber gaskets) are intact. A damaged or crushed seal leads to hold flooding in heavy weather.
Hatch cover su geçirmezliği hose test ve: Hatch cover weathertightness is verified periodically by hose test or ultrasonic test. Before heavy weather, it is checked that the drainage non-return valves are working and that the compression bars are making contact. This double check eliminates the most common cause of water ingress.
Tüm weathertight ve watertight açıklıkla: All weathertight and watertight openings (hatches, ventilators, air pipes, manholes, sounding pipe caps) are closed and dogged before heavy weather. Closing the ventilators is especially important; an open ventilator lets water into the hold/store when a wave breaks over it. The Chief Officer checks these closures physically.
Güverte üzerindeki tüm hareketli/gevşek: All movable/loose equipment on deck turns into lethal projectiles in heavy weather. The Chief Officer checks the lashing of the pilot ladder, gangway, hoses, drums, welding equipment, store hatches and all loose items. Nothing is assumed to "stay put under its own weight"; everything is secured.
Container gemilerinde parametric rolling: If there is a risk of parametric rolling on container ships, lashing forces increase greatly; in that case a change of speed/course is the only safe solution. Major container losses such as ONE Apus (2020) and Maersk Essen (2021) resulted from a combination of heavy weather + inadequate lashing/securing.
Güverteye binen su hızla tahliye olmalıd: Water shipped on deck must drain away quickly; otherwise the accumulated water (water on deck) endangers stability through both its weight and its free surface effect. The Chief Officer verifies that the freeing ports (openings in the bulwarks) and scuppers are not blocked and that the freeing port flaps (if fitted) open freely. The Load Line Convention makes these mandatory.
Yük artığı, çöp, halat veya buz freeing: Cargo residues, garbage, ropes or ice can block a freeing port; it is cleaned before heavy weather. Blocked drainage leads to a deadly accumulation of water.
Soğuk bölgelerde güverte üstü buzlanma (: In cold regions, icing on deck and superstructure (superstructure icing) raises the center of gravity and seriously threatens stability. The Chief Officer monitors ice accumulation, coordinates de-icing measures and prevents the freeing ports from becoming blocked with ice. Excessive icing is a cause of capsizing in fishing vessels and small ships.
Ağır hava başladığında Birinci Zabit (Ka: When heavy weather begins, the Chief Officer (with the Master's approval) issues and enforces an order prohibiting or strictly restricting access to the deck. A wave coming on board (boarding sea/green water) can sweep a person overboard instantly. No one goes on the open deck unless it is essential; if it is necessary, they go with a lifeline, lifejacket and a companion.
İç koridorlarda ve kamaralarda da loose: Loose items (furniture, sliding equipment) in internal alleyways and cabins are also secured; the crew are told to expect violent motion and to hold on. Precautions are taken in the mess room/galley against slipping and burns.
Tüm watertight kapılar kapatılır, accomm: All watertight doors are closed and accommodation entrances are dogged. The bridge watch is reinforced; decisions on course and speed are reviewed continuously. When preparations are complete, the Chief Officer reports "deck sea-secured" to the bridge.
Belirli dalga periyotları geminin doğal: If certain wave periods are close to the ship's natural roll period, parametric rolling or synchronous rolling occurs; the roll angle reaches dangerous levels, lashing forces multiply and containers/cargo are lost. MSC.1/Circ.1228 recommends adjusting speed/course to change the encounter period in order to avoid these situations.
Broaching ve pooping (kıçtan dalga binme: Broaching and pooping (seas boarding over the stern) are dangerous in a following sea. The Chief Officer is prepared for these risks with regard to cargo/lashing; the final maneuvering decision lies with the bridge, but preparation on the deck side is critical.
Yarı dolu tanklardaki serbest yüzey etki: The free surface effect in partially filled tanks reduces the effective GM in heavy weather and impairs stability. The Chief Officer (in coordination with ballast management) ensures that tanks are kept pressed up (completely full) or empty where possible; the number of slack tanks is minimized. This is a frequently neglected but critical part of heavy weather stability.
Hava sakinleştiğinde Birinci Zabit güver: When the weather calms down, the Chief Officer carries out a deck inspection: hatch covers, lashing condition, cargo damage, water ingress, freeing ports and deck equipment are checked. Damage is photographed, hold soundings are taken and the necessary repairs/re-lashing are carried out. If there is cargo damage, a Letter of Protest and a damage report are prepared.
Ağır hava, denizciliğin en eski ve en öl: Heavy weather is the oldest and deadliest hazard of seafaring. The Chief Officer's success depends on foreseeing the danger, completing preparations in calm seas, preventing water ingress and cargo shift and, above all, keeping the crew off the deck so that no life is put at risk. A well-prepared ship rides out the storm; an unprepared ship makes the news.
Bir geminin ticari kullanımı charter par: The commercial employment of a ship is governed by a charter party (C/P). Under a voyage charter the ship is hired for a specific voyage and under a time charter for a specific period; under a bareboat charter the ship passes entirely to the charterer. The concepts of NOR, laytime and demurrage are especially critical in voyage charters, because these documents allocate the cost of port time between the parties.
Yaygın C/P formları: kuru yükte GENCON,: Common C/P forms: GENCON for dry cargo, ASBATANKVOY for tankers, NYPE/BALTIME for time charters. The Chief Officer must know the NOR provisions, the conditions for the commencement of laytime and the special clauses (rider clauses) of the applicable C/P, because these determine the timing of the documents.
Birinci Zabit, denizci olmasının yanında: Besides being a seafarer, the Chief Officer is the on-site representative of the ship's commercial interests. Correct and timely documents secure demurrage income and protect the ship against unjustified claims. Wrong or late documents leave the company defenseless in court. Care with documents is therefore as important as seamanship.
NOR, geminin yüke/boşaltmaya fiilen ve h: The NOR gives notice that the ship is physically and legally ready to load/discharge. The ship must have arrived at the correct berth/anchorage, completed the necessary free pratique and customs formalities and have its holds/tanks ready. An NOR given before these conditions are met is considered invalid and laytime does not start; this leads to loss of demurrage.
NOR verilme yeri (berth, anchorage, \"Wh: Where the NOR is to be given (berth, anchorage, "Whether In Berth Or Not — WIBON") and how it is to be given (in writing, e-mail, letter, telegram) are defined in the C/P. The Chief Officer prepares the NOR in exact accordance with the C/P terms, tenders it with a time stamp and keeps proof of delivery.
NOR uyuşmazlıkları laytime davalarının ç: NOR disputes make up most laytime cases. Situations such as "NOR tendered when the ship was not actually ready", "tender before free pratique was granted" or "tender at the wrong place" invalidate the NOR. The Chief Officer confirms all readiness conditions before tendering NOR; the wording "NOR tendered without prejudice" is used under some C/Ps but does not always give protection.
Statement of Facts, port operasyonunun k: The Statement of Facts is the chronological record of the port operation: ship's arrival, NOR tendering and acceptance, anchoring/berthing times, start and finish of operations, gang changes, draft survey, weather delays, equipment breakdowns and all stoppages. Demurrage/laytime is calculated directly from the SoF; every event must therefore be recorded in real time and correctly.
Birinci Zabit SoF'u hazırlar; terminal/a: The Chief Officer prepares the SoF; it is signed jointly with the terminal/agent. If the parties disagree on the time records, a reservation is entered in the "remarks" section. An error of one hour in the SoF can make a difference of thousands of dollars in the demurrage calculation.
Mate's Receipt (MR), yükün gemiye fiilen: The Mate's Receipt (MR) is the internal record documenting that the cargo has actually been received on board and its "apparent order and condition". The Chief Officer checks the quantity (by draft survey/tally) and the condition of the cargo loaded. If the cargo shows visible damage, wetness, rust or shortage, the Chief Officer writes the appropriate reservations (clausing/remarks) on the MR.
MR üzerinden Bill of Lading hazırlandığı: Since the Bill of Lading is prepared from the MR, the condition recorded on the MR is reflected directly in the B/L. Failing to record damage makes the ship/company liable for that damage. The Chief Officer's careful cargo inspection is therefore critical for legal protection.
Bill of Lading, yükün taşınmak üzere alı: The Bill of Lading is the basic document showing that the cargo has been received for carriage, and it serves as a document of title/carriage. A "clean B/L" shows that the cargo was received in good order; a "claused (dirty) B/L" shows a condition with reservations. Signing a clean B/L for damaged cargo (usually under shipper pressure, against a letter of indemnity) is a serious P&I risk and may be considered fraud.
Birinci Zabit, MR'deki çekincelerin B/L': The Chief Officer ensures that the reservations on the MR are correctly carried over to the B/L. The Hague-Visby Rules govern the carrier's liability and the right to make reservations. A wrongly issued clean B/L makes the carrier liable for the actual condition of the cargo and leads to large claims.
Letter of Protest, gemi adına bir durumu: A Letter of Protest is the formal protest/recording of a situation on behalf of the ship. The Chief Officer issues an LOP in situations such as slow loading/discharge rate, equipment breakdown, cargo quantity discrepancy (ship figure vs shore figure), contaminated/damaged cargo, a claim of poor hold preparation or unjustified delay. The LOP forms evidence in any future claim.
LOP, ilgili tarafa (terminal, charterer,: The LOP is presented to the party concerned (terminal, charterer, surveyor); if they refuse to sign, it is recorded with the note "received but refused to sign". A protest not made in time weakens a claim raised later; it is therefore important to write the LOP at the time of the event.
En sık LOP konuları: ship/shore figure f: The most frequent LOP subjects: ship/shore figure differences (especially ullage/quantity discrepancies on tankers), slow rate, terminal equipment breakdown, weather delays, cargo condition and late berthing. The Chief Officer issues a separate, dated and clear LOP for each. The other party may also issue LOPs to the ship; these are also recorded and answered.
SOLAS VI/2 (2016 değişikliği), konteyner: SOLAS VI/2 (2016 amendment) requires the Verified Gross Mass (VGM) of containers to be declared before loading; a container without a VGM is not loaded. The Chief Officer checks that the VGM data are consistent with the stowage/stability calculation. A wrongly declared weight corrupts the stability and strength calculations (the MSC Napoli case of 2007 showed poor weight declaration).
Shipper, yük hakkında doğru bilgi (IMSBC: The shipper is obliged to provide correct information about the cargo (IMSBC group, IMDG class, MSDS, stowage factor). The Chief Officer checks that this information is complete and agrees with the manifest; missing/wrong information stops the loading.
Cargo manifest, liman ve gümrük otoritel: The cargo manifest is the official list of the cargo for port and customs authorities. The Chief Officer checks that the manifest agrees with the cargo actually loaded/discharged; inconsistency leads to customs problems and fines. The Dangerous Goods manifest is kept separately and held on the bridge.
Tüm ticari belgeler (NOR, SoF, time shee: All commercial documents (NOR, SoF, time sheet, MR, B/L copies, LOPs, manifest, draft survey reports) are archived systematically and forwarded to the company. A laytime/demurrage dispute may go to court years later; the documents drawn up on the day are the only line of defense. The Chief Officer ensures that the records are complete, signed and dated.
Birinci Zabit, NOR ve SoF'u zamanında ag: The Chief Officer forwards the NOR and SoF to the agent and the company in good time; the demurrage calculation is made by the operations/chartering department. Instructions are requested from the company on any uncertainties in the documents. In legally critical situations (major damage, claims), the P&I club becomes involved; the Chief Officer preserves the evidence and records.
Yük belgeleri yönetimi, denizcilik ile t: Cargo documentation management is an area where seafaring and commercial law meet. A single signature or a one-hour recording error by the Chief Officer can win or lose the company tens of thousands of dollars. Success comes from understanding the charter party, drawing up documents correctly and in real time, and protecting the ship against unjustified claims with records.
CSM gemiye özeldir; başka geminin manual: The CSM is ship-specific; another ship's manual cannot be used. The Chief Officer makes sure that the CSM is up to date, approved and on board; if equipment is changed, the manual is revised. Failure to comply with the CSM results both in a PSC finding and, in the event of an accident, in legal liability.
MSL (Maximum Securing Load), bir lashing: MSL (Maximum Securing Load) is the maximum load that a lashing item can safely carry and is usually defined as a proportion of the item's breaking load (e.g. 80% of BL for wire, 50% for web lashing). In calculations, a safety factor is also applied to obtain the CS (Calculated Strength); CSS Code Annex 13 standardizes this calculation.
Birinci Zabit, kullanılan her ekipmanın: The Chief Officer knows the MSL of every item used and assesses the adequacy of the lashing arrangement against these values. A wrong MSL assumption leads to inadequate lashing and loss of cargo.
Her sefer öncesi Birinci Zabit, lashing: Before every voyage, the Chief Officer checks the lashing equipment (twistlocks, lashing rods, turnbuckles, bottle screws, D-rings, wire/chain, shackles) item by item for wear, cracks, deformation, corrosion and thread damage. SWL markings must be legible; unmarked or damaged equipment is withdrawn from use. A worn twistlock can fail to hold a container stack and cause its loss.
Ekipman envanteri CSM'e göre tam olmalıd: The equipment inventory must be complete in accordance with the CSM; the ship does not sail with missing/insufficient lashing gear. The Chief Officer checks the spare equipment stock and the storage arrangement (lashing bins).
Lashing ekipmanı düzenli bakım gerektiri: Lashing equipment needs regular maintenance: greasing (turnbuckle threads), removing corrosion and replacing damaged parts. Replacement criteria (e.g. a certain number of broken wires in wire lashings, cuts/UV damage in web lashings) are applied in accordance with the CSM/maker's instructions. The Chief Officer keeps the maintenance records integrated with the PMS.
Konteyner istif emniyeti, stack weight (: Container stowage safety depends on the limits for the total weight of containers stowed one above another at each row position and on corner casting load limits. The CSM and the lashing software (e.g. lashing computer) show the maximum permissible load for each bay-row-tier. Putting a heavy container in a high tier overloads the corner castings and lashings below it. The Chief Officer verifies that the plan complies with these limits.
Hatch cover üstü (on-deck) istif, hold i: Stowage on hatch covers (on-deck) requires different lashing from stowage in the hold (in-hold); wind and wave loads are much higher on deck. When the tier limit is exceeded, a single lashing is not enough; double lashing or a lashing bridge comes into play.
Twistlock + lashing rod + turnbuckle kom: Twistlock + lashing rod + turnbuckle is the standard pattern. The lashing software calculates the dynamic forces according to GM, speed and course and shows whether each stack is safe; if it gives an alarm, the stowage is revised. The Chief Officer keeps the software output (PSC/vetting may ask for it) and checks that the actual lashing follows the pattern.
Parametric rolling, container yükünü kat: Parametric rolling is the most dangerous condition, multiplying the loads on containers. Major losses such as ONE Apus (2020, 1816 containers lost) and Maersk Essen (2021) resulted from a combination of lashing tightness problems, inadequate patterns and neglect of weather routing.
Tahıl (grain) yükü serbest yüzey gibi da: Grain cargo behaves like a free surface; when the ship rolls, it shifts (grain shift) and creates a dangerous list. The International Grain Code makes the grain heeling moment calculation and the necessary measures (trimming, bundling, saucers, overstowing, feeders) mandatory. The Chief Officer carries out/checks the grain loading stability calculation and obtains NCB approval.
Konsantre (concentrate) ve ince taneli y: Concentrates and fine-grained cargoes also carry a risk of shifting and liquefaction; the IMSBC Code Group A rules apply. The trimming (leveling) of the cargo surface and the filling level of the hold determine the shifting risk.
Çelik bobin (steel coil), levha, kütük (: Steel coils, plates, logs and breakbulk cargoes require special lashing. Steel coils are secured against shifting with wedges/chocks and lashings; wrong lashing leads to a deadly shift inside the hold. The Chief Officer applies the correct pattern for each cargo type in accordance with the CSS Code and the CSM.
RoRo gemilerinde araç ve trailer'lar, de: On RoRo ships, vehicles and trailers are secured to deck pad-eyes/D-rings with web or chain lashings. The CSM sets the minimum number and the angle of lashing points according to vehicle type and weight; heavy self-propelled units are secured at no fewer than four points, and at more points depending on weight and acceleration. The lashing angle (vertical/horizontal component) directly affects safety.
Deck dayanımı (decking strength) ve lash: Deck strength (decking strength) and lashing point density are verified against the CSM. Overloading or insufficient lashing points cause vehicles to shift and deck damage in heavy weather.
Transformatör, jeneratör, vinç gövdesi g: For heavy lift/project cargo such as transformers, generators and crane structures, a detailed lashing plan and engineering calculation are made (usually coordinated between the shipper and the Chief Officer). The plan requires the approval of the Master and class. The center of gravity, lashing angles and deck reaction forces are calculated; a wrong calculation endangers both the cargo and the ship.
CSS Code Annex 13, standart olmayan yükl: CSS Code Annex 13 provides a practical calculation method for non-standardized cargoes: the transverse, longitudinal and vertical acceleration forces acting on the cargo are calculated according to the ship's size and the sea conditions. It is shown mathematically that these forces are taken by the lashing arrangement (friction + lashing CS).
Sürtünme katsayısı (yük-güverte arası, ö: The coefficient of friction (between cargo and deck, e.g. steel-timber 0.3, steel-steel 0.1) affects the calculation; a wet or oily surface reduces friction. The Chief Officer verifies that the "balance of forces" and "balance of moments" criteria are met; otherwise lashings are added.
Sürtünmeyi artırmak için anti-slip mat (: To increase friction, anti-slip mats (rubber pads) and suitable dunnage (timber) are used; this can reduce the number of lashings required. The Chief Officer checks that the right material is placed between cargo and deck. The calculation assumes that friction alone is not sufficient; lashing is always essential.
Lashing planı, software çıktısı, ekipman: The lashing plan, software output, equipment inspection records and tightness checks are documented. These records are requested in PSC inspections, vetting and accident investigations. In the event of container loss or cargo damage, records showing that the CSM was correctly applied are the company's only defense.
Cargo Securing Manual, kâğıt üzerinde de: The Cargo Securing Manual is a discipline applied on site, not on paper. The Chief Officer's success lies in inspecting the equipment meticulously, applying lashings with the correct calculation and the correct pattern, monitoring them throughout the voyage and recording everything. Inadequate lashing leads to cargo losses worth millions of dollars and to loss of life; correct lashing is an invisible but life-saving achievement.
Enclosed space (kapalı alan), sınırlı gi: An enclosed space is a space that has limited openings for entry/exit, is not continuously ventilated and is not designed for continuous occupancy. On board, these include cargo holds, ballast/fuel/oil tanks, void spaces, cofferdams, duct keels, pump rooms, chain lockers, sewage tanks and similar spaces. The atmosphere of these spaces cannot be judged by eye; it may be oxygen-deficient or toxic.
Tehlike sinsidir çünkü atmosfer normal g: The danger is insidious because the atmosphere looks normal but is lethal. Oxygen deficiency (due to rusting, cargo off-gassing or inert gas) causes loss of consciousness within seconds. When a victim collapses, the second and third persons who rush in unprepared to rescue also die in the same atmosphere; the "multiple fatality" pattern is the hallmark of such accidents.
Oksijen eksikliği: çelik paslanması (oks: Oxygen deficiency: rusting of steel (consumes oxygen), cargo oxidation/off-gassing (e.g. steel, coal, agricultural products), inert gas and microbial activity. Toxic gases: H₂S (decaying organic matter, slops), CO (incomplete combustion, self-heating cargo), cargo vapors (VOC). Flammable gases: hydrocarbon vapor (tankers), methane. From the previous use of the space, the Chief Officer anticipates which hazard is likely.
Birinci Zabit, permit imzalamadan önce a: Before signing the permit, the Chief Officer personally verifies the atmosphere test results, ventilation, rescue arrangements, communications and PPE. The permit is valid for a specified period and is renewed if conditions change (change of watch, atmosphere). The signature means taking on responsibility; it is not a routine formality.
Permit öncesi, işe özgü risk assessment: Before the permit is issued, a job-specific risk assessment is carried out: the previous use of the space, possible hazards, the equipment required and the emergency scenario are assessed. In a toolbox meeting, the entry team and standby personnel review their duties, the hazards and the emergency plan. The Chief Officer leads this briefing and makes sure everyone understands the "enclosed space rule".
Birinci Zabit, ölçüm sonuçlarını permit': The Chief Officer records the measurement results on the permit. If the values are not within the safe range, entry is prohibited; ventilation is continued and measurements are repeated. After entry, continuous monitoring is carried out inside (personal monitor), because the atmosphere can change.
Çoklu-gaz dedektörlerinin kalibrasyon se: The calibration certificate of multi-gas detectors must not be more than one year old, and a bump test (function test with a known gas) must be carried out regularly (before each use). An instrument that has not been calibrated or bump-tested can give a false safe reading and cause a death. The Chief Officer checks the instrument records and the validity of the calibration.
Sensörlerin ömrü sınırlıdır (özellikle e: Sensors have a limited life (especially electrochemical H₂S/CO sensors); expired sensors are replaced. A spare instrument and spare batteries are kept ready.
Kapalı alan, giriş öncesi ve giriş süres: An enclosed space must be supplied with fresh air by continuous mechanical ventilation (forced ventilation) before and during entry. Natural ventilation is insufficient. Ventilation must reach all corners of the space (no dead zones), and if it stops, entry must be suspended immediately. The Chief Officer confirms the adequacy of ventilation by measurement; ventilation is maintained so that "the atmosphere stays safe".
Alan, ex-proof (yanıcı gaz riski varsa): The space is lit with ex-proof lighting (if there is a flammable gas risk). Access/exit routes must be clear and safe; ladders/staging are checked for soundness. Hazardous systems (pipelines, pumps, heating) are isolated/locked (lock-out tag-out) so that no chemical/liquid/steam can enter. The Chief Officer verifies these isolations.
Giriş süresince, giriş ağzında bir stand: Throughout the entry, a standby person (attendant) remains at the entrance at all times and is in uninterrupted communication with the team inside (radio, voice, visual or rope signals). The standby person NEVER goes in, but raises the alarm and calls the rescue team if there is a problem. Rushing in alone and becoming the second victim is the main cause of enclosed space deaths.
Haberleşme yöntemi önceden kararlaştırıl: The method of communication is agreed and tested in advance. Personnel inside give a regular "all OK" signal; if the signal stops, the emergency procedure starts. The Chief Officer makes sure that the standby person fully understands the duty.
Rescue planı; SCBA (Self-Contained Breat: The rescue plan covers SCBA (Self-Contained Breathing Apparatus), rescue harness, lifting system (tripod/winch), resuscitation equipment and first aid. This equipment is kept ready at the entrance. SOLAS III/19 makes regular (at least every two months, depending on the ship) enclosed space entry and rescue drills mandatory; the Chief Officer organizes these drills, runs them with realistic scenarios and records them.
Tatbikatlar, kurtarmanın hızlı ve doğru: Drills ensure that rescue is carried out quickly and correctly; in a real accident, seconds save lives. Deficiencies found in drills are corrected.
Self-heating kargo (kömür, DRI) bulunan: In holds/voids containing self-heating cargo (coal, DRI), O₂ is depleted and CO/methane accumulates. From the cargo declaration, the Chief Officer anticipates the hazard these spaces present and always takes measurements before entry. Even a hold that "looks empty" can have a lethal atmosphere because of the previous cargo.
Her enclosed space entry permit, atmosfe: Every enclosed space entry permit is archived with the atmosphere measurement results, instrument calibration record, standby assignment and entry/exit times. These records are among those most often examined in PSC inspections, vetting and accident investigations. The Chief Officer makes sure that the records are complete and reflect reality.
Kapalı alan ile ilgili near-miss'ler (ör: Near-misses involving enclosed spaces (e.g. instrument failure, ventilation interruption) are reported and analyzed. The Chief Officer continuously reinforces the culture that "an enclosed space is never entered without testing". This culture is vital in an area where a single lapse in discipline can bring death.
Kapalı alan girişi, kurallara harfiyen u: Enclosed space entry is an operation that is safe when the rules are followed to the letter and lethal at the slightest deviation. The Chief Officer's success lies in applying the permit-test-standby-rescue chain in full for every entry, ensuring the reliability of the instruments and instilling in the team the culture of "never enter without testing, never rush blindly into a rescue". This discipline directly saves lives.
MARPOL Annex V, gemilerden kaynaklanan t: MARPOL Annex V regulates the management of all garbage from ships. The basic principle is that the discharge of plastics into the sea is completely prohibited and that other wastes may be discharged into the sea only under certain conditions (distance, speed, category). The 2013 revision of Annex V tightened the rules and moved to the approach "discharge generally prohibited, exceptions defined".
Special Area'larda (Akdeniz, Baltık, Kar: In Special Areas (Mediterranean, Baltic, Black Sea, Red Sea, Gulfs area, North Sea, Antarctic, etc.) the discharge rules are much stricter; generally only comminuted food waste is permitted, and only under certain conditions. In polar waters (Polar Code) the rules are stricter still. The Chief Officer applies the correct rule for the area the ship is in; discharge in the wrong area is a serious violation.
Genel kural: plastik, pişirme yağı, inci: General rule: plastics, cooking oil, incinerator ash, operational waste and e-waste must not be discharged into the sea; they are retained on board and delivered ashore. Food waste and non-HME cargo residues may be discharged subject to distance and other conditions.
Etkili ayrıştırma, kaynağında doğru topl: Effective segregation starts with correct collection at source. The Chief Officer places labeled, color-coded garbage bins at suitable points on deck and in the accommodation: separate bins for plastics, food, paper/cardboard, glass, metal and hazardous waste/e-waste. Labels must be clear and multilingual (because of the diversity of the crew). Wrongly segregated waste makes later sorting difficult and creates a risk of improper discharge.
Toplanan atık, sınıflandırılarak saklama: Collected waste is sorted and taken to the garbage storage area. Plastics and other waste to be delivered ashore are stored in an orderly way, free of odor and leaks; food waste is managed separately for hygiene reasons.
Garbage Record Book, her atık işlemini k: The Garbage Record Book records every garbage operation: Part I records ship-generated garbage (discharge, incineration, delivery ashore) and Part II records cargo residues. Each entry includes the date, time, ship's position, garbage category, estimated amount (m³) and type of operation (discharge into the sea/incineration/delivery). The responsible officer signs each entry; the Master approves the pages. The Chief Officer is responsible for the accuracy of the records.
GRB en az iki yıl gemide saklanır. PSC,: The GRB is kept on board for at least two years. PSC looks for consistency between the GRB, the actual generation of garbage and the delivery receipts; any inconsistency raises suspicion of a deliberate violation.
Shore reception facility'ye yapılan her: For every delivery to a shore reception facility, the receipt obtained (garbage disposal receipt) is kept with the quantity and category and is cross-checked against the GRB. A mismatch between the receipt and the GRB leads to a serious finding at inspection. The Chief Officer estimates the amount of waste before delivery and verifies it against the receipt.
Birinci Zabit, port stay süresine ve atı: The Chief Officer plans delivery to the shore reception facility according to the length of the port stay and the amount of waste accumulated. Because some waste (plastics, e-waste, HME residues) can only be delivered ashore, a suitable port and facility are arranged in advance. Advance waste notification is mandatory in most ports; the Chief Officer submits this notification through the agent.
Yetersiz reception facility durumunda (ö: Where reception facilities are inadequate (particularly in some ports), this can be reported under MEPC.1/Circ.834. If waste cannot be delivered, the Chief Officer manages the storage capacity and plans for the next suitable port.
Atık teslimi maliyetlidir; ancak yasadış: Delivering waste ashore costs money; however, this cost is insignificant compared with the penalty for illegal discharge. The company SMS usually applies a "no overboard discharge" policy and requires all waste to be delivered ashore. The Chief Officer ensures that cost pressure never leads to falsified records or illegal discharge.
Doğru atık yönetimi, tüm mürettebatın ka: Proper waste management requires the participation of the whole crew. The Chief Officer trains the crew on segregation rules, discharge prohibitions and the importance of the GRB, and includes these in familiarization. The Garbage Management Plan is kept where everyone can access it, and responsibilities are clearly defined.
Birinci Zabit, her liman öncesi GRB-makb: Before each port, the Chief Officer checks GRB–receipt consistency, bin labels and the storage arrangements. PSC inspectors frequently examine garbage management; consistent records, orderly segregation and a valid plan prevent findings. Regular internal audits keep environmental compliance sustainable.
Boya kovaları, kimyasal bidonları, kayna: Paint tins, chemical drums, welding electrode stubs and other operational waste (category F) must not be discharged into the sea; they are stored separately as hazardous waste and delivered to a suitable facility. Chemical waste is managed in accordance with the MSDS; incorrect mixing creates a risk of fire or chemical reaction. The Chief Officer supervises the correct storage of this waste.
Atık saklama alanlarında sızıntı (özelli: Leaks in garbage storage areas (particularly from food waste and oily waste) are prevented, and the risk of deck contamination and of waste reaching the sea is controlled. Mixing different categories (e.g. plastics + food) both spoils segregation and makes the waste ineligible for discharge. Orderly, clean storage is important for both hygiene and regulatory compliance.
Atık yönetimi, küçük günlük disiplinleri: Waste management is the sum of small daily disciplines, but it has major consequences at inspections. The Chief Officer succeeds by setting up a correct segregation system, keeping honest, real-time records, delivering waste through legal channels and instilling in the crew a culture of "not a single piece of garbage goes into the sea". Clean records and a clean sea protect the ship from heavy penalties and the company from loss of reputation.
IMDG, yükleri 9 ana sınıfa ayırır (patla: The IMDG Code divides goods into 9 main classes (explosives, gases, flammable liquids, flammable solids, oxidizing substances, toxic substances, radioactive material, corrosives, miscellaneous). Each class has its own handling, stowage and emergency response requirements.
Segregasyon tablosu, hangi sınıfların ya: The segregation table specifies which classes may be side by side, one on top of the other, or in adjacent compartments. The Chief Officer ensures that incompatible goods (e.g. oxidizing + flammable) are separated by a safe distance. On container ships, the bay-row-tier plan is checked against these rules.
Cargo Transport Unit (CTU) packing certi: The Cargo Transport Unit (CTU) packing certificate documents that the stowage and securing inside the container have been carried out correctly. The Chief Officer checks that DG containers are correctly labeled/placarded and undamaged, and that there is no leakage or odor.
Dangerous Goods Manifest, geminin taşıdı: The Dangerous Goods Manifest lists all DG on board and their stowage positions; the MFAG gives medical first aid guidance and the EmS gives emergency response procedures. These documents must be kept on the bridge, quickly accessible in an emergency. The Chief Officer ensures they are up to date and complete.
IMSBC, dökme yükleri sıvılaşabilir (Grou: The IMSBC Code divides bulk cargoes into cargoes that may liquefy (Group A), cargoes with chemical hazards (Group B) and low-risk cargoes (Group C). With Group A cargoes (nickel ore, iron ore fines, bauxite fines), if the moisture content is above the TML (Transportable Moisture Limit), the cargo may liquefy and capsize the ship. The Chief Officer questions the TML/moisture declaration; if in doubt, loading is refused.
DG operasyonunda özel PPE, hazır yangın: DG operations require special PPE, fire hoses ready for use, a cordoned-off area and an authorized supervisor. In the event of a leak or fire, the response follows the EmS guide. The Chief Officer ensures that the crew is prepared for the relevant scenarios and that DG drills are carried out.
Tehlikeli yük yönetimi, Birinci Zabitin: Dangerous goods management is one of the Chief Officer's duties carrying the highest responsibility; a small oversight can turn into a major disaster. Correct classification, strict segregation, complete documentation and disciplined monitoring protect the ship, the crew and the environment from the risks of dangerous goods.
ISM Code Element 10, şirketin gemi ve ek: ISM Code Element 10 requires the company to keep the ship and its equipment in a condition that complies with the approved rules and company procedures. This includes regular inspection of critical equipment, back-up arrangements in case of sudden failure, and record keeping. PMS software (AMOS, ShipManager, BASSnet, TM Master, etc.) digitizes this requirement through a job/component hierarchy.
Birinci Zabit, güverte component ağacınd: The Chief Officer links each item in the deck component tree (crane, winch, hatch, mast, deck crane) to periodic jobs and distinguishes between calendar-based, running-hours-based and condition-based maintenance. Each completed job is closed out with a record of parts, hours and personnel.
PMS, klasın Annual, Intermediate ve Spec: The PMS is aligned with the class Annual, Intermediate and Special (5-yearly) survey cycle. Some companies, under a class-approved "Planned Maintenance Scheme for Machinery" (PMS class notation), gain the right to have part of the machinery surveys carried out on board by their own engineers. On the deck side, records such as hatch cover ultrasonic tests, mooring equipment records and LOLER-type crane records are requested at survey.
Birinci Zabit'in sorumluluk alanındaki t: The main items within the Chief Officer's area of responsibility are deck/cargo cranes, mooring/anchor winches, the windlass, capstans, hatch covers (hydraulic/mechanical), air vent (ventilation) systems, sounding pipes, freeing ports, the accommodation ladder/gangway, the pilot ladder, deck pipelines (on tankers) and deck machinery.
Vinç ve winch gibi kalemlerde running ho: For items such as cranes and winches, the running hours counter is the maintenance trigger. Condition-based monitoring, on the other hand, is done by counting broken wires in wire ropes, checking fiber ropes for abrasion/UV degradation, analyzing hydraulic oil for contamination and measuring corrosion of hatch cover plating. By entering these observations in the PMS, the Chief Officer enables early action.
Birinci Zabit, haftalık planlama toplant: At the weekly planning meeting, the Chief Officer prioritizes and allocates work orders together with the Bosun. Each work order includes the job description, the required PPE, the risk assessment reference, the required parts/materials and the estimated duration. For high-risk jobs (working aloft, overside work, hot work, enclosed space), a Permit to Work is also issued.
Planlama, liman/sefer ritmiyle uyumlanır: Planning is matched to the port/voyage rhythm: noisy or hazardous work is done outside port, painting in suitable weather and humidity conditions, and crane maintenance in a window with no cargo operations.
Tamamlanan iş emri, harcanan saat, kulla: A completed work order is closed with the hours spent, the parts used and observations. Jobs left unfinished or postponed are flagged as "overdue" and the reason is recorded; overdue critical jobs are the most frequent cause of findings at inspections. The Chief Officer reports the overdue list to the Master every week.
Mooring halatları (HMPE, polyester, mixe: Mooring lines (HMPE, polyester, mixed) and wires are inspected regularly for external wear, internal abrasion, UV degradation, splice integrity and elongation. Every line must have retirement criteria under a "line management plan". OCIMF MEG4 is the industry standard for managing line service life and LDBF (Line Design Break Force).
Wire rope'ta belirli uzunlukta izin veri: A wire rope is taken out of service when the permitted number of broken wires over a given length is exceeded, or when a kink or birdcage is found. Lubrication (greasing) and correct storage extend its service life.
Mooring winch fren tutma kapasitesi, bra: The holding capacity of the mooring winch brake is verified by a brake holding test; the target is generally about 60% of the wire/line MBL (depending on the design). If brake rendering is not set correctly, either the line parts or the brake fails to hold; both are dangerous. Test results are recorded.
Hatch cover su geçirmezliği; rubber pack: Hatch cover weathertightness depends on the integrity of the rubber packing (seal), compression bar, drainage channel/non-return valve and the cleat/quick-acting cleat system. The Chief Officer regularly checks the seals for permanent set, the compression bars for corrosion and the cleat adjustment. On bulk carriers and container ships, water ingress means cargo damage and a stability risk.
Su geçirmezlik; hose test, chalk test ve: Weathertightness is verified by a hose test, a chalk test or an ultrasonic tightness test. The ultrasonic test is the most reliable method for holds that cannot be drained and is preferred before surveys.
Hidrolik açma/kapama sistemlerinde yağ s: In hydraulic opening/closing systems, the oil level, leaks, hose aging and cylinder packings are monitored. Rollers, hinges and wheel tracks are greased; corrosion is chipped and painted. On mechanical (folding) covers, maintenance of chains/wires and rollers has priority.
Korozyon yönetimi, güverte bakımının en: Corrosion management is the largest single item of deck maintenance. The correct sequence is: mechanical chipping/needle gun → wire brush → solvent cleaning → primer → intermediate coat → top coat. The humidity, surface temperature (at least 3°C above the dew point) and film thickness (DFT) requirements in the paint manufacturer's data sheet must be followed; otherwise the paint will not adhere.
Su altı gövdesi ve ballast tanklarında s: Consumption of sacrificial anodes (zinc/aluminum) on the underwater hull and in ballast tanks is monitored; on ships with an ICCP (Impressed Current Cathodic Protection) system, current/potential readings are recorded. Anode depletion is assessed at the drydock survey.
Birinci Zabit, güverte için kritik yedek: The Chief Officer sets minimum stock levels for critical deck spares and raises requisitions through the PMS. Typical items are hatch cover seals, hydraulic seals, anodes, paint, wire/rope, twistlock/lashing equipment and greasing materials. Supply is coordinated with the port/agent and the company's purchasing department.
Bütçe sınırlıdır; Birinci Zabit, emniyet: The budget is limited; the Chief Officer puts safety-critical and survey-critical items ahead of cosmetic work. Decisions to postpone work are shared, with the reasons, with the Master and, if necessary, with the technical department.
PSC, vetting (SIRE/CDI) ve klas denetiml: In PSC, vetting (SIRE/CDI) and class inspections, PMS logs, the overdue list, function test records of critical equipment and paint/corrosion condition reports are requested. The Chief Officer ensures that records are up to date, traceable and realistic; "complete on paper but deficient on site" is the most serious finding.
Birinci Zabit, tekrarlayan arızaları (re: The Chief Officer tracks recurring defects as a trend and carries out root cause analysis. If the same item keeps needing attention, there may be a design or usage problem; this is reported to the company in a defect report and the PMS interval is revised.
İyi yönetilen bir PMS, arızaları kaza ha: A well-managed PMS catches failures before they become accidents; a poorly managed PMS produces inspection findings, delays and safety risks. The Chief Officer's task is to combine planning with the reality on site and with record-keeping discipline.
SOLAS III ve II-2, geminin can kurtarma: SOLAS III and II-2 require the ship to keep its life-saving and fire-fighting equipment ready for use at all times. Even though the Chief Officer assigns the daily LSA/FFE checks to junior officers, the Chief Officer remains ultimately responsible for readiness, the accuracy of records and compliance with the service schedule. When a finding is raised at inspection, the Chief Officer is the one held accountable.
Bu sorumluluk; aylık/haftalık kontrol ru: This responsibility takes the form of monthly/weekly check routines, annual/certified servicing, defect records and the procurement of missing or expired items. Safety equipment is equipment "that may be needed at any unpredictable moment, but must work 100% when it is needed".
Can salları, hydrostatic release unit'le: Liferafts, hydrostatic release units (HRUs), inflatable lifejackets, EPIRBs, SARTs and fixed fire-extinguishing systems are subject to periodic servicing at manufacturer-approved service stations. By tracking service dates (next due date), the Chief Officer prevents the ship from sailing with out-of-date (expired) equipment; expired LSA/FFE is a ground for PSC detention.
Filikalar; haftalık görsel/fonksiyonel k: Lifeboats are subject to weekly visual/functional checks, monthly operation (engine start, davit movement), launching and floating out during drills every 3 months, and an annual full function test. On-load release gear requires an overhaul and a dynamic load test every 5 years; this mechanism needs particular attention because it has caused many fatal accidents in the past.
Davit fren testi, wire/fall yenileme (ge: Critical items are the davit brake test, renewal of wires/falls (generally every 5 years or according to condition) and the check of the limit switches. For free-fall lifeboats, a simulated release test and a check of the rail system are also carried out.
Kurtarma botu, her ay denize indirilip m: The rescue boat is tested every month by launching it and maneuvering it in the water (weather permitting). The engine, steering, integrity of the inflatable boat and the davit/launching system are checked. Fast rescue boats need more frequent testing. These tests verify the MOB (Man Overboard) response capability.
EPIRB battery ve HRU expiry tarihleri il: EPIRB battery and HRU expiry dates and the annual shore-based service date are tracked in the PMS. A monthly self-test is carried out and recorded. The SART (Search and Rescue Transponder) battery expiry and mounting position are checked. These devices must also have current registration.
Makine dairesi ve kargo bölgesi sabit CO: Fixed CO2/clean agent systems for the engine room and the cargo area are subject to annual inspection and periodic weighing/pressure checks. The Chief Officer (usually in coordination with the Second/Third Engineer) monitors the cylinder fill percentage, the distribution piping, the alarm/time delay and the functioning of the release mechanism. An inadvertent release is fatal; this is why the alarm that clears personnel from the space before release, and the interlock, are critical.
Tankerlerde deck foam sistemi ve foam co: On tankers, the deck foam system and foam compound expiry, the fixed foam monitors and the high-expansion foam system (where required) are also checked.
Yangın algılama (smoke/heat detector), m: Fire detection (smoke/heat detectors), manual call points, the fire alarm panel and the general alarm are function tested periodically. A contaminated detector causes false alarms or late detection; testing and cleaning are scheduled zone by zone.
Portable yangın söndürücüler (foam, dry: Portable fire extinguishers (foam, dry powder, CO2) are checked for position, pressure gauge, seal, expiry and service date; they undergo annual inspection and periodic hydrostatic testing (generally every 10 years). The presence of fire hydrants, hoses, nozzles and the international shore connection is checked, and the fire pump and emergency fire pump are function tested.
Fireman's outfit (koruyucu giysi, eldive: Fireman's outfits (protective clothing, gloves, boots, helmet, lifeline, lamp, axe) and SCBA sets are kept complete and ready; SCBA cylinder pressure and mask seals are checked regularly. EEBD (Emergency Escape Breathing Device) locations and expiry dates are tracked. The breathing air compressor is checked for proper operation.
Muster list, her mürettebata acil durum: The muster list shows each crew member's emergency duty, muster station and the meaning of the signals. When personnel change, the Chief Officer updates the muster list and posts it in conspicuous places. Everyone who joins receives safety familiarization within 24 hours: donning a lifejacket, finding the muster station, recognizing the alarms and using LSA are demonstrated.
Birinci Zabit, abandon ship, fire, enclo: The Chief Officer plans abandon ship, fire, enclosed space rescue, MOB and emergency steering drills around scenarios, runs them under realistic conditions and identifies weak points in a debrief. Each drill is recorded with the date, participants, scenario, equipment used and observations; real hands-on practice is expected, not a "paper drill".
Gemide onaylı LSA/FFE arrangement plan (: An approved LSA/FFE arrangement plan (including the fire control plan) is kept on board and kept up to date. Inventory records show the location, quantity, service/expiry date and condition of each item. By planning ahead with the expiry schedule, the Chief Officer arranges servicing/renewal in port.
PSC ve vetting denetiminde LSA/FFE en sı: LSA/FFE are among the areas most frequently checked in PSC and vetting inspections: expired pyrotechnics, expired immersion suit lights, an emergency fire pump that does not work and low SCBA pressure are typical findings. By ensuring that records match the actual condition on board, the Chief Officer reduces the risk of detention.
Emniyet ekipmanı yönetiminde başarı, hiç: Success in safety equipment management is not a voyage in which the equipment is never used; it is every item working fully when it is needed. The Chief Officer's disciplined inventory, service tracking and realistic drills directly determine the crew's chances of survival in an emergency.
Çalışma izni, rutin olmayan ve enerji/at: A permit to work is issued for non-routine jobs that carry a fatal risk from energy, atmosphere or height. The ship's SMS typically makes the following categories subject to a permit: enclosed space entry, hot work (welding, grinding, open flame), working aloft (height above 2 m), working overside (outside the ship's side), electrical isolation, opening of pressurized systems and cold work in hazardous areas.
Birinci Zabit, hangi işin izne tabi oldu: The Chief Officer is the authority who decides which jobs are subject to a permit. Even if a job looks "small", a permit is mandatory if it involves a fatal energy source. Most accidents happen during tasks described as "just a short, simple job"; a culture of exceptions must therefore be avoided.
İzin akışı; talep eden (issuing officer': The permit flow separates the roles of the requester (who applies to the issuing officer), the issuer (generally the Chief Officer or the relevant head of department), the approver (the Master, for critical jobs) and the performer (performing personnel). A signature is not a transfer of responsibility; it is a record that the conditions have been verified.
İzin süresi vardiya veya iş penceresiyle: A permit's validity is limited to a watch or to the work window (generally 8–12 hours or a single watch). If conditions change (weather deterioration, equipment failure, change in the atmosphere), the permit is suspended or canceled. When the job is finished, "permit closure" verifies that the site has been cleaned up, isolations removed and systems returned to normal.
Her izin, bir Job Safety Analysis (JSA): Every permit starts with a Job Safety Analysis (JSA) or Risk Assessment. The job is broken down into steps; for each step the hazard is identified and a risk score is calculated by multiplying likelihood by severity. A high/medium/low color matrix shows which controls are mandatory.
Kontrol hiyerarşisi (hierarchy of contro: The hierarchy of controls is applied: first elimination (make the job unnecessary), then substitution, engineering controls, administrative controls and, last of all, PPE. PPE is never the first defense; it is regarded as the "last line". The Chief Officer does not sign the permit without verifying that the team has reduced the risk to an "acceptable" level.
Statik form yetmez; koşullar saha boyunc: A static form is not enough; conditions change on site as the work proceeds. Dynamic risk assessment includes the performing party's "STOP WORK" authority: when a hazard is noticed, anyone can stop the job without fear of punishment. This culture is directly linked to near-miss reporting.
Havalandırma sürekli çalışır; giriş boyu: Ventilation runs continuously and the atmosphere is monitored throughout the entry. The standby person waits at the entrance, keeps continuous communication and never leaves the post. No entry is made until the rescue plan and rescue equipment (tripod, winch, SCBA, resuscitator) are ready.
Hot work (kaynak, kesme, taşlama, açık a: Hot work (welding, cutting, grinding, open flame) is done under standard controls in designated areas such as the workshop. In a non-designated area (particularly near tanks, holds or the fuel oil area) a much stricter permit is required; a gas-free certificate, atmosphere checks of the surrounding tanks and a fire watch are mandatory.
Kaynak/taşlama bittikten sonra metal saa: After welding or grinding is finished, the metal stays hot for hours and can start a hidden fire. The fire watch keeps the area under watch for at least 30–60 minutes after the work ends; concealed voids that sparks may have reached are checked. The permit is closed only when the area has fully cooled down and is clean.
Direk, baca, vinç bomu veya yüksek güver: Work on a mast, funnel, crane boom or high deck equipment requires a full body harness, a double lanyard (100% tie-off) and an independent lifeline. The area below the work is cordoned off; a dropped hand tool can be fatal, so tools are tethered to the wrist with a lanyard.
Radyo/radar antenleri yakınında çalışıla: If work is to be done near radio/radar antennas, the transmitters are switched off and a "DO NOT TRANSMIT — MEN ALOFT" tag is posted; otherwise there is a risk of RF burns and high-frequency hazards. When working near the funnel, the exhaust gas risk (CO, SO2, heat) is assessed.
Working overside (boya, pas raspalama, f: Working overside (painting, rust chipping, freeboard work) requires the combination harness + life jacket + ready lifebuoy with line. One person continuously watches the water surface and the worker. In port, it is verified that propellers/thrusters are not running and that no other ship is maneuvering; if necessary, "no movement" is coordinated.
Elektrik, hidrolik, basınçlı hava ve buh: Hazardous energy sources such as electricity, hydraulics, compressed air and steam are isolated, locked (lock-out) and tagged (tag-out) before work on them begins. The key to the lock stays with the person doing the job; nobody else can re-energize the system. If several people are working, a multi-lock hasp is used.
Birinci Zabit (veya elektrik işlerinde Ç: The Chief Officer (or, for electrical work, in coordination with the Chief Engineer) confirms by a "try-out" test that the isolation is effective: after the energy is cut off, a start is attempted and it is seen that nothing moves. Stored energy (capacitors, pressure, springs) is also released.
Toolbox meeting, izin imzalandıktan sonr: The toolbox meeting is a short on-site briefing, held after the permit is signed, that gives the team the scope of the job, the hazards, the controls and the emergency escape route. It is confirmed that everyone understands their role, has had the chance to ask questions and has confirmed "understood". If there is a language barrier, the common working language or visual explanations are used.
Brifing kayda geçer; katılımcılar imzala: The briefing is recorded and the participants sign. This is evidence both for safety and for inspections. The Chief Officer observes whether the team's morale and attention are as they should be and whether there are any signs of fatigue.
PPE, işin riskine göre seçilir ve durumu: PPE is selected according to the risk of the job, and its condition is checked: hard hat, safety shoes, gloves (chemical/mechanical), eye protection, ear protection, respiratory protection, harness. Damaged PPE is not used; harnesses are subject to periodic inspection and have an expiry date.
İzin imzalanmasıyla iş bitmez; Birinci Z: The job does not end when the permit is signed; the Chief Officer or the designated officer inspects the site periodically. It is confirmed that the gas monitor is working, the standby person is in position and conditions have not changed. The job is stopped if the weather deteriorates, an alarm sounds or anything unexpected happens.
İş bittiğinde alan temizlenir, alet/malz: When the job is finished, the area is cleaned, tools and materials are collected, isolations are removed, systems are returned to normal and, if required, the fire watch is completed. The permit is signed as "closed" and filed; a permit left open creates a major finding at inspection.
PTW sistemi bir kağıt egzersizi değil, ö: The PTW system is not a paper exercise; it is a ring of discipline that keeps lethal energy under control. The rigor the Chief Officer shows here makes the difference between "an accident-free voyage" and "an investigation file". No job is more urgent than a human life.
ISM Code, şirketin bir Safety Management: The ISM Code requires the company to establish a Safety Management System (SMS) and implement it on board. The main actors of the system in the field are the Master (the highest shipboard authority under ISM), the Designated Person Ashore (DPA) and the shipboard Safety Officer. The Safety Officer is usually the Chief Officer and is the person who keeps the safety system "alive".
Safety Officer, denetleyici değil kolayl: The Safety Officer is a facilitator, not an inspector. The role is to make hazards visible, encourage reporting, follow up actions and make safety performance measurable. The basic aim is to build a "just culture" instead of a blame culture; otherwise reporting stops and risks are hidden.
Şirket DOC (Document of Compliance), gem: The company holds a DOC (Document of Compliance) and the ship holds an SMC (Safety Management Certificate). These certificates are verified by periodic and intermediate audits. The Safety Officer ensures that records and practices on board are ready for audit at any time; missing records create a non-conformity.
Safety committee, Kaptan başkanlığında,: The safety committee, chaired by the Master, meets regularly (usually monthly) with representatives of all departments (officers, engine, deck ratings, catering). The Chief Officer prepares the agenda: status of previous actions, near-misses/accidents during the period, drill results, PSC/vetting findings and suggestions from the crew.
Toplantı tutanağa geçer; her aksiyon içi: The meeting is minuted; a responsible person and a target date are assigned to each action. The minutes are sent to the DPA, and open items are followed up at the next meeting. The meeting is not a formality; it is the channel through which the voice of the people doing the work reaches management.
İyi bir komite, sadece zabitanın konuştu: A good committee is one where not only the officers speak, but even the most junior rating can give an opinion. The Chief Officer encourages people to speak up without fear, applies the principle that "there are no stupid questions", takes suggestions seriously and puts at least one of them into practice. An implemented suggestion is the factor that increases participation most.
Near-miss (ramak kala), yaralanma/hasar: A near-miss is an event that did not cause injury or damage but could have. The Heinrich/Bird pyramid shows that beneath every serious accident there are dozens of near-misses and hundreds of unsafe acts. Collecting near-misses is the cheapest way to prevent accidents.
Safety Officer, near-miss raporlamasını: The Safety Officer encourages near-miss reporting and never punishes the person who reports. On the contrary, low reporting does not mean "everything is fine"; it means "problems are being hidden". The aim is the combination of high near-miss reporting and few actual accidents.
Safety observation (BBS — Behaviour Base: Safety observation (BBS — Behavior-Based Safety) cards record safe and unsafe behavior as it happens. The Safety Officer collects the cards, carries out trend analysis (e.g. repeated PPE deficiencies, slip risk in the same area) and plans targeted interventions.
Bir kaza/near-miss sonrası olay araştırı: After an accident or near-miss, the event is investigated. The process includes collecting evidence (photos, witness statements, records), building a timeline, root cause analysis (5 Whys, fishbone, TRIPOD) and deciding on corrective/preventive actions. The aim is not to find someone to blame but to close the gap in the system.
Yüzeysel neden (\"dikkatsizlik\") yeterl: A superficial cause ("carelessness") is not enough; the investigation goes deeper by asking "why was the person careless?". Latent (hidden) factors such as fatigue, inadequate training, missing procedures and poor design are brought to light. This is the only way to achieve real prevention.
Düzeltici (corrective) aksiyon mevcut so: A corrective action eliminates the existing problem; a preventive action stops a similar one from occurring. Each action is defined in SMART terms (responsible person, date, measurable outcome). The Safety Officer follows up open actions; an action that is not closed creates a repeat finding at audit.
Drill bir \"kutu işaretleme\" değildir;: A drill is not "box-ticking"; every drill is evaluated, weaknesses are recorded and lessons are drawn for the next one. Scenarios must not become routine; night drills, different fire locations and "missing person" variations test real readiness.
Yeni gelen her personel, görevine başlam: Every new joiner is familiarized with the ship before starting duties: escape routes, alarm signals, muster station, PPE locations and the use of personal life-saving equipment. The Safety Officer keeps a record of this process; incomplete familiarization can be a ground for PSC detention.
Şirket SMS'i periyodik internal audit ya: Under the company SMS, periodic internal audits are carried out. Findings are classified as non-conformity (NC), observation or improvement. The Safety Officer prepares a response to the finding based on root cause analysis, defines the corrective action and closes it with evidence. A superficial response ("crew warned") does not close a finding.
DPA, gemi ile şirketin en üst yönetimi a: The DPA is the direct link between the ship and the highest level of company management and plays ISM's "bridge" role between ship and shore. The Safety Officer reports safety performance, open actions and resource needs to the DPA. Access to the DPA must not be restricted by any obstacle; this is a fundamental safeguard of ISM.
Emniyet performansı; LTIF (Lost Time Inj: Safety performance is monitored with indicators such as LTIF (Lost Time Injury Frequency), TRCF (Total Recordable Case Frequency), the number of near-miss reports/observations, the drill completion rate and the number of open actions. The Safety Officer analyzes the trends and presents them at the safety committee.
Lagging indicators (kaza sonrası) tek ba: Lagging indicators (after the accident) are not enough on their own; leading indicators (near-misses, observations, training) give forward-looking early warning. A good system monitors and balances both.
Safety Officer rolü, gemideki emniyet kü: The Safety Officer role is the pulse of the safety culture on board. Here the Chief Officer does not just keep records; the Chief Officer is the person who makes hazards visible, encourages reporting and closes the gaps in the system. A strong safety culture saves more lives than the best single piece of "equipment".
Güverte departmanı tipik olarak Birinci: The deck department typically consists of the Second Officer, Third Officer, Bosun, Able Seamen (AB), Ordinary Seamen (OS) and cadets under the Chief Officer. The Chief Officer organizes navigational watch and cargo operation duties for the officers, while managing the ratings' daily maintenance and operational work through the Bosun. These two channels (watchkeeping system + day work system) must not clash; rest hours must be protected in both.
Reis, Birinci Zabit'in saha temsilcisidi: The Bosun is the Chief Officer's representative on deck: the Bosun allocates the jobs given at the morning toolbox meeting to the ratings, obtains equipment and materials and checks the quality of the work. The Chief Officer, in turn, prepares the weekly work plan, sets priorities and closes out the PMS (Planned Maintenance System) deck items on time.
Geminin Minimum Safe Manning Document (M: The ship's Minimum Safe Manning Document (MSMD) is issued by the flag State and specifies the minimum qualified personnel that must be on board. The Chief Officer must assess whether the planned workload can be completed with the personnel available without violating rest hours. During busy periods such as port operations, heavy weather and tank cleaning, the work plan must be prioritized realistically and non-critical work postponed.
Yorgunluk (fatigue), denizcilik kazaları: Fatigue is the most common human factor behind marine accidents. The Chief Officer plans so that real rest is achieved, not so that rest hours add up on paper; "adjusting the records" (manipulating records) is both an MLC violation and a serious safety risk.
Birinci Zabit, PMS çıktıları, klas/PSC t: The Chief Officer draws up the weekly work plan based on PMS output, the class/PSC schedule, charterer requests and the condition of the hull. The plan covers which areas will be painted, which equipment will be taken in for maintenance, which lashing/securing work will be done and which survey preparations will be carried out. At the short meeting with the Bosun every morning (toolbox talk), the day's jobs, their risks and the necessary permits (hot work, enclosed space, working aloft) are reviewed.
İyi bir plan, hava durumunu, geminin dem: A good plan takes into account the weather, whether the ship is at anchor, at sea or in port, and the number of personnel. Painting cannot be done in the rain; overside work (outside the ship) is not planned in heavy weather; working aloft is postponed while there is vibration from the ship being under way. The Chief Officer leaves room for flexibility.
Seyirde tayfalar zabitlerle birlikte 4-s: At sea, ratings stand 4-hour watches together with the officers (e.g. 4-on/8-off); a lookout is mandatory under STCW at night and in restricted visibility. In port, a gangway watch, cargo watch and security watch (ISPS) system is set up. The Chief Officer prepares the watch schedule without violating the rest regime and ensures that the handover is complete at every change of duty.
Gemiye yeni katılan her personel, görev: Every new joiner receives safety familiarization in accordance with ISM Code Section 6 and SOLAS before taking up duties. The Chief Officer (or an officer the Chief Officer designates) shows the lifejackets, immersion suits, muster station, liferafts/lifeboats, fire extinguisher locations, alarm signals, emergency escape routes and mustering procedures. This training is documented and signed for.
Görev-özel familiarization ise personeli: Job-specific familiarization relates to the person's actual work: the mooring station, crane operation, the enclosed space procedure, personal protective equipment (PPE), the permit-to-work system and the relevant sections of the company SMS. New personnel are not assigned alone to hazardous work until full familiarization has been completed.
Yeni personel, deneyimli bir AB ile eşle: New personnel are paired with an experienced AB (buddy system) and work under supervision during the first weeks. The Chief Officer holds a review within the first 2 weeks to assess the person's adaptation, language/communication skills and abilities. In multinational crews, a common working language (usually English) and a clear command structure are critical for safety.
Birinci Zabit, güverte personelinin yetk: The Chief Officer continuously develops the competence of deck personnel through drills and onboard training. Fire, abandon ship, enclosed space rescue, man overboard, pollution (SOPEP) and security drills are scheduled and coordinated with the Bosun. A debrief is held after each drill; deficiencies are recorded and corrected in the next drill.
Kadet eğitimi ayrı bir sorumluluktur: Tr: Cadet training is a separate responsibility: Training Record Book (TRB) tasks are signed off according to a plan, and the cadet takes part in real operations under supervision. The Chief Officer monitors both the theoretical and the practical development of the cadet.
Her personelin STCW sertifikaları, sağlı: The validity dates of each person's STCW certificates, medical fitness certificate and documents such as GMDSS/tanker endorsements are tracked. The Chief Officer follows the validity of the department's documents in a matrix and notifies the Master and the company in advance of documents about to expire; personnel with expired certificates cannot remain on duty, and this leads to PSC detention.
Gemide disiplin, can ve mal emniyetinin: Discipline on board is the foundation of the safety of life and property. The Chief Officer clearly sets out the standard of conduct within the department; PPE use, the drug & alcohol policy, compliance with work permits and respect for the hierarchy are non-negotiable rules. In the event of a violation, the progressive disciplinary process defined in the company SMS (verbal warning → written warning → formal report) is applied.
Disiplin, cezalandırmadan çok güvenli ve: Discipline aims to create a safe and fair working environment rather than to punish. The Chief Officer earns the team's trust by acting consistently and without bias; discrimination, harassment and bullying are dealt with under the MLC with zero tolerance.
İyi bir Birinci Zabit, otorite ile erişi: A good Chief Officer balances authority with approachability. Regular department meetings, open feedback and fair allocation of work keep motivation high. In multinational teams, sensitivity to cultural differences and clear communication reduce misunderstandings and tension. A motivated team works both more safely and more efficiently.
Her personel için günlük çalışma/dinlenm: Daily hours of work and rest are recorded for each person (rest hours record). The Chief Officer checks that these records are kept accurately and that they do not breach STCW/MLC limits. Software-based systems (e.g. rest hours planning modules) flag violations automatically. These records are among the first documents requested in PSC and MLC inspections.
İhlal kaçınılmazsa (örn. acil durum, uzu: If a violation is unavoidable (e.g. an emergency, a long maneuver), it must be recorded with its real reason and compensatory rest must be given. Systematically "fitting" the records within the limits is, when detected, a ground for a serious finding (deficiency) and even detention.
MLC 2006; barınma, beslenme, sağlık, eğl: MLC 2006 sets minimum standards on matters such as accommodation, food, health, recreational facilities and paid leave. The Chief Officer looks after the deck personnel's living conditions in the accommodation, laundry/cleaning arrangements and general welfare, and finds solutions by passing problems on to the Master. Crew satisfaction reduces turnover and preserves accumulated experience.
Birinci Zabit, güverte personelinin perf: The Chief Officer periodically evaluates the performance of deck personnel using the company appraisal forms. The appraisal covers technical competence, safety awareness, work ethic, teamwork and leadership potential. It is based on objective observation and examples; subjective bias is avoided. The results are shared with the person and areas for development are identified together.
İyi performans gösteren personelin terfi: Recommending well-performing personnel to the company for promotion/re-employment creates motivation and a sense of belonging in the team. Poor performance, on the other hand, is supported with coaching and additional training; if there is no improvement, it is reported on record.
Sağlıklı bir güverte departmanında near-: In a healthy deck department, near-miss reporting is encouraged; the aim is learning, not punishment. The Chief Officer analyzes reported events, finds the root cause and builds the corrective measures into the work plan. Suppressing a near-miss prepares the ground for the next real accident.
Birinci Zabit'in personel yönetimindeki: The Chief Officer's success in managing people is the ship's invisible insurance: a well-trained, rested, motivated and disciplined deck team is what makes the difference in heavy weather, in an emergency and during intensive cargo operations. Managing people correctly comes before managing equipment correctly, because in the end every piece of equipment is operated by people.
Birinci Zabit, pilot station'a varmadan: Before arriving at the pilot station, the Chief Officer prepares a mooring plan based on the port's berthing prospectus, the type of berth (fixed jetty, dolphin, finger pier, SBM) and the available bollard arrangement. The plan shows the numbers of head lines, breast lines, springs and stern lines, which winch/windlass will be used and through which fairleads the lines will be led. Under MEG4, a symmetrical arrangement (lines balanced in each direction) and breast lines as close as possible to perpendicular (90°) to the berth are essential.
Plan, mevcut çevre kuvvetlerine (rüzgar,: The plan assesses whether the number of lines is sufficient for the prevailing environmental forces (wind, current, swell, passing ship effect). MEG4 requires the MBL (Minimum Breaking Load) of each line and the distribution of forces relative to the SDMBL (Ship Design MBL) to be documented. The plan must be consistent with the mooring line management plan (MLMP).
Manevra öncesi Birinci Zabit, baş üstü e: Before maneuvering, the Chief Officer gives a toolbox briefing to the forward mooring team (bosun + deck ratings): who will operate the winch, who will throw the heaving line, who will hold the stopper and who will handle communications. Everyone must know their task and their own snap-back zone. The radio channel between the bridge and the forward/aft stations must be clear and confirmed.
Personelin PPE'si (kask, eldiven, çelik: Personnel PPE (helmet, gloves, steel-toe boots, lifejacket if required) is checked. Fatigue management is critical; STCW rest hours must not be violated during long maneuvers. The Chief Officer makes sure that the team is physically ready.
Halatlar düzenli olarak elden geçirilir:: Lines are inspected regularly for abrasion, cuts, glazing (heat damage), internal fiber breakage and UV degradation. The MEG4 retirement criteria (replacement when residual strength falls below 75%) are applied. A worn line increases the risk of snap-back.
Mooring winch'ler brake holding capacity: Mooring winches are set according to their brake holding capacity; MEG4 recommends keeping the brake rendering point at 60% of the SDMBL (for steel) or 80% (for synthetic). A brake test (brake holding capacity test) must be carried out regularly and recorded. A brake set too tight leads to the line parting; a slack brake lets the ship move off the berth.
Stopper (chain stopper, carpenter stoppe: The stopper (chain stopper, carpenter stopper or rope stopper) holds the load while the line is transferred from the winch to the bollard. Incorrect stopper technique (e.g. a chain stopper on a synthetic line) creates a life-threatening hazard. The Chief Officer checks that the correct stopper is used on the correct line. On "self-tailing" winches, the minimum number of turns of the line on the drum must be maintained.
Bir mooring line gerildiğinde içinde dep: When a mooring line is under tension, elastic energy is stored in it; if the line parts, this energy is released as a whiplash (snap-back) movement in both directions from the point of parting. In highly elastic lines such as nylon, this movement reaches lethal speed. Snap-back is the source of the most frequent fatal accidents in seafaring; a line that strikes a person kills instantly.
MEG4, eski \"boyalı snap-back zone\" yak: MEG4 has revised the old "painted snap-back zone" approach: zones are no longer treated as individual painted lines but as "the whole mooring deck being a potential danger zone", because the direction of snap-back can change with the lead angle of the line and with fairlead failure. The Chief Officer forbids personnel to stand inside a bight, in line with a fairlead, or between the line and the bollard while a line is under tension.
Birinci Zabit, ekibi line ile mümkün old: The Chief Officer positions the team as close as possible to right angles to the line and where the escape route is clear. Personnel throwing the heaving line move to a safe area before the line comes under load. Standard commands such as "slack away", "heave up", "hold on" and "make fast" are passed between the bridge and the station with clear radio confirmation; ambiguity is an invitation to an accident.
Römorkör yardımlı manevralarda Birinci Z: In tug-assisted maneuvers, the Chief Officer supervises the safe securing of the tug line (usually with the tug's own gear or the ship's messenger) to the ship's bitt/fairlead.
