ETO, single-line diagram üzerinden hangi: From the single-line diagram, the ETO must know which consumers are connected to the emergency switchboard (navigation lights, emergency lighting, GMDSS, fire pump, steering gear, watertight door controls, general alarm) and which are bridged by the transitional battery. This overview is critical for correct prioritization in the event of a failure.
Emergency generator, ana güç kaybından s: The emergency generator must start automatically after loss of main power and supply the emergency busbar within 45 seconds at the latest. During this changeover, the transitional source of emergency power (accumulator battery) supplies the mandatory loads without interruption. The supply duration is 36 hours on passenger ships and 18 hours on cargo ships.
ETO, emergency generator'ın start güveni: The ETO is responsible for ensuring the starting reliability of the emergency generator: the state of charge of the starting batteries, the starting air (if fitted), the fuel level and the health of the automatic start panel are verified by a weekly test. If the automatic start attempt fails, manual starting and manual energizing of the busbar are kept ready as a backup.
ETO, emergency generator'ı her hafta tes: The ETO tests the emergency generator every week. The standard test verifies the engine's starting reliability and its ability to run on load. In the monthly test (or more often if class requires), a blackout is simulated: the supply to the main busbar is cut off (or the sensing cable is opened), and the test is timed to confirm that the generator starts automatically within 45 seconds and supplies the emergency busbar.
Emergency generator genellikle elektrik: The emergency generator is usually equipped with electric (battery) start and/or compressed air start; a dual system provides reliability. The ETO regularly checks the terminal voltage of the starting batteries, the electrolyte level (vented type), the state of charge and the output of the battery charger. A weak starting battery is the most frequent cause of a failure to start during a blackout.
Start denemesi limiti (genellikle 3 ardı: The start attempt limit (usually 3 consecutive attempts) and the waiting time between attempts are set on the panel. The ETO checks these setpoints and the starting air pressure (if fitted); if draining and moisture control in the compressed air system are neglected, the starting valves can stick.
Emergency switchboard'un kalbi, ana bara: The heart of the emergency switchboard is the interlock logic between the bus-tie breaker connected to the main busbar and the emergency generator breaker. When a blackout is detected, the bus-tie opens, the generator starts and the generator breaker closes. By testing this transfer sequence, the ETO verifies that the interlock prevents both breakers from being closed at the same time (risk of back-feed).
ETO, emergency switchboard içindeki koru: The ETO periodically checks the protective devices (MCCBs, fuses), busbar connections and indicating instruments inside the emergency switchboard. A thermal camera scan for loose connections and insulation measurements ensure the reliability of the switchboard.
ETO, emergency switchboard'a bağlı olmas: The ETO physically verifies that every consumer that must be connected to the emergency switchboard is actually supplied from it: navigation lights, emergency lighting, GMDSS, emergency fire pump, steering gear (at least one unit), general alarm, watertight door controls and bilge alarms. The connection layout is compared with the class-approved list.
Gemide UPS'ler kritik tüketicilere kesin: On board, UPS units supply uninterrupted, clean power to critical consumers: ECDIS, radar, the GMDSS console, automation/IAS servers, cargo control and the VDR. An online (double-conversion) UPS feeds the load continuously through the inverter and carries on without any changeover when the mains supply fails; a line-interactive UPS, which has a short changeover time, is used in simpler applications.
ETO, her UPS'in beslediği yükü, batarya: The ETO must know the load fed by each UPS, the battery autonomy time (usually 30 min, or longer where required by class) and the bypass capability. For critical navigation/communication equipment, class requires a minimum autonomy time and periodic testing of UPS condition.
UPS bakımı veya batarya değişimi için yü: For UPS maintenance or battery replacement, the UPS must be transferred to static/manual bypass without interrupting the load. The ETO follows the correct sequence: first transfer the load to static bypass, then close the maintenance (manual) bypass switch and isolate the UPS. A wrong sequence can cause a momentary loss of power to the load.
UPS bataryaları (genellikle VRLA tip) za: UPS batteries (usually VRLA type) lose capacity over time; the ETO verifies the actual autonomy time with a periodic discharge test. The terminal voltage, internal resistance (impedance test) and temperature of the battery blocks are measured; a single weak cell degrades the performance of the whole string. Blocks whose internal resistance rises 25-50% above the reference value are replaced.
ETO, batarya değişim tarihini ve seri öm: The ETO keeps track of the battery replacement date and the service life of the string (typically 4-7 years for VRLA). High temperature (battery room/UPS cabinet) seriously shortens life: every 8-10°C above 25°C halves the service life. Cooling and ventilation are therefore critical.
UPS inverter'ı, DC bataryayı temiz AC'ye: The UPS inverter converts the DC battery supply into clean AC; the ETO checks the inverter output waveform, the output voltage/frequency and the cooling fans. A blocked fan or dusty cooling ducts cause overheating and loss of capacitor life. DC bus capacitors and filter elements are checked periodically.
Acil aydınlatma, blackout anında kaçış y: During a blackout, emergency lighting illuminates the escape routes, the engine room, the liferaft embarkation areas and other important areas. A central system fed from the emergency switchboard and/or self-contained fittings with their own batteries are used. The ETO periodically tests the battery condition of the self-contained fittings and that they switch on automatically when the main supply fails.
Navigation light panel (seyir feneri pan: The navigation light panel provides a dual supply (main + emergency) for each light, on/off monitoring and a lamp failure alarm. The ETO verifies that each light is fed from two independent sources, that spare lamps are ready and that the lamp failure alarm works.
GMDSS reserve source of energy (batarya): Under SOLAS, the GMDSS reserve source of energy (batteries) must supply the GMDSS equipment on loss of main and emergency power for at least 1 hour (if an emergency generator is fitted) or 6 hours (if not). The ETO checks the specific gravity of the GMDSS batteries (vented type), their terminal voltage and the charger output daily/weekly, and carries out the annual discharge test.
Emergency generator'ın blackout anında s: Failure of the emergency generator to start during a blackout is the most critical scenario. Causes: a weak/flat starting battery, fuel shortage or air in the fuel system, a cold engine, a start panel fault or a sticking solenoid. The ETO must know the manual start and manual busbar energizing procedure and must eliminate the root cause. Regular weekly testing greatly reduces this risk.
Yaşlanmış UPS bataryası, şebeke kesilinc: An aged UPS battery cannot provide the expected autonomy when the mains supply fails, and the critical load (ECDIS, IAS) drops out immediately. In addition, a wrong bypass sequence can cause loss of the load during maintenance. The ETO manages these risks through periodic capacity testing and correct bypass discipline.
Acil güç sistemi, gemi en savunmasız anı: The emergency power system is the last safety net, coming into action when the ship is at its most vulnerable; therefore "tested but never needed" is the measure of success. The ETO's disciplined weekly testing, trending of battery condition and annual verification of the transfer logic ensure that this net deploys quietly and reliably at the moment of a critical blackout.
Direct-on-line (DOL) yol verme en basiti: Direct-on-line (DOL) starting is the simplest, but it draws a starting current of 6-8 times the motor rated current; it is therefore used on small motors (usually <15-22 kW). Star-delta starting reduces the starting current to about 1/3 and is common on medium-power motors; however, a torque and current surge occurs at the changeover from star to delta.
Soft starter, tristör (SCR) ile gerilimi: A soft starter gives a smooth start by raising the voltage gradually with thyristors (SCR) and reduces mechanical shock. A VFD (Variable Frequency Drive) varies frequency and voltage together, giving both a smooth start and speed control; on pumps and fans it gives significant energy savings because of the affinity laws. The ETO verifies that the correct starter type has been selected and that each one is maintained.
Motor Control Center (MCC), bir geminin: The Motor Control Center (MCC) is the modular switchboard that houses all of a ship's motor starters. Each starter module contains a main switch/fuse, contactor(s), a thermal overload relay, a control transformer and indicators/push buttons. The ETO periodically checks the thermal condition of the MCC, the condition of the contactors and the integrity of the control circuits.
Kontaktör, motoru şebekeye bağlayan elek: A contactor is the electromechanical switch that connects the motor to the supply; every opening and closing causes arcing and wear on the contacts. The ETO checks the contact surfaces for signs of wear, pitting and overheating. Burnt or welded contacts are replaced immediately, as they can cause the motor to run uncontrolled.
Kontaktör bobini (coil) gerilimi ve çekm: The contactor coil voltage and pick-up/drop-out behavior are checked; a chattering contactor is a sign of low control voltage or dirty contacts. The ETO tests the soundness of the mechanical interlocks (especially the interlock that prevents two contactors from pulling in at the same time in reversing and star-delta applications).
Kontrol devresindeki yardımcı röleler ve: Auxiliary relays and timer relays in the control circuit (especially for star-delta changeover timing) ensure that the start sequence works correctly. The ETO verifies that the timer relay setting is correct (star-delta changeover typically 5-15 s) and that the relay contacts are clean. Wrong timing causes an excessive current surge at changeover.
Termik overload rölesi, motoru aşırı akı: The thermal overload relay protects the motor against overcurrent (mechanical jamming, phase loss, overload). The ETO sets the relay current setpoint according to the motor's rated value (FLA - Full Load Ampere), typically 105-115% of FLA. Too low a setting means nuisance trips; too high a setting means a burnt-out motor.
Modern elektronik overload röleleri ek k: Modern electronic overload relays provide additional protection: phase loss (single phasing), phase imbalance, earth leakage and motor winding temperature monitoring through a thermistor (PTC) input. The ETO verifies that these functions are active and that the trip class (usually Class 10 or 20) suits the motor characteristics.
Bir fazın kaybolması (single phasing), k: Loss of one phase (single phasing) causes overcurrent in the remaining two phases and rapid burnout of the motor. The ETO verifies that phase-loss protection is active and that phase imbalance (the difference between the phase currents) is monitored. In three-phase motors, a 5% voltage imbalance leads to about 30% current imbalance and overheating.
VFD üç ana katmandan oluşur: doğrultucu: A VFD consists of three main stages: the rectifier converts AC to DC, the DC bus capacitor bank smooths/stores this DC, and the inverter (IGBT) produces AC at the required frequency and voltage by PWM. Motor speed is set in proportion to frequency (n = 120f/p). The motor magnetic flux is maintained by keeping the V/f ratio constant.
VFD'ler harmonik akım üretir ve bu, şebe: VFDs generate harmonic currents, which affect the power quality of the network. On large VFDs, the ETO must know the harmonic mitigation measures (line reactor, 12/18-pulse rectifier, active front end) and must check the filter elements. In addition, the high dV/dt at the VFD output can stress the motor insulation and the bearings (bearing current); an output reactor or a dV/dt filter is used.
VFD'nin doğru çalışması, doğru parametre: Correct operation of a VFD depends on the correct parameter set: motor nameplate values (voltage, current, frequency, power), ramp-up/down times, current/torque limits, minimum/maximum frequency and protection settings. The ETO records the parameters at commissioning and backs them up regularly; when a board is replaced after a failure, this backup allows rapid restoration.
ETO, VFD fault log'unu düzenli inceler:: The ETO reviews the VFD fault log regularly: overcurrent, overvoltage (DC bus), undervoltage, overtemperature, ground fault and motor overload trips are valuable for root cause analysis. A recurring fault code is an early sign of a developing hardware problem.
VFD'ler önemli ölçüde ısı üretir; soğutm: VFDs generate considerable heat; clean cooling fans and heat sinks are critical for service life. The ETO periodically checks that the cooling fans are turning, that the air inlet filters are clean and that there is no dust/salt build-up on the heat sink. Blocked cooling raises IGBT and capacitor temperatures and leads to early failure.
Elektrolitik DC bus kapasitörleri, VFD'n: Electrolytic DC bus capacitors are the component of a VFD with the most limited life (typically 5-10 years, depending on temperature). Aging shows as an increase in ESR (Equivalent Series Resistance) and a drop in capacitance; bulging, leakage or an opened pressure vent are physical signs of failure. The ETO knows how to re-form the capacitors (reforming) of VFDs that have been in storage for a long time.
Motor sargı yalıtımı, nem, sıcaklık ve y: Motor winding insulation deteriorates with moisture, temperature and aging. The ETO isolates the motor and measures the winding-to-earth insulation resistance (IR) with a 500 V megger (LV motor). Under IEEE 43, the minimum acceptable IR depends on the winding voltage; in practice, 1 MΩ + 1 MΩ per kV of rated voltage is a practical lower limit, but the trend is more important.
Polarization Index (PI = 10 dakika IR /: The Polarization Index (PI = 10-minute IR / 1-minute IR) shows how clean and dry the insulation is; PI < 1 indicates wet/contaminated insulation and PI > 2 indicates healthy insulation. The ETO corrects the measurement for temperature (40°C reference) and keeps a trend record. Low values require drying with the space heater.
Düşük IR ölçülen motorlar space heater d: Motors with a low IR reading are dried by switching on the space heater or with external hot air. The ETO verifies that the space heaters of standby motors are working; the windings of a stopped motor absorb moisture. During drying, IR is measured periodically and drying continues until the value stabilizes.
Aşırı motor titreşimi; rulman aşınması,: Excessive motor vibration is a sign of bearing wear, unbalance, misalignment or looseness. The ETO measures the RMS velocity (mm/s) at the bearing points with a vibration analyzer and compares it with the ISO 20816 limits. Spectrum analysis identifies the fault type from the frequency components (1× running speed = unbalance, 2× = misalignment, high frequency = bearing).
VFD beslemeli motorlarda yüksek frekansl: In VFD-fed motors, high-frequency common-mode voltage creates a parasitic current between shaft and earth (bearing current) and causes fluting damage on the bearing surfaces. On these motors, the ETO checks that a shaft grounding ring or insulated bearings are fitted and in good condition.
Motor kontrol ve güç elektroniği bakımı,: Maintenance of motor control and power electronics calls for an unseen but continuous discipline: a correctly set overload relay saves a motor from burning out, while regular megger and vibration trending turn unplanned failures into planned maintenance. The ETO's mastery in this area is measured by keeping the ship's hundreds of items of rotating equipment running quietly and by making a tangible contribution to energy efficiency.
Elektrik çarpması, akımın vücuttan geçme: Electric shock occurs when current passes through the human body; the moisture and metal structure of the shipboard environment increase contact with earth and so raise the risk. An AC current of 50 mA can cause cardiac fibrillation; touch voltage limits (usually 50 V AC) are therefore critical. Arc flash is the plasma and pressure wave created by a short-circuit arc, which reaches 19,000°C in a fraction of a second.
ETO, her çalışmada gerilim seviyesini, m: For every job, the ETO assesses the voltage level, the prospective short-circuit current and the conditions in the space. On high-energy switchboards (main switchboard, HV switchgear), arc flash is the most serious hazard; no live work is done without appropriate PPE and safe distance.
Gemi şebekeleri genellikle izole (IT) to: Ship networks are usually insulated (IT) systems: the neutral is not connected to earth. This allows operation to continue after a first earth fault (continuity advantage), but a second fault becomes a phase-to-phase short circuit. The ETO detects the first fault with the insulation monitoring device (IMD) and clears it before a second fault occurs.
LOTO, bir ekipmanın enerjisinin güvenli: LOTO means safely disconnecting the energy supply to equipment and preventing it from being accidentally re-energized. The ETO applies the standard sequence: plan and announce the work, identify the relevant power sources, open the switches/breaker, fit a physical lock, hang a warning tag, discharge stored energy (capacitors, motor inertia) and finally test for absence of voltage.
Anahtar (kilit) yalnızca işi yapan kişid: The key to the lock must be held only by the person doing the work; the "one person - one lock" principle applies. Where several people are working, each person fits their own lock (group lockout). The ETO ensures that removal of the isolation is also controlled: first a check of the area, then removal of tags/locks, and energizing last.
Yüksek riskli elektrik işlerinde Permit: A Permit to Work (PTW) system is applied for high-risk electrical work: the job description, isolation list, risks, PPE and approval signatures are documented. The ETO tests the voltage detector used to prove absence of voltage on a known live source before and after use (prove-test-prove principle); this ensures that the instrument is sound.
Gemide gövde (hull), referans toprak gör: On board, the hull serves as the reference earth; all metal equipment enclosures are bonded with protective earthing (PE). This limits the touch voltage in the event of an insulation fault. The ETO periodically checks equipment earthing connections for integrity, corrosion and looseness; earthing of portable equipment and temporary connections in particular is carefully verified.
HV ve yüksek enerjili sistemlerde izolas: On HV and high-energy systems, working earths (earthing/grounding) are applied after isolation as protection against residual/induced voltage. The ETO deliberately earths the section to be worked on with the earthing switch or a portable earthing set; in this way, accidental energizing or capacitive/inductive voltage does not endanger the person working. The earthing is removed as the last step when the work is finished.
Insulation Monitoring Device (IMD), izol: The Insulation Monitoring Device (IMD) continuously measures the phase-to-earth insulation resistance of an insulated network and gives an alarm when it falls below the set threshold. The ETO never ignores an IMD alarm; it may be the first and only warning of a developing earth fault. After the alarm, the faulty consumer is isolated by the branch-by-branch method.
ETO, IMD'nin alarm setpoint'ini (tipik o: The ETO regularly checks the IMD alarm setpoint (typically in the range of a few hundred kΩ to a few kΩ, depending on system voltage) and its test function. Some modern IMDs can locate the faulty circuit automatically (EDS - insulation fault location), which greatly shortens fault-finding time.
IMD sürekli izleme yapsa da, ETO devre/e: Although the IMD monitors continuously, the ETO trends gradual insulation deterioration through periodic megger measurements on each circuit/item of equipment. Measurements are corrected for temperature and recorded; a falling trend gives early warning of a developing problem that has not yet raised an alarm.
Arc flash, mevcut kısa devre akımı ve ar: Depending on the prospective short-circuit current and the arc clearing time, an arc flash releases a large amount of thermal energy (incident energy, cal/cm²). The ETO assesses the arc flash energy and the safe approach limits (arc flash boundary) at critical switchboards using the IEEE 1584 methodology. The appropriate level of arc-rated PPE is determined for high-energy switchboards.
Arc flash riskini azaltmak için koruma r: The basic strategies for reducing arc flash risk are shortening the clearing time of the protection relays, using faster protection settings in maintenance mode (maintenance switch) and eliminating live work. The ETO ensures that arc flash warning labels (incident energy, boundary, required PPE) are posted on high-energy switchboards.
Makine dairesi sintinesi, tank içleri, k: The risk of electric shock increases in damp/conductive environments such as the engine room bilges, the inside of tanks, the boiler room and the open deck. In these spaces, low-voltage (e.g. 24 V) hand lamps, double-insulated or earthed portable tools and, where necessary, an isolating transformer are used. The ETO verifies that portable equipment is suitable for these spaces.
Tankerlerde ve gaz tehlikesi olan mahall: On tankers and in spaces with a gas hazard, electrical equipment must be of the explosion-protected (Ex) type. The ETO maintains the integrity of Ex equipment (flameproof enclosure, gaskets, full set of bolts); opening an Ex fitting or repairing it incorrectly invalidates its protection rating and creates a risk of explosion.
6.6 kV ve üzeri HV sistemlerde her manev: On HV systems of 6.6 kV and above, every switching operation is carried out under a written switching program and a Permit to Work. The ETO must hold an additional HV training certificate and work as an authorized person. The switching sequence is written in advance, checked by a second person and carried out with each step signed off.
HV sistemlerde gerilime asgari yaklaşma: On HV systems, the minimum approach distances to live parts are strictly observed. Insulating gloves are checked before each use with an air leak (inflation) test, undergo periodic dielectric testing and are worn with leather over-gloves for mechanical protection. The ETO keeps track of the certificate and test validity dates of the HV PPE inventory.
Pek çok elektrik kazasının kök nedeni ek: The root cause of many electrical accidents is incomplete or unverified isolation: opening the wrong breaker, not testing for absence of voltage, or overlooking multiple supplies (e.g. a UPS, another busbar). The ETO ensures that the isolation list covers all supply sources and that absence of voltage is physically measured.
Elektrik güvenliği, prosedürler kadar kü: Electrical safety depends as much on culture as on procedures. The ETO encourages near-miss reporting without hesitation, shares electrical risks in toolbox talks and teaches LOTO discipline to junior crew members. Safety is achieved in an environment where even the most competent person does not take shortcuts.
Elektrik güvenliği, ETO'nun pazarlık kon: Electrical safety is the ETO's non-negotiable first priority. The discipline of isolate, lock, tag, test and, where necessary, earth is the simple but life-saving chain that prevents an error from turning into a fatal outcome. The ETO's success is measured by a ship operating with zero electrical accidents and by instilling this discipline in the whole crew.
Tüm parçaları aynı miktarda stoklamak ne: Stocking all parts in the same quantity is neither economical nor possible. The ETO classifies parts by criticality and lead time: parts whose failure would stop the ship (e.g. a main switchboard protection relay, a propulsion drive PCB) are always kept in stock; easily obtained, low-criticality parts are kept at a minimum level.
Stok yönetimi minimum/maksimum seviye ve: Stock is managed with minimum/maximum levels and a reorder point. The ETO updates the levels by monitoring the consumption trend; the stock level of a component that fails frequently is increased. The PMS software is used to deduct used parts automatically and to trigger orders.
Sınıf kuruluşları ve SOLAS, belirli krit: Classification societies and SOLAS require minimum spare parts to be carried for certain critical systems. The ETO ensures that this "required spares" list is always complete; when an item is used, it is reordered immediately. A missing required spare results in a finding (deficiency) at a class survey or PSC inspection.
Modern gemilerde otomasyon, drive ve hab: On modern ships, automation, drive and communication systems are based on PCBs (printed circuit boards) and modules. The ETO stocks at least one spare of each critical board (controller CPU, I/O boards, drive control board, AVR board). Replacing a board usually requires parameters/software to be loaded; the ETO backs up these configurations.
PCB'ler ESD (elektrostatik deşarj) ve ne: PCBs are sensitive to ESD (electrostatic discharge) and moisture; they are therefore kept in antistatic bags in a dry, cool place. The ETO periodically checks the condition of critical boards in the store and watches for the risk of aging on boards with electrolytic capacitors that have been in storage for a long time.
Sigortalar (fuse) doğru tip, akım ve kes: Fuses must be stocked with the correct type, current rating and breaking capacity; a wrong fuse both fails to protect and creates a safety risk. The ETO keeps sufficient spares of every fuse type in use (fast/time-delay, HRC, semiconductor fuse). Relays, sensors (pressure, temperature, level, current transformer) and connectors are also stocked according to criticality.
ETO, sigorta ve koruma elemanlarının asl: The ETO applies the principle that fuses and protective devices are never "bridged with a higher rating"; when the correct spare is not available, temporary bridging can cause fire and equipment damage. For connectors, keeping spares is particularly important because of corrosion in the marine environment.
Gemi Planlı Bakım Sistemi (PMS) yazılımı: The ship's Planned Maintenance System (PMS) software (AMOS, TM Master, ShipManager, etc.) manages the spare parts linked to each item of equipment, the stock levels and the order status. The ETO updates the stock when a part is used; when the reorder point is reached, the system creates a requisition. Correct, up-to-date records ensure that the stock on record agrees with the physical count.
ETO, periyodik fiziksel stok sayımı yapa: The ETO verifies that the system agrees with the physical stock by carrying out periodic physical stock counts; discrepancies (parts used but not deducted, or stored in the wrong place) are corrected. Part storage codes (shelf/cabinet numbers) are critical for quick access in an emergency.
Yedek parça siparişi, tedarik süresini (: Spare part orders allow for the lead time and the ship's itinerary; on long voyages, deliveries must be timed to coincide with port calls. The ETO marks critical orders as priority, checks parts on receipt (correct part, damage, certificate) and stores them under suitable conditions.
Kalibrasyon, bir ölçüm cihazının çıktısı: Calibration is the comparison of the output of a measuring instrument with a known reference standard to determine its deviation. A wrongly calibrated pressure sensor or gas detector leads to wrong decisions and safety risks. The ETO ensures that calibration is traceable to national/international standards; the certificate documents this chain of traceability.
ETO uhdesindeki birçok cihaz periyodik k: Many instruments in the ETO's charge require periodic calibration: gas detectors (oxygen, LEL, H2S, CO), pressure/temperature/level transmitters, tachometers, tank radar/gauging, draft sensors, multimeters and test instruments, the oily water separator 15 ppm bilge alarm and emissions monitoring equipment. Each has a different calibration interval.
ETO, tüm kalibrasyon gerektiren cihazlar: The ETO keeps an inventory of all instruments requiring calibration, with their last/next calibration dates, in the PMS. The system automatically warns of upcoming calibrations; the ETO plans calibrations allowing for the ship's itinerary and the availability of service providers. An overdue calibration results in a finding at inspections and calls the validity of the measurements into question.
Bazı kalibrasyonlar gemide (gaz dedektör: Some calibrations can be done on board (gas detector bump test/calibration, multimeter comparison), while others require a certified external service or a shore laboratory. For those that can be done on board, the ETO stocks calibrators/reference gas cylinders and also keeps track of their expiry dates.
Kalibrasyon sertifikaları, denetimlerde: Calibration certificates are requested at inspections (class, PSC, company); the ETO keeps them in an orderly, accessible and up-to-date file (digital and/or printed). Each certificate is matched to its instrument; the certificate number and the calibration and expiry dates are recorded. A missing or expired certificate is assessed negatively at an inspection.
ETO'nun doğru ve güvenilir ölçüm aletler: Having accurate and reliable measuring instruments is fundamental to the ETO's work: a digital multimeter, clamp meter, megger (insulation tester), voltage detector, thermal camera, cable/continuity tester and, where necessary, a secondary injection test set. The accuracy of these instruments is critical for both safety and fault diagnosis.
Test cihazları da bakım ve doğrulama ger: Test instruments also need maintenance and verification: multimeter probes and fuses, the megger battery and the prove-test function of the voltage detector are checked regularly. For critical measurements, the ETO increases confidence by cross-checking with two independent instruments (especially when proving absence of voltage).
Yedek parça ve kalibrasyon yönetimi, kri: Spare parts and calibration management is a discipline built up on quiet days, not in a crisis: when the right part is ready at the right moment, a breakdown is resolved within hours, whereas missing stock stretches the same breakdown over days. The ETO's success in this area is measured by short unplanned downtime, clean spares/calibration records at inspections and the reliability of every measurement.
Mekanik soğutma çevrimi dört temel bileş: The mechanical refrigeration cycle is based on four basic components: the compressor (compresses the gas), the condenser (rejects heat and liquefies the gas), the expansion valve (reduces the pressure) and the evaporator (absorbs heat and provides cooling). The ETO manages the electrical control (compressor motor, fan motors, valve solenoids, sensors) and the safety devices of this cycle.
Gemide tipik soğutma uygulamaları: provi: Typical shipboard refrigeration applications are: the provision plant (provision cold rooms), accommodation air conditioning (accommodation HVAC), engine room/control room ventilation and cargo refrigeration on reefer ships. The ETO must know the set temperatures, alarm limits and control logic of each system.
Soğutucu akışkanlar (refrigerant) çevre: Refrigerants are subject to environmental regulations. The Montreal Protocol has phased out ozone-depleting substances such as CFCs/HCFCs, while the F-gas Regulation and the Kigali Amendment are reducing HFCs with a high global warming potential. As a legal requirement, the ETO keeps track of the refrigerant types on board, the leak records and that charging is carried out by licensed persons.
Soğutma kompresörü motoru, sistemin en y: The refrigeration compressor motor is the largest electrical load in the system. The ETO monitors the motor current (balance of the three phases), voltage and operating temperature; unbalanced current indicates a phase problem or a mechanical problem. In hermetic/semi-hermetic compressors the motor is cooled by the refrigerant gas, so a low charge can overheat the motor.
ETO, kompresör motorunun yalıtım direnci: The ETO periodically measures the insulation resistance of the compressor motor (megger); in hermetic compressors, breakdown of the winding insulation, which is in contact with the refrigerant, leads to acid formation and contamination of the system. The motor protection relays (overload, phase loss, motor temperature thermistor) are correctly set.
Kompresör, yüksek basınç (HP) ve düşük b: The compressor is protected by high-pressure (HP) and low-pressure (LP) pressure switches. The HP cut-out stops the compressor on excessive pressure caused by a fouled condenser or insufficient cooling water; the LP cut-out prevents operation with a low charge or a clogged filter. The ETO periodically tests the setpoints of these pressure switches and that they trip correctly.
Yağ basınç emniyet presostatı (oil press: The oil pressure safety switch (oil pressure differential) monitors whether compressor lubrication is adequate and stops the compressor on insufficient oil pressure. The ETO checks the time delay and trip value of this safety device; a disabled oil safety switch can lead to compressor seizure.
Kondenser, deniz suyu (shell&tube) veya: The condenser is cooled by seawater (shell&tube) or by air (fan). The ETO checks that the fan motors of air-cooled condensers are working and, in seawater-cooled systems, the condition of the cooling water circulating pump and of the flow monitoring. Insufficient cooling leads to high discharge pressure and HP trips.
Evaporatör yüzeyinde nem yoğuşur ve düşü: Moisture condenses on the evaporator surface and frost forms at low temperature; this reduces heat transfer. The ETO checks that the defrost system (electric heater, hot gas or off-cycle) works correctly, that the defrost timer/thermostat is set and the insulation of the defrost heater circuits. A faulty defrost turns the evaporator into a block of ice and stops refrigeration.
ETO, evaporatör fan motorlarının çalışma: The ETO verifies that the evaporator fan motors are working and that the defrost termination thermostat ends the defrost correctly. Too long or incomplete defrosting causes excessive icing, water overflow or unnecessary energy consumption.
Her soğutma mahalli, set sıcaklığını kor: Each refrigerated space is controlled by a thermostat (mechanical or electronic) that maintains the set temperature. The ETO checks the thermostat's accuracy against a calibrated reference thermometer; a drifting thermostat causes either unnecessary cooling (wasted energy) or insufficient cooling (spoiled food). On electronic controllers, the sensors (PT100/NTC) and parameter settings are checked.
Solenoid valfler, refrigerant akışını el: Solenoid valves open and close the refrigerant flow electrically; the liquid line solenoid closes when the thermostat is satisfied, and the system stops the compressor safely by pump-down. The ETO checks the condition of the solenoid coils, the sound of the valve opening/closing and its tightness. A stuck solenoid leads to loss of control and compressor short cycling.
ETO, sistemin emme (suction) ve basma (d: The ETO monitors the system's suction and discharge pressures; these give information on the state of charge and the health of the system. Low suction pressure indicates a low charge or a restriction; high discharge pressure indicates a condenser problem. Bubbles in the sight glass are a sign of a low charge or moisture (saturated drier).
Refrigerant kaçağı hem performans kaybı: A refrigerant leak means both a loss of performance and an environmental/legal problem. The ETO finds leak points with an electronic leak detector or a soap bubble test and keeps the leak/charging records as required by regulations. Charging and repairs are carried out by a licensed technician with recovery equipment; refrigerant is not released to the atmosphere.
Reefer (refrigerated) konteynerler, gemi: Reefer (refrigerated) containers are supplied from the ship's network (usually 440 V 60 Hz) through reefer sockets, and each has its own refrigeration unit. The ETO ensures the condition of the reefer socket panels, the reliability of the supply and that the set/actual temperature of each container is monitored from the central monitoring system. A temperature deviation alarm on sensitive cargo requires immediate action.
ETO, reefer plug'lardaki bağlantı bütünl: The ETO checks the reefer plugs for connection integrity and corrosion; in the marine environment, a loose/corroded socket causes faults and heating. The total electrical demand of the reefer load is included in the PMS power balance; a large number of reefers significantly increases the generator load.
Bir reefer ünitesi arızalandığında ETO,: When a reefer unit fails, the ETO assesses the alarm priority (sensitivity of the cargo), rules out a supply/socket problem and, if necessary, diagnoses the fault inside the unit (compressor, fan, control). For critical cargo, transfer to a spare socket/container or a rapid repair is required; every incident is recorded.
Soğutma sistemleri, yüksek/düşük sıcaklı: Refrigeration systems are fitted with high/low temperature, pressure and compressor failure alarms; these alarms are relayed to the bridge/control room. The ETO verifies (by testing) that the alarm circuits and sensors work correctly, that the alarm setpoints are appropriate and that the alarm actually gets through. A silenced or bypassed alarm can lead to loss of cargo/food.
Soğutma ve iklimlendirme bakımı, gıda gü: Refrigeration and air conditioning maintenance has a wide impact, from food safety to cargo value and crew comfort. The ETO's success with these systems is measured by reliable compressor operation, alarms that genuinely protect, refrigerant leaks managed with legal discipline and energy that is not wasted. Thanks to the ETO's careful maintenance, these unseen but continuously running cycles quietly keep the ship cool.
VSAT sistemi; stabilize bir anten (ADE -: A VSAT system consists of a stabilized antenna (ADE - Above Deck Equipment), cabling, a modem (BDE - Below Deck Equipment), a router and switches connecting to the ship's network. The satellite link uses Ku-band or Ka-band; Ka-band offers higher speeds but is more susceptible to rain fade. The ETO knows the band in use, the hub/teleport and the service plan.
Anten, geminin yalpa/baş-kıç vurması (pi: To remain pointed at the satellite during the ship's rolling, pitching and yawing motions, the antenna has a stabilization system (gyro/sensor based) and a satellite tracking mechanism. The ETO monitors the antenna pointing accuracy, the blockage zones (shadow of the funnel/mast) and the skew/polarization setting.
ETO, link sağlığını anahtar metriklerle: The ETO monitors link health with key metrics: signal strength, SNR/Es/No (signal-to-noise ratio), Tx/Rx data rate and packet loss. A falling SNR indicates antenna pointing drift, weather (rain fade), blockage or a hub problem. These metrics are followed on the modem web interface and the service provider's portal.
Anten stabilizasyonu; jiroskoplar/IMU, m: Antenna stabilization compensates for ship motion by means of gyroscopes/IMU, motors (azimuth, elevation, cross-level) and a control board. The ETO checks the condition of the motors and belts/gears, the gyro/sensor calibration and that the antenna tracks the satellite without losing it. A worn belt or a faulty motor leads to loss of signal when the ship is moving.
Antenin radome (koruyucu kubbe) bütünlüğ: The integrity of the antenna radome (protective dome) is critical; a cracked or leaking radome lets in moisture and salt, leading to corrosion of the electronics and loss of signal. The ETO periodically checks the radome gaskets and bolts and the humidity inside the dome (desiccant/heater, if fitted).
ADE-BDE arası RF/IF kabloları ve konnekt: The RF/IF cables and connectors between ADE and BDE can cause signal loss (insertion loss) due to corrosion and moisture in the marine environment. The ETO checks the connector joints, their weatherproofing and the integrity of the cables. A corroded connector is a common and often overlooked cause of gradual signal degradation.
Modem, uydu link'ini kurar ve IP trafiği: The modem establishes the satellite link and manages IP traffic; its configuration (satellite/transponder settings, IP plan, QoS) is provided by the service provider. The ETO backs up the modem configuration, applies firmware updates in a controlled manner and uses the modem logs for fault diagnosis. A wrong configuration leads to loss of the link.
Gemi router'ı; operasyonel trafiği (köpr: The ship's router separates operational traffic (bridge, engine, company) from crew internet and prioritizes the limited satellite bandwidth with QoS (Quality of Service). The ETO ensures that critical operational traffic (reporting, navigation data, e-mail) is given priority over crew traffic and that bandwidth quotas are applied.
Güvenli bir gemi ağı, fonksiyonlara göre: A secure ship network is divided into segments (VLANs) by function: OT (bridge/engine control), operational IT (company/administrative), the crew welfare network and the guest/passenger network. The ETO ensures that these segments are isolated from each other and that traffic between them is controlled by firewall rules. A flat network allows a breach in one zone to spread to the whole ship.
WLAN (kablosuz ağ), kapsama ve güvenlik: A WLAN (wireless network) requires a balance between coverage and security. The ETO applies strong encryption (WPA2/WPA3), strong passwords, hidden/separate SSIDs and guest network isolation. Access point firmware is kept up to date and scans are carried out for unauthorized devices/access points (rogue APs).
IMO Resolution MSC.428(98) ile geminin G: Under IMO Resolution MSC.428(98), the ship's Safety Management System (SMS) must address cyber risk management; MSC-FAL.1/Circ.3 recommends the identify-protect-detect-respond-recover framework. The ETO implements the technical cyber controls on board: access control, update management, monitoring and incident response.
Taşınabilir medya (USB), gemiye zararlı: Removable media (USB) are the most common route for malware to enter the ship; service technicians' laptops and chart update media are particularly risky. The ETO restricts USB use by policy, applies scanning with a kiosk/scanner and blocks unauthorized media on OT systems. Firmware/software updates are applied in a controlled manner, from a verified source and, where possible, after testing.
ETO, kritik sistemlerin yedeklerini (kon: The ETO regularly backs up critical systems (configurations, ECDIS charts, automation parameters); up-to-date backups are the key to rapid recovery after a cyber incident or failure. Backups are kept off the network (offline) so that they are not affected by ransomware.
VSAT bir konfor/operasyonel sistem olsa: Although VSAT is a comfort/operational system, GMDSS (safety of life communications) is a separate, mandatory and class-approved system. The ETO ensures that VSAT maintenance does not affect GMDSS; formal maintenance of GMDSS equipment is usually the responsibility of the radio operator/a certified service, but the ETO provides support with the power supply and antenna infrastructure. The boundaries between the two systems are kept clear.
Bir bağlantı kesintisinde ETO, sorunu ka: In a connection outage, the ETO narrows down the problem layer by layer: is it the user device, the ship network/switch, the router/firewall, the modem or the satellite link (antenna/weather/hub)? The fault is located using ping/traceroute, the modem signal indicators and the service portal. A systematic approach avoids unnecessary intervention and service costs.
Uydu hub'ı, beam tahsisi veya hesap soru: Problems with the satellite hub, beam allocation or the service subscription are outside the ship's control; in these cases the ETO works in coordination with the service provider. The ETO clearly reports the signal values, logs and the steps taken; this speeds up remote diagnosis. If necessary, the modem configuration is updated together with remote support.
VSAT ve ağ yönetimi, ETO'nun rolünü gele: VSAT and network management is the area that extends the ETO's role from traditional electrical work to modern IT/cyber security. Success is measured by uninterrupted operational connectivity, a ship network whose confidentiality and integrity are protected, and robust segmentation that limits the impact of a cyber incident. By keeping this invisible infrastructure healthy, the ETO safeguards both the ship's link with the world and the security of critical control systems.
Stajyer köprüüstüne çıktığında ilk yapma: When the cadet comes onto the bridge, the first thing to do is to tell the OOW why they are there and make clear whether they are present as an "extra lookout" or for "training". When navigating in darkness, the cadet follows the red lighting rules and "lookout" discipline so as not to impair the OOW's night vision. Following the taking-over and handing-over (handover) process from start to finish is the basis for the cadet learning the watchkeeping culture.
Stajyer, her vardiyadan önce Kaptan'ın S: Before each watch, the cadet must read the Master's Standing Orders and the Night Order Book. These documents contain critical instructions such as the minimum passing distance (CPA), when the Master is to be called and under what conditions the engine is to be put on standby. The cadet confirms having read these orders by signing them and observes how the OOW makes decisions within the framework of these orders.
Kaptanı çağırma kriterleri (calling the: The criteria for calling the Master are one of the most important lists a cadet must memorize: the Master is called immediately when visibility falls below a set limit, when traffic density increases, when there is doubt about the navigation, in the event of equipment failure or when the specified CPA cannot be maintained. The cadet internalizes the principle that "if in doubt, call the Master" is never a weakness but a professional reflex.
Stajyer, radarın temel kontrollerini OOW: Under the OOW's supervision, the cadet learns the basic radar controls: gain, sea clutter (STC), rain clutter (FTC), tuning, range scale selection and use of the EBL/VRM (Electronic Bearing Line / Variable Range Marker). The cadet sees in practice that a wrongly adjusted radar can suppress real targets or create interference. The cadet grasps the discipline of changing range: long ranges to watch the overall traffic picture and short ranges to watch close-in dangers.
Head-up, course-up ve north-up gösterim: The head-up, course-up and north-up display modes and the difference between relative motion and true motion are concepts the cadet must understand clearly. The cadet learns how own ship's and the targets' true movements appear in north-up + true motion mode, and how risk of collision is more easily assessed in relative motion mode.
ARPA (Automatic Radar Plotting Aid), hed: ARPA (Automatic Radar Plotting Aid) tracks targets automatically and calculates their CPA (Closest Point of Approach) and TCPA (Time to CPA). The cadet learns that after a target is acquired, the ARPA vector solution needs time to stabilize; the data from the first few minutes must not be trusted blindly. The cadet observes how the OOW uses the trial maneuver function to test how a course/speed change will affect the traffic.
Stajyer, ARPA'nın bir karar verici değil: The cadet must understand that ARPA is not a decision-maker but a decision-support tool. ARPA can lose track of a target (target swap), may not fully acquire small craft and may give delayed data on targets maneuvering in narrow waters. ARPA data is therefore always cross-checked by visual observation and conventional radar plotting.
ECDIS (Electronic Chart Display and Info: ECDIS (Electronic Chart Display and Information System) is the approved electronic navigation system that replaces the paper chart. The cadet learns what the safety contour, safety depth, shallow/deep contour and safety frame (look-ahead) settings mean and how they are determined. A wrongly set safety contour can cause the shallow water warning to come too late; these settings are therefore made according to the ship's draft and the UKC (Under Keel Clearance) policy.
Stajyer, ENC (Electronic Navigational Ch: The cadet learns the difference between ENCs (Electronic Navigational Charts) and raster charts, the importance of scale selection (overscale/underscale warnings) and how to use the "chart 1" symbol library. Together with the OOW, the cadet follows how the route planning, route check and route monitoring modes work on ECDIS.
ECDIS, cross-track error, anchor watch,: ECDIS generates many alarms, such as cross-track error, anchor watch, safety contour crossing and dangerous target. The cadet learns that none of these alarms should be muted or routinely "acknowledged"; every alarm has a reason. Accidents caused by over-reliance on ECDIS hold an important place in maritime history.
Stajyer, ECDIS'in tek başına yeterli olm: The cadet internalizes that ECDIS alone is not sufficient and that the position must be verified from independent sources (visual bearings, radar ranges, a second GNSS). Timely application of ECDIS updates (ENC updates) and checking the accuracy of the sensor inputs (GPS, gyro, log) are also among the daily routines the cadet must observe.
AIS (Automatic Identification System), d: AIS (Automatic Identification System) broadcasts the identity, position, course, speed and maneuvering information of other ships. The cadet learns to read the MMSI, ship name, type and CPA/TCPA information of an AIS target. However, the cadet also understands that AIS can never be used on its own for collision avoidance: not all targets carry AIS, AIS data may have been entered incorrectly and AIS may update with a delay. COLREG Rule 7 requires the assessment of risk of collision to be based on radar/ARPA; AIS supplements this.
Stajyer, AIS hedef bilgisinin radar hede: The cadet observes how AIS target information is associated with the radar target (AIS-radar association) and how the OOW cross-checks these two sources. The benefits and risks of communicating by VHF with a ship whose maneuvering intentions are unclear (the VHF-assisted collision trap) are also discussed at this stage.
Stajyer; gyro pusula ile manyetik pusula: The cadet learns the difference between the gyro compass and the magnetic compass, the concepts of gyro error and compass error (deviation + variation), and how compass error is found by azimuth/transit. Reading the speed log (speed), the echo sounder (depth of water) and the rate of turn indicator is also part of bridge awareness.
GMDSS (Global Maritime Distress and Safe: The cadet is introduced to the GMDSS (Global Maritime Distress and Safety System) equipment — VHF DSC, MF/HF, EPIRB, SART, NAVTEX. The cadet learns that sending a distress alert by accident (false alert) has serious consequences and does not touch this equipment without authorization, but grasps the logic of GMDSS by observing the flow of alerts and messages.
Stajyer, pozisyon belirlemenin (fixing): The cadet practices several methods of position fixing: the visual three-bearing fix, radar range + bearing, transits (leading lines) and dead reckoning (DR) / estimated position (EP) calculation. The cadet learns that the size of the "cocked hat" triangle formed by three bearings shows the quality of the fix; a small triangle means a good fix, while a large triangle means a source of error (gyro error, wrong identification of an object).
Açık denizde fix aralığı seyrek olabilir: In the open sea, fixes may be taken at long intervals, while close to the coast and in narrow waters the frequency of fixes increases. The cadet understands the importance of fixing the position every few minutes in coastal navigation, of the parallel indexing technique and of using clearing bearings/clearing ranges. Recording every position with its time in the deck logbook and on the chart (or in ECDIS) is a basic discipline.
Stajyerin en değerli öğrenme aracı, kend: The cadet's most valuable learning tool is recognizing their own plotting errors. Wrong identification of an object, parallax error, ignoring gyro error and a wrong time stamp are the most common errors. The OOW reviews the cadet's fixes and gives feedback; the cadet notes this feedback in the Training Record Book.
Stajyer, \"vessels in sight of one anoth: The cadet understands that the rules for "vessels in sight of one another" (Part B Section II) and for "restricted visibility" (Rule 19) are different. In restricted visibility there is no stand-on/give-way distinction; every ship proceeds at a safe speed and takes action to avoid collision based on radar plotting. The cadet also learns the rules for narrow channels (Rule 9) and traffic separation schemes (Rule 10) and the priorities of vessels restricted in their ability to maneuver/not under command (Rule 18).
Seyir jurnali, geminin resmi ve hukuki k: The deck logbook is the ship's official and legal record; it has evidential value in court. The cadet learns what information is entered in the deck logbook: positions, course and speed changes, weather and sea state, visibility, significant points passed, engine orders, drills and unusual events. The bell book (course and engine movement book), kept during maneuvering and pilotage, contains a record of all helm and engine orders accurate to the second.
Stajyer, kayıtların gerçek zamanlı, okun: The cadet learns that entries must be made in real time, legibly and in permanent ink, and that corrections are made by striking through (never by erasing or scribbling out). False or subsequently altered entries have serious disciplinary and legal consequences. This discipline is the foundation of the cadet's credibility as a seafarer.
Stajyer, VDR (Voyage Data Recorder) ve S: The cadet learns that the VDR (Voyage Data Recorder) and S-VDR continuously record bridge audio, the radar/ECDIS display, helm/engine orders and sensor data. After an incident, the VDR data must be preserved (save/preserve button). Consistency between the manual logbook and the electronic records is key to the legal protection of the ship and crew.
Yoğun trafikte stajyer, OOW'nin tüm hede: In heavy traffic, the cadet observes how the OOW manages the simultaneous assessment of all targets. Priority is given to the target with the smallest CPA/TCPA and the fastest approach. The cadet learns not to fixate on a single target (target fixation) and lose the "big picture"; the whole horizon and all radar ranges must be scanned periodically.
Durum farkındalığı (situational awarenes: Situational awareness has three levels: perception, comprehension and projection of the future. The cadet learns to project mentally how the current traffic situation will develop over the next few minutes. The cadet also recognizes how fatigue, monotony and distraction degrade this awareness.
BRM (Bridge Resource Management), köprüü: BRM (Bridge Resource Management) is the effective use of all human and technical resources on the bridge. The cadet observes how orders given to the helmsman are repeated (closed-loop communication: "Starboard ten" → "Starboard ten" → "Ten of starboard wheel on") and learns how this discipline prevents misunderstandings. The cadet learns to report a hazard they have noticed to the OOW clearly and without hesitation (challenge and response); hierarchy must not prevent safety information from being shared.
Köprüüstü vardiyasında kazanılan her bec: Every skill gained on bridge watch is entered against the relevant STCW competence item in the Training Record Book: taking fixes, radar plotting, applying COLREG, using ECDIS, keeping the log, etc. After each task, the cadet obtains the signature and assessment of the training officer. These records are the main evidence for a future application for the OICNW certificate of competency.
Stajyer, öğrendiği her cihaz ve prosedür: The cadet should also keep personal notes on every item of equipment and every procedure learned: the make/model of the equipment, its particular settings, ship-specific procedures and problems encountered. This personal "bridge familiarisation" notebook becomes invaluable when joining the next ship and when preparing for the certificate examination.
Etkili eğitim, düzenli geri bildirimle o: Effective training depends on regular feedback. The cadet accepts feedback from the OOW and the Master without becoming defensive and applies it on the next watch. Mistakes (a wrong fix, a late maneuver proposal, an incomplete record) are learning opportunities; what matters is not repeating the same mistake.
Köprüüstü vardiyasına eğitim amaçlı katı: Taking part in the bridge watch for training is the most critical stage at which the deck cadet turns into a future officer of the watch. Here the cadet acquires technical skill, regulatory knowledge and, most importantly, professional discipline together. Having no authority for independent decisions is not a restriction but a privilege: learning free from the pressure of mistakes and responsibility. Making the best use of this privilege through constant observation, asking questions and careful record-keeping is the cadet's own responsibility.
Modern seyir planlaması IMO A.893(21) il: Modern passage planning is defined by IMO A.893(21) in four stages: Appraisal, Planning, Execution and Monitoring. In the appraisal stage all relevant information is gathered; in the planning stage the detailed route is laid down; execution is the ship carrying out the plan, and monitoring is the continuous checking of adherence to the plan. The cadet supports the Second Officer especially in the first two stages (appraisal and planning) by collecting data and making preliminary plots.
Stajyer, seyir planının \"berth to berth: The cadet understands that the passage plan must be made "berth to berth"; planning covers not only the open sea but also the pilotage area, the anchorage, the maneuvering area and the berth. The plan is prepared allowing for the ship's draft, maneuvering characteristics, the weather forecast and ECDIS/paper chart coverage.
Stajyer; harita düzeltmelerini yapar, NA: The cadet makes chart corrections, processes NAVTEX/NtM records, drafts distance and course calculations and prepares UKC tables. However, all of this work is checked by the Second Officer and the final plan is approved by the Master. The cadet never forgets that everything they do in the planning process is the work "of a student under training, not of an independent professional".
Stajyer, planlama sırasında karşılaştığı: The cadet must ask the Second Officer without hesitation about any uncertainty met during planning (for example, how an NtM is to be applied to the chart, or the turning radius at a waypoint). A single wrongly applied correction or an overlooked danger can turn into a real navigational risk; the discipline of "if I am not sure, I ask" is therefore vital.
Appraisal aşamasında stajyer, gerekli tü: In the appraisal stage, the cadet helps to check that all required nautical publications are on board and up to date: the relevant charts (paper/ENC), Sailing Directions (Pilot Books), List of Lights, List of Radio Signals, Tide Tables, Tidal Stream Atlas, Ocean Passages for the World and Routeing Charts. The charts required are determined from the Admiralty NP Catalogue or the ECDIS chart catalogue.
Stajyer, açık deniz geçişleri için \"gre: For ocean passages, the cadet learns the difference between "great circle" and "rhumb line" tracks; over long distances the great circle is shorter, but it requires a course alteration on each segment. Ocean Passages for the World and climatological routeing charts give information on seasonal winds, currents, ice limits and tropical storm areas; the cadet learns to read them.
Stajyer, hava tahmini kaynaklarını (NAVT: The cadet learns to follow weather forecast sources (NAVTEX weather bulletins, weather routing service, GMDSS MSI) and to reflect seasonal hazards (tropical cyclone season, ice limits, fog areas) in the plan. Currents and tides determine the timing of transits, especially in narrow passages and port approaches; calculating the "tidal window" is a critical skill the cadet must learn.
Stajyer ayrıca yasal ve fiziksel kısıtla: The cadet also helps to assess legal and physical constraints: TSS (Traffic Separation Schemes), ECA (Emission Control Areas), VTS reporting lines, military/fishing areas, depth restrictions and compulsory pilotage in canals/straits. This information is compiled in the appraisal stage and incorporated into the route in the planning stage.
Kağıt haritalar, haftalık yayımlanan Adm: Paper charts are kept up to date with the weekly Admiralty Notices to Mariners. The cadet learns how to read NtMs, which chart they affect and how the correction is applied to the chart (in violet ink, with the NtM number written in the margin). T&P (Temporary & Preliminary) notices are kept in a separate file and announce temporary changes (for example, a light temporarily out of service).
Her haritanın sol alt köşesindeki \"Smal: The last NtM number entered on the "Small Corrections" line in the bottom left-hand corner of each chart shows up to which date the chart is corrected. The cadet learns to check this line before using a chart for navigation and to complete any missing corrections. The cadet understands that for larger changes made by block correction (tracing), the tracing must be pasted onto the chart in exact alignment.
ECDIS kullanan gemilerde ENC (Electronic: On ships using ECDIS, ENC (Electronic Navigational Chart) updates are applied from the weekly update CD/DVD or an online service (e.g. AVCS). The cadet observes the ENC update loading process, base/permit management and how the update status (chart status) is verified. Although electronic updating is faster than manual correction, confirmation that the update has loaded successfully must not be skipped.
Stajyer, kağıt ve elektronik harita düze: The cadet learns that paper and electronic chart correction records (Chart Correction Log — NP133A or its electronic equivalent) are kept meticulously. This record is the official proof of the NtM up to which each chart is corrected and is frequently checked during inspections.
NAVTEX (Navigational Telex), GMDSS kapsa: NAVTEX (Navigational Telex) is an automatic system within the GMDSS that broadcasts MSI (Maritime Safety Information) on 518 kHz (international, in English), 490 kHz (national language) and 4209.5 kHz. The cadet learns the B1-B4 character coding of NAVTEX messages: B1 is the station identity, B2 the message type (A=navigational warning, B=meteorological warning, D=SAR, etc.), and B3-B4 the message serial number.
Stajyer, A, B ve D tipi mesajların (seyi: The cadet learns that message types A, B and D (navigational warnings, meteorological warnings, SAR) can never be disabled on the receiver; these messages are safety-critical. Reviewing incoming messages and reflecting the relevant ones in the plan or on the chart (for example, a temporary obstruction, a wreck or a drill area) is one of the routines the cadet supports.
Dünya, MSI yayını için 21 NAVAREA/METARE: For MSI broadcasts, the world is divided into 21 NAVAREAs/METAREAs; each area has a responsible coordinator country. On ocean passages, once outside NAVTEX range, MSI is received via Inmarsat-C SafetyNET (EGC). The cadet learns which method is used to receive warnings in which area and how the receiver is set up for the areas being transited.
Stajyer, alınan ve işlenen seyir uyarıla: The cadet observes that navigational warnings received and acted on are recorded. Relevant warnings are noted in the passage plan and plotted on the appropriate chart, and expired warnings are filed. This discipline keeps planning synchronized with the real-time flow of information.
Rota, ardışık waypoint'ler (dönüş noktal: A route consists of successive waypoints (turning points) and the legs joining them. For each leg, the cadet learns to calculate the course, distance, planned speed and estimated time on the leg. Calculating the ETA (Estimated Time of Arrival) from the total distance and the average speed is critical for charterer reporting and the tidal window.
Stajyer, waypoint'lerin güvenli yerlere: The cadet learns that waypoints must be placed in safe positions: turns are planned clear of dangers, in sufficient depth of water and to suit the ship's turning radius (turning circle / wheel-over point). The wheel-over point is the point at which the rudder must be put over and comes before the waypoint itself; it is calculated allowing for the ship's turning diameter.
Her leg için XTD (Cross-Track Distance /: For each leg, the XTD (Cross-Track Distance / cross-track limit) is the limit of how far the ship may stray from the planned track; ECDIS gives an alarm when this limit is exceeded. The cadet learns that XTD is kept small in narrow waters (e.g. 0.1 NM) and wider in the open sea. XTD defines a safe corridor around the track, clear of no-go areas.
Stajyer, kıyı seyrinde radar ile rota iz: The cadet learns how the parallel indexing technique for monitoring the track by radar in coastal navigation, and clearing bearings/clearing ranges, are prepared in the planning stage. These auxiliary lines make it possible to notice quickly when the ship deviates from the planned track and form the basis of the monitoring stage.
UKC (Under Keel Clearance), geminin omur: UKC (Under Keel Clearance) is the net distance between the ship's keel and the seabed. The cadet learns the components of the UKC calculation: charted depth, height of tide, the ship's static draft, squat (sinkage due to motion), the effect of heel/list and the wave allowance. The company SMS usually specifies a minimum UKC allowance (e.g. 10% of the draft in the open sea, a specified number of meters in a channel).
Stajyer, charted depth'in chart datum'a: The cadet understands that charted depth is given relative to chart datum (usually LAT — Lowest Astronomical Tide) and that the height of tide at the time must be added to obtain the actual depth of water. The height of tide is found from the Tide Tables and, for intermediate times, by the "rule of twelfths" or algebraic interpolation. The cadet learns to do this calculation in practice.
Squat, geminin hareket halinde sular alt: Squat is the ship sinking deeper and changing trim when underway, because of the drop in pressure it creates beneath it. Squat increases in proportion to the square of speed and becomes significant particularly in shallow water and in narrow channels (blockage factor). The cadet learns the empirical squat formulae (e.g. the Barrass formula) and their relationship with the block coefficient (Cb).
Stajyer, squat'ın geminin baş veya kıç t: The cadet learns that squat may be greater at the bow or at the stern (usually by the head in full-form ships with a high Cb), and that the point of minimum UKC at the shallowest point must therefore be allowed for. The most practical way to reduce squat is to reduce speed; this is a basic safety measure in shallow water transits.
Stajyer, INT/Admiralty harita sembolleri: The cadet learns to use "Chart 5011 — Symbols and Abbreviations Used on Admiralty Charts", which explains INT/Admiralty chart symbols. Depth figures, the low-water line (drying heights, underlined figures), wrecks (wreck symbols and the dangerous/non-dangerous distinction), rocks, buoys (IALA buoyage Regions A/B), light characteristics and danger symbols are learned from this publication.
Stajyer, IALA buoyage sistemindeki A ve: The cadet understands the basic difference between IALA buoyage Regions A and B (the red/green sides of lateral marks are reversed). Memorizing the meanings and light characteristics of lateral, cardinal, isolated danger, safe water and special marks is a basic competence for both planning and watchkeeping.
ECDIS'te ENC sembolleri IHO S-52 standar: In ECDIS, ENC symbols are displayed in accordance with the IHO S-52 standard; the cadet learns the difference between the base/standard/all display modes and that the SCAMIN (Scale Minimum) attribute can hide some objects at certain scales. A suitable display setting is critical so that important objects are not missed because of the scale selected.
Stajyer, ECDIS üzerinde overscale (harit: The cadet understands the meaning of the overscale (zooming in on a chart beyond its own scale) and underscale warnings in ECDIS. Information displayed when overscaled can be misleading; the ENC of the appropriate scale (closest to the compilation scale) must therefore always be used. This awareness is an important part of checking the plan.
Tamamlanan passage plan, gemi formatına: The completed passage plan is entered on a form in the ship's format: waypoint list, leg parameters, no-go areas, reporting points (VTS/coast guard), pilot boarding position, anchorage, critical UKC points, abort point and contingency (alternative) plans. The cadet learns that the plan must be complete "berth to berth", with no stage left blank.
Hazırlanan plan önce İkinci Zabit tarafı: The prepared plan is first reviewed by the Second Officer; the cadet's calculations, chart corrections and waypoints are checked. The plan is then submitted to the Master; until the Master approves it, the plan remains a "draft". The whole bridge team holds a briefing on the plan before the voyage; by attending this briefing, the cadet grasps the plan as a whole.
Stajyer, planın yalnızca bir kağıt çalış: The cadet learns that the plan is not merely paperwork but a "shared mental model" held by the ship's whole bridge team. The plan is the constant reference during the monitoring stage; if actual conditions invalidate the plan (weather, traffic, breakdown), the plan is revised in a controlled manner and the revision is recorded.
Seyir planlamasına destek, güverte stajy: Supporting passage planning is one of the most valuable areas of training on the deck cadet's way to becoming a future navigating officer. Here the cadet learns not only to correct charts or calculate waypoints, but to think holistically "berth to berth", to foresee danger and to document with discipline. The plan produced at the end of this process is the written guarantee of the ship's safe navigation; the cadet's contribution to building this guarantee is a sign of both technical and professional maturity.
Stajyer, güverte operasyonlarına bağımsı: The cadet takes part in deck operations not as an independent crew member but under supervision, for support and training. Before every job, the officer in charge or the Bosun gives a job briefing (toolbox talk); in this briefing the cadet learns their role, the stop points and the emergency exit. The cadet never carries out an order they do not understand; when in doubt, they ask.
Stajyer, kişisel koruyucu donanımı (PPE): The cadet wears full personal protective equipment (PPE): safety helmet, steel-toecap safety boots, gloves, safety glasses and, where necessary, a lifejacket/safety harness. For overside work and work at height, a safety harness and a lifeline are mandatory. Behavior that could distract attention during the task is avoided; a moment's inattention during a deck operation can cause serious injury.
Her güverte operasyonu öncesinde, ISM/SM: Before every deck operation, a risk assessment is carried out as required by ISM/SMS; by taking part in this process, the cadet learns to recognize hazards and the control measures taken. A Permit to Work (PTW) is also issued for work such as hot work, enclosed space entry, work at height and overside work. The cadet observes why a PTW is needed, which signatures are obtained and why the validity of the permit is time-limited.
Stajyer, \"stop work authority\" (işi du: The cadet learns the concept of "stop work authority": every person on board can stop a job they consider unsafe and cannot be penalized for doing so. The cadet too must not hesitate to speak up on noticing a hazard; this is not weakness but professionalism.
Stajyer; doğal lif halatlar, sentetik ha: The cadet learns the properties of natural fiber ropes, synthetic ropes (polypropylene, polyester, nylon, HMPE) and steel wire ropes. Each material has different stretch, floating and breaking behavior; for example, because of its high elongation, nylon snaps back dangerously when it parts, whereas HMPE has low elongation and high strength. The cadet understands how ropes are protected from sunlight, chafing, chemicals and crushing, and the need for regular inspection.
Stajyer, temel denizci bağlarını (bowlin: The cadet learns to make the basic seaman's knots (bowline, clove hitch, reef knot, figure-of-eight) and splices. The cadet practices how lines are made fast on bitts and cleats and led through fairleads, and how they are slacked and heaved under control at the windlass/winch warping ends (slack/heave). The cadet learns that a damaged rope (cut, crushed, internally rotten) must be taken out of service.
Stajyer, bağlama düzeninin (mooring patt: The cadet learns how the mooring pattern is planned: head/stern lines, springs and breast lines have different functions. A well-balanced mooring prevents the ship from ranging along the berth and from moving under the effect of waves/current/wind. Equal tension in all mooring lines (load sharing) is important for load distribution.
Bağlama/çözme manevralarında stajyer, ba: During mooring/unmooring maneuvers, the cadet works at the forward or aft station alongside the officer in charge (mooring officer). Radio communication (UHF) between the bridge and the station must be clear and closed-loop: "Heave away on the head line" → repeat back → execute. The cadet learns how the heaving line, the messenger line and the order of sending and receiving lines are managed.
Stajyer, halat verilirken eldeki gerginl: The cadet learns to control the tension on the line in hand while a line is being sent ashore, and to distinguish between the commands "make fast" and "let go". Throughout the operation, it is ensured that no one on deck stands between the bitts and the fairlead or under a line. Adequate lighting and visibility are provided for night operations.
Çözme sırasında halatlar köprüüstünün ta: During unmooring, lines are let go in a set order on the bridge's instructions; usually slack lines first and the "last line" last. The cadet observes the coordination with the shore linesmen and the timing needed to keep the line from falling into the water or fouling the propeller. Synchronizing the single-up (reducing to single lines) and let-go commands with the maneuver is critical.
Stajyer, çözme sonrası halatların temiz: The cadet learns that after unmooring, lines are recovered neatly, dried and properly stowed (coiling/faking). Maintenance to prevent wet and dirty lines from rotting is part of seamanship discipline.
Stajyer; demir (anchor), zincir (chain c: The cadet learns parts such as the anchor, chain cable, shackles, shackle marks, windlass, chain stopper (devil's claw/bow stopper), hawse pipe and chain locker, and the "shackle" as a unit of length (approximately 27.5 m / 15 fathoms). The length of cable is expressed as a number of shackles and is followed by paint/wire markings.
Stajyer, demirleme için gereken zincir m: The cadet learns that the amount of cable needed for anchoring is determined by the depth of water, the type of seabed, wind and current; a typical starting rule is to pay out 4-6 times the depth of water in cable, but this varies with conditions. Monitoring the anchor's holding and detecting dragging is done through coordination between the bridge and the forward station.
Demir atma (let go) ve toplama (heave up: During letting go and heaving up (weighing) the anchor, the cadet learns at the forward station to report to the bridge the direction of the cable (which way is the cable leading), its tension (up and down, brought up) and the number of shackles. The cadet understands the significance for the maneuver of terms such as "anchor aweigh" (anchor has broken out of the seabed) and "anchor home/clear".
Demirde yatarken stajyer, anchor watch (: While at anchor, the cadet learns how dragging is monitored during the anchor watch: GPS anchor alarm, ECDIS anchor watch, visual transit bearings and observation of the cable tension. When the weather deteriorates, the engine is put on standby and, if necessary, the second anchor is used or more cable is paid out.
Stajyer, gemi tipine göre yük operasyonl: The cadet observes cargo operations according to ship type: on dry cargo/bulk carriers, hatch covers and the use of cranes/grabs; on container ships, lashing/twistlocks; on tankers, the manifold, cargo hoses/arms and ISGOTT procedures. Each cargo type has its own risks and safety rules; the cadet first grasps the logic of the operation by observing.
Stajyer, yük planının (cargo/stowage pla: The cadet observes how the cargo plan (cargo/stowage plan) is put into effect, the relationship between the loading sequence and stability and strength, and how the deck team communicates with the bridge/cargo control room. The cadet learns that changes in draft, list and trim are monitored continuously during loading/discharging.
Stajyer, gemi vinçlerinin (derrick/crane: The cadet learns the SWL (Safe Working Load) limits of the ship's derricks/cranes and the periodic inspection and certification of slings, shackles and lifting accessories. No lifting appliance is loaded above its SWL and no one stands under a suspended load. Hand signals and communication between the signalman (banksman/signaller) and the crane operator are standardized.
Stajyer, kaldırma kayıtlarının (Register: The cadet observes that lifting records (Register of Lifting Appliances) and test certificates are kept and that equipment is tracked with color-coded inspection marks. A damaged sling or shackle is taken out of service immediately and tagged out.
Güverte bakımının büyük kısmı korozyonla: Most deck maintenance is a fight against corrosion. The cadet learns the sequence of rust removal (chipping/needle gun), surface preparation, primer and topcoat application. Paint applied without proper surface preparation soon flakes off; cleanliness and dryness are therefore important. PPE (dust mask, ear protection, goggles, gloves) is used against dust, noise and chemical exposure.
Stajyer, boya ve solventlerin tehlikeli: The cadet learns that paints and solvents are hazardous substances, that they are stored in accordance with the MSDS/SDS information and that they are not used in an enclosed space without ventilation. The cadet understands that used paint, solvents and rags are managed as special waste under MARPOL Annex V.
