Stajyer; güverte ekipmanlarının yağlanma: The cadet learns routine maintenance such as greasing deck equipment, tightening nuts and bolts, renewing gaskets and checking drains/freeing ports. These jobs are usually defined in the Planned Maintenance System (PMS); the cadet understands that every maintenance job has a reason and an interval. The tightness of hatch covers, doors (watertight doors) and ventilator openings is critical for the ship's watertight integrity.
Kapalı/kapalı mahaller (ambarlar, balast: Enclosed spaces (cargo holds, ballast tanks, cofferdams, chain lockers, empty tanks) are among the most lethal causes of accidents at sea; oxygen deficiency and toxic or flammable gas can be fatal. The cadet learns that an enclosed space is NEVER entered without a permit, without gas testing and without an attendant. Ventilation, gas testing (oxygen 20.9%, toxic and flammable gas limits) and a PTW are mandatory before entry.
Sıcak iş (kaynak, taşlama, kesme) yangın: Hot work (welding, grinding, cutting) carries a risk of fire and explosion; it requires a gas-free certificate, a fire watch and a PTW. For work at height and overside work, the safety harness, lifeline, stage/basket safety and the risk of falling tools are managed. The cadet takes part in this work only under supervision and with suitable equipment; no overside work is done while the ship is at sea.
Stajyer, güverte ekipmanlarını sistemati: The cadet learns the deck equipment systematically: mooring winches/anchor windlasses, winches/cranes, hatch cover hydraulics, the deck connections of the steering gear, watertight doors, freeing ports and the deck drainage system. Learning each item's working principle, check points and signs of failure is the basis for troubleshooting later as an officer.
Stajyer, ekipmanların hidrolik/elektrik/: The cadet learns the hydraulic/electric/pneumatic power sources of the equipment and its emergency stop points. Noticing and reporting signs such as unusual noise, leaks or overheating in a piece of equipment becomes a habit.
Stajyer, güverte işlerinin hava ve deniz: The cadet learns that deck work depends on the weather and sea state: in heavy weather, overside work and work at height are stopped, and when there is a risk of seas being shipped on deck, personnel do not go out on the open deck. Closing hatch covers and ventilators before heavy weather (battening down) is critical for the ship's watertight integrity. The cadet observes how the work plan changes in line with the weather report and the Master's instructions.
Güverte operasyonlarına katılım, stajyer: Taking part in deck operations is the most tangible area in which the cadet turns theoretical knowledge into real seamanship. Every minute spent at the end of a line, at the anchor cable or at the winch builds both skill and vital safety reflexes. The cadet's duty is never to work outside supervision, to read the risk continuously and to record what has been learned meticulously in the TRB. The discipline acquired on deck forms the foundation of the safety culture of the future deck officer.
Gerçek bir acil durumda insan düşünmez,: In a real emergency, people do not think; they do what they have drilled. This is why drills are critical: the cadet becomes able to put on a lifejacket, respond to the alarm signals and carry out their duty by reflex rather than from memory. Taking part in drills seriously saves lives later.
Alarm çaldığında stajyer, can yeleğiyle: When the alarm sounds, the cadet goes to the muster station with a lifejacket and carries out the duty defined in the Station Bill. From the first day, the cadet learns the muster station, the alarm signals and their own duty. Muster is where everyone is counted and where an organized response begins.
Stajyer; can yeleğini doğru ve hızlı giy: The cadet learns to put on a lifejacket correctly and quickly, to escape from a smoke-filled space with an EEBD (Emergency Escape Breathing Device) and to use a fire extinguisher correctly (PASS: Pull-Aim-Squeeze-Sweep). These skills are reinforced by repetition in drills.
EEBD yalnızca kaçış içindir, yangınla mü: An EEBD is for escape only, not for firefighting, and supplies air for a limited time (e.g. ~10-15 min). The cadet knows this limit; no one enters a fire with an EEBD, it is used only to escape to a safe area.
Stajyer, gemideki kaçış yollarını, alter: The cadet learns the escape routes, alternative exits and muster points on board. The cadet becomes familiar with finding the way in darkness/smoke (low-location lighting, escape route signs). Knowing the right escape route in a fire saves lives.
Stajyer, katıldığı her tatbikatı ve öğre: The cadet records every drill attended and every skill learned in the TRB and has it approved by the training officer. This record both reinforces learning and provides evidence of competence.
Emniyet tatbikatlarına katılım, güverte: Taking part in safety drills lays the life-safety foundation of the deck cadet's seagoing career. Taking drills seriously, being able to use basic equipment by reflex and knowing the escape routes protect the lives of both the cadet and the crew in a real emergency.
TRB, stajyerin hangi yetkinlikleri ne za: The TRB documents which competences the cadet acquired, when and how. It is structured according to the STCW competence tables and is the main evidence in the certification process. An incomplete or belatedly completed TRB puts the right to sit the examination and career progression at risk.
TRB, görev yapıldıkça doldurulmalıdır; a: The TRB must be filled in as tasks are done; entries left until the end of the month or the end of the contract end up incomplete and superficial. Every day, the cadet records the work done and what was learned in concrete terms. This discipline both reinforces learning and keeps the book realistic.
TRB; seyir, yük işlemleri, gemi operasyo: The TRB covers competence areas such as navigation, cargo handling, controlling the operation of the ship and care for persons on board, safety and environmental protection. In each area, the cadet completes the specified tasks and records evidence of observation/performance. Areas still outstanding are completed according to a plan.
Her tamamlanan görev, eğitmen zabit (tra: Each completed task is signed and assessed by the training officer. This approval confirms that the entry is genuine and that the competence has been acquired. The cadet meets the training officer regularly to obtain feedback and to close any gaps.
TRB stajyerin sertifika hakkının belgesi: The TRB is the document of the cadet's entitlement to certification; losing it causes problems that are hard to remedy. The cadet keeps the book safe and, where possible, keeps a digital backup/photographs. The cadet preserves its integrity (no missing pages, no erasures), because this book is official evidence.
TRB yönetimi, güverte stajyerinin kariye: Managing the TRB is the deck cadet's most direct investment in their career; every page filled in with discipline today is evidence for an officer's certificate tomorrow. Daily entries, the training officer's approval and careful safekeeping form a solid foundation for the cadet's progress.
Safety Management System (SMS), geminin: The Safety Management System (SMS) is the set of procedures established to conduct all of the ship's operations safely and in compliance with regulations. The cadet learns that the SMS is not "a binder sitting on a shelf" but the framework of daily work, and understands that every procedure was born from the lesson of an accident.
Risk değerlendirmesi (risk assessment),: Risk assessment means identifying the hazards before a job and planning control measures. The cadet learns hazard identification, likelihood/severity assessment and the logic of the hierarchy of controls (elimination, substitution, engineering, administrative, PPE). This way of thinking is the basis of safety throughout a career.
Yüksek riskli işler (enclosed space, hot: High-risk work (enclosed space, hot work, aloft, electrical) is carried out under a Permit to Work; the job, the precautions and the approval are recorded. The cadet learns why the PTW exists and that no high-risk work may be done without a permit.
Stajyer; ISPS kapsamında güvenlik seviye: The cadet learns about security levels, access control, restricted areas and visitor management under ISPS. The cadet understands that security is a field distinct from, but complementary to, safety, and becomes familiar with the basics of dealing with unauthorized boarding, stowaways and threats.
Stajyer, near-miss raporlamanın değerini: The cadet learns the value of near-miss reporting (every near-miss reported is an accident prevented) and the structure of the Safety Committee. The cadet also becomes familiar with environmental protection procedures under MARPOL, such as garbage, oil and emissions management. The cadet internalizes that protecting the sea is a duty.
ISM ve güvenlik prosedürlerini öğrenmek,: Learning ISM and safety procedures turns the deck cadet into a seafarer who does not merely "apply the rules" but "understands why they are applied". Risk-based thinking, permit discipline and an open reporting culture lay the foundation for the cadet to become a safe officer in the future.
Stajyer, gemiyi bir sistemler bütünü ola: The cadet learns the ship as a set of systems: the purpose of each system, its operating logic, its controls and its behavior in an emergency. This learning is based on understanding, not memorization; knowing "why" a system works the way it does makes it possible to make the right decision in a breakdown or an emergency.
Stajyer; ballast (stabilite/trim), bilge: The cadet learns the ballast (stability/trim), bilge (bilge pumping), fire main (fire water), steering gear and anchoring systems. The purpose and control of each, and its role in safety, are understood. For example, the cadet learns why it is vital to keep the fire main pressurized at all times.
Stajyer; ECDIS, radar/ARPA, AIS, GMDSS,: The cadet becomes familiar with bridge equipment such as ECDIS, radar/ARPA, AIS, GMDSS, the gyro/magnetic compass and the echo sounder. The capabilities and limitations of each are learned, and the cadet understands that the equipment must be used together, with cross-checking. This foundation is the key to safe watchkeeping in the future.
Stajyer; gemi tipine göre (bulk, tanker,: The cadet learns the basic principles of cargo operations by ship type (bulk, tanker, container, ro-ro), their effect on stability/strength and the safety precautions. Awareness of dangerous goods (IMDG/IMSBC) begins in this period. Understanding how cargo affects the ship is fundamental to becoming an officer.
Kaptan ve zabitler, stajyere yapılandırı: The Master and officers give the cadet structured training modules. The cadet completes them, asks questions and records what was learned in the TRB. Active participation — doing and asking rather than watching — makes learning last.
Teknik bilgi ve sistem öğrenimi, güverte: Technical knowledge and learning the ship's systems are the core that turns the deck cadet into a competent future officer. Truly understanding the ship — logic, not memorization — lays the foundation for the cadet to make the right decisions in breakdowns, emergencies and complex operations in the future.
STCW, zabit yeterliliği için belirli sür: STCW requires a specified period of approved seagoing service for officer certification. The Sea Service Certificate is the official proof of this period. However good the training and the TRB may be, undocumented sea service delays or prevents entitlement to certification.
Belge; gemi adı/bayrağı/tipi, görev tanı: The certificate contains information such as the ship's name/flag/type, the capacity in which the holder served, the dates of service (signing on - signing off), the trading area and the ship's tonnage/engine power, and is signed by the Master. These details determine whether the service counts as "valid" for certification.
Stajyer; belgeyi her sözleşme/gemi değiş: At every change of contract/ship, the cadet requests the certificate correctly, keeps it safe and documents the period in full. Discharge book/seaman's book entries also form part of this record. Correct and continuous documents ensure that no problems arise later when applying for the examination.
Deniz hizmeti, TRB ve eğitim tamamlandığ: When sea service, the TRB and training are complete, the cadet applies to the flag State/Administration for a certificate of competency (CoC). The sea service documents, the TRB and the training certificates are the basis of this application. Complete, orderly paperwork speeds up the process.
Stajyer, tüm belgelerini (sea service, T: The cadet keeps all documents (sea service, TRB, training certificates, medical certificate, passport/seaman's book) in an orderly file and monitors their validity dates. This order is useful at every stage of a career and makes it possible to produce a document needed at short notice immediately.
Deniz hizmet belgesi ve sertifika süreci: The sea service certificate and the certification process are the administrative basis on which the deck cadet turns what has been learned into a career. Requesting documents correctly, keeping them complete and tracking the service period secure the cadet's progress toward becoming an officer.
Yetersiz stabilite alabora; aşırı stabil: Insufficient stability means capsizing; excessive stability (stiff) means violent rolling and high lashing loads; an incorrect distribution with respect to strength means hull damage. The cadet learns that stability is not "an abstract calculation" but the basis of the ship's survival. Many marine casualties have been caused by stability/cargo errors.
Stajyer; GM (metasantr yüksekliği — başl: The cadet learns the concepts of GM (metacentric height — the measure of initial stability), trim (difference between forward and aft drafts) and list (transverse inclination). A low GM makes a "tender" ship and a high GM a "stiff" ship; both carry risks. The optimum range provides safety, comfort and cargo safety.
Kısmen dolu bir tanktaki sıvının hareket: The movement of liquid in a partly filled tank (free surface effect) reduces stability by lowering the effective GM. The cadet therefore learns that tanks are kept completely full ("press up") or empty as far as possible and that the number of slack tanks is limited.
Yük dağılımı, gövde boyunca bending mome: Cargo distribution creates bending moments and shear forces along the hull. Heavy cargo amidships tends to cause sagging and heavy cargo at the ends tends to cause hogging; both strain the hull. The cadet learns that the loading computer is used to keep these values below the 100% limit.
Stajyer, Birinci Zabit gözetiminde loadi: Under the Chief Officer's supervision, the cadet works through simple scenarios on the loading computer/stability software: entering tank/hold loads and reading the GM/trim/draft and strength output. The cadet learns to read values such as displacement, TPC and MCT from the hydrostatic tables; understanding "what the software calculates" is critical.
Draft survey, draft okumaları ve hidrost: A draft survey calculates the quantity of cargo loaded/discharged from draft readings and hydrostatic data. The cadet learns draft reading, the water density correction and the logic of the calculation by observing. This is an important skill from both a commercial and a stability point of view.
Stabilite ve yük hesabına eğitim katılım: Taking part in stability and cargo calculations for training is the critical area in which the deck cadet begins to understand the physics of the ship. Seeing the concepts of GM, trim, free surface and strength in practice prepares the cadet to become an officer who will make safe loading decisions in the future.
Manevrada geminin atalet, dümen/pervane: During maneuvering, the ship's inertia, the response to rudder/propeller, the effect of wind/current, the use of tugs and team coordination can all be observed at the same time. The cadet sees textbook knowledge in real motion. Good observation lays the foundation for the cadet's own maneuvering decisions in the future.
Stajyer; pilot boarding (kılavuz biniş),: The cadet observes each phase of the pilot boarding, approach, swing, berthing, line ashore and tug operations. The cadet notes the purpose of each phase and the team's duties in the TRB. Speed, angle and the use of tugs during the transition between phases are watched closely.
Stajyer; pilot card (geminin manevra öze: The cadet learns the contents of the pilot card (summary of the ship's maneuvering information), the maneuvering booklet and the wheelhouse poster. The cadet understands what data such as the turning circle, stopping distance and crash stop mean. These data show the "physical limits" of maneuvering.
Stajyer, bağlama istasyonundan gözlem ya: When observing from the mooring station, the cadet sees line handling, winch operation and the snap-back hazard at close quarters. The cadet understands the importance of communication between the bridge and the station. The rules on safe positioning and PPE apply here too.
Stajyer, gözlemlediği manevraları ve öğr: The cadet records the maneuvers observed and the data learned in the TRB and reviews them with the training officer. This record both reinforces learning and provides evidence of competence.
Manevra ve bağlama gözlemi, güverte staj: Observing maneuvering and mooring gives the deck cadet the opportunity to learn the most dynamic moments of seafaring live. Observing the phases, understanding the maneuvering data and the discipline of observing safely prepare the cadet to become an officer who will make their own maneuvering decisions with confidence in the future.
Köprü ve makine dairesi arasında \"Unman: Even on ships with an "Unmanned Machinery Space (UMS)" notation, the daily noon report between the bridge and the engine room and 4-hourly log entries are standard. The Second Engineer reviews the manual logs taken by the watchkeeping engineers (exhaust gas temperature of each cylinder, scavenge air pressure, jacket cooling water inlet/outlet, LO inlet temp/press, fuel rack/index, turbocharger rpm) and cross-checks them with the data from the automatic data logger (alarm monitoring system).
Modern gemilerde Kongsberg, Praxis veya: On modern ships, alarm/monitoring systems such as Kongsberg, Praxis or Lyngsø collect all parameters every second. The Second Engineer reviews the trend screens of this data daily, focusing on the "rate of change" rather than the absolute value. For example, a rise of 20-30°C in the exhaust temperature of a single cylinder, even while the absolute value is still within limits, is a warning sign of a fuel valve (fuel injector) fault.
Noon report; mil/gün, ortalama hız, ME/A: The noon report includes miles/day, average speed, ME/AE/boiler FO and DO consumption, LO consumption, slip percentage and weather/sea conditions. The Second Engineer calculates the specific fuel oil consumption (SFOC, g/kWh) and compares it with the shop-test/sea-trial reference curve. A persistent increase in SFOC indicates fouling, injection faults, loss of T/C efficiency or governor deviation.
Slip (apparent slip), pervane ile gemi h: Slip (apparent slip) is the theoretical difference between the propeller's advance and the ship's actual movement; excessive positive slip indicates hull/propeller fouling or heavy weather, while negative slip is the effect of current or an external push. Using trend graphs, technical justification is presented to the Chief Engineer for hull cleaning and propeller polishing decisions.
Her silindirin egzoz sıcaklığı, o silind: The exhaust temperature of each cylinder is a direct indicator of that cylinder's share of the load. The deviation between all cylinders is generally kept within ±5% (approximately ±15-20°C). A high reading on one cylinder may mean late combustion, a leaking exhaust valve or fuel index imbalance; a low reading may mean low compression, a misfiring injector or a fuel pump leak.
T/C öncesi (before turbine) ve sonrası (: Exhaust temperatures before the T/C (before turbine) and after it (after turbine) show the turbocharger efficiency. A rise in the after-turbine temperature indicates T/C fouling (nozzle ring/turbine fouling) and may require water washing (turbine/compressor water washing).
Scavenge air pressure (boost pressure),: Scavenge air pressure (boost pressure) shows the engine's "breathing" capacity; a drop indicates air cooler fouling, a T/C fault or a clogged air intake filter. Pmax (maximum combustion pressure) and Pcomp (compression pressure) are measured with an indicator/PMI instrument, and balance is achieved when these two values are equal in all cylinders.
LO ana hat basıncı, ana yatak ve crosshe: LO main line pressure is the guarantee of main bearing and crosshead lubrication; a sudden drop triggers an alarm and, if necessary, a slowdown/shutdown. The Second Engineer determines the root cause of low-pressure alarms (clogged filter, pump wear, a bypass left open) and produces a permanent solution rather than a temporary fix.
Diyagramdan Pmax, Pcomp, mean indicated: Pmax, Pcomp, mean indicated pressure (Pi), indicated power and the combustion angle (timing) are derived from the diagram. The Pmax-Pcomp difference is an indicator of fuel injection timing; late injection lowers Pmax and raises the exhaust temperature, while early injection raises Pmax dangerously and causes mechanical overload.
Silindirler arası güç dengesi (power bal: Power balancing between cylinders is done by adjusting the fuel index/VIT (Variable Injection Timing). On electronically controlled ME/RT-flex engines the ECU maintains this balance automatically, while on mechanical MC engines the Second Engineer corrects it manually by fuel pump rack adjustment and shims.
Dengesizlik kalıcı ise neden enjektör, y: If the imbalance persists, the cause may be an injector, wear of the fuel pump plunger/barrel or a suction/puncture valve fault. The Second Engineer enters the measurement results in the PMS, opens a work order to overhaul the fuel valve concerned if necessary and verifies the result with a new diagram.
Scavenge drain (cylinder drain oil) numu: A scavenge drain (cylinder drain oil) sample is the most practical tool for showing the condition of the cylinder liner and the piston ring zone. The Second Engineer organizes the taking of a separate sample from each cylinder and has an on-board quick test carried out for Fe content (e.g. magnetic chip / colorimetric kit).
Yüksek Fe içeriği (genelde >200 ppm bir: A high Fe content (generally >200 ppm is a warning, >400 ppm serious) means corrosive or adhesive wear of the liner, or the onset of scuffing. The residual BN (Base Number) of the drain oil shows the acid neutralization capacity; a low BN means inadequate lubrication against fuel sulfur and a risk of cold corrosion.
Periyodik olarak numuneler shore laborat: Samples are sent periodically to a shore laboratory (spectrometric element analysis, BN, viscosity, water, contamination). The results are entered in a trend table. A sudden jump in the Fe trend triggers a scavenge port inspection of the cylinder concerned and, if necessary, an increase in the cylinder oil feed rate.
İkinci Mühendis, bu veriyi cylinder oil: The Second Engineer evaluates this data together with the optimization of cylinder oil consumption (feed rate in g/kWh). When changing to low-sulfur fuel (MARPOL Annex VI VLSFO/MGO), a change to a lower-BN cylinder oil is required; the wrong BN choice leads either to cold corrosion or to deposit/blow-by problems.
Belirli çalışma saatlerinde (tipik 500-1: Scavenge port inspections are carried out at set running-hour intervals (typically 500-1000 hours). The Second Engineer plans this work and ensures gas testing in line with the enclosed space entry permit procedure and safe isolation (turning gear engaged, starting air shut off). The inspection covers carbon deposits on the piston crown and ring zone, ring freedom/breakage, the liner surface (glazing, scuffing, vertical scratches) and the underside of the cylinder cover.
Bulgular fotoğraflanır ve raporlanır. Gl: Findings are photographed and reported. Glazing (a shiny mirror-like surface) disrupts the oil film and reduces ring conformability; scuffing (longitudinal scratches/burn marks), if it progresses, leads to seizure. At the first signs, the Second Engineer recommends to the Chief Engineer a feed rate adjustment, a running-in procedure or honing of the liner.
Scavenge box içinde biriken yanmamış yak: Unburnt fuel and oil accumulating in the scavenge box can be ignited by hot blow-by gas and cause a scavenge fire. Signs include a rise in the exhaust/scavenge temperature of the cylinder concerned, T/C surging, blistering paint and a drop in load. The Second Engineer manages this risk through regular cleaning of the scavenge drains and maintenance of the under-piston space.
Turbocharger rpm, before/after turbine s: T/C efficiency is monitored by evaluating turbocharger rpm, before/after turbine temperatures and scavenge pressure together. If the compressor side becomes fouled, boost falls and SFOC rises; compressor-side water washing (generally daily/every two days) and turbine-side dry/water washing are therefore scheduled.
İkinci Mühendis, T/C surging (ani hava g: The Second Engineer takes T/C surging (a sudden air blow-back noise and vibration) seriously; surging may result from heavy weather, sudden load changes, a fouled turbine or a single-cylinder fault, and causes mechanical damage to the T/C blades.
Scavenge air cooler (charge air cooler): Scavenge air cooler (charge air cooler) performance is monitored by the air inlet/outlet temperatures and the water-side differential pressure. Air-side fouling lowers the boost; water-side fouling impairs cooling. A clogged water mist catcher after the cooler, or a condensate drain that is not kept open, leads to water entering the cylinders.
Hava emiş filtreleri ve engine room vent: Air intake filters and engine room ventilation also affect performance; a high intake temperature (hot climate) leads to a wrong diagnosis if it is not evaluated with ambient correction.
Bunker analiz raporu (CCAI, density, sül: The bunker analysis report (CCAI, density, sulfur, water, ash, cat fines/Al+Si) is evaluated. High cat fines (aluminum+silicon) cause abrasive wear of liners and injection equipment; settling/service tank and purifier performance are therefore critical.
ECA giriş/çıkışında HFO↔MGO/VLSFO change: On entering/leaving an ECA, the HFO↔MGO/VLSFO changeover is carried out slowly and under control (to prevent thermal shock and loss of viscosity). During the changeover, the Second Engineer monitors fuel pump and injector leakage; with low-viscosity fuel, internal pump leakage increases and the fuel index rises.
Bu geçişler performans loglarında geçici: These changeovers create temporary deviations in the performance logs; by labeling these deviations with the fuel type, the Second Engineer ensures that the trend interpretation is not distorted.
MARPOL Annex VI kapsamında EEXI (Energy: Under MARPOL Annex VI, the EEXI (Energy Efficiency Existing Ship Index) and the annual CII (Carbon Intensity Indicator) rating are in force. The performance data kept by the Second Engineer (SFOC, speed-power curve, fouling trends) directly affects the ship's CII rating and provides the justification for SEEMP Part III actions (hull cleaning, derating, trim optimization).
NOx Technical Code kapsamında Tier II/II: Under the NOx Technical Code, Tier II/III compliance requires injection timing, EGR/SCR systems and engine group parameters to be kept in line with the EIAPP/Technical File. The Second Engineer ensures that setting changes remain within the approved limits and that the Record Book of Engine Parameters is kept up to date.
İkinci Mühendis, periyodik performance r: The Second Engineer submits the periodic performance report to the Chief Engineer and to the company's technical department (superintendent). Most companies use shore-based performance monitoring platforms such as CASPER, Marorka or Eniram; the data from the ship is compared there with the fleet as a whole.
Anormal trendler (SFOC artışı, T/C verim: By turning abnormal trends (rising SFOC, loss of T/C efficiency, increasing Fe content) into an early maintenance plan, the risk of unexpected breakdown and of off-hire under the charter party is reduced.
İkinci Mühendis, anormal bir parametreyi: The Second Engineer does not interpret an abnormal parameter on its own; it is evaluated together with related parameters (e.g. high exhaust temperature + low Pmax + high Fe) and the likely root cause hypothesis is tested. This approach avoids costly and risky methods such as trial-and-error parts swapping.
Tüm ölçümler, ayarlar ve müdahaleler PMS: All measurements, settings and interventions are entered in the PMS and the engine log. These records are the ship's evidence of "due diligence" at class surveys and at PSC, flag and P&I inspections. Missing records are interpreted against the ship in insurance and liability cases.
Vardiya devir tesliminde açık işler, izl: At watch handover, open jobs, abnormalities being monitored and temporary arrangements (temporary repairs) are handed over in writing; this continuity ensures that performance management does not depend on one individual.
İkinci Mühendisin ana makine performans: The Second Engineer's success in main engine performance management comes from disciplined measurement, trend reading and early intervention — work that remains invisible "while everything is going well" but protects the ship's voyage safety and commercial continuity when a failure comes. A well-kept performance log both prevents a mechanical disaster and maintains the ship's MARPOL Annex VI compliance and the charterer's confidence.
PMS iş emirleri üç tetikleyiciyle üretil: PMS work orders are generated by three triggers: calendar-based (e.g. testing of generator safety devices every 3 months), running-hour-based (e.g. separator overhaul at 6000 hours) and condition-based (according to vibration, oil analysis or thermography results). The Second Engineer pulls the upcoming work orders from the PMS screen weekly (look-ahead list) and prioritizes them.
Klas onaylı PMS-CM (Planned Maintenance: In class-approved PMS-CM (Planned Maintenance and Condition Monitoring) systems, the survey items (continuous machinery survey) are linked directly to the PMS. Maintenance of an item is carried out under the supervision of the authorized engineer (the Chief Engineer), and the record is submitted to the class surveyor for acceptance. The Second Engineer ensures that the evidence for these items (photographs, measurements, clearance values) is collected in full.
ISM kapsamında \"critical equipment\" li: Under ISM, a "critical equipment" list is defined: main engine, steering gear, generators, emergency generator, fire/bilge pumps, IGS, maneuvering equipment. Maintenance of this equipment cannot be postponed; alternative/standby arrangements (standby pump, second supply line) must have been tested for use in the event of failure. The Second Engineer marks the work orders for critical items as "high priority".
İkinci Mühendis, hafta başında (genelde: At the start of the week (usually Monday), the Second Engineer takes the 1–4 week due/overdue list from the PMS. Jobs are ranked by safety criticality, the class/PSC schedule, the port/sea status (at sea or in port), spare parts availability and personnel availability. Jobs that must be done during a port stay (requiring immobilization) are put in a separate bucket and coordinated with the Chief Engineer + Master.
Günlük \"toolbox talk\" (vardiya başı br: During the daily "toolbox talk" (start-of-watch briefing), the day's jobs are explained to the ratings and the duty engineer; for each job, the risk assessment, the isolation required, PPE and the need for a standby person are discussed. Work is allocated by matching experience to the job; an experienced person always accompanies an overhaul being done for the first time.
Bir iş emri açıldığında; ekipman, görev: When a work order is opened, the equipment, the job description, the spares/consumables required, the estimated duration and the assigned personnel are recorded. While the job is carried out, the parts used are deducted from the PMS stock module (consumption logging). When the job is complete, it is closed by entering the work done, the measured values (clearance, bearing temp, pressure), the serial numbers of the parts replaced and a note for the next maintenance (e.g. "approaching wear limit").
İkinci Mühendis, kapanan iş emirlerini g: The Second Engineer reviews closed work orders daily and rejects incomplete/superficial close-outs. If the feedback is poor, a finding (deficiency) arises at the next survey because of insufficient evidence.
Yüksek riskli işler Permit-to-Work (PTW): High-risk jobs start with a Permit-to-Work (PTW): hot work (welding/grinding), enclosed/confined space entry, work at height, electrical isolation, opening up pressurized systems. The Second Engineer is usually the person who approves/coordinates the PTW; it is signed together with the Chief Engineer. Lock-Out/Tag-Out (LOTO) is applied for energy isolation; every energy source (electrical, compressed air, hydraulic, steam, spring energy) is made safe and tagged.
Stored energy (akümülatör basıncı, sıkış: Stored energy (accumulator pressure, a compressed spring, hot fluid) is the hidden cause of many accidents. Work does not start until the isolation has been verified (try-out: attempt to operate). The Second Engineer ensures that the keys are held in one place and that a multi-lock hasp is used if more than one team is working on the same panel.
Standart olmayan veya yüksek enerjili he: A written risk assessment (JSA/JHA) is made for every non-standard or high-energy job: hazard–exposure–existing barriers–additional measures. The Second Engineer adapts the generic risk assessment to the specifics of the job; a "copy-paste" risk assessment masks the real hazards. At the toolbox talk the whole team signs the risk assessment, and everyone is reminded of their right to ask questions and to say "stop" (stop-work authority).
İkinci Mühendis, makine dairesi yedekler: The Second Engineer tracks the ROB (Remaining On Board) of engine room spares through the PMS stock module. Minimum/maximum levels are defined for critical spares (injectors, fuel pump elements, separator gasket sets, compressor valve sets, main engine bearings); when the minimum is reached, a requisition is generated automatically. SOLAS and class require certain critical spares to be carried on board.
Talepler Baş Mühendis onayıyla şirket sa: Requisitions are forwarded to company purchasing with the Chief Engineer's approval; long-lead-time parts (e.g. a crankshaft bearing) are ordered early. When a spare is received, the correct part number, absence of damage and the certificate (class-approved if required) are checked, and it is put away in the correct locker (with a location code).
Bir overhaul'a başlamadan önce gereken t: Before starting an overhaul, the availability of all required gaskets, O-rings and wear parts is physically verified. Otherwise the equipment ends up dismantled and out of service while waiting for parts; on critical equipment this creates a safety gap. The Second Engineer makes this verification a condition for opening the work order.
İkinci Mühendis, işleri personelin ehliy: The Second Engineer allocates jobs according to the qualifications and experience of the personnel. The Third/Fourth Engineer carries out maintenance of the equipment in their area of responsibility (generators, boiler, purifiers, auxiliary systems); the fitter and oilers do the mechanical dismantling/assembly, cleaning and carrying. For jobs done for the first time or high-risk jobs, the Second Engineer personally supervises on site.
Çalışma–dinlenme saatleri (STCW/MLC) göz: Hours of work and rest (STCW/MLC) are observed; critical jobs are not given to fatigued personnel. If intensive maintenance is planned during a port stay, the balance between overtime and rest is calculated in advance and, if necessary, the work is spread over the schedule.
Denizde bakım, ekipmanın seyir emniyetin: Maintenance at sea is done provided that it does not affect navigational safety (e.g. maintenance of a standby generator or the second air compressor). Jobs that will immobilize the main engine (general overhaul of injectors, scavenge space entry) are done only under safe anchorage/port conditions and with the bridge's approval. Before immobilization, the Second Engineer coordinates notification to the bridge, the telegraph/UMS mode and the time needed to return the engine to service.
Her kapatılan iş emri bir veri noktasıdı: Every closed work order is a data point. Bearing clearances, exhaust temperature distribution, vibration and oil analysis results form trends over time. By monitoring these trends, the Second Engineer proposes interval optimization; for example, if a purifier's seal life is shorter than expected, the interval is shortened or the root cause (feed temperature, quality) is investigated.
Defect/breakdown durumunda ayrı bir arız: In the event of a defect/breakdown, a separate defect report is opened; the root cause analysis (5-Why) and the corrective action are recorded. Recurring failures are escalated to the company's technical department.
Klas continuous survey, PSC ve vetting (: PMS records are examined at class continuous surveys, PSC inspections and vetting (SIRE/CDI) inspections. Inconsistent dates, "completed" entries without evidence, accumulated overdue jobs and unrecorded bypasses are typical findings. Before an inspection, the Second Engineer reviews the PMS together with the Chief Engineer and closes any gaps.
Yakıt/yağ filtre değişimi, separatör bow: Fuel/oil filter changes, separator bowl cleaning, cooler cleaning, valve grinding and gasket renewal are the core jobs of the engine room. In these jobs, cleanliness (foreign object / FOD control), correct torque values and a leak test after assembly are critical. The Second Engineer is personally present at the first start after maintenance.
Büyük overhaul'larda (enjektör, pompa el: In major overhauls (injectors, pump elements, bearing renewal), the maker's clearance and torque tables are the reference. Measurements are taken with calibrated tools; rubber seals are treated as single-use and renewed. The Second Engineer records the "as found / as left" values (found on dismantling / left on reassembly); this shows the rate of wear.
Plansız arıza (breakdown) durumunda İkin: In an unplanned breakdown, the Second Engineer makes the situation safe (isolation, fire/leak control), informs the Chief Engineer, decides together with the Chief Engineer on a temporary/permanent repair and, if necessary, calls in company/maker technical support. Temporary repairs are recorded and a permanent solution is planned.
Bir kritik ekipman arızalandığında yedek: When an item of critical equipment fails, the standby/alternative arrangement is brought into use and, if a "single point of failure" situation exists, the navigational risk is reassessed (e.g. if only one generator remains, speed/load restrictions or a decision to make for port). The Second Engineer reports this situation immediately to the Chief Engineer and the bridge.
İkinci Mühendisin bakım yönetimindeki ba: The Second Engineer's success in maintenance management comes from the triangle of planned thinking, discipline on site and complete records. A well-run PMS reduces breakdowns, gets the ship through surveys without problems and, most importantly, protects the crew and the ship. Maintenance that is delayed or closed without evidence, on the other hand, always comes back as a more expensive breakdown and an inspection finding.
Scavenge port'tan yapılan inspection, mo: Inspection through the scavenge ports is the most practical way of seeing the internal condition without dismantling the engine. The condition of pistons, rings and liners, deposit build-up and possible traces of scavenge fire are observed here. With this regular check, the Second Engineer catches major failures early.
İkinci Mühendis; piston crown karbon bir: The Second Engineer inspects carbon deposits on the piston crown, ring condition (broken, sticking/collapsed, free movement), liner wear/scuffing and the underside of the cylinder cover. Ring sticking both lowers performance and increases the risk of scavenge fire through blow-by.
Scavenge box'ta biriken yağ/karbon, blow: Oil/carbon accumulating in the scavenge box can be ignited by hot blow-by gas (scavenge fire). Signs: a rise in scavenge temperature at the unit concerned, a temperature alarm, a drop in power and sometimes local heating on the casing. When detected, the load is reduced immediately, the lubrication of the cylinder concerned is adjusted, the scavenge port is closed and extinguishing (fixed system/CO2) is applied.
Scavenge fire'ı önlemenin yolu; scavenge: The way to prevent scavenge fire is to keep the scavenge box clean of oil/carbon deposits, to monitor ring condition (to reduce blow-by) and to set the cylinder lubrication correctly. Keeping the drains open allows accumulated oil to drain away.
Scavenge inspection, motor durdurulmuş,: Scavenge inspection is carried out with the engine stopped, cooled down and isolated by LOTO; the turning gear must be engaged and locked. Appropriate PPE and care are needed against the risks of hot surfaces and confined spaces. Nothing is opened until the isolation has been verified.
Her inspection'ın bulguları (foto dahil): The findings of each inspection (including photographs) are recorded and the trend is followed. A recurring finding (e.g. increasing deposits on a particular unit) triggers a root cause investigation. The Second Engineer uses these records to guide maintenance decisions.
Scavenge ve under-piston inspection, İki: Scavenge and under-piston inspection is a valuable diagnostic tool with which the Second Engineer observes the internal condition of the main engine without dismantling it. Regular inspection, cleaning of the scavenge box and rapid response to signs of scavenge fire protect the main engine from both fire and major wear damage.
Crankcase, motorun ana hareketli parçala: The crankcase houses the engine's main moving parts; bearing damage or a loose tie bolt can lead to catastrophic failure. Through regular inspection, the Second Engineer monitors the condition of these parts and catches problems early. At the same time, because of the explosion risk, the crankcase is the area approached with the greatest care.
Oil Mist Detector, crankcase içindeki ya: The Oil Mist Detector monitors the oil mist concentration in the crankcase; when a bearing overheats and vaporizes oil, the mist increases and the OMD gives an alarm. This alarm is the early warning of impending bearing damage and a potential explosion. The Second Engineer ensures that the OMD is working and calibrated.
Oil mist alarmında motor yavaşlatılır/du: On an oil mist alarm, the engine is slowed down/stopped and, because of the crankcase explosion risk, a strict waiting period is applied to let the bearings cool (generally at least ~30 minutes); the crankcase doors are NOT OPENED until bearing temperatures have stabilized. Admitting fresh air into a hot crankcase can trigger a secondary explosion.
Crankcase inspection'da; main bearing, c: During crankcase inspection, the condition of the main bearings, crank pin (bottom end) bearings and crosshead bearings, white metal smear (smeared white metal — a sign of overheating), tie bolt looseness and the general condition of the oil film are checked. White metal smear or discoloration shows that a bearing has overheated and needs attention.
Inspection, motor durdurulmuş, soğutulmu: The inspection is carried out with the engine stopped, cooled down and isolated by LOTO, and with the turning gear engaged/locked. Entry into the crankcase is subject to the enclosed space and hot surface rules. Naked flames/sources of sparks are kept away. The Second Engineer verifies all of these steps.
Inspection bulguları (yatak durumu, ölçü: Inspection findings (bearing condition, measurements, photographs) are recorded and the trend is followed. Recurring heating of a bearing or increasing particles require a root cause investigation and planned intervention. These records are the basis for making decisions before a major failure.
Crankcase inspection ve oil mist takibi,: Crankcase inspection and oil mist monitoring is the task in which the Second Engineer both protects the most critical parts of the main engine and observes the most serious safety rule. Respecting the oil mist alarm, strictly following the cooling-down rule and careful bearing inspection prevent both crankcase explosion and catastrophic bearing damage, protecting life and machinery safety together.
Bunker nomination şirket/charterer taraf: The bunker nomination is given by the company/charterer: fuel type (e.g. VLSFO ≤0.50% S or MGO), quantity, supplier and port. The Second Engineer verifies the current ROB (by tank soundings), distributes the quantity to be received among the tank capacities and calculates the 95–98% filling limit and the allowance for thermal expansion (temperature expansion). The plan makes clear which tank is to be filled in which order, the valve line-up and the high alarm levels for preventing overflow.
Sülfür uyumu kritiktir: ECA bölgesinde %: Sulfur compliance is critical: 0.10% S in an ECA and a global limit of 0.50% S. The Second Engineer assesses whether the fuel received suits the voyage profile and whether mixing it with the fuel already on board (commingling) will cause incompatibility (sludging/stability problems).
Bunker barç/terminal ile pre-transfer to: A pre-transfer meeting is held with the bunker barge/terminal: starting/maximum pumping rate, topping-up rate, communication method (VHF channel + hand signals), emergency stop signal, hose connection point and maximum allowable pressure. The Second Engineer and the barge representative sign the Bunkering Safety Checklist (based on ISGOTT) together.
Bunker öncesi tüm güverte scupper'ları (: Before bunkering, all deck scuppers are plugged/blanked so that any spill cannot reach the sea. Drip trays are placed under the manifold and hose connection, with absorbent inside. SOPEP equipment (absorbent pads, rags, shovels, drums, sprayer) is kept ready and accessible. The location of the spill kit is made known to the whole team.
İkinci Mühendis, scupper plug'larının su: The Second Engineer makes sure that the scupper plugs do not cause ponding/deck loading if water accumulates; controlled draining is planned in case of rain. The manifold drip tray is checked regularly throughout the operation.
Tank seviyesi sürekli izlenir (sounding: The tank level is monitored continuously (sounding + remote gauge). The high and high-high alarms must have been tested. During topping-up the rate is reduced; only one tank is left open to make control easier. Air vent/sounding pipe openings must be clear; a blocked vent causes overpressure and rupture/overflow.
Bunker boyunca sürekli akıştan (drip/con: Throughout bunkering, the MARPOL sample is taken from the continuous flow (drip/continuous drip sampler); this sample is sealed, labeled and retained on board for at least 12 months (or as required by the rules). In addition, a fuel quality sample is taken for laboratory testing and sent promptly for the ISO 8217 parameters (density, viscosity, water, sulfur, ash, CCAI, catalytic fines Al+Si, flash point).
İkinci Mühendis, numune alma noktasının: The Second Engineer ensures that the sampling point is the ship's manifold (not the barge side); the barge representative witnesses the sealing and the seal numbers are entered on the BDN. In a dispute, this sample and the chain of seals are decisive.
Alınan miktar hacim olarak ölçülür; metr: The quantity received is measured by volume; conversion to metric tons requires the density (at 15°C) and a temperature correction (ASTM 54B / VCF). The Second Engineer compares the barge measurements with the ship's measurements; if there is a discrepancy (short delivery, expansion tricks through heating), a Letter of Protest is issued. Air pockets (gas pocket / froth) can artificially inflate the quantity; time is therefore allowed beforehand for the fuel to stabilize.
Storage tanktan settling tanka, oradan s: Fuel transfer from storage tank to settling tank and from there to service tank is done in a planned and supervised manner. The Second Engineer verifies the transfer pump, heating and valve line-up; a valve wrongly left open can overflow a tank or unintentionally mix two different grades (commingling). During transfer the level is monitored; when it is complete, the valves are closed and the status is written in the log.
Settling tank, su ve katı kalıntının çök: The settling tank allows water and solid residues to settle out; the water/sludge at the bottom is removed by regular draining. The service tank is the clean fuel tank that feeds the engine directly; it is fed continuously by the purifier and its level is kept high. The Second Engineer routinely checks the draining and temperature of both tanks.
Santrifüj separatör, yoğunluk farkıyla y: A centrifugal separator separates water and solid residues from the fuel by the difference in density. For efficient separation, the feed temperature must be correct (typically 98°C for HFO), the throughput low (lower still if the density is high) and the gravity disc correctly selected (automatic water discharge on modern clarifiers). The Second Engineer monitors separation quality (water/sludge removed and clarity of the outlet).
Modern separatörler purifier/clarifier m: Modern separators perform automatic water monitoring and self-cleaning (sludge discharge) in purifier/clarifier mode. Series operation (two units) increases separation security for heavy fuels (high density/water content).
Ana makine sistem yağı (sump), cylinder: Main engine system oil (sump), cylinder oil, generator oil and gear/turbocharger oils are monitored separately. The Second Engineer follows daily consumption and the sump level; excessive consumption is a sign of leakage, burning (blow-by) or contamination. The top-up plan is based on ROB and voyage duration; LO bunkers (drums or bulk) are requested in good time.
Sistem yağı periyodik analiz edilir (vis: System oil is analyzed periodically (viscosity, BN/TBN, water, wear metals). Water or fuel contamination is a sign of a cooler leak or poor combustion; the main engine LO separator (purifier) is kept running continuously to remove water/residues.
Cylinder lub feed rate (g/kWh), yakıt sü: The cylinder lube feed rate (g/kWh) is adjusted according to the fuel sulfur content and load; with low-sulfur fuel a high-BN oil causes excessive deposits, while with high-sulfur fuel a low-BN oil causes corrosion. This adjustment is generally made together with scrape-down analysis (see the relevant task section). The Second Engineer maintains the balance between feed rate and fuel quality.
Laboratuvar sonucu spec dışı (yüksek su,: If the laboratory result is off-spec (high water, cat fines, low flash point, stability problem), the Second Engineer informs the Chief Engineer immediately; if possible, the fuel is quarantined (not used), a Letter of Protest/claim is raised with the supplier and the company's technical department becomes involved. If the fuel has to be used, separation is intensified and the equipment is closely monitored.
Farklı kaynaklı yakıtların karışımı çökm: Mixing fuels from different sources can cause sedimentation/sludging (asphaltene precipitation). Where possible, the Second Engineer keeps new fuel in a separate tank; if mixing is unavoidable, a compatibility test is carried out. Fuel whose stability has broken down clogs filters/purifiers and leads to loss of fuel supply.
Bunker, dahili transfer, separatör sludg: Bunkering, internal transfers, separator sludge, settling tank draining and the other relevant fuel operations are entered in the Oil Record Book Part I. Entries are made completely and on time, with date, tank, quantity and operation code. The Second Engineer oversees the accuracy of the entries together with the Chief Engineer; ORB inconsistencies are among the most common PSC/USCG findings.
BDN'ler ve MARPOL numuneleri kurala uygu: BDNs and MARPOL samples are retained for the period required by the rules; the time/position of the changeover on entering/leaving an ECA is entered in a separate log. These records are evidence both of MARPOL Annex VI compliance and in fuel disputes.
Yakıt ve yağ operasyonları, makine daire: Fuel and oil operations are the most sensitive work of the engine room, both environmentally and technically. Disciplined preparation, continuous supervision and honest records prevent marine pollution and heavy penalties on the one hand, and protect the main engine from the abrasive effects of poor-quality fuel on the other. The Second Engineer's care in this area directly determines both the ship's environmental record and the service life of its machinery.
Geleneksel düzende makine dairesi 7/24 v: In the conventional arrangement, the engine room is manned 24/7 on watches: typically a watchkeeping engineer and an oiler are on duty in 4-on/8-off periods. On ships approved for UMS (Unattended Machinery Space), the engine room may be left unmanned at night; in that case a comprehensive alarm system, the dead-man alarm and the duty engineer call system come into operation. The Second Engineer decides which arrangement is to be applied according to the voyage profile and class approval.
UMS'te \"duty engineer\" rotasyonu kurul: Under UMS, a "duty engineer" rotation is set up; the engineer on duty is always reachable, keeps the alarm panel/pager at hand and checks the engine room on periodic rounds. The validity of UMS depends on all safety alarms and standby systems being in working order.
Liman manevrası, dar su geçişi, ağır hav: During port maneuvering, narrow water transits, heavy weather and critical operations, the engine room goes to "stand-by engine" status; the engine room is fully manned on watch, the main engine is taken from UMS to manual control and the duty engineer stands by at the engine controls. The Second Engineer coordinates these changes with the bridge program and adjusts the watch schedule to suit the maneuvering requirements.
İkinci Mühendis, mevcut kadroyu (Üçüncü/: The Second Engineer assigns the available personnel (Third/Fourth Engineer, fitter, oilers) to watches according to their competence and certification. It is essential that each watch has adequate competence (a competent watchkeeper), that the balance between experienced and inexperienced personnel is maintained and that language/communication barriers are overcome. The watch bill is drawn up so as not to breach the rest hour rules.
Çizelge, gemiye katılım/iniş (crew chang: The watch bill is updated for crew changes (joining/leaving), leave and sickness. No watch is left uncovered; if there is a shortage of personnel, the Chief Engineer and the company are informed and a temporary arrangement is made (e.g. reducing the workload, making use of the port stay).
Vardiya çizelgesi makine kontrol odası v: The watch bill is posted in the engine control room and in a common area, where everyone can read it. Changes are entered with signature/approval. The Second Engineer makes sure that every person knows their own watch, their responsibilities and their emergency duty (consistent with the muster list).
Vardiya teslimi yapılandırılmış olmalıdı: The watch handover must be structured: the condition of the machinery, equipment running/on standby, ongoing maintenance/bypasses, alarms and temporary arrangements, fuel/oil status, bilge level, expected operations (maneuvering, bunkering) and instructions from the bridge are handed over. The relieving engineer does not take over the watch without physically verifying the condition of the equipment.
İkinci Mühendis, devir standardını (chec: The Second Engineer sets the handover standard (checklist/format) and checks that it is applied. "Verbal, incomplete" handovers are a main source of errors; in particular, if a bypassed protection or an ongoing isolation is not handed over, an accident results.
Her vardiya; ana makine devri, yük, egzo: Each watch enters in the engine log the main engine rpm, load, exhaust temperatures, pressures, fuel consumption, auxiliary machinery status, alarms/events and the actions taken. The Second Engineer reviews the daily logs, reports abnormalities to the Chief Engineer and has missing/inconsistent entries corrected.
Personelin asgari dinlenme saatleri yasa: The minimum rest hours of personnel are protected by law: at least 10 hours of rest in any 24-hour period and at least 77 hours in any 7-day period; rest may be divided into no more than two periods, one of which must be at least 6 hours uninterrupted, and the interval between consecutive periods of rest must not exceed 14 hours. The Second Engineer draws up the watch and maintenance plan so as not to breach these limits.
Rest-hours kayıtları (work/rest record): Rest-hours records (work/rest record) are kept daily and signed by the crew member and the person responsible; where there is a violation, its reason and how it was compensated are recorded. These records are examined during PSC and MLC inspections; systematic violation is a serious finding.
Yorgunluk; dikkat dağınıklığı, gecikmiş: Fatigue shows up as distraction, delayed reactions, more errors and impaired decision-making, and it can be fatal in the engine room. The Second Engineer gives priority to rest after busy port stays and consecutive maneuvers, does not give critical jobs to fatigued personnel and spreads the workload evenly across the team. A workload piled onto one person is both a violation and an accident risk.
Garanti edilen mesai dışındaki çalışma (: Work outside the guaranteed hours (overtime) is recorded and paid according to the contract/CBA. The Second Engineer makes sure that overtime is distributed fairly and does not breach the rest-hour rule. Excessive overtime is both a fatigue problem and a morale problem; if it has a structural cause (insufficient manning), it is escalated to the company through the Chief Engineer.
Çalışma/dinlenme ve overtime kayıtları t: Work/rest and overtime records must be consistent; the engine log, watch bill, maintenance records and rest-hours records must not contradict each other. Before an MLC/PSC inspection, the Second Engineer checks that these records are consistent. Contradictory records produce a finding and also a loss of trust.
Gemiye yeni katılan personel, vardiyaya: Personnel newly joining the ship receive engine room familiarization before they start keeping watch: escape routes, emergency duties, critical equipment, alarms and communications. The Second Engineer ensures that everyone clearly knows their job description and reporting line. Unclear responsibility leaves a "nobody was responsible" gap when an accident happens.
Çok uluslu ekiplerde ortak dil (working: In multinational crews, a common language (working language) and open communication reduce accidents. The Second Engineer strengthens the safety culture by encouraging a fair distribution of work, respectful leadership and everyone's right to say "stop" (stop-work authority). Reported errors/near-misses are not punished; they are turned into learning (just culture).
Manevra, ağır hava, bunker ve kritik bak: In situations such as maneuvering, heavy weather, bunkering and critical maintenance, additional personnel are called to duty. The Second Engineer plans these call-outs in advance (e.g. adjusting rest according to the port arrival time) and keeps the arrangement consistent with the emergency muster list. In an emergency, the engine room roles (fire team, bilge/flooding, blackout recovery) are clearly assigned.
Düzenli tatbikatlar (engine room fire, b: Regular drills (engine room fire, blackout, flooding, enclosed space rescue) are planned so that they do not clash with the watch arrangement, and personnel from every watch take part. After each drill, the Second Engineer feeds the lessons learned back into the watchkeeping procedures.
İyi yönetilen bir vardiya düzeni, makine: A well-managed watch system is the engine room's "invisible safeguard": a competent person is on duty at all times, handovers are complete, personnel are rested and the records reflect reality. The Second Engineer's leadership here protects legal compliance, safety and team morale at the same time. A disciplined routine is where an accident is prevented before it happens.
Makine dairesi; sıcak yüzeyler (egzoz ma: The engine room is a high-risk space where hot surfaces (exhaust manifold, turbine, boiler), high-pressure fuel/oil lines and electrical equipment are found together. A fuel/oil leak dripping onto a hot surface is the main fire scenario of SOLAS II-2 and the leading cause of engine room fires. Housekeeping is the first line of defense that reduces the "ignition probability" of this scenario.
İyi housekeeping aynı zamanda kayma, tak: Good housekeeping also prevents slip, trip and fall (slip-trip-fall) accidents. An oil film building up on the floor plates, scattered tools or loose hoses can cause serious injuries, especially when the ship is moving. The Second Engineer proactively identifies and eliminates these risks during the daily round.
PSC ve özellikle vetting denetimlerinde: In PSC inspections and especially in vetting inspections (SIRE 2.0, CDI), the condition of the engine room is an item that is scored directly and sets the overall impression. Oil-soaked insulation, dirty bilges, unlabeled chemical drums and obstructed escape routes are frequently seen non-conformity headings.
İkinci Mühendis, denetim öncesi bir \"de: Rather than a "deep clean" before an inspection, the Second Engineer aims for continuous, standard order. An inspector can easily tell whether the order is "natural" or "last-minute cosmetics" from the way the hoses are coiled, the tool board and the bottom of the bilges.
İkinci Mühendis, sızıntıları \"drip\", \: The Second Engineer classifies leaks as "drip", "weep" and "spray". A small leak dripping into a drip tray can be monitored, whereas a spray leak from a pressurized line requires immediate action, because atomized fuel can ignite instantly on a hot surface. The source of the leak (flange, fitting, pump gland, injector) is tagged and a work order is raised in the PMS.
Geçici çözüm (clamp, drip tray) ile kalı: A clear distinction is kept between a temporary fix (clamp, drip tray) and a permanent repair (gasket, gland packing, renewal of the line). A temporary arrangement is always recorded and passed on at handover, because a forgotten "temporary" fix is the most frequent cause of fire.
Tüm pompa, filtre ve flanş bölgelerinde: Save-alls (drip trays) are fitted at all pump, filter and flange areas and are drained regularly; a full drip tray overflows and contaminates the bilge. The Second Engineer ensures that the drip trays drain not into the bilge but into the appropriate sludge/oil collecting line.
Emici pad ve granül stoğu erişilebilir t: A stock of absorbent pads and granules is kept accessible; however, contaminated absorbent material, as oily waste (oily rag), carries a risk of spontaneous combustion, so it is collected in a metal container with a lid and disposed of properly. Oily rags left lying in the open are a cause of fire in themselves.
İkinci Mühendis, bilge well seviyelerini: The Second Engineer monitors the bilge well levels and the operation of the high-level bilge alarms daily. A rising bilge level is the warning sign of a leak (seawater, cooling water, oil) and is followed up until the source is found. Bilge pumping records are kept consistent with the ORB under MARPOL Annex I.
Sintine içeriğinin yağ oranı önemlidir;: The oil content of the bilge water matters; excessively oily bilge water clogs the OWS and makes it harder to achieve 15 ppm. For this reason, housekeeping (preventing oil leaks at the source) is also a precondition for environmental compliance.
Periyodik sintine temizliği planlanır; s: Periodic bilge cleaning is planned; the oil removed is transferred to the appropriate sludge/bilge holding tank. Work in the bilges often carries an enclosed/confined space risk (low O2, hydrocarbon vapor); gas testing, ventilation and, where necessary, a permit are applied.
Yetersiz aydınlatma; hatalı okuma, kaza: Poor lighting means misreadings, accidents and incomplete maintenance. The Second Engineer ensures that light fittings that are not working are replaced immediately, especially the lamps at the maneuvering console, in the boiler room and along the walkways.
Acil aydınlatma ve kaçış yolu işaretleme: Emergency lighting and escape route marking (photoluminescent / battery-backed) are tested regularly. In a blackout scenario, the emergency lighting coming on is critical for the crew to escape safely.
Makine dairesi ventilasyonu hem yanma ha: Engine room ventilation is critical both for combustion air and for personnel; clogged intake grilles and dirty filters adversely affect both engine performance and the ambient temperature. The Second Engineer includes the cleaning of the ventilation and the hoods in the housekeeping program.
Yüksek gürültülü bölgelerde işaretleme v: In high-noise areas, warning signs and access to hearing protection are provided (as required by MLC for the working environment). Build-up of dust, soot and leaking steam is cleaned regularly, which reduces both the respiratory risk and the fire risk.
Makine dairesinde en az iki bağımsız kaç: The engine room has at least two independent escape routes, and these must be unobstructed at all times. The Second Engineer ensures that tools, materials, hoses or temporary storage left in passageways are removed immediately; an escape route is never a storage area.
Escape trunk kapıları, korkuluklar ve me: The condition of the escape trunk doors, handrails and ladder steps is checked. In a fire or flooding emergency, seconds matter; a blocked escape route can have fatal consequences.
Taşınabilir yangın söndürücüler, EEBD (E: Portable fire extinguishers, EEBDs (Emergency Escape Breathing Device), fire stations and quick-closing valve controls are kept clear, marked and accessible. A fire station with materials piled in front of it is as good as no fire station at all.
İkinci Mühendis, acil kapatma (emergency: During the housekeeping round, the Second Engineer verifies that the emergency shutdown points (emergency stop, remote shut-off, quick-closing valve) can be reached at all times. These points are marked consistently with the muster list and the fire plan.
Alet panosunda \"her aletin bir yeri\" i: The "a place for every tool" principle is applied on the tool board (shadow board); a missing tool is visible at once and shows that a job has been left unfinished or that a tool has been forgotten inside the machinery (FOD risk). The workshop bench and the grinding/lathe area are kept clean and free of swarf.
Yedek parçalar, deniz hareketine karşı e: Spare parts are stowed secured against the ship's motion (lashing/racks) and protected from moisture; heavy parts are kept on the lower shelves. The location of critical spares must be labeled and consistent with the stock records, so that no time is lost in an emergency breakdown.
Boiler/cooling water kimyasalları, solve: Boiler/cooling water chemicals, solvents, paints and oils are labeled, their MSDS/SDS are kept accessible and they are stored in suitable compartments. Incompatible chemicals are kept apart; a spill kit is kept ready in case of spillage.
Yağlı atık, sludge, kullanılmış filtre v: Oily waste, sludge, used filters and garbage are segregated under MARPOL Annex I/V. The Second Engineer makes sure that engine room waste is taken to the proper collection points and that the delivery records are kept.
İkinci Mühendis, makine dairesini bölgel: The Second Engineer divides the engine room into zones and assigns responsibility for the cleanliness and order of each zone to the watch engineers and the oilmen/wipers. Daily, weekly and monthly housekeeping tasks are tracked with the PMS or a checklist; this clear ownership avoids the "everybody's job is nobody's job" trap.
Düzenli \"engine room walk-round\" sıras: During the regular "engine room walk-round", findings are recorded, photographed and followed up until closed. Housekeeping is managed not as a one-off clean-up but as a routine that is continuously improved.
Housekeeping bulguları ve kapanışları ka: Housekeeping findings and their close-outs are recorded; during an inspection these records are the ship's evidence of "due diligence". At the watch handover, the Second Engineer passes on open housekeeping jobs, leaks being monitored and temporary arrangements in writing.
Denetim öncesi panik temizliği yerine sü: The aim is a continuous standard rather than a panic clean-up before an inspection; even so, a preliminary check round is made to clear critical findings such as oily insulation, blocked escape routes and unlabeled chemicals.
Makine dairesi housekeeping'i, İkinci Mü: Engine room housekeeping is the most visible and most continuous test of the Second Engineer's leadership quality. Disciplined order reduces the risk of fire and accidents, makes environmental compliance easier, increases equipment reliability and shapes a positive impression of the ship at every inspection. A well-managed engine room marks the ship as "well operated" before a single record has been examined.
Boiler water treatment, kazan suyu kalit: Boiler water treatment prevents corrosion and scale formation by keeping the boiler water quality (pH, alkalinity, chloride, conductivity) within the correct range. Regular blow-down (bottom/surface blow-down) removes accumulated deposits and sludge. The Second Engineer manages these tests and the chemical dosing.
Kazan safety valve'i, aşırı basınca karş: The boiler safety valve is the last safeguard against overpressure and is tested/adjusted regularly. The flame failure device prevents an explosion by shutting off the fuel if the flame is lost. The Second Engineer verifies that these safety devices are working; if one of them is defective, the boiler cannot be operated safely.
Yakıt/yağ separatörleri (purifier), su v: Fuel/lube oil separators (purifiers) supply clean fuel/lube oil by separating out water and solid particles. The Second Engineer plans bowl/disc cleaning, gasket replacement and overhaul; correct gravity disc selection and correct operating parameters are critical. The backwash/desludge system is checked regularly.
Bakımsız bir purifier, su/partikül geçiş: A poorly maintained purifier lets water/particles pass through and leads to wear in the engine fuel system. A well-maintained separator directly protects the fuel quality and, through it, the health of the main engine.
Start hava kompresörleri, ana makine sta: The starting air compressors supply compressed air for starting the main engine. The Second Engineer manages valve maintenance, intercooler/aftercooler cleaning, the automatic drains and checks of the safety devices (relief valve, fusible plug). Excessive temperature and oil carry-over can create a risk of explosion in the air receivers.
İkinci Mühendis, yardımcı sistem bakımla: The Second Engineer plans auxiliary system maintenance according to the PMS schedule and the operating program; because some maintenance is done with the equipment stopped, it is timed to fit the port or sea passage window. Spare parts and tools are prepared in advance.
Yardımcı sistemlerde bakım öncesi LOTO u: Before maintenance on auxiliary systems, LOTO is applied, pressure is released and hot surfaces are allowed to cool. Boilers and pressurized systems need special care; no work is started until the isolation has been verified.
Kazan, separatör ve hava kompresörü bakı: Boiler, separator and air compressor maintenance is the Second Engineer's daily discipline that keeps the engine room safe and efficient. Correct water treatment, working safety devices and well-maintained auxiliary systems protect both safety and the health of the main engine together.
Denize yağlı su deşarjı çok katı kuralla: Discharge of oily water to sea is subject to very strict rules, and violations are punished most severely. The Second Engineer knows that no shortcut is acceptable in this area; bypasses such as a "magic pipe" are both a crime and an act that destroys the reputation of the ship and the company.
OWS, bilge suyundaki yağı ayırarak yalnı: The OWS separates the oil from the bilge water so that only water below 15 ppm is discharged to sea (under permitted conditions). If the limit is exceeded, the 15 ppm oil content meter automatically stops the discharge and returns the water to the bilge tank (three-way valve). The Second Engineer ensures that the OWS and the alarm work correctly and without any bypass.
Yakıt/yağ arıtımından ve kaçaklardan olu: Sludge produced by fuel/lube oil treatment and by leaks is collected in the sludge tank and either burned in an approved incinerator or delivered to a shore reception facility in port. The Second Engineer monitors sludge generation, the tank level and disposal, and ensures that sludge never gets into the sea.
Her yağ işlemi (bilge transfer, OWS deşa: Every oil operation (bilge transfer, OWS discharge, sludge incineration/delivery, internal transfer) is entered in ORB Part I correctly, on time and in a way that reflects what actually happened. The Second Engineer ensures that the ORB is consistent with the physical operations (tank levels, meter readings). ORB inconsistencies are among the most frequent causes of penalties/detention at PSC.
Bir yağ kaçağı/dökülmesi durumunda SOPEP: In the event of an oil leak/spill, the SOPEP is activated; the response equipment (absorbents, booms), the notification list (coastal State, company, P&I) and the initial response steps are applied. The Second Engineer takes part in the rapid response and notification for leaks originating in the engine room.
Bilge, sludge ve çevresel deşarj yönetim: Bilge, sludge and environmental discharge management is the Second Engineer's most sensitive responsibility, both legally and ethically. An OWS without any bypass, an honest ORB and correct sludge disposal protect the sea, keep the ship away from heavy penalties and uphold the environmental integrity of the seafaring profession.
Makine dairesinde güvenlik, ekibin ekipm: Safety in the engine room depends on the team knowing the equipment and the risks. The Second Engineer sees training not as a formality but as the foundation of accident prevention and operational continuity. A well-trained team acts correctly both in routine work and in an emergency.
Yeni gelen mühendis/tayfa; makine daires: Newly joined engineers/ratings are briefed on their first day on the engine room layout, emergency exits, locations of safety equipment (EEBD, fire extinguishers, emergency stops), alarm signals and basic procedures. The Second Engineer carries out this familiarization and completes the checklist.
İkinci Mühendis; LOTO (enerji izolasyonu: The Second Engineer teaches the team the LOTO (energy isolation), Permit to Work, enclosed space entry and hot work procedures, and explains with examples why these high-risk jobs are subject to strict rules. A team that knows "why" it follows a procedure takes it seriously.
Bazı ekipmanlar (otomasyon, purifier, öz: Some equipment (automation, purifiers, special pumps, BWMS) requires manufacturer-specific knowledge. The Second Engineer coordinates access to the vendor manuals and training, and makes sure that the team uses the equipment correctly and does not damage it through incorrect intervention.
İkinci Mühendis; blackout recovery (kara: The Second Engineer takes part in blackout recovery (recovery from a blackout/loss of electrical power), engine room fire and flooding drills and trains the team. When these scenarios are drilled realistically, the team carries out the right actions in a real incident without having to think. Use of the quick-closing valves, emergency stops and the fixed extinguishing system is drilled.
Makine personeli eğitimi, İkinci Mühendi: Training of engine personnel is the most valuable investment the Second Engineer makes in the team and in the safety of the ship. Proper familiarization, sound safety training and realistic emergency drills make the engine room both efficient in routine operation and resilient in a crisis.
Şartlandırılmamış soğutma suyu, motor iç: Untreated cooling water causes corrosion, cavitation damage and mineral deposits (scale) on the internal surfaces of the engine (liner, cylinder cover, cooling passages). A corrosion inhibitor (DCA — nitrite-based, etc.) prevents this damage. The Second Engineer protects the internal integrity of the engine by keeping the water within the correct range.
İkinci Mühendis; nitrit (inhibitor seviy: The Second Engineer tests nitrite (inhibitor level), pH (acidity/alkalinity), chloride (indicator of a seawater leak) and total hardness. Low nitrite means insufficient corrosion protection; high chloride points to a seawater leak from the cooler. Each parameter is kept within its criteria range.
Klorür değerinde ani artış, cooler'da bi: A sudden rise in the chloride value indicates a seawater leak in a cooler and is investigated. A seawater leak both accelerates corrosion and reduces cooling efficiency; early detection prevents major damage.
İkinci Mühendis, gemi test kiti ile düze: The Second Engineer carries out regular (usually weekly) tests with the ship's test kit and records the results in the log. If the nitrite/inhibitor level is low, the calculated quantity of DCA/corrosion inhibitor is added. The correct quantity matters, because overdosing can also cause waste and side effects.
Gemi test kiti temel parametreleri verir: The ship's test kit gives the basic parameters; for a comprehensive analysis, samples are periodically sent to a shore-side laboratory. The lab report verifies the shipboard tests and reveals more subtle problems (e.g. microbiological ones).
Sonuçların trendi, ani bir sapmadan (kaç: The trend of the results gives more information than a single sudden deviation (leak, dosing error). By following how the parameters develop over time, the Second Engineer catches problems early. Regular records form the basis both for maintenance decisions and for inspections.
Soğutma sistemine eklenen makyaj suyu (m: Make-up water added to the cooling system must be low in chloride (usually distilled/evaporator water); otherwise every addition brings in chloride/hardness. The Second Engineer monitors the make-up water source and the expansion tank level.
Soğutma suyu analizi ve dozajlama, İkinc: Cooling water analysis and dosing is a discipline through which the Second Engineer protects the internal health of the engine "out of sight". Correct water chemistry, early leak detection and trend monitoring prevent liner/cover corrosion and secure a long service life for the main engine and the generators.
