Doğrama sırasında \"köprü tutuş\" ve doğ: When chopping, the "bridge hold" and correct cutting technique are used, and fingers are kept clear of the blade. In heavy weather, chopping is postponed or reduced where possible; knife control becomes difficult when the ship is rolling. In the event of a cut, the food is contaminated and first aid is given.
Kamarot, aşçının talimatıyla basit ön ha: On the cook's instructions, the steward does simple preparation: washing, peeling and chopping vegetables and fruit, weighing ingredients and taking them out of the refrigerator. Vegetables are washed thoroughly to remove dirt and any residues; this is part of food safety. Chopping is done to the size and arrangement the cook requires.
Hazırlanan malzeme, kullanılana kadar uy: Prepared ingredients are kept at a suitable temperature until they are used; ingredients left at room temperature for a long time enter the danger zone. Raw meat/poultry is prepared last or in a separate area, and surfaces are sanitized afterwards.
Buzdolabı ve dondurucu düzeni gıda güven: The organization of refrigerators and freezers is fundamental to food safety. Raw food is always stored on the bottom shelf (so that drips do not contaminate cooked food), and cooked/ready-to-eat food on the top shelf. Storage follows the "FIFO" (first in, first out) principle: what arrives first is used first, and older stock is moved to the front. Opened food is transferred to a covered container and labeled (with the date).
Buzdolabı sıcaklığı (0-5°C) ve dondurucu: Refrigerator (0-5°C) and freezer (≤ -18°C) temperatures are checked regularly; doors are not left open for long. Products that are past their expiry date or spoiled are set aside and reported to the cook. A well-organized cold store prevents both safety problems and waste of stock.
Servis ve hazırlık sonrası tüm çalışma y: After service and preparation, all work surfaces (worktops, cutting area), the area around the range, the sink and touch points are cleaned and sanitized. Food-contact surfaces are cleaned with green-coded equipment. Grease build-up is removed; accumulated grease is both a hygiene and a fire risk.
Mikrodalga, fırın, mikser, et kıyma maki: Equipment such as the microwave, oven, mixer and meat mincer is cleaned after use; equipment that can be dismantled is taken apart and washed. Care is taken with hot surfaces, and electrical equipment is unplugged before cleaning.
Davlumbaz (galley range hood) ve yağ fil: The galley range hood and grease filters are cleaned regularly; accumulated grease is the most common cause of galley fires. A greasy filter can catch fire and carry the fire into the ventilation duct. This cleaning is done weekly/on a schedule and is never neglected.
Yer giderleri (floor drains) ve evye süz: Floor drains and sink strainers are cleared regularly; a blocked drain causes odors and standing water (slipping hazard) and attracts pests. Pouring grease down the drain causes blockages; grease is collected separately.
Galley iş kazaları açısından geminin en: The galley is one of the riskiest areas of the ship for occupational accidents: hot surfaces, boiling liquids, hot oil and sharp tools all come together. Hot pans are carried with gloves, boiling water is poured off carefully, and water is never poured onto hot oil. The floor is not left wet/greasy; non-slip shoes are worn.
Ağır havada galley operasyonu özel riskt: Galley operation in heavy weather is a particular risk: a pot of boiling liquid tipped over by rolling causes serious burns. In bad weather, range fiddles (pot clamps) are used, pans are only partly filled and high-risk cooking/chopping is reduced. In these conditions, the steward moves more slowly and uses grab rails/handrails.
Galley'de yağ/fritöz yangınına asla su i: In the galley, water is never used on a cooking oil/deep-fryer fire; water makes the hot oil erupt, spreading the fire and causing serious burns. In a cooking oil fire, the heat source is cut off, a fire blanket or an extinguisher of the appropriate class is used (a special extinguisher is usually provided in the galley) and the alarm is raised immediately.
Yıkanan ve kurutulan tabaklar, bardaklar: Washed and dried plates, glasses, cutlery and serving dishes are put away in their correct places in tidy, clean cupboards. Items put away damp pick up stains and germs; thorough drying is essential. Well-organized crockery storage allows the next service to start quickly and hygienically.
Servis kaşıkları, maşalar ve özel servis: Serving spoons, tongs and special serving utensils are cleaned and kept separate. Broken/cracked plates and glasses are removed from use; a cracked surface carries the risk of both injury and harboring bacteria.
Bulaşık alanı her vardiya sonunda temizl: The dishwashing area is cleaned at the end of each working period; the sink, worktop and floor are sanitized. Food waste is separated in accordance with MARPOL Annex V and emptied without delay. Cooking oil and grease are collected separately and are not poured down the drain. A tidy dishwashing area is the measure of the galley's overall hygiene.
Bulaşık ve mutfak desteği görünürde sıra: Dishwashing and galley support may look ordinary, but they are in fact the cornerstone of food safety on board. A correctly washed plate, a correctly separated cutting board and a clean galley quietly prevent an outbreak. Doing this task meticulously protects both the health of the crew and the ship's uninterrupted voyage.
Gemi çamaşırhanesi (ship's laundry) tipi: The ship's laundry typically contains industrial or semi-industrial washing machines, a tumble dryer, an iron/ironing board, laundry trolleys and a bag system that keeps dirty and clean laundry apart. The steward sets up a one-way workflow: "dirty in → sorting → washing → drying → folding/ironing → clean out". The paths of dirty and clean laundry never cross; this is the basic principle for preventing cross-contamination.
Çamaşır toplama programı genellikle yata: The laundry collection schedule is usually weekly for bedding and as needed for uniforms and personal laundry. Depending on the ship's practice, officers' and ratings' laundry may be tracked with separate schedules or labeling, but the hygiene standard is the same for both. The steward applies the labeling/bagging system meticulously so as not to mix up which laundry has come from which cabin.
MLC 2006 Regulation 3.1 ve Standard A3.1: MLC 2006 Regulation 3.1 and Standard A3.1 require suitable facilities on board for the crew to wash their laundry and maintain personal hygiene. Keeping the laundry working, clean and accessible is the employer's obligation; the steward is the one who delivers this facility on the ground. A broken washing machine or a dirty laundry is a direct finding (deficiency) in an MLC inspection.
Temiz yatak takımı ve havlu sağlamak, sa: Providing clean bedding and towels is not just a matter of comfort but of health. Textiles that are not changed regularly, are poorly dried or are moldy cause skin infections, allergies and respiratory problems. The steward manages these risks by keeping the laundry cycle running without interruption.
Yıkama öncesi ayrıştırma, hem çamaşırın: Sorting before washing determines both the life of the laundry and the standard of hygiene. Whites and light colors are separated from dark colors; otherwise color bleeding spoils the whole load. Fabric types are also separated: delicates, towels, sheets and uniforms require different programs and temperatures. Heavily soiled or oily work clothes are never washed in the same load as clean textiles.
Kirlilik düzeyi ayrıştırmanın kritik boy: The degree of soiling is a critical aspect of sorting. Laundry from sick crew members, textiles contaminated with blood/body fluids and oily clothes from the galley/deck are collected separately and processed separately. This separation prevents cross-contamination and the spread of infection. Pockets are checked before items go into the washing machine; a forgotten lighter, pen or metal object can ruin both the laundry and the machine.
Bazı lekeler (kan, çay/kahve, yağ, mürek: Some stains (blood, tea/coffee, oil/grease, ink) do not come out in a normal wash; pre-treatment is required. The type of stain is identified and the appropriate pre-treatment is applied: protein-based stains (blood) are treated with cold water, because hot water coagulates the protein and sets the stain. Oil-based stains, on the other hand, need pre-treatment and a higher temperature.
Ön işlem kimyasalları da kontrollü kulla: Pre-treatment chemicals are also used in a controlled way; too much bleach wears out fabric and causes yellowing/thinning. The steward avoids the "bleach for every stain" approach, applies the right product to the right stain and follows the washing instructions on the fabric care label.
Deterjan dozajı, su sertliği ve çamaşır: Detergent dosage is adjusted according to water hardness and the amount of laundry. Too much detergent is not fully removed in rinsing; it leaves residues in textiles, irritates the skin and damages the machine. Too little detergent weakens cleaning and disinfection. The steward follows the dosage instructions on the product label and the machine capacity; measured use, rather than "guesswork", is essential.
Yumuşatıcı (fabric softener) konfor sağl: Fabric softener adds comfort but, as it reduces the absorbency of towels, it is used sparingly on towels. Bleach (sodium hypochlorite) is used in a controlled way, only on whites and where disinfection is needed; it fades colors and wears out fabric. The most critical rule: bleach is never used together with acid-based products, as toxic chlorine gas is released.
Çamaşır makinesi ne aşırı doldurulur ne: A washing machine is neither overfilled nor underloaded. An overfilled machine does not wash or rinse properly; too small a load wastes water and energy. Laundry is put in loosely, not packed in. The program is selected according to the fabric type and degree of soiling; a high temperature disinfects but damages delicate textiles.
Gemide tatlı su ve enerji sınırlı kaynak: On board, fresh water and energy are limited resources. The steward avoids starting unnecessary cycles before a full load has been collected; this means saving water/energy and reducing the generator load. When washing is complete, laundry is not left in the machine; it produces damp and odors.
Kurutucu (tumble dryer), çamaşırı hızlı: The tumble dryer dries laundry quickly, but incorrect use puts both the textiles and the machine at risk. Excessive heat shrinks delicate fabrics and damages the fibers; an overfilled dryer dries unevenly and wastes energy. The temperature is selected according to the fabric type, and delicate textiles are dried at low heat or hung up.
Kurutucudan çıkan çamaşır tamamen kuruma: Laundry from the dryer is not folded and put in lockers until it is completely dry; damp textiles produce mold and odors. The steward checks that laundry is dry before folding it and processes again any items that are still damp.
Çamaşırhanedeki en ciddi yangın riski, k: The most serious fire risk in the laundry is the combustible fluff that builds up in the dryer's lint filter and exhaust duct. Accumulated lint can be ignited by the dryer's heat and lead to a fire on board; P&I and loss prevention records frequently report laundry fires caused by lint. The lint filter is therefore cleaned after EVERY cycle, and the exhaust duct is checked periodically.
Ütüleme, kumaş tipine göre sıcaklık ayar: Ironing requires the temperature to be set according to the fabric type: cotton is ironed at high heat and synthetics at low heat; the wrong temperature melts synthetic fabric or yellows and scorches cotton. The ironing board is set up properly, the iron is left standing upright, and it is never left switched on and unattended while hot. The risk of burns with a steam iron is high; care is taken with the water reservoir and steam vents.
Ütü, kullanılmadığında mutlaka fişten çe: When not in use, the iron is always unplugged and left to cool. A hot iron forgotten on fabric or a combustible surface is one of the common causes of laundry fires. After ironing, the steward makes sure the iron is switched off and unplugged and is not put away until it has cooled completely.
Temiz, kuru çamaşır düzgün katlanır ve s: Clean, dry laundry is folded neatly and returned correctly to its owner/cabin. The labeling or bagging system ensures that laundry does not get mixed up; it is particularly important for privacy and trust that personal laundry reaches the right person. Bedding is distributed to the relevant cabins, and the surplus is stored neatly in the clean linen locker.
Temiz çamaşır, kirli çamaşırın bulunduğu: Clean laundry is kept covered and separate from the area where dirty laundry is kept. Clean laundry is not put next to the dirty laundry trolley; this causes cross-contamination. The linen locker is kept clean, dry and tidy; clean laundry stored in a damp environment goes moldy.
Çamaşırhane ekipmanı, hijyen kaynağı old: Laundry equipment is a factor in hygiene, and it also needs maintenance. The washing machine drum is cleaned periodically with an empty high-temperature cycle or a machine cleaner; otherwise detergent residue, mold and bad odors build up. The detergent drawer and the door seal (door gasket) are cleaned regularly; these are the most common places for mold to grow.
Kurutucu lint filtresi her çevrimde, egz: The dryer lint filter is cleaned after every cycle and the exhaust duct periodically. If abnormal noise, vibration, a water leak or overheating is noticed in the engines, they are not operated, and this is reported to the engine crew/the person responsible for technical matters. The steward is responsible for basic cleaning and filter maintenance; electrical/mechanical faults are left to the authorized team.
Çamaşırhane mahalli her gün temizlenir;: The laundry space is cleaned every day; the floor is swept and mopped, worktops are wiped and lint/dust deposits are removed. Lint accumulating on the floor is both a slipping hazard and fuel for a fire. Drains and water outlets are checked for blockages; a blocked drain causes flooding and odors.
Çamaşırhane havalandırması önemlidir; ne: Ventilation of the laundry is important; a damp, hot environment produces mold and stuffy air. Ventilation grilles are kept clean, and moisture is removed by leaving the door/vent open. Laundry trolleys and bags are washed and disinfected regularly; equipment that carries dirty laundry is a carrier of bacteria.
Çamaşırhanenin kesintisiz çalışması, det: Uninterrupted operation of the laundry depends on detergent, softener, bleach, stain remover and pre-treatment products being kept in stock at all times. The steward sets a minimum stock level for these products and raises a resupply request when stock approaches that level. "Reporting when it runs out" is too late; running out of stock on long voyages stops the laundry cycle.
Stok takibi basit bir envanter listesiyl: Stock is tracked with a simple inventory list: product name, quantity on hand, rate of consumption and reorder point. By monitoring consumption, the steward forecasts how much is needed for a typical voyage and passes the resupply request to the person responsible for provisions (usually the chief cook or the Chief Officer).
Çamaşırhane kimyasalları (özellikle çama: Laundry chemicals (especially oxidizers such as bleach, and acid-based products) are stored separately and labeled, in accordance with the SDS information. Oxidizers (hypochlorite) and acids are kept on separate shelves; accidental contact between them causes a dangerous reaction. Chemicals are kept in their original labeled containers; decanting them into unlabeled containers is both misuse and a legal violation.
Depo havalandırılmış, gıdadan ve ısı kay: The store is kept ventilated and away from food and heat sources. In the event of a spill, the response instructions in the SDS are followed. The steward must know the dilution ratio, contact time and incompatibilities of every chemical used.
Bulaşıcı hastalık şüphesi olan veya kan/: Laundry from a suspected infectious case, or contaminated with blood/body fluids, is collected and processed separately without being mixed with other laundry. These textiles are handled with gloves, kept in a separate bag and washed at high temperature (above 60°C where possible) so that they are disinfected. Shaking them out is prohibited; shaking spreads microorganisms into the air. Afterwards, hands are washed and the equipment used is disinfected.
Norovirus, deri enfeksiyonları ve solunu: Norovirus, skin infections and respiratory pathogens spread easily via contaminated textiles. During outbreaks (COVID, norovirus, etc.), the laundry handling protocol is tightened: separate collection, high temperature, extra disinfection and increased use of personal protective equipment.
Kamarot, kirli çamaşır ve kimyasallarla: When working with dirty laundry and chemicals, the steward uses personal protective equipment: gloves and, when necessary, an apron and mask. Hands are always washed after handling laundry, and especially after contact with contaminated textiles. The laundry is kept physically and operationally separate from food preparation; the steward pays attention to hand hygiene when moving between the two.
Renk kodlu temizlik mantığı çamaşırhaney: The color-coded cleaning principle extends to the laundry as well: equipment used for contaminated textiles is not mixed with clean items. Laundry bags and trolleys are disinfected regularly; this equipment is an unseen but critical link in the hygiene chain.
Gemide tatlı su (fresh water) sınırlı ve: On board, fresh water is a limited and valuable resource; it is either bunkered or produced by the fresh water generator. Washing laundry consumes a lot of water, so running full loads, avoiding unnecessary cycles and choosing the correct program are the basis of saving water. Excessive rinsing wastes water; the correct detergent dosage gives adequate cleaning with less rinsing.
Çamaşır makinesi ve kurutucu yüksek ener: Washing machines and dryers draw a lot of power, and this power comes from the generators. Saving energy means saving fuel (bunkers) and reducing emissions. By planning laundry runs around the high-load periods of the bridge/engine room, the steward can help balance the electrical load.
Çamaşırhaneden çıkan ambalaj atığı (dete: Packaging waste from the laundry (detergent drums, plastic, cardboard) is separated in accordance with MARPOL Annex V. Plastic waste is never discharged into the sea; it is retained on board and landed in port. Empty chemical containers are handled according to the SDS instructions; some may fall into the hazardous waste category and are collected separately.
Lint atığı da düzenli toplanır; çöpe atı: Lint waste is also collected regularly; when it is disposed of, it is borne in mind that it is combustible, and it is kept away from heat/sources of ignition. By separating waste correctly, the steward contributes to the ship's compliance with the Garbage Management Plan.
Çamaşırhane hizmetleri, kamarotun mürett: Laundry services are among the steward's tasks that most directly affect crew welfare: clean bedding, dry towels and neat uniforms are a quiet but decisive part of the ship's quality of life. This task also has a serious safety dimension; the risk of lint fires and chemical mixing makes the laundry one of the hidden fire points on board. When correct sorting, chemical discipline, lint control and stock tracking come together, the laundry becomes a reliable part of both MLC compliance and fire safety. Maintaining the standard every day is the fundamental professional principle of the steward's job.
Sarf malzeme, hijyenin görünmeyen lojist: Consumables are the unseen logistics of hygiene. By ensuring that supplies are replenished before they run out, the steward guarantees that the accommodation stays clean and comfortable at all times. An item that is not requested in time may be unavailable for the whole voyage.
Kamarot; temizlik kimyasalları (deterjan: The steward monitors cleaning chemicals (detergent, disinfectant, glass/surface cleaner), paper products (toilet paper, paper towels), soap/hand sanitizer, laundry supplies and general accommodation consumables. The current stock (ROB) and rate of consumption of each item are recorded.
Stok minimuma yaklaşan kalemler için kam: For items whose stock is approaching the minimum, the steward prepares a requisition and passes it to the responsible officer (usually the Chief Officer/Master). The requisition contains the item, current stock, quantity required and urgency. Accurate forecasting prevents both shortages and unnecessary overstocking.
Temizlik kimyasalları, SDS bilgisine uyg: Cleaning chemicals are stored in accordance with the SDS information; incompatible chemicals (acids/alkalis, oxidizers) are kept apart and stored in labeled containers. The steward oversees safe storage and the integrity of labels; incorrect mixing can cause a dangerous reaction.
Kamarot, stok hareketlerini (ikmal, tüke: The steward records stock movements (resupply, consumption). This record shows the consumption trend and makes planning the next resupply easier. A regular inventory prevents both waste and shortages.
Sarf malzeme stok takibi, kamarotun yaşa: Tracking consumable stock is the unseen logistics that allows the steward to maintain hygiene in the accommodation without interruption. Knowing consumption, requesting in time and storing chemicals safely together protect hygiene, crew comfort and safety.
Gemi, kalabalık ve kapalı bir ortamdır;: A ship is a crowded, closed environment; an infection can spread quickly and is difficult to manage with limited medical facilities. By maintaining hygiene, the steward prevents illness at the outset. Clean accommodation is critical for health, morale and inspections alike.
Kamarot; banyo/tuvaletleri, ortak alanla: The steward regularly cleans and disinfects bathrooms/toilets, common areas (mess, saloon, alleyways) and high-touch surfaces (door handles, handrails, switches). The correct disinfectant is used with the correct contact time; a hasty wipe does not disinfect.
Yaşam mahalli çöpü ayrıştırılır ve MARPO: Garbage from the accommodation is separated and managed in accordance with MARPOL Annex V; food waste, plastics and other garbage are handled differently. The steward ensures that garbage is collected hygienically and delivered to the correct disposal point (incinerator/shore reception). Accumulated garbage creates both a hygiene and a pest risk.
COVID, norovirus gibi bulaşıcı hastalık: During periods of infectious disease risk such as COVID or norovirus, the frequency and intensity of cleaning are increased; high-touch surfaces are disinfected more often and, if there is isolation, the areas concerned are cleaned under a separate protocol. The steward applies these enhanced protocols meticulously; in an outbreak, hygiene is the first line of defense.
Salgın döneminde veya izolasyon alanı te: During an outbreak or when cleaning an isolation area, the steward uses suitable PPE (gloves, mask) and also protects their own health. Contaminated waste is collected separately. The steward's health is important for continuity of service.
Hijyen, haşere (hamamböceği, kemirgen) k: Hygiene is the basis of pest control (cockroaches, rodents); food scraps and dirt attract pests. The steward prevents pests through cleaning and reports any signs seen (droppings, tracks, live pests). The steward supports the pest management program (traps, bait).
Hijyen ve sağlık standartlarının korunma: Maintaining hygiene and health standards is the steward's direct contribution to the health of the crew. Regular cleaning, correct disinfection, garbage management and outbreak protocols are the most effective defense for preventing illness in a closed environment and keeping the accommodation healthy.
Acil durumda kamarot \"servis personeli\: In an emergency, the steward is not "service staff" but a crew member with assigned duties. The steward knows and carries out the role defined in the Station Bill. As one of the people who know the accommodation best, the steward can play a valuable role in evacuating it and in the head count.
Alarm çaldığında kamarot, can yeleğiyle: When the alarm sounds, the steward goes to the muster station with a lifejacket and carries out the assigned duty. The steward knows where the lifejacket is and how to put it on correctly, the alarm signals and the muster point. These basic skills are reinforced by repetition in drills.
Yaşam mahallindeki yangın kapıları (fire: Fire doors in the accommodation are kept closed; wedging them open allows fire/smoke to spread. Escape routes must be kept clear and unobstructed at all times. The steward follows these rules while working and corrects/reports violations (wedged doors, blocked routes).
Kamarot, Station Bill'e göre yaralı bakı: In accordance with the Station Bill, the steward may assist the casualty care party (stretcher, first-aid support) or the head count. As the steward knows the accommodation well, the steward plays a valuable role in checking cabins and confirming that no one has been left behind.
Kamarot yaşam mahallinde çok dolaştığı i: Because the steward moves around the accommodation a great deal, the steward may be the first person to notice signs of fire (smoke, smell, heat). In such a case, the steward raises the alarm immediately and acts according to the procedure. Early detection and a quick alarm prevent a fire from growing.
Emniyet ve acil durum görevleri, kamarot: Safety and emergency duties are among the steward's most important responsibilities on board; beyond the service role, the steward contributes to saving lives as a crew member. Knowing one's duty, following fire door/escape route discipline and the reflex to raise the alarm early make the difference in a real emergency.
Bir denetçi gemiye geldiğinde, ilk gördü: When an inspector comes on board, the condition of the accommodation, which is the first thing seen, creates an impression of the ship's general maintenance culture. A clean, tidy environment inspires confidence, whereas an untidy one may trigger a stricter inspection. The steward plays a direct role in forming this impression.
Kamarot; gelen surveyor, denetçi, acente: The steward provides courteous and professional service to visiting surveyors, inspectors, agents and guests. Drinks/refreshments are prepared, the meeting area is set up and the guests' comfort is ensured. Professional hospitality reflects the ship's corporate image.
Denetim/toplantı öncesi kamarot, toplant: Before an inspection/meeting, the steward prepares the meeting room/saloon: cleanliness, tidiness, the necessary items (water, coffee, seating) and general comfort. A ready, tidy room helps the meeting run efficiently and the ship appear professional.
Ziyaretçi yönetimi, ISPS güvenlik kurall: Visitor management must comply with the ISPS security rules; visitors are registered, escorted and restricted to authorized areas. During service, the steward follows the security rules and reports unauthorized access/suspicious situations to the responsible officer.
Yaşam mahallinin denetim standardına uyg: Keeping the accommodation up to inspection standard is a job done every day, not only on the day of a visit. By keeping the environment consistently tidy, the steward ensures that the ship is ready even for an unannounced inspection. Living conditions under the MLC are also part of this order.
Ziyaretçi ve misafir yönetimi desteği, k: Supporting visitor and guest management is the steward's contribution to the ship's corporate image and to successful inspections. Tidy accommodation, professional hospitality and security awareness strengthen the impression that the ship is well managed and pave the way for inspections to go well.
Revir, hasta/yaralı bakımı için ayrılmış: The sick bay is a space set aside for the care of sick/injured persons and must be clean, tidy and ready for use at all times. A dirty or untidy sick bay both puts patient care at risk and results directly in an MLC non-conformity finding during inspections. The steward ensures this readiness of the sick bay every day.
Kamarot; revirin zemini, yatak/yatak tak: The steward regularly cleans and disinfects the sick bay floor, berth/bedding, worktop, washbasin and instruments. Sanitation checks (ventilation, odor, hygiene) are carried out. Medical instruments and surfaces are kept clean so as to reduce the risk of infection.
Revirde yatan hasta mürettebata kamarot;: For sick crew members confined to the sick bay, the steward brings meals, drinks and basic necessities and ensures the comfort of the room (temperature, ventilation, cleanliness). Suitable food for the patient (light/diet food if necessary) is coordinated with the cook. This support contributes to the patient's recovery and morale.
Bulaşıcı hastalık şüphesinde kamarot, ar: If an infectious disease is suspected, the steward applies enhanced disinfection protocols: frequent and intensive disinfection, particularly of toilets, shared surfaces and the patient's room. The steward uses suitable PPE (gloves, mask), collects contaminated waste separately and works in a way that prevents cross-contamination.
Kamarot, hasta bakımı ve revir temizliği: During patient care and sick bay cleaning, the steward also protects their own health, using PPE and paying attention to hand hygiene. The steward's health is important for continuity of service and for protecting the rest of the crew.
Kamarot, tıbbi sorumlu zabit (genelde İk: The steward works in coordination with the officer responsible for medical care (usually the Second Officer/Medical Officer) and reports changes in the patient's condition (not eating, fever, deterioration). Cleanliness of the sick bay and patient comfort are teamwork that complements medical care.
Revir temizliği ve tıbbi yardım desteği,: Sick bay cleaning and medical support is a task through which the steward contributes directly to the recovery of sick crew members and to the ship's MLC compliance. A sick bay that is always ready, attentive patient care and meticulous infection control protect both the individual's health and the hygiene of the whole ship.
Yaşam mahalli yangınları çoğu zaman küçü: Accommodation fires often start from a small moment of carelessness — an unextinguished cigarette, an overloaded socket, an unauthorized heater — and grow rapidly. Because the steward sees these areas constantly, the steward can spot risks early. Fire safety is a natural part of the steward's daily work.
Sigara yalnızca izin verilen alanlarda i: Smoking is permitted only in designated areas; the steward checks the cleanliness of these areas and the correct use of ashtrays (ones that fully extinguish embers). If the steward notices signs/smell of smoking in a bunk or in an unauthorized area, the steward reports it. Smoking is one of the main causes of accommodation fires.
Yaşam mahalli yangın kapıları kapalı (ve: Fire doors in the accommodation are kept closed (or self-closing); wedging them open allows fire and smoke to spread. The steward applies this rule while working and corrects/reports a wedged door. This common violation has fatal consequences in a real fire.
Yangın detektörlerinin (duman/ısı) önü k: Fire detectors (smoke/heat) must not be obstructed; a detector that is covered or painted over does not work. The steward makes sure that the detectors in the accommodation remain uncovered and functional; an obstructed detector is reported.
Kamaralarda izinsiz elektrikli alet (ısı: If unauthorized electrical appliances (heaters, high-power devices), uncontrolled multi-socket adapters or naked flame sources are found in cabins, the steward reports them immediately. These devices can cause overloading and fire. Company policy usually prohibits certain appliances.
Tek başına çalışırken kamarot, bir yangı: Working alone, the steward may be the first person to notice signs of fire (smoke, smell, heat). In such a case, the steward raises the alarm immediately and acts according to the procedure. Early detection saves lives in an accommodation fire.
Kamara ve ortak alanlarda yangın/sigara: Fire/smoking safety in cabins and common areas is a valuable monitoring task that arises from the steward's constant presence in the accommodation. Ashtray discipline, fire door and detector awareness, reporting of risky appliances and early alarm protect the accommodation from being the area where fires most often start.
Stajyer, STCW A-III/1 yeterlilik kazanma: The cadet is a trainee engineer working towards STCW A-III/1 competence; however, legal responsibility for the watch always rests with the EOOW on duty. Under no circumstances may the cadet independently start/stop machinery, switch valves, close breakers or reset alarms. Before every action, the cadet states the intention to the EOOW, obtains approval and carries out the action under supervision.
Bu prensip \"challenge and response\" (s: This principle is part of the "challenge and response" culture. If the cadet notices an abnormality, the cadet is expected to report it to the EOOW immediately; an observation that seems minor (for example a leak at a flange or a rise in bearing temperature) may be an early sign of a serious failure. The cadet is expected to report, not to stay silent.
Modern gemilerin çoğu UMS (Unattended Ma: Most modern ships are UMS (Unattended Machinery Space) certified; the engine room may be left unmanned at night and alarms are routed to the bridge and to the duty engineer's cabin. The cadet learns how the engine room is monitored in both attended (manned) and unattended periods.
Vardiya devri, EOOW'lar arasında yapılan: The watch handover is a formal transfer of information between EOOWs. By following this process closely, the cadet learns which information is critical: the status of running machinery, maintenance work in progress, isolated equipment (under LOTO), tank levels, transfers in progress (fuel, ballast, bilge) and outstanding alarms.
STCW, gelen mühendisin vardiyayı devralm: STCW requires the relieving engineer to be fully informed about the condition of the equipment, operations in progress and potential hazards before taking over the watch. If the relieving engineer feels physically or mentally unfit for duty, the watch is not taken over. By observing this, the cadet internalizes the professional discipline of this standard.
Engine Log Book, makine dairesinin yasal: The Engine Log Book is the legal memory of the engine room. Hourly parameters (RPM, exhaust gas temp, scavenge air pressure, jacket cooling temp, LO pressure, FO temp/viscosity), tank levels and significant events are recorded. The cadet first takes readings under supervision, then starts keeping the log personally under the EOOW's control.
Kayıtlar gerçek, zamanında ve düzeltilme: Entries must be true, timely and unaltered (no false data). If a parameter goes outside its limits, both the value and the action taken are recorded. These records have evidential value in Port State Control (PSC) inspections, insurance investigations and casualty investigations.
Tur, genellikle yukarıdan aşağıya veya b: The round is usually made in a logical order, from top to bottom or from one system to the next: the main engine and its surroundings, generators, boiler, purifier room, pump platforms, separators/clarifiers, air compressors, cooling systems, steering gear room and bilge wells. During the round, the cadet learns to use four senses: "look, listen, smell, touch" (by sight, by sound, by smell, by temperature).
Gözle: sızıntı, gevşek bağlantı, anormal: Look: leaks, loose connections, abnormal levels, vibration. Listen: unusual knocking, cavitation, rubbing noise. Smell: burnt insulation, oil/fuel vapor, exhaust gas leaks. Touch (carefully): bearing housing temperature, temperature differences between pipes. This sense-based diagnosis reveals early faults that panel readings cannot catch.
Bilge well seviyeleri turun kritik bir p: Bilge well levels are a critical part of the round. A rising bilge level may indicate a hidden leak (seawater, cooling water, FO/LO). The cadet learns the bilge alarm system, the Oily Water Separator (OWS) and the logic of the 15 ppm bilge alarm/oil content monitor; however, pumping out bilges is never within the cadet's independent authority.
MARPOL Annex I, makine dairesi sintine s: MARPOL Annex I requires that engine-room bilge water may be pumped overboard only through the OWS and at less than 15 ppm. Every bilge transfer is recorded in the Oil Record Book Part I. The cadet learns this recording logic; unlawful bilge discharge (magic pipe) is one of the most severely punished maritime offenses.
Stajyer, ana makinenin temel parametrele: The cadet learns the main engine's key parameters and their normal ranges: the exhaust gas temperature of each cylinder (cylinder exhaust deviation), scavenge air pressure, turbocharger RPM, jacket cooling water inlet/outlet, piston cooling oil outlet, LO inlet pressure/temp and fuel oil viscosity/temp. These values are interrelated; the trend is interpreted, not a single value.
Örneğin bir silindirin egzoz sıcaklığı d: For example, if the exhaust temperature of one cylinder deviates noticeably from the others (deviation), that cylinder may have a combustion problem, an injector fault or a fuel index imbalance. By learning these correlations, the cadet grasps the physical meaning behind the panel readings.
Jeneratör yükü, kazan buhar basıncı, hav: Generator load, boiler steam pressure, air receiver pressure, cooling water temperatures and the sea water cooling system differential pressure (an indicator of filter clogging) are read regularly. On modern ships, the Alarm and Monitoring System (AMS) logs these values continuously; the cadet learns to read the trend displays.
Trend analizi proaktif bakımın temelidir: Trend analysis is the basis of proactive maintenance: a slowly rising bearing temperature, a gradually falling LO pressure or an increasing differential pressure gives a warning days before a sudden failure. Instead of saying "it is within limits for now", the cadet learns to ask "which way is it going?"
Makine dairesi alarmları kademelidir: ön: Engine room alarms are graded: first a warning (alarm), then slow-down (automatic speed reduction) and finally shut-down (automatic stop). Critical alarms (LO low pressure, jacket water high temp, scavenge fire, overspeed) trigger automatic intervention to protect the engine. The cadet learns the meaning of each alarm and the action it triggers.
Bir alarm çaldığında stajyer paniğe kapı: When an alarm sounds, the cadet, without panicking, reads the alarm, informs the EOOW and verifies the relevant parameter on the panel and locally. The cadet does not silence/reset the alarm independently. With multiple alarms (alarm flooding), identifying the most critical one and finding the root cause is the EOOW's job; the cadet assists.
Oil Mist Detector (OMD) alarmı, krank ka: An Oil Mist Detector (OMD) alarm indicates that a bearing inside the crankcase has overheated and is producing oil mist; this is a precursor of a crankcase explosion. On this alarm the crankcase doors must never be opened; wait until the engine has cooled down (usually 20-30 min). The cadet must know this lethal risk.
Scavenge fire ise scavenge boşluğunda bi: A scavenge fire is the ignition of oil accumulated in the scavenge space; the exhaust temperature rises, the load is reduced and the fixed smothering system (steam/CO2) is kept ready. These events are critical safety lessons on which the cadet must base the answer to the question "why do we wait on a crankcase alarm?"
ERRM, köprüüstündeki BRM'in (Bridge Reso: ERRM is the engine room counterpart of BRM (Bridge Resource Management) on the bridge. It is based on the principles of open communication, task sharing, situational awareness and breaking the error chain. The cadet is the most junior member of the team but an important part of the "speak up" culture.
Closed-loop communication (kapalı döngü: Closed-loop communication is essential: when an order is given, the receiver repeats it (read-back) and the sender confirms. The order "Put No. 2 generator on standby" is confirmed as "No. 2 generator on standby, understood". This prevents accidents caused by misunderstanding.
Manevra durumlarında (liman giriş-çıkış,: During maneuvering (entering/leaving port, narrow channels), the engine room goes to standby: an extra generator is put in parallel, the main engine is switched from UMS to manual control and the EOOW stands by in the control room. The cadet observes the coordination between telegraph orders, speed requests from the bridge and the "stand by engines / finished with engines" orders.
Tank seviyelerinin doğru takibi, makinen: Correct monitoring of tank levels ensures an uninterrupted fuel/oil supply to the engine and prevents overflow/spillage. The cadet learns why a service tank level is kept within a certain range (settling time, need for water draining).
FO/DO iç transfer, LO yenileme ve fresh: Internal FO/DO transfers, LO replenishment and fresh water transfers are operations in which the cadet takes part under supervision. Before the transfer, the valve alignment is verified and the overflow tank level is checked; throughout the transfer, the level is monitored continuously. An incorrect valve line-up or an uncontrolled transfer creates a risk of overflow and pollution.
Stajyer her transferde \"kaynaktan hedef: In every transfer, the cadet learns to build the complete line-up "from source to destination" mentally: which valve is open, which pump is running, which tank is filling. This discipline is the basic skill that will prevent wrong-transfer errors later, as an independent engineer.
Sıcak yüzeylere (egzoz manifoldu, buhar: Bare contact with hot surfaces (exhaust manifold, steam line), standing near a rotating shaft/coupling and careless movement on an oily floor are causes of accidents. The cadet learns to use ladders with "three points of contact", the correct lifting technique and the locations of the emergency stop buttons.
Stajyer, tank/sintine/cofferdam gibi kap: The cadet learns the importance of the enclosed space entry permit and atmosphere testing (O2, LEL, H2S, CO) for enclosed spaces such as tanks, bilges and cofferdams. Unauthorized enclosed space entry is one of the deadliest types of accident at sea. Under no circumstances does the cadet enter an enclosed space without a permit and without supervision.
Aynı şekilde sıcak iş (hot work — kaynak: In the same way, the cadet learns the purpose of the hot work (welding, grinding) and electrical lockout (LOTO) procedures. These procedures are covered in detail in later sections; during watch participation, the cadet observes how they relate to watch safety.
Her vardiya katılımı, Training Record Bo: Each watch participation is entered under the relevant competence area of the Training Record Book (TRB): "engineering watch keeping", "monitor machinery performance", "maintain safe engineering watch". The cadet records every task performed under supervision (keeping the log, rounds, transfers, observing alarm response) in the TRB and has it signed by the training engineer.
TRB'nin tamamlanması, OOW (Engine) yeter: Completion of the TRB is a legal prerequisite for sitting the OOW (Engine) certificate of competency examination. The cadet should therefore see watch participation not merely as "filling hours" but as a process of accumulating concrete evidence of competence.
Eğitmen mühendis, stajyerin gözlem keski: The training engineer regularly assesses the cadet's sharpness of observation, compliance with procedures and safety awareness. The cadet should actively ask for feedback: "What did I miss on this round?", "Did I respond correctly to this alarm?". This feedback loop is the basis of the progression from supervised participation to independent competence.
Makine stajyerinin vardiya katılımındaki: The engine cadet's success in watch participation comes not from moving fast but from observing correctly, reporting on time and respecting the limits of authority. The discipline learned under supervision today forms the basis of the safety culture of the engineer who will keep an independent watch tomorrow. A good cadet learns what is "normal" so well that he or she notices what is "abnormal" before anyone else.
Her planlı bakım, PMS yazılımında açılan: Every planned maintenance job starts with a work order opened in the PMS software. The work order contains the job to be done, the spare parts and tools required, the estimated duration and the OEM procedure reference. By reading the work order, the cadet understands the scope of the job, its critical steps and its safety requirements in advance.
Bakım öncesi risk değerlendirmesi (risk: A risk assessment and a toolbox talk are held before maintenance: the hazards of the job, the need for isolation, the PPE required and emergency measures are discussed. The cadet attends the toolbox talk, asks questions and understands the allocation of tasks. The principle "think before you start" prevents most maintenance accidents.
Bakıma başlamadan önce gereken tüm takım: Before maintenance starts, all the tools, spare parts, gasket/O-ring sets, cleaning materials and sealing elements required are prepared. The cadet learns to recognize the right tool: torque wrench, hammer, puller, feeler gauge, micrometer, dial gauge, Allen key/socket sets. Using the wrong tool harms both the job and the operator.
Yedek parçaların OEM orijinali veya onay: It is important that spare parts are OEM originals or approved equivalents; the wrong part leads to early failure. The cadet learns to lay out dismantled parts in order (labeling them according to the assembly sequence); this eliminates the risk of errors and missing parts during reassembly.
Hiçbir bakım, ekipman enerji altındayken: No maintenance starts while the equipment is energized. With Lockout-Tagout (LOTO), electrical, pressure, thermal and kinetic energy are isolated; the isolated valve/breaker is tagged and locked. The cadet learns to verify that the equipment to be worked on is actually isolated (zero energy state).
Sıcak iş veya kapalı alan gerektiren bak: For maintenance requiring hot work or enclosed space entry, the relevant permit (Permit to Work) is obtained. The cadet internalizes the principle "no work without a permit". Before any equipment is dismantled, it is confirmed that the system pressure has been released, the temperature has dropped and rotating parts have stopped.
Bakım alanı temiz, aydınlık ve düzenli o: The maintenance area must be clean, well lit and tidy. Dismantled parts are laid out in order on a tray/cloth, oily waste is collected in a suitable container and walkways are not blocked. A disorderly work area creates a risk both of slip/fall accidents and of lost parts/incorrect assembly.
Stajyer \"5S\" benzeri bir düzen disipli: The cadet learns a "5S"-type housekeeping discipline: put back what you use, segregate waste, leave the area clean. Good maintenance work shows itself when, on completion, the area is cleaner than before the work started.
Santrifüj pompa overhaul'unda; coupling: In a centrifugal pump overhaul, the coupling is removed, the casing is opened and the impeller, wear ring, mechanical seal and bearings are checked. The cadet learns the function of each part: the impeller creates the flow, the wear ring limits internal leakage and the mechanical seal prevents leakage along the shaft.
Aşınma ölçümleri yapılır: impeller-wear: Wear measurements are taken: impeller-to-wear ring clearance, shaft run-out, bearing clearance. The measurements are compared with the OEM tolerances; parts outside the limits are renewed. The cadet grasps the question "why do we measure": a part that looks good may be out of tolerance and cause a loss of performance/efficiency.
Mechanical seal montajı pompanın en hass: Fitting the mechanical seal is the most delicate operation on a pump: the seal faces must not be touched by hand, scratched or run dry. Incorrect fitting results in early seal failure and leakage. The cadet learns the importance of clean assembly, correct orientation and proper lubrication.
Montaj sonrası coupling alignment (laser: After assembly, coupling alignment is carried out (with a laser or dial gauge); misalignment leads to vibration, bearing wear and seal failure. The cadet learns that alignment is a measured value, not something that "looks aligned".
Gate, globe, butterfly, check (non-retur: Gate, globe, butterfly, check (non-return) and ball valves have different functions: gate valves for fully open/closed isolation, globe valves for flow control, check valves for one-way flow and butterfly valves for quick isolation. The cadet learns which valve is used where and why their maintenance differs.
Valf bakımında disc/seat lapping (alıştı: Valve maintenance includes disc/seat lapping, renewal of spindle/gland packing and a tightness test. Lapping is a grinding-in process carried out with lapping paste; it restores the contact surface between the disc and the seat. The cadet learns this manual skill by observing and assisting.
Gasket (conta), flanşlar arasındaki sızd: The gasket provides the seal between flanges. The correct material (suitable for the fluid and temperature), the correct thickness and correct cutting are critical. The cadet learns to cut a gasket from gasket sheet using the flange as a template, to position the bolt holes correctly and to cut the inner diameter so that it does not obstruct the flow.
Flanş montajında cıvatalar çapraz (star: When a flange is assembled, the bolts are tightened in a cross (star pattern) sequence and in torque stages; uneven tightening leads to crushing of the gasket and leaks. The cadet learns why the correct torque value and tightening sequence are important.
LO, FO ve hava filtreleri düzenli temizl: LO, FO and air filters are cleaned/changed regularly. A clogged filter shows itself by an increase in differential pressure; when this difference exceeds a set limit, an alarm is given or the bypass opens. The cadet learns why filters must be changed on time (insufficient supply, damage to equipment).
Duplex (çift) filtrelerde bir taraf çalı: On duplex filters, one side can be taken out for maintenance while the other is in service; the changeover is done carefully so that the supply is not interrupted and no air lock forms. The cadet learns the changeover sequence and the need for venting (air release).
Purifier (separator), yakıt ve yağdan su: The purifier (separator) separates water and solid sediment from fuel and oil by centrifugal force. Opening the bowl, cleaning the disc stack, selecting the gravity disc and renewing O-rings are parts of the maintenance. The cadet experiences that learning the order and fitting direction of the discs is critical (incorrect assembly impairs separation efficiency).
Bowl ağır ve hassas bir parçadır; doğru: The bowl is a heavy and delicate part; correct lifting technique and balanced assembly are important. An unbalanced bowl creates dangerous vibration at high speed. In purifier maintenance, the cadet sees the direct relationship of cleanliness and precision with efficiency.
Cıvataların doğru torkla sıkılması, hem: Tightening bolts to the correct torque is critical both for tightness and for structural integrity. Insufficient torque leads to leaks and loosening, while excessive torque leads to bolt failure and flange distortion. The cadet learns the correct use of the torque wrench and how to read the OEM torque table.
Büyük flanş ve ana yatak gibi kritik bağ: On critical joints such as large flanges and main bearings, stepwise and cross-pattern tightening is essential; in some cases a hydraulic tensioner or the angle-tightening method is used. The cadet learns why these methods differ.
Titreşimli ortamda cıvataların gevşememe: To prevent bolts from loosening in a vibrating environment, split pins, locking wire, lock washers or thread-locker are used. The cadet learns which locking device is used in which application and what kind of failure a forgotten locking wire can cause.
Bakım sırasında oluşan yağlı bez, kullan: Oily rags, used filters, waste oil and sludge generated during maintenance are collected separately under MARPOL Annex I/V and disposed of properly (burning in the incinerator or delivery ashore in port). The cadet learns the discipline of waste segregation (oily rags, contaminated waste, scrap metal).
Yağlı atığın denize karışması veya yanlı: Oily waste entering the sea or being wrongly segregated means serious pollution and penalties. The cadet also learns that solvents/chemicals used for cleaning must be used in accordance with the MSDS and require proper waste management.
Temizlik solventleri, pas sökücüler ve d: Cleaning solvents, rust removers and degreasers may be flammable and toxic. The cadet learns to read the MSDS, provide adequate ventilation, use gloves/a mask and keep these products away from sources of ignition. Incorrect use of solvents is both a health and a fire hazard.
Bakım desteğinin önemli bir kazanımı, ek: An important gain from assisting with maintenance is learning the correct English/technical names of equipment parts: impeller, gland, bushing, journal, liner, gasket, O-ring, sleeve, key/keyway, circlip. The cadet learns that using the correct term prevents communication errors (such as ordering the wrong part).
Teknik dil hem yedek parça siparişinde h: Technical language is critical for ordering spare parts, reading OEM manuals and working with a multinational crew. The cadet learns new terms on every maintenance job and enters them in the TRB notes.
Stajyer, \"yaklaşık\" değil \"ölçülen\": The cadet learns to work with "measured" rather than "approximate" values. In using the micrometer, feeler gauge and dial gauge, the cadet gains awareness of correct reading, parallax error, temperature effects and calibration. Precise measurement is the basic language of engineering.
Bakım biten ekipman devreye alınmadan ön: Before equipment that has been maintained is put back into service, it is checked: are all bolts torqued, have the tools been collected (tool count), has the isolation been removed, is the valve line-up correct? The first start (recommissioning) is done under supervision; leaks, vibration, abnormal noise and temperature are monitored.
Stajyer, \"monte ettik bitti\" değil \"t: The cadet learns the discipline not of "we assembled it, job done" but of "we tested it, verified it and recorded it". A small leak noticed on first start can be corrected without dismantling the equipment again; an error that is missed later turns into a major failure.
Bakım tamamlanınca PMS'te iş emri kapatı: When the maintenance is completed, the work order is closed in the PMS: the work done, spare parts used, values measured and observations are recorded. This record builds up the ship's maintenance history and forms the basis for future failure analysis. The cadet observes the logic of closing a work order.
Stajyer ayrıca katıldığı her bakımı TRB': The cadet also enters every maintenance job taken part in under the "maintenance and repair" competence area of the TRB and has it signed by the training engineer. In this way, the practical skills acquired become part of the official record.
Makine stajyerinin bakım desteğindeki ge: The engine cadet's real gain from assisting with maintenance is not just dismantling and reassembling a pump, but experiencing planning, isolation, measurement, precision and documentation together. Manual skill is gained through repetition, technical language through curiosity and safety awareness through discipline. The meticulousness learned under supervision today is the signature discipline of the engineer who will carry out maintenance independently tomorrow.
Her makine sistemi bir girdi alır, dönüş: Every machinery system takes an input, converts it and gives an output. The main engine converts fuel energy into shaft power; the fuel system supplies it, the lubrication system reduces friction, the cooling system removes heat and the air system enables combustion. By making these connections, the cadet understands the engine room as a whole.
Bir sistem arızalandığında etkisi diğerl: When one system fails, the effect spreads to the others: if cooling is insufficient, the oil thins, the oil pressure drops, bearings are damaged and the engine stops. By learning these chain dependencies, the cadet lays the foundation for fault-diagnosis logic.
Stajyer, makine dairesini fiziksel olara: By walking around the engine room, the cadet memorizes where each piece of equipment is: main engine, generator flat, boiler, purifier room, pump platform, compressors, switchboard room, steering gear room, separators and tank locations. In an emergency, reaching the right equipment quickly may be vital.
Lokasyon öğrenimi, General Arrangement ç: Learning these locations is reinforced by matching the General Arrangement drawing with the actual spaces. The cadet develops the skill of "finding on site what I see on the drawing"; this is a true engineering competence.
Büyük ticari gemilerin çoğu, doğrudan pe: Most large merchant ships use two-stroke, low-speed, crosshead-type diesel engines directly coupled to the propeller. The cadet learns the scavenging, compression, combustion (expansion) and exhaust phases, the principle of uniflow scavenging and how the crosshead keeps the side thrust off the piston.
Ana makinenin alt sistemleri birbirine b: The main engine's subsystems are interconnected: fuel injection, scavenge air (turbocharger + air cooler), jacket cooling water, piston/crosshead LO, cylinder lubrication and exhaust. The cadet learns how each subsystem contributes to the healthy running of the engine.
Ana makine; overspeed trip, LO low press: The main engine is equipped with multi-layered protection such as the overspeed trip, LO low pressure shut-down, jacket water high temp slow-down, oil mist detector and scavenge fire alarm. The cadet learns what each protection prevents: the overspeed trip prevents the engine from breaking apart on loss of load, and the OMD prevents a crankcase explosion.
Crankcase relief valve (patlama kapağı): There are also mechanical protections such as crankcase relief valves (explosion doors) and the turning gear interlock (which prevents starting while the turning gear is engaged). The cadet learns that these devices must never be bypassed.
Gemi elektriği, dört zamanlı orta devirl: The ship's electrical power is supplied by four-stroke, medium-speed diesel generators. The cadet learns the logic of parallel operation of generators, load sharing, synchronization and preferential trip (disconnecting low-priority consumers on overload).
Şaft jeneratörü (PTO) ve emergency gener: The shaft generator (PTO) and the emergency generator are also sources of electrical power. The cadet learns how the electrical supply is managed in normal, maneuvering and emergency conditions, and why enough generators are kept in parallel to prevent the risk of a blackout.
Jeneratör; reverse power, over-current,: The generator has reverse power, over-current, over/under-voltage and over/under-frequency protection. The cadet learns how these protections safeguard the electrical system and the generator. In addition, cooling water, oil pressure and exhaust temperature alarms protect the engine side.
Auxiliary (oil-fired) boiler, port'ta ve: The auxiliary (oil-fired) boiler produces steam in port and at low load; the exhaust gas economizer produces steam at sea from the main engine exhaust heat (waste heat recovery). Steam is used for heating fuel/oil, tank heating and general services. The cadet learns how the two sources complement each other.
Su seviyesi kontrolü buhar kazanlarında: Water level control is vital in steam boilers: a low water level can lead to boiler damage and explosion. The cadet learns to read the gauge glass and learns the water level alarm and automatic feed water control.
Safety valve (emniyet supabı), kazan bas: The safety valve limits the boiler pressure; it opens at excessive pressure and releases steam. The cadet learns the set pressure of the safety valve and the requirement for periodic testing. The pressure gauge, water level controller and flame failure device are also part of boiler safety.
Ana makine basınçlı hava ile çalıştırılı: The main engine is started with compressed air (starting air, usually ~30 bar). Air compressors fill the air bottles (air receivers). In addition, control air (control/service air) supplies the pneumatic systems. The cadet learns the difference between the two air systems and why they are kept separate.
Hava şişelerinin doluluğu kritiktir: yet: The pressure in the air bottles is critical: without sufficient starting air the engine cannot be started, or maneuverability is lost. The cadet learns to monitor bottle pressure and the logic of automatic filling by the compressors.
Makine dairesinde santrifüj (cooling wat: The engine room has centrifugal pumps (cooling water, ballast), positive displacement pumps (FO/LO transfer, screw/gear) and eccentric screw pumps (sludge). The cadet learns which pump type is used in which system and why (according to pressure/flow/viscosity requirements).
Pompa sistemleri yedekli (duty/standby): Pump systems are designed with redundancy (duty/standby); if one pump fails, the standby pump cuts in automatically or manually. The cadet learns the auto-start logic and why critical services have redundancy.
Boru hatları renk kodlarıyla işaretlenir: Pipelines are marked with color codes (according to the type of fluid) and the flow direction is shown by arrows. By physically following a pipeline (line tracing), the cadet learns the path of a system from source to consumer; this is a basic skill for valve alignment and fault isolation.
Modern gemiler merkezi soğutma sistemi k: Modern ships use a central cooling system: sea water (low temp sea water) cools the fresh water circuit through a central cooler, and the fresh water (LT/HT fresh water) in turn cools the engine and auxiliary equipment. This keeps the corrosive effect of seawater away from the equipment. The cadet learns the difference between the LT and HT circuits.
Plate ve shell-and-tube tipi ısı değişti: Plate and shell-and-tube heat exchangers are used. The cadet learns that cooling efficiency drops because of fouling (clogging/deposits), and that the time for cleaning is determined by monitoring the differential pressure and the temperature difference.
Three-way thermostatic valve, soğutma ak: A three-way thermostatic valve keeps the engine temperature at the optimum by regulating the cooling flow. Running too cold (especially at low load) is also harmful because of wear and sulfuric acid corrosion. The cadet learns the balance of "warm enough, but not too hot".
Ağır yakıt (HFO) makineye girmeden önce: Before entering the engine, heavy fuel oil (HFO) passes through the settling tank → purifier → service tank chain; water and solid sediment are separated, and the fuel is heated and its viscosity adjusted. The cadet learns why this treatment chain is critical for healthy combustion in the engine.
LO da benzer şekilde sürekli purifier'da: Similarly, LO is kept clean by passing it continuously through the purifier. The cadet learns the purifier's separator (water separation) and clarifier (solids separation) modes and the importance of selecting the gravity disc.
Yakıt hazırlama sistemi, ana makine ve j: The fuel treatment system directly affects main engine and generator performance. Poorly purified fuel leads to injector clogging, liner wear and exhaust temperature imbalance. The cadet sees concretely that the output of one system determines the health of another.
P&ID (Piping and Instrumentation Diagram: A P&ID (Piping and Instrumentation Diagram) shows a system's valves, pumps, tanks, sensors and line connections with standard symbols. The cadet learns to read valve types, pump symbols, flow direction and instrument tags (PI, TI, LI, PT). The diagram simplifies the complexity of the plant in the mind.
Stajyer, bir P&ID'yi okuyup sahada doğru: By reading a P&ID and verifying it on site (finding on site the valve seen on the drawing), the cadet brings the two worlds together. This skill is the basis of valve alignment, fault isolation and operation planning.
Bir transfer veya switching işlemi önces: Before a transfer or changeover operation, the cadet learns to work out the line-up on the P&ID: which valve is open, which pump will run, which tank will be affected. This mental rehearsal reduces the likelihood of errors on site.
Makine sistemlerini öğrenmek, ekipman is: Learning machinery systems is not memorizing equipment names but understanding the path of the fluid, the conversion of energy and the dependencies between systems. When the cadet learns each system in terms of "purpose, flow, failure, protection", the engine room stops being a puzzle and becomes a meaningful whole. This holistic understanding lays a solid foundation for fault diagnosis and operational management later on.
STCW Bölüm A-III/1, makine vardiya mühen: STCW Section A-III/1 requires completion of a structured onboard training program in order to become an engineer officer in charge of a watch. The TRB is the evidence that this program has been implemented and assessed. The Administration (flag State) issues the candidate's certificate of competency only together with an approved TRB and valid sea service.
TRB; eğitim kuruluşu (akademi/MET instit: The TRB is a document that bridges the training institution (academy/MET institution), the company and the ship. It shows that the theoretical knowledge gained at the academy has been put into practice on board, that each competence area has actually been applied and that it has been assessed by an authorized engineer. For this reason, the TRB is also seen as "the contract between the school and the ship".
OOW (Engine) yeterlilik belgesine giden: On the way to the OOW (Engine) certificate of competency there are three chains of evidence: (1) approved sea service (Sea Service), (2) a completed TRB, (3) mandatory courses (firefighting, survival, medical first aid, security awareness, etc.), and finally the certificate of competency examination. The TRB is the middle link of this chain; if it is incomplete, the other links are not sufficient.
Stajyer, TRB'yi sınav dosyasının çekirde: The cadet should see the TRB as the core of the examination file. In the Administration's review, the answer to "how many months did you spend at sea?" is in the Sea Service record, and the answer to "what did you learn and what is your evidence?" is in the TRB. The two complement each other.
Standart bir Engine Cadet TRB; kişisel b: A standard Engine Cadet TRB consists of personal details, ship record pages (vessel record / particulars), familiarization checklists, task records, supervisor assessment pages and summary approval sections. On joining each ship, the ship's details (type, tonnage, main engine, class) are entered on the relevant page.
TRB'nin kalbi, STCW Table A-III/1 yetkin: The heart of the TRB is the task record section, which links the STCW Table A-III/1 competence areas to shipboard tasks. Here, the fields "what was done, when, which competence it corresponds to, trainer's assessment" are completed for each task. The familiarization section is completed on first joining the ship and documents the safety, escape route and equipment familiarization.
Table A-III/1 dört ana fonksiyon altında: Table A-III/1 defines competences under four main functions: Marine Engineering, Electrical/Electronic and Control Engineering, Maintenance and Repair, and Controlling Operation of the Ship and Care for Persons on Board. TRB tasks are distributed among these functions; the cadet must accumulate sufficient evidence in each function.
Örneğin \"Maintain a safe engineering wa: For example, the competence "Maintain a safe engineering watch" is filled with watch participation records, "Operate main and auxiliary machinery" with system operation observations and "Maintenance and repair of shipboard machinery" with maintenance participation records. Knowing which task supports which competence, the cadet progresses through the book in a balanced way.
Bir görev yapıldığı gün TRB'ye işlenmeli: A task must be entered in the TRB on the day it is done. An entry written while the memory is fresh is accurate in terms of date, equipment, work done and lesson learned. Entries written in bulk weeks later are vague and general and have weak evidential value; the training engineer also finds it difficult to approve such entries.
Stajyer, her vardiya veya bakım işi sonr: After each watch or maintenance job, the cadet takes a few minutes to record the task: which system, which operation, observations, tools used, safety points observed. This discipline both feeds the TRB and serves as the cadet's own learning journal.
İyi bir TRB kaydı şu sorulara yanıt veri: A good TRB entry answers these questions: What was done? On which equipment/system? Which procedure was followed? Which safety precautions were taken? What was learned? It must be concrete: not "I looked at the pump" but "I assisted, under the trainer's supervision, in replacing the mechanical seal of No. 2 transfer pump; LOTO was applied, the old seal was removed, a new gasket was cut".
Kaydın sahte veya abartılı olmaması esas: It is essential that entries are not false or exaggerated. Entering in the TRB a job in which the cadet did not actually take part is a serious disciplinary offense; these tasks are also questioned in the oral examination, and superficial entries are exposed. The TRB is the mirror of the cadet's real competence.
Gemide TRB sürecinden sorumlu kişi genel: The person on board responsible for the TRB process is usually the Chief Engineer or a senior engineer designated by the Chief Engineer (training officer). The trainer reads the cadet's entries, verifies that the task was actually done and performed to an appropriate standard, requests corrections if necessary and signs the entries found satisfactory.
Onay sadece bir imza atma işlemi değildi: Approval is not just a matter of signing; the trainer makes an assessment by observing the cadet's competence. The trainer looks for answers to the questions "Can the cadet do it, has the cadet understood it, is the cadet working safely?". For this reason, the cadet should submit entries for signature at regular intervals (e.g. weekly) and not leave them until the end of the voyage.
İdeal pratik, haftalık veya iki haftalık: The ideal practice is a weekly or two-weekly signing cycle. With this rhythm, the trainer assesses fresh entries and shows the cadet the areas for development. Signing hundreds of entries accumulated until the end of the voyage all at once both burdens the trainer and lowers the quality of the assessment.
Stajyer, her imza turunu bir geri bildir: The cadet should turn every signing round into a feedback opportunity: "In which competence am I weak, what should I focus on next month?" These questions turn the TRB from a passive record into an active development tool and strengthen the mentoring relationship with the trainer.
Her yeni gemiye çıkışta TRB'nin familiar: On joining each new ship, the familiarization section of the TRB is completed as a priority. This section covers the locations of safety equipment, escape routes, the muster station, lifejacket/immersion suit locations, emergency alarm signals, engine room emergency stop buttons and enclosed space entry points. The ISM Code requires every person joining the ship to receive familiarization before taking up duties.
Aşinalık sadece bir kutu işaretleme egze: Familiarization is not just a box-ticking exercise; it is the cadet loading a "mental picture" of the ship into memory so as to be able to act independently later. The cadet must reach the level of being able to find the escape route with eyes closed and of knowing where the emergency stop button is.
PSC (Port State Control) ve şirket denet: During PSC (Port State Control) and company inspections, whether the crew are familiar with the ship is questioned. The signed familiarization record in the TRB is the document showing that the cadet has received this training. A missing familiarization record is both an inspection finding and a lethal risk in a real emergency.
Stajyer, gemi değişikliklerinde (yeni ge: When changing ships (transferring to a new ship), the cadet must not forget to complete familiarization again. Each ship's layout, equipment and procedures are different; familiarization from the previous ship is not automatically carried over to the new one.
TRB'nin yaygın bir zaafı, bazı yetkinlik: A common weakness of TRBs is that some competences are over-filled while others are under-filled. If the cadet goes on watch every day, the "watchkeeping" record fills up, but "maintenance and repair" or "electrical systems" may remain weak. The cadet should periodically review the gaps in the book and turn to the incomplete areas.
Pratik yöntem, aylık bir öz-değerlendirm: The practical method is a monthly self-assessment: which STCW function has been sufficiently evidenced, and which has fallen behind? For the area that has fallen behind, the cadet asks the training engineer for opportunities ("may I take part in the electrical switchboard job in the coming maintenance plan?"). This proactive approach avoids being left with large gaps at the end of the voyage.
Cadet training may be completed on more than one ship. Although the ship record pages are completed separately for each ship, the evidence of competence accumulates in a single book. When changing ships, the cadet should plan to close on the new ship a gap left on the previous one; for example, if the tanker fuel system was not learned on the previous ship, priority is given to this opportunity on the new ship.
TRB'nin fiziksel güvenliği de süreklilik: The physical safety of the TRB is also critical for continuity. The book must not get wet or be lost, and its pages must not be torn. Many cadets keep a photo/scan backup of completed pages; if the original is lost, a trace of the approved entries remains. Nevertheless, official validity lies with the original bearing wet-ink signatures.
Sea Service Certificate \"ne kadar süre: The Sea Service Certificate answers the question "how long did you spend at sea", and the TRB the question "what did you learn in that time and what is your evidence". The Administration requires both together with the examination application. Sea service time alone is not sufficient; completion of structured training during that time must be proven by the TRB.
Stajyer, iki belgenin tarihlerinin tutar: The cadet must make sure that the dates in the two documents are consistent: the task dates in the TRB must match the periods on board documented in the Sea Service record. Inconsistent dates are questioned during review and undermine the validity of the documents.
Sınav başvurusundan önce stajyer, TRB'yi: Before applying for the examination, the cadet reviews the TRB from beginning to end: have all mandatory competences been evidenced, are all pages signed, are the familiarization sections complete for each ship, are the trainer's and the Master's approvals present? This final check prevents the application from being rejected for missing documents.
İdarelerin TRB tamamlanma kriterleri far: Administrations' criteria for TRB completion may differ; the flag State's guidance must be read. Some Administrations require a minimum number of repetitions of certain tasks, others look for minimum evidence in each function. The cadet should learn the specific requirements of their own flag at the start of the voyage.
En sık hata, TRB'yi sefer sonuna kadar b: The most common mistake is leaving the TRB blank until the end of the voyage and trying to fill it in all at once. This produces entries that are both poor in quality and difficult for the trainer to approve. The second mistake is writing tasks in a vague and general way ("I looked at the engine"); the third is recording only easily accessible tasks without regard to the balance of competences.
Dördüncü ciddi hata, fiilen yapılmamış i: The fourth serious mistake is entering in the TRB work that was not actually done. This is both a disciplinary offense and a risk that will be exposed in the oral examination. The TRB is also a test of the cadet's honesty; an exaggerated book creates distrust in the examination interview.
Doğru pratik şudur: günlük ve somut kayı: Correct practice is: daily and concrete entries, a weekly signing rhythm, a monthly gap analysis, a balanced spread of competences, repeated familiarization on every new ship and physical safety of the book. A cadet who adopts these disciplines will be ready for the examination file at the end of the voyage with a complete and strong TRB.
TRB ayrıca stajyerin kariyer boyu sürece: The TRB is also the first step in a learning habit that will last the cadet's whole career. Systematic recording, sharp observation and self-assessment are the basic professional disciplines of the engineer who will later become an OOW, and then Second/Chief Engineer.
TRB yönetimi, makine stajyerinin sertifi: TRB management is the most concrete responsibility in the engine cadet's certification journey. A well-managed book not only secures the right to sit the examination; it also documents the cadet's real competence, honesty and professional discipline. Daily recording discipline, balanced evidence of competence and regular approval are the three cornerstones of a complete TRB. A cadet who neglects this book risks the valuable months spent at sea being left without evidence.
Deniz kazalarının büyük çoğunluğu tek bi: Most marine casualties result not from a single error but from small overlapping omissions (error chain). Safety procedures are designed to break this chain at specific points: LOTO isolates energy, the PTW assesses the risk in advance and atmosphere testing reveals invisible hazards. Every procedure is a lesson from fatal accidents of the past.
Stajyer, prosedürleri \"bürokrasi\" deği: The cadet should see procedures not as "bureaucracy" but as "survival tools". The thought "I will cut corners this time" is the first link in the accident chain. Experienced engineers know that following the procedure even in the most routine job is the mark of professionalism.
Stajyer, emniyet prosedürlerine gözetiml: The cadet takes part in safety procedures under supervision: applies LOTO, reads the PTW form, observes atmosphere testing. However, under no circumstances does the cadet independently remove an isolation, enter an enclosed space without a permit or start hot work. Every safety-critical operation is carried out with the approval and under the supervision of an authorized person.
Stajyerin en güçlü emniyet aracı \"speak: The cadet's strongest safety tool is the right to "speak up". On seeing an unsafe situation — whatever the difference in seniority — the cadet must know to stop and report. In many accidents, a junior crew member's failure to voice a hazard they had noticed has ended in disaster.
LOTO, bir ekipman üzerinde çalışılırken: LOTO prevents equipment from starting unexpectedly, or stored energy (electrical, pressure, steam, hydraulic, mechanical) from being released, while work is being done on it.
