Before maintenance on a pump, fan, compressor or electric motor, the energy source is isolated, locked (lock) and tagged (tag).
Standart LOTO adımları: hazırlık ve bild: Standard LOTO steps: preparation and notification, stopping the equipment, isolating all energy sources, fitting locks and tags, releasing stored energy (pressure relief, capacitor discharge) and verification of zero energy (try-out: attempt to start, see that it does not run). Each worker fits their own lock; another person's lock may not be removed.
Stajyer, gözetimli bir bakım işinde kend: In a supervised maintenance job, the cadet learns to fit their own lock and learns the importance of zero energy verification. The attitude "we fitted the lock but did not test it" is dangerous; the proof of real isolation is attempting to start and seeing that the equipment does not run (try-to-start).
Stajyer ayrıca grup LOTO mantığını öğren: The cadet also learns the logic of group LOTO: if more than one person is working on the same equipment, everyone fits their own lock and removes it when their work is finished. The equipment cannot be energized until the last lock is removed. This ensures that nobody is "forgotten" and left in danger.
PTW, yüksek riskli işlerin başlamadan ön: The PTW is a formal permit system documenting that high-risk work has been systematically assessed and the necessary precautions taken before it starts. Work such as hot work, enclosed space entry, aloft work (working at height), electrical isolation and diving usually requires a separate permit. The permit defines the job, the risks, the precautions taken, the responsible person and the period of validity.
PTW süreci risk değerlendirmesini (risk: The PTW process makes a risk assessment mandatory: what hazards there are, who may be affected, what controls will be applied. When the job is finished, the permit is closed and the area returns to normal. Work cannot continue on an expired permit until it is renewed.
Stajyer, bir permit formunun nasıl doldu: The cadet learns how a permit form is completed, which questions are asked and which approvals are required. The cadet understands that a permit is not just a piece of paper; each line represents a concrete precaution. The line "Has the atmosphere been tested?" is the guarantee of a life.
Stajyer, kendi katıldığı işlerin permit': The cadet should read the permit for the jobs they take part in and ask themselves "what is the risk in this job and how are we protected?" This habit forms the basis of the risk awareness of the responsible engineer who will sign permits in the future.
Kapalı alanlar (tanklar, cofferdam, ball: Enclosed spaces (tanks, cofferdams, ballast tanks, bilges, chain lockers, boilers) may contain invisible lethal atmospheres: oxygen deficiency, toxic gases (H2S), explosive vapors (LEL) and carbon monoxide. Human senses cannot detect most of these hazards; therefore atmosphere testing before and during entry is vital.
Giriş prosedürü: alanı izole et ve haval: Entry procedure: isolate and ventilate the space, test the atmosphere (O2, LEL, toxic gases), issue the permit, assign standby personnel, ensure continuous communication and monitoring, keep a rescue plan ready. Nobody may enter until the readings are within the safe range. Oxygen must be around 20.9%, LEL 0% and toxic gases below their threshold limits.
Stajyer için en katı kural budur: hiçbir: This is the strictest rule for the cadet: under no circumstances is an enclosed space entered without a permit, without testing and without supervision. Thoughts such as "I'll just take a quick look" or "I'm only going to get my tool" are fatal. Most enclosed space fatalities are people who went in "just for a moment".
Daha da önemlisi: içeride biri baygın gö: More importantly: if someone is seen unconscious inside, the cadet first raises the alarm and calls for help; the cadet does not rush into an unsupervised and unequipped rescue. The statistics of enclosed space accidents are painful: a significant proportion of those who die are rescuers who ran to save the first victim and were asphyxiated in the same atmosphere.
Hot work (kaynak, taşlama, kesme, açık a: Hot work (welding, grinding, cutting, open flame) significantly increases the risk of fire and explosion on board. Fuel vapor, oily surfaces and combustible materials can be ignited by a spark. For this reason, hot work requires a separate permit and the atmosphere is verified as "gas-free".
Önlemler: çalışma alanını yanıcılardan a: Precautions: clear the work area of combustibles, close nearby openings, have a fire extinguisher and a fire watch present, test the atmosphere, and keep the area under watch for a set time after the work is finished (risk of a spark starting a delayed fire). Hot work is particularly restricted on tankers and near flammable cargo.
Stajyer, hot work sırasında genellikle f: During hot work, the cadet is usually present as fire watch support or as an observer. The cadet learns how critical the fire watch is: a small spark can start a fire even minutes later. The cadet must know the location, type and use of the extinguisher.
Stajyer ayrıca \"neden bu işten önce tan: The cadet also learns the answer to the question "why was the tank made gas-free before this job?" In the past, many tankers and other ships have exploded, with loss of life, as a result of hot work carried out with inadequate preparation. Every step of the procedure is the lesson of a death.
Blackout, tüm ana güç kaynağının kaybedi: A blackout is the loss of all main power; the ship is plunged into darkness and left immobile. In this case, the emergency generator starts automatically and supplies the critical loads (emergency lighting, steering gear, communications, fire pump). The recovery procedure includes diagnosing the cause, manual/automatic start of the generators, stepwise load acceptance and restarting the main engine.
Stajyer, blackout recovery'yi gözlemleye: By observing blackout recovery, the cadet learns the prioritization of the power system: first the emergency switchboard, then the main generators, then heavy loads. A blackout during maneuvering or in confined waters creates a risk of collision/grounding, so the speed of recovery is critical.
Makine dairesi yangını en tehlikeli gemi: An engine room fire is one of the most dangerous fires on a ship; fuel, oil and hot surfaces are present together. The response includes the steps of shutting off the fuel supply (quick-closing valves), shutting down the ventilation (ventilation flaps), withdrawing personnel, closing off the space (boundary cooling) and activating the fixed smothering system (CO2/foam/water mist). A personnel count is always carried out before the fixed system is released.
Su basması (flooding) ise hull/boru hasa: Flooding may result from hull/pipe damage or failure of the sea water system. The bilge pumps, emergency bilge suction and damage control are brought into action. The cadet learns the bilge alarm system, the capacities of the bilge pumps and the early signs of flooding (rising bilge level).
Makine dairesinin en az iki bağımsız kaç: The engine room has at least two independent escape routes; one of these may be a protected (fire-protected) escape trunk. The cadet must know the escape routes well enough to find them with eyes closed, because in a real fire smoke can reduce visibility to zero. Emergency lighting and photoluminescent signs then show the way.
Muster station (toplanma yeri), acil dur: The muster station is the designated place where the crew assemble in an emergency. The muster list shows each person's duty in an emergency (fire party, liferaft, first aid, etc.). The cadet must know their own muster duty and station by heart; this is learned during familiarization and reinforced through drills.
Tatbikatlar (drills), acil durum prosedü: Drills ensure that emergency procedures become ingrained in muscle memory. The cadet takes an active part in abandon ship, fire, enclosed space rescue and man overboard drills. Treating a drill as a "formality" is dangerous; when a real incident occurs, people can only do what they have rehearsed.
Stajyer her tatbikattan sonra kendine so: After every drill, the cadet should ask: "Did I know my duty? Did I use the equipment correctly? What could I have done faster/more safely?" This self-assessment and the post-drill debrief determine performance in a real emergency.
PPE, riskin kaynakta giderilemediği duru: PPE is the last line of defense where the risk cannot be eliminated at source. Basic PPE in the engine room is safety shoes (steel toe cap), a boiler suit, ear protection (mandatory in zones above 90 dB), a hard hat, safety glasses and, depending on the situation, gloves (heat/chemical), a respirator and a face shield. Selecting PPE suitable for the work being done is critical.
Gevşek giysi, takı ve açık saç dönen eki: Loose clothing, jewelry and loose hair are a lethal hazard near rotating equipment; entanglement accidents result in serious injury or death. The cadet must get into the habit of checking clothing and accessories when entering the engine room.
PPE ancak doğru kullanıldığında korur. Y: PPE protects only when used correctly. Incorrectly fitted ear protection, a leaking mask or cracked goggles give a false sense of safety. The cadet must check their PPE before every use, replace it if damaged and learn to put it on and take it off correctly.
PPE bireysel sorumluluktur ama aynı zama: PPE is an individual responsibility, but it is also a visible sign of safety culture. A cadet who uses the full PPE both protects themselves and sets the right example for the team. The excuse "it's only a one-minute job" is the most frequent cause of injury.
Emniyet prosedürlerini öğrenmek, makine: Learning safety procedures is the engine cadet's most vital task at sea. LOTO, PTW, enclosed spaces, hot work and PPE are each lessons drawn from past deaths, and none of them is a "formality that can be shortened". The cadet must internalize that following procedures is the mark of professionalism and that stopping and speaking up in an unsafe situation is a right. The safety discipline learned under supervision today is the most valuable legacy of the engineer who will lead a team tomorrow.
Bir mühendis, bir sistemi sadece fizikse: An engineer cannot fully understand a system just by seeing it physically; where the pipes go, which valve isolates what and the design logic of the system can only be learned from the drawing. When a fault is being traced, an isolation is being planned or a transfer line is being set up, the drawing is the engineer's guide.
Stajyer, çizim okumayı sistem tanıma ile: The cadet learns to read drawings in parallel with learning the systems: tracing on site a line seen on the drawing, and finding on the drawing a valve seen on site. This drawing-to-site matching (drawing-to-deck verification) is the basis of true engineering understanding. Memorized equipment knowledge, combined with the ability to read drawings, becomes mastery of the system.
Piping diagram (P&ID benzeri boru devre: A piping diagram (a P&ID-type piping circuit diagram) shows the pipes, valves, pumps and instruments of a fluid system (fuel, oil, cooling water, ballast, bilge). An electrical diagram (single line diagram / wiring diagram) shows power distribution, the switchboard, breakers and motor supply lines. The general arrangement (GA) gives the general layout of the ship/engine room.
Bunların yanında capacity plan (tank yer: In addition, there are the capacity plan (tank layout), the fire control plan and OEM equipment drawings (sectional views, assembly drawings). The cadet learns which question each drawing answers: "where does the fluid go?" is answered in the piping diagram, "where does the power come from?" in the electrical diagram and "where is the equipment?" in the GA.
Piping diagram standart semboller kullan: A piping diagram uses standard symbols: different valve types (gate, globe, ball, butterfly, non-return/check, relief), pumps, filters, heat exchangers, tanks and instruments (pressure/temperature gauges). Lines are usually colored or labeled according to the type of fluid (FO, DO, LO, SW, FW, steam, air).
Çizimi okumak için stajyer \"akışı takip: To read the drawing, the cadet learns the method of "following the flow": tracing the line from the source (tank/pump) to the destination (equipment/tank) and identifying the valves and instruments along the way. A non-return valve indicates that the flow is one-way, a relief valve indicates overpressure protection and a three-way valve indicates diversion.
Bir ekipman üzerinde bakım yapılacaksa,: If maintenance is to be carried out on equipment, the valves to be closed are determined from the drawing. For isolating a pump, the cadet identifies on the drawing the suction and discharge valves and, if necessary, the bypass and drains. Incorrect valve isolation can leave a line thought to be isolated still under pressure and lead to an accident.
Stajyer, çizim üzerinde planladığı izola: The cadet verifies on site the isolation planned on the drawing: the valve number on the drawing must match the label on site, the valve must actually close and LOTO must be applied. This sequence of "from drawing to plan, from plan to site, from site to verification" is the basis of safe maintenance.
Tek hat şeması (single line diagram), ge: The single line diagram shows the backbone of the ship's power system: generators, main switchboard (MSB), bus-tie breakers, transformers, emergency switchboard and distribution boards. The cadet learns how power travels from the generator to the consumer and which breaker protects what.
Wiring/motor starter diagram ise bir mot: The wiring/motor starter diagram details the supply and control circuit of a motor: contactor, overload relay, start/stop buttons, interlocks. The cadet learns to use this diagram when finding out why a pump does not run: has the breaker tripped, has the overload tripped, has an interlock opened the circuit?
Elektrik şeması, izolasyonun nereden yap: The electrical diagram shows where the isolation is to be made. If maintenance is to be done on a motor, the relevant breaker is located, opened and locked (LOTO), and zero energy is verified by measuring the voltage. The cadet learns that saying "we switched off the breaker" is not enough; confirmation by measurement is essential.
Stajyer, elektrik işlerinin yetkili elek: The cadet learns that electrical work is done under the supervision of authorized electrical personnel (ETO/Electro-Technical Officer or an authorized engineer) and that high-voltage (HV) systems require special procedures. The cadet does not intervene in electrical systems independently.
General Arrangement planı, geminin tüm g: The General Arrangement plan shows the layout of all the ship's decks and the engine room. From this plan, the cadet learns which platform/deck each piece of equipment is on, as well as the escape routes, doors and passages. The GA provides quick orientation, particularly on joining a new ship.
Capacity plan ise tankların yerleşimini: The capacity plan shows the arrangement and volumes of the tanks; it is used in sounding and stability calculations. The fire control plan shows the fire zones, fixed systems, extinguisher locations and release points, and is an important part of PSC inspections.
Makine üreticisinin (OEM) bakım el kitap: The sectional and assembly drawings in the machinery manufacturer's (OEM) maintenance manuals show the internal construction of a piece of equipment part by part. In a pump overhaul, these drawings give the dismantling/assembly sequence of the parts, torque values and part numbers.
Stajyer, OEM çizimlerini bakım işiyle bi: The cadet learns to use OEM drawings together with the maintenance job: which part is dismantled in which order, which gasket goes where, which clearance is measured. These drawings also contain spare part codes; these codes are critical for ordering the correct part in the PMS.
PMS, gemideki tüm ekipmanların bakım per: The PMS is software that digitally manages the maintenance intervals, procedures and history of all equipment on board (examples: AMOS, TM Master, ShipManager, BASSnet). Maintenance intervals (running-hour or calendar based) are defined for each piece of equipment; the PMS generates the maintenance that falls due as a work order.
Sınıf kuruluşları (Class), bazı gemiler: For some ships, classification societies (Class) accept an approved PMS under a "Planned Maintenance Scheme" in place of traditional periodic survey. For this reason, the PMS is not just a convenience but a class and ISM requirement. A well-functioning PMS increases equipment reliability and reduces unplanned failures.
PMS'te bakım türleri tanımlanır: önleyic: Maintenance types are defined in the PMS: preventive (planned, periodic), condition-based (according to measurements) and corrective/breakdown (after failure). Preventive maintenance is done as planned, before any failure; condition-based maintenance is triggered by indicators such as vibration/oil analysis.
Bakım aralıkları çalışma saati (running: Maintenance intervals may be based on running hours or on the calendar. For example, a purifier requires maintenance "every 2000 hours" or a safety valve "once a year". The PMS generates work orders automatically from running hours entries or as the date advances.
Bir iş emri (work order), PMS'te bir bak: A work order represents a maintenance task in the PMS: which equipment, which job, which procedure, the spare parts and time required. The PMS generates work orders automatically for planned jobs; for an unplanned failure, a work order is opened manually. A work order passes through the stages of planning, material preparation, execution and close-out.
İş bitince iş emri kapatılır (close-out): When the job is finished, the work order is closed (close-out): the work done, hours spent, parts used, measurements (clearance, pressure) and observations are recorded. This close-out record builds up the equipment's maintenance history and is used in planning the next maintenance, as well as evidence in class surveys.
Stajyer, gözetimli olarak iş emri okumay: Under supervision, the cadet learns to read a work order and to find the relevant procedure and required parts in the PMS. When taking part in a maintenance job, the cadet opens the relevant work order, follows the procedure and observes how the close-out record is made at the end of the job. This is where drawing-reading and PMS skills come together with maintenance.
Stajyer, iş emri kapanış kaydının kalite: The cadet learns the importance of the quality of the work order close-out record: writing "done" is not enough; measured values, replaced parts and observations must be recorded. A good close-out record tells the next engineer the real condition of the equipment.
Her yedek parça, PMS/envanter sisteminde: Every spare part is identified in the PMS/inventory system by a code (part number / IMPA or OEM code). This code is critical for ordering the correct part; two parts that look similar may have different codes, and ordering the wrong part causes delay and cost. The part code is usually found in the OEM maintenance manual and the equipment drawing.
Stok kontrolü, kritik yedek parçaların m: Stock control ensures that the minimum stock level of critical spare parts is maintained. When a part is used, it is deducted from the inventory; when the level falls below the minimum, a reorder is triggered. Critical spares (for safety and the main engine) are always kept in stock; class may require them to be carried.
Stajyer, bir bakım işi için doğru parçay: The cadet learns to find the correct part for a maintenance job in the PMS, to match the part code with the drawing/manual and to deduct the part used from the inventory. Although this discipline may look like "shelf keeping", it is the basis of the ship's operational continuity: an incorrect record leads to a part not being found at a critical moment.
Stajyer ayrıca periyodik stok sayımının: The cadet also learns why periodic stocktaking is carried out: the physical stock and the system record must agree. A discrepancy shows either that the records have not been updated or that a part has been used without being recorded. Disciplined recording is the only way to a reliable inventory.
Teknik çizim okuma ve PMS kullanımı, mak: Reading technical drawings and using the PMS are the two basic skills that turn the engine cadet from an observer who "knows the equipment" into an engineer who "manages the system". The drawing shows the logic of the system and the route to safe isolation; the PMS makes maintenance planned, recorded and sustainable. As the cadet develops the discipline of finding on site what is seen on the drawing, confirming on the drawing what is seen on site and recording every maintenance job correctly in the PMS, the cadet becomes a reliable part of the ship's technical memory.
STCW, yeterlilik belgesi için \"qualifyi: STCW defines "qualifying seagoing service" for certificates of competency. This covers periods when the ship is actually at sea on voyages and the candidate serves in a position relevant to the duties. Time waiting in port, in the shipyard (lay-up) and periods without duties are generally not counted at the same rate; the rules of the flag Administration determine this distinction.
Makine stajyeri için deniz hizmeti, maki: For the engine cadet, sea service means the period of structured training and supervised duties in the engine room. This period is not just "being on board" but the active period during which the training program (TRB) is carried out. This is why Sea Service and the TRB complement each other: one proves the duration, the other the content.
Deniz hizmeti birden fazla belgeyle izle: Sea service is tracked by more than one document. The seafarer's book (seafarer's discharge book / service record book) officially records each signing on and signing off. The Seafarer's Employment Agreement (SEA — the employment contract required by MLC 2006) documents employment. The Sea Service Certificate confirms the summary of a given period with the Master's signature.
Stajyer, bu belgelerin tutarlı olmasına: The cadet must make sure that these documents are consistent: the sign-on/sign-off dates in the seafarer's book, the SEA periods and the periods in the Sea Service certificate must match. Inconsistencies are questioned in an Administration/inspection review and undermine the validity of the documents.
Geçerli bir Sea Service Certificate; gem: A valid Sea Service Certificate contains the seafarer's identity details, the ship's name, IMO number, flag, type and tonnage, main engine power (propulsion power — kW), rank/capacity, dates of joining and leaving and the total length of service. The certificate is signed by the Master and bears the ship's stamp.
Bu bilgiler tesadüfi değildir: ana makin: This information is not incidental: main engine power (kW) is related to the tonnage/power limitations of certain certificates; the ship type shows what kind of experience has been gained; the rank determines in which position the service will be counted. A missing field may lead to the certificate being rejected by the Administration.
Stajyer, her gemiden ayrılırken eksiksiz: The cadet should regard obtaining a complete Sea Service Certificate on leaving each ship as their own responsibility. If this certificate is forgotten or obtained incomplete in the rush of signing off, it can be very difficult to obtain later; the ship may have gone to another port, or the Master may have changed. The attitude "I'll get it later" is a serious risk.
Belgeyi alırken stajyer tüm alanları kon: When receiving the certificate, the cadet checks all fields: are the dates correct, are the ship's details complete, is the engine power stated, are the signature and stamp present? An incorrect certificate may become almost impossible to correct when it is noticed at the time of the examination application.
Deniz hizmeti, katılış ve ayrılış tarihl: Sea service is calculated as the number of days between the dates of joining and leaving; however, each Administration's acceptance rules differ. Some Administrations count watchkeeping days specifically, others count shipyard/lay-up periods partly or not at all. The cadet should learn, at the start of the voyage, the rules of their flag and of the Administration to which they will apply.
STCW, OOW (Engine) için belirli bir asga: STCW prescribes a minimum period of approved seagoing service for OOW (Engine) (within a structured training program accepted by the Administration). Knowing the target period, the cadet plans voyages and tracks the time still outstanding; before applying for the examination, the cadet makes sure the period has been completed.
Stajyer, farklı gemilerdeki Sea Service: The cadet must make sure that the dates of the Sea Service certificates from different ships do not overlap; service on two different ships on the same date cannot be shown. In addition, Sea Service dates must be consistent with the seafarer's book entries and the TRB task dates. This three-way consistency is the basis of the reliability of the document file.
Çakışma veya tutarsızlık, idare inceleme: An overlap or inconsistency raises the question of "document reliability" in the Administration's review and may lead to the entire file being subjected to further scrutiny. For this reason, each time a document is received, the cadet should enter the dates in a personal record sheet and check consistency continuously.
Watchkeeping Certificate (Engine) ve nih: For the Watchkeeping Certificate (Engine) and the final OOW certificate, Sea Service is not enough; all competence areas under STCW Table A-III/1 must have been completed in the TRB and approved by the training engineer. Sea Service answers the question "how long", and the TRB the question "what was learned and what is the evidence"; together they make up the examination file.
Stajyer, TRB'sini Sea Service süresiyle: The cadet should progress the TRB in parallel with the Sea Service period. If the evidence of competence is incomplete when the period runs out, even additional sea service will not secure the right to sit the examination. For this reason, the TRB gap analysis (see the TRB management section) is carried out together with sea service planning.
Sea Service belgesi kaptan onayı, TRB is: The Sea Service certificate requires the Master's approval and the TRB the approval of the training engineer (usually the Chief Engineer). The cadet must complete both approvals at the end of each period. A missing approval — for example unsigned TRB pages or an unstamped Sea Service certificate — may invalidate the application.
Onay sürecinde stajyer proaktif olmalı,: In the approval process, the cadet should be proactive and obtain signatures regularly without waiting for the end of the voyage. Trying to get hundreds of pages accumulated by the end of the voyage signed at the last minute is risky and also lowers the quality of the assessment.
OOW (Engine) Certificate of Competency (: An application for an OOW (Engine) Certificate of Competency (CoC) requires several documents to be brought together: approved Sea Service certificates, a completed TRB, mandatory STCW course certificates (Basic Safety, Advanced Firefighting, Survival Craft, Medical First Aid, Security Awareness, etc.), a valid medical certificate and the training institution's diploma/approval. A missing document holds up the application.
Stajyer, başvuru öncesi idarenin güncel: Before applying, the cadet should obtain the Administration's current list of requirements and check every item. Requirements may be updated over time (such as the STCW Manila amendments); relying on old information leads to an incomplete application. Early planning prevents last-minute gaps.
Belge dosyası kabul edildikten sonra ada: Once the document file has been accepted, the candidate enters the examination/assessment stage prescribed by the Administration; this may include written, oral and/or simulator assessment. In the oral examination, the tasks in the candidate's TRB may be questioned; honest and concrete TRB entries are therefore the best examination preparation.
Sınav başarısının ardından idare CoC'yi: After the examination has been passed, the Administration issues the CoC and adds the necessary endorsements. The cadet must learn the certificate's period of validity, the revalidation requirements and the tonnage/power limitations; it is a mistake to think a CoC has no expiry date, as it requires periodic revalidation and recent sea service.
Sea Service belgeleri, cüzdan ve TRB; yı: Sea Service certificates, the seafarer's book and the TRB are evidence accumulated over years and very difficult to reproduce. Their loss, theft or damage (getting wet, fire) may result in the training period not being recognized. The cadet should keep these documents in a waterproof, secure place and protect them carefully when traveling.
Pratik koruma yöntemi, tüm belgelerin yü: A practical method of protection is to make high-resolution digital copies (scans/photos) of all documents and keep them in secure cloud/backup storage. If the original is lost, the digital copy provides a reference for reissue; however, official validity always lies with the original bearing wet-ink signatures.
Stajyer, her gemiden döndüğünde belgeler: On returning from each ship, the cadet immediately adds the documents to their personal file and updates the service record sheet. Documents are kept in chronological order together with their digital backups. This discipline allows the file to be prepared within minutes when applying for the examination.
Belge yönetimi, sadece bir bürokratik gö: Document management is not just a bureaucratic task; it is the protection of the evidence of a career. Even years later, in an application for a higher certificate (Second/Chief Engineer), these early records may serve as a reference. Disciplined filing is the foundation of a habit that lasts a whole career.
En sık problem, eksik veya geç alınan Se: The most frequent problem is a missing or late Sea Service certificate; the certificate is not obtained when leaving the ship and cannot be obtained afterwards. The second problem is missing fields on the certificate (engine power not stated, no stamp, incorrect date). The third is inconsistency between the Sea Service dates and the seafarer's book/TRB dates.
Dördüncü problem, deniz hizmeti süresini: The fourth problem is sea service being calculated incorrectly under the Administration's rules, so that a period the candidate thought was sufficient turns out to be insufficient on the accepted basis. The fifth is that the validity of mandatory courses has expired at the time of application. Most of these problems are prevented by early planning and checks.
Bu sorunların çözümü reaktif değil önley: The solution to these problems is preventive, not reactive: obtain the complete certificate when leaving each ship, check the fields, enter the dates in your personal record sheet, learn the Administration's rules at the start of the voyage and track course validity with a calendar. Review the file months before applying for the examination.
Stajyer, belge sürecini \"sınav zamanı h: The cadet should regard the document process not as "a job to be dealt with at examination time" but as "a natural part of every period at sea". When each period is closed out properly, applying for the examination is simply a matter of bringing together documents that are already prepared.
Sea Service belgesi ve sertifika süreci,: The Sea Service certificate and the certification process are the point at which the valuable months the engine cadet has spent at sea become legal evidence. Complete certificates, consistent dates, a completed TRB and valid courses are the load-bearing pillars of the file leading to the OOW certificate. Obtaining certificates on time and correctly, keeping dates consistent and storing everything securely are the cadet's most basic responsibilities towards their own career. A poorly managed document process can leave even the most successful training period without evidence and invalid.
Yakıt sistemi, ham bunker yakıtını depol: The fuel system stores, heats and cleans (separator) the raw bunker fuel and delivers it to the engine at the correct viscosity/temperature. The lubrication system lubricates, cools and cleans moving parts and prevents wear. Both must operate continuously, cleanly and to the correct specification; otherwise the engine may stop or suffer serious damage.
Risk profili yüksektir: yakıt yanıcıdır: The risk profile is high: fuel is flammable (fire/explosion), hot fuel/oil carries a risk of spraying, and if either enters the sea it constitutes a pollution offense. When learning these systems, the cadet must understand both the technical operation and the safety and environmental aspects together.
Gemilerde başlıca yakıt türleri HFO (Hea: The main fuel types on ships are HFO (Heavy Fuel Oil), VLSFO (Very Low Sulphur Fuel Oil), MGO/MDO (Marine Gas/Diesel Oil) and, increasingly, alternative fuels such as LNG. Each has a different viscosity, sulfur content and treatment requirement. ISO 8217 defines marine fuel specifications; fuel received is expected to comply with this specification.
MARPOL Annex VI, ECA (Emission Control A: MARPOL Annex VI sets the sulfur limits in ECAs (Emission Control Areas) and in general waters (global limit 0.50% m/m, within an ECA 0.10% m/m). The cadet learns which fuel is used in which area, the fuel changeover procedure and the importance of the BDN (Bunker Delivery Note) record.
Bunkering, gemiye yakıt alınması operasy: Bunkering is the operation of taking fuel on board and carries a high risk of pollution/fire. Before the operation, the bunker plan is prepared, tank capacities and ullages are calculated, the line is checked, the valve alignment is verified, SOPEP equipment is kept ready and the scuppers (deck drain holes) are plugged. The ship-shore checklist is completed and communication is established.
Bunker sırasında sürekli izleme yapılır:: During bunkering, continuous monitoring is carried out: tank levels, flow rate (loading rate), overflow tank condition and line leaks. The emergency stop signal is agreed in advance. By following the bunkering operation under supervision, the cadet learns both the technical and the safety aspects; however, valve/pump control rests with authorized personnel.
Bunker tesliminde Bunker Delivery Note (: On bunker delivery, the Bunker Delivery Note (BDN) documents the quantity, density, sulfur content and delivery details of the fuel; under MARPOL Annex VI it is retained for a set period. During delivery, the MARPOL sample (representative sample) is taken and sealed; in a dispute or a PSC inspection, this sample is analyzed.
Yakıt kalitesi kritiktir: spesifikasyon: Fuel quality is critical: off-specification fuel (off-spec — water, solids, cat fines, high sulfur) can cause serious damage to the engine. The cadet observes the logic of sampling, sealing and checking the BDN. Suspect fuel should not be used in the engine before the laboratory analysis (fuel testing) result has been received.
Yakıt, depolama tankından (storage/bunke: Fuel flows from the storage tank (storage/bunker tank) to the settling tank and from there to the service tank. In the settling tank, the fuel is heated and allowed to stand; heavy water and sediment sink to the bottom and are drained off (settling). The service tank holds clean fuel that has passed through the separator, ready to be pumped to the engine. This chain cleans the fuel in stages.
Stajyer, bu tank zincirinin neden bu sır: The cadet learns why this tank chain is arranged in this order: the settling time allows water/sediment to separate, the separator removes the remaining impurities and the service tank holds the final clean reserve. If the settling tank water drain is not done regularly, water reaches the engine and combustion/injection problems arise.
Ağır yakıt (HFO/VLSFO) makineye doğru vi: Heavy fuel (HFO/VLSFO) must reach the engine at the correct viscosity; for this reason, heating (heating coils, trace heating) is fitted in the tanks and lines. The Viscotherm/viscosity controller automatically adjusts the temperature to bring the fuel to the optimum viscosity before injection (usually ~12-15 cSt). Incorrect viscosity causes poor atomization and combustion problems.
Stajyer, yakıt sıcaklık ve viskozite kon: The cadet learns the direct relationship between fuel temperature/viscosity control and engine performance: fuel that is too cold/viscous atomizes poorly, and fuel that is too hot can cause problems in the injection pumps. This balance is the basis of clean and efficient combustion in the engine.
Separatör (purifier/clarifier), yüksek h: The separator (purifier/clarifier) separates water and solid particles from fuel/oil by high-speed centrifugal force. In purifier mode, water and oil are separated (the water is discharged); in clarifier mode, only solids are separated. Separation, which is based on the difference in density, is balanced by gravity disc selection (in conventional separators) or by automatic water detection (in modern separators).
Stajyer, separatör operasyonunu gözetiml: The cadet follows separator operation under supervision: feed temperature (the optimum temperature for oil/fuel improves separation), throughput, water outlet (water seal) and periodic desludging (sludge discharge). The correct temperature and throughput determine the separation efficiency; excessive throughput impairs cleaning.
En sık separatör sorunu, yağ/yakıtın su: The most frequent separator problem is oil/fuel escaping through the water outlet (overboard); this may be caused by loss of the water seal, the wrong gravity disc or excessive throughput, and creates a risk of both fuel loss and pollution. Other problems are vibration (bowl imbalance), insufficient desludging and leaks.
Stajyer, separatörün \"normal\" çalışma: The cadet must learn the separator's "normal" running sound, vibration and appearance so as to be able to notice what is abnormal. Separator overhaul (bowl cleaning, gasket replacement) is a regular PMS job; by taking part in this maintenance, the cadet learns the internal construction. The sludge removed is managed subject to entry in the ORB.
Ana makine yağlama sistemi; LO sump tank: The main engine lubrication system consists of the LO sump tank, LO pumps, LO cooler, filters and distribution lines. The oil lubricates and cools the main bearings, the crosshead/crankpin bearings, the piston (piston cooling oil) and the cam mechanism, then returns to the sump. Circulation is continuous and under pressure.
Stajyer; LO inlet pressure/temperature,: The cadet learns to monitor LO inlet pressure/temperature, sump level, filter differential pressure and cooler inlet/outlet temperatures. Falling LO pressure (pump/filter/leak) is a critical alarm and triggers slow-down/shut-down; for this reason, the LO system is under constant monitoring.
Büyük iki-zamanlı dizel makinelerde iki: Large two-stroke diesel engines have two separate oils: system oil (crankcase lubrication, cooling) and cylinder oil (lubrication of the cylinder liner wall, dosed by the lubricators). Cylinder oil is selected with a BN (Base Number) suited to the sulfur content of the fuel; the correct BN and feed rate are critical for neutralization of the sulfur.
Stajyer, cylinder oil feed rate'in (g/kW: The cadet learns why the cylinder oil feed rate (g/kWh) is adjusted according to fuel sulfur: insufficient lubrication causes liner wear and scuffing, while excessive lubrication causes deposits and cost. Scrape-down oil analysis is one way of monitoring cylinder condition. This balance is fundamental to engine life.
Yakıt ve yağ numuneleri düzenli alınır:: Fuel and oil samples are taken regularly: the MARPOL bunker sample, a fuel sample before use and periodic LO samples (used oil analysis). Samples must be representative and taken under clean conditions; a contaminated sample gives a false result. Samples are labeled and either tested quickly on board or sent to a laboratory.
LO analizi; viskozite, su içeriği, BN, a: LO analysis shows the condition of the oil in terms of viscosity, water content, BN, wear metals (Fe, Cu, Cr) and deposits. Increasing wear metals may be an early sign of a bearing/liner problem. By observing, the cadet learns sampling discipline and what the analysis results reveal.
Viskozite ve density (yoğunluk) ölçümü,: Viscosity and density measurements are key parameters for fuel quality and separator setting. Density affects the separator's density setting (and, in older separators, gravity disc selection); with very high-density fuels, water separation becomes difficult. Viscosity is the basis of heating/atomization control.
Stajyer, gemide bulunan ölçüm cihazlarıy: The cadet observes how measurements are taken with the instruments on board (viscometer, density meter / hydrometer) and learns how these values are reflected in operating settings. Measurement is not an abstract laboratory task; it is a practical tool directly serving the clean and safe operation of the engine.
MARPOL Annex I gereği, makine dairesi ya: Under MARPOL Annex I, engine-room oil operations are recorded in the Oil Record Book Part I: bunkering, internal fuel/oil transfers, pumping bilge water overboard through the OWS, sludge disposal (incinerator/ashore/tank) and tank cleaning. Each operation is recorded under specific code letters (A, B, C, D, E, F, G, H, I) with the date, quantity and details, and signed by the responsible engineer.
Stajyer, ORB formatını okumayı ve her ka: The cadet learns to read the ORB format and what each type of entry means: why and how a bilge transfer is recorded, where sludge was sent, how separator sludge was managed. The ORB is one of the documents most frequently examined in PSC inspections; entries must be consistent with the actual tank levels and with machinery operation.
Bilge suyunu OWS'yi by-pass eden gizli b: Pumping bilge water overboard through a hidden line bypassing the OWS (magic pipe), or making false entries in the ORB, is among the most severely punished offenses at sea. Companies have been fined millions of dollars and crew members have been sentenced to prison. The cadet must learn why the ORB is taken so seriously and why honest recording is non-negotiable.
Stajyer ORB'yi imzalama yetkisine sahip: The cadet is not authorized to sign the ORB; this authority rests with the responsible engineer. However, the cadet learns the recording logic and internalizes the legal weight of this book, which one day will bear the cadet's own signature. Honesty in the ORB is part of the honor of the engineering profession.
Yakıt ve yağlama sistemleri, geminin kal: The fuel and lubrication systems are the arteries that feed and protect the heart of the ship. Bunkering safety, the tank chain, separator operation and LO circulation are the basis of reliable engine operation. At the same time, under MARPOL, these systems are among the most critical sources of marine pollution; honesty in the ORB and safe operation unite the technical and ethical dimensions of engineering. While learning these systems, the cadet must internalize the question "how are the environment and safety protected?" as much as the question "how is the engine fed and protected?"
Geminin ana güç ve kontrol sistemleri ar: When the ship's main power and control systems fail — blackout, fire, flooding — independent emergency systems with their own power sources are needed to maintain safety. These are located separately from the main systems (usually above the main deck, in a watertight compartment) and can operate without main power. The aim is to maintain basic safety functions even in the worst-case scenario.
Acil sistemler yalnızca var olmakla yetm: It is not enough for emergency systems simply to exist; they must be kept "ready to operate at any moment" by regular testing and maintenance. An emergency generator or fire pump that is not tested runs the risk of not working in a real emergency. For this reason, the regulations make periodic testing of these systems mandatory; the cadet learns by observing these tests.
Stajyer, acil sistem testlerine gözlemci: The cadet attends emergency system tests as an observer; the cadet does not start the system or intervene independently, but carefully follows the test procedure, the system's response and the success criteria. With each test, the cadet reinforces the answer to the question "when, why and how does this system cut in?"
Stajyer için acil sistem testleri çok de: For the cadet, emergency system tests are very valuable learning opportunities: scenarios not seen in normal operation (loss of power, automatic cut-in) are observed under controlled conditions. The cadet enters every test in the TRB and discusses the observations with the training engineer.
Emergency generator, ana güç (main gener: When main power (main generators) is lost, the emergency generator cuts in automatically and supplies the critical loads through the emergency switchboard: emergency lighting, navigation lights, steering gear, communications (GMDSS), fire detection, watertight doors and the emergency fire pump. It is usually located above the main deck, with its own fuel tank and starting system.
Blackout olduğunda emergency generator o: In a blackout, the emergency generator starts automatically (auto-start) and is usually ready to take load within 45 seconds (SOLAS requirement). Its starting source is independent (battery or compressed air). By observing the auto-start test, the cadet learns how the system detects the loss of power and cuts in.
Emergency generator testi, hem manuel st: The emergency generator test includes both a manual start (weekly trial) and an auto-start (simulated loss of power). During the test, starting success, achieving the required running time, voltage/frequency stability, load transfer to the emergency switchboard and the fuel/oil condition are observed. After the test, the system is returned to standby mode.
Stajyer, testte özellikle \"süre\" boyut: In the test, the cadet pays particular attention to the "time" dimension: how quickly was the generator ready to take load? Did the auto-start detect the loss of power correctly? Is the fuel tank sufficient (it is usually kept at a capacity for running for a set period)? These observations are indicators of the system's reliability in a real emergency.
Emergency fire pump, ana yangın pompalar: The emergency fire pump supplies firefighting water when the main fire pumps cannot operate (for example when an engine room fire has put the main pumps out of action). For this reason, it is located outside the engine room, in a separate compartment, and has its own independent power source (a motor supplied from the emergency generator, or an independent diesel).
Pompanın bağımsız konumu kritiktir: maki: The independent location of the pump is critical: in an engine room fire, the main pumps may be inaccessible; in this scenario, the emergency fire pump continues to supply pressure to the fire main. SOLAS specifies the pump's capacity and requires a minimum pressure at specified fire hydrants.
Stajyer, testte pompanın ne kadar sürede: In the test, the cadet observes how long the pump takes to supply pressure and observes the remote start mechanism. On most ships, the pump can be started remotely from outside the engine room; this makes it possible to respond to a fire without entering the engine room. The cadet learns where this remote start point is.
Ana makinenin başlatılması (start) genel: The main engine is usually started with compressed air; this air is stored in air bottles (air receivers) and filled by the main air compressors. The emergency air compressor is an independent capacity that provides enough air to restart the main engine when the main compressors cannot operate (as in a blackout); on some ships it may be driven by an independent diesel or supplied from emergency power.
Stajyer, blackout recovery'de emergency: The cadet learns the role of the emergency air compressor in blackout recovery: there must be enough starting air to start the main engine. Keeping the air bottle pressure at a set level and keeping the emergency compressor in working order are prerequisites for recovery after a blackout. The test verifies the compressor's ability to build up pressure.
Dümen sistemi (steering gear), geminin m: The steering gear is fundamental to the ship's ability to maneuver and avoid collision; for this reason it is designed with redundancy. If the main steering gear fails or power is lost, emergency steering mode is used: the second hydraulic pump is started or local/manual control is applied from the steering gear room. Communication (telephone) between the bridge and the steering gear room, and a rudder angle indicator, are provided.
Stajyer, emergency steering tatbikatını: The cadet observes the emergency steering drill: how control is transferred from the bridge to the steering gear room, how local control is carried out, how communication is maintained. SOLAS requires emergency steering drills to be held regularly; when a real steering failure occurs, the team must already have rehearsed.
Quick closing valve, yakıt/yağ tankların: Quick-closing valves are valves fitted at the outlets of fuel/oil tanks that can be closed remotely (usually from outside the engine room, from a control station). In an engine room fire, these valves are closed remotely to cut off the fuel supply to the fire; this is one of the most critical steps in preventing the fire from spreading.
Valfler genelde yay veya pnömatik/hidrol: The valves are usually closed by a spring or pneumatic/hydraulic mechanism, operated by a lever or button at a remote position. The cadet learns which tanks have quick-closing valves, where the remote closing position is and how the fuel supply is cut off after closing. Periodic testing of these valves (do they actually close?) is important.
Emergency stop butonları, makine dairesi: Emergency stop buttons stop fuel pumps, separators, fans and other critical equipment remotely from outside the engine room. In a fire, this stops the supply of fuel/oil and the circulation of air to the space and so makes firefighting possible. Ventilation flaps are closed remotely to cut off the entry of air (oxygen) into the engine room.
Fixed smothering system (CO2 veya benzer: Before the fixed smothering system (CO2 or similar) is activated, the ventilation flaps must be closed and the fans stopped; otherwise the extinguishing gas is expelled and the fire cannot be extinguished. The cadet learns the order of these remote controls in the firefighting chain: shut off fuel → stop equipment → close ventilation → count personnel → release the fixed system.
Blackout, tüm ana jeneratörlerin güç kay: A blackout is when all main generators lose power and the ship is left without electricity and immobile. Causes may be a generator trip (overload, fault), interruption of the fuel supply, an automation fault or a main switchboard problem. At the moment of blackout, the emergency generator cuts in automatically and supplies the critical loads; the recovery process starts immediately.
Recovery'nin ilk adımı nedeni hızlıca te: The first step in recovery is to diagnose the cause quickly: which generator tripped, and why? Then a generator is started manually/automatically, connected to the main switchboard and loaded in stages (critical consumers first, then heavy consumers). Rushing to take all the load at once may lead to a new trip (cascade blackout).
Blackout, özellikle dar suda veya manevr: A blackout is most dangerous in confined waters or during maneuvering; the ship rapidly loses maneuvering and steering capability, and a risk of collision/grounding arises. For this reason, the engine room is put on standby before maneuvering (an extra generator in parallel), and the speed of recovery is critical. Immediate coordination between the bridge and the engine room is essential.
Stajyer, blackout recovery tatbikatını v: The cadet treats a blackout recovery drill, or observing a real one, as a major learning opportunity: prioritization of the power system, paralleling of generators, the role of starting air and team communication are displayed intensively within a few minutes. The cadet follows each step, notes questions and discusses them with the training engineer.
Acil sistem testleri ve tatbikatları, IS: Emergency system tests and drills are recorded as required by ISM and SOLAS. The test date, result, abnormalities found and corrective actions are documented. These records are the evidence in PSC inspections and class surveys that the system has been tested regularly. A system that the records show has not been tested constitutes a serious inspection finding.
Stajyer, test kayıtlarının nasıl tutuldu: The cadet learns how test records are kept and enters every test/drill attended in the TRB. This supports both regulatory discipline and the TRB evidence of competence. A record is the only way to go beyond saying "the system exists" and to say "the system has been tested and works".
Acil sistemler, \"her an çalışmaya hazır: Emergency systems must be "ready to operate at any moment"; this requires regular maintenance. The emergency generator fuel/oil levels and battery, the fire pump priming system, the air compressor and the quick-closing valve mechanisms are checked periodically. The PMS manages this maintenance through planned work orders.
Stajyer, acil sistemlerin bakımına gözet: By taking part in the maintenance of emergency systems under supervision, the cadet both gets to know the system and grasps the question "why is this maintenance critical": a poorly maintained emergency system runs the risk of not working in a real emergency, which is even more dangerous than not having the system at all (a false sense of safety). An emergency system kept ready is the ship's insurance.
Acil sistemler, geminin \"en kötü gün\": Emergency systems are the ship's preparation for its "worst day"; they remain invisible in normal operation but determine the survival of the ship and crew in a crisis. The emergency generator, fire pump, air compressor and steering gear; quick-closing valves and remote controls; blackout recovery — none of them is reliable unless tested regularly. By observing these tests, the cadet learns the answers to "how does the system work, and does it really work?" together. The emergency system logic grasped today as an observer forms the basis of the composure and preparedness of the engineer who will manage a crisis tomorrow.
Reis, güverte bölümünün en kıdemli tayfa: The Bosun is the most senior rating in the deck department and works directly under the Chief Officer. The Bosun's authority is limited to interpreting the work order, allocating the team, ensuring safety on site and checking the quality of the work. Authority for planning and prioritization remains with the Chief Officer; the Bosun turns this plan into work on site. Knowing this distinction prevents taking unnecessary initiative and stepping outside safe limits.
Reis aynı zamanda tayfanın \"abisi\"dir;: The Bosun is also the "big brother" of the ratings, passing on technical knowledge, shipboard etiquette and safety culture. A good Bosun leads by example rather than by giving orders; the Bosun personally demonstrates the hardest job and stands at the front at the riskiest point. Team discipline comes not from fear but from this trust.
Tipik bir bakım gününde Reis, ekipten ön: On a typical maintenance day, the Bosun gets up before the team and reviews the weather, the ship's situation (in port/at sea), active work orders and work left over from the previous day. The Bosun holds a short synchronization with the Chief Officer: which job has priority today, which area is closed because of operations, which permit will be needed.
08:00'de güverte ekibi toplanır. Reis, g: At 08:00 the deck team assembles. The Bosun explains the day's work, the team allocation, the risks and the PPE requirements. This toolbox meeting is the most important 15 minutes of the day; a well-planned morning means an accident-free and productive day.
Birinci Zabit, PMS (Planned Maintenance: The Chief Officer gives the Bosun the work orders generated by the PMS (Planned Maintenance System) software. Each order contains the equipment, the work to be done, the materials list, the PPE required, the relevant risk assessment reference, the estimated duration and the evidence of completion (photo, measurement, signature). Before carrying out the order, the Bosun confirms that the materials and tools are available.
Reis emri yorumlarken sahanın gerçeğini: When interpreting the order, the Bosun brings in the reality on the ground: weather, sea state, the ship's port/sea schedule, the team's current fatigue and operations running at the same time. A plan that is perfect on paper cannot be carried out on deck in a storm; the Bosun sees this difference and gives feedback to the officer.
İşler; emniyet kritikliği, klas/PSC takv: Jobs are ranked according to safety criticality, the class/PSC schedule, the weather window and operational dependency. Safety equipment (liferaft servicing, fire main, LSA) and inspection preparation jobs always have priority. These are followed by voyage-critical jobs (lashing, hatch cover tightness), and then by cosmetic maintenance (painting, cleaning).
Her tayfanın yetkinliği, sertifikası ve: Each rating's competence, certification and experience differ. The Bosun matches qualified (AB - Able Seaman), general (OS - Ordinary Seaman) and novice (deck cadet/trainee) personnel to jobs according to the risk. High-risk work (working aloft, overside, enclosed space, hot work) is given only to trained personnel under supervision.
Reis, ekibi tanır: kimin yüksekte rahat: The Bosun knows the team: who works comfortably at height, who is meticulous with paint, who is quick with ropework. Putting the right person on the right job increases both safety and productivity; a wrong match means unfinished work or injury.
Bazı işler tek kişiyle yapılamaz: workin: Some jobs cannot be done by one person: working aloft requires a standby person at deck level, enclosed space entry a standby person plus atmosphere testing, and overside work a lookout ready for MOB. The Bosun sets the team size according to the minimum safe number of personnel for the job; risky work is not started with too few people.
Genç personel, deneyimli bir tayfa ile e: Young personnel are paired with an experienced rating and work within a "buddy system". This serves both teaching and safety; a novice is never left alone in a high-risk area.
Toolbox meeting (toolbox talk), iş başla: The toolbox meeting (toolbox talk) is a short safety briefing held before work starts. The Bosun explains what the job is, its steps, its risks, the precautions to be taken and what to do in an emergency. Participation is two-way; the ratings are asked to point out where they see hazards.
İyi bir toolbox; somut, kısa ve işe özel: A good toolbox talk is concrete, short and specific to the job. Saying "be careful" is not enough; specific instructions are given, such as "when changing the grinder disc, cut off the air, check the flange, put on the face shield". For important jobs, a job-specific risk assessment (JSA) is completed and the participants sign it.
Çok uluslu ekiplerde ortak çalışma dili: In multinational teams, a common working language (usually English + maritime jargon) is used. The Bosun confirms by read-back that the instruction has been understood. An order that is not understood is carried out wrongly on site, and that means an accident. Visual demonstration and showing by doing are the most effective ways to overcome the language barrier.
Reis, ekibin baret, emniyet ayakkabısı,: The Bosun checks that the team is wearing a hard hat, safety shoes, boiler suit, gloves, goggles, ear protection and job-specific equipment (harness, face shield, dust mask, lifejacket), complete and in good condition. Damaged PPE is replaced immediately. PPE is the last line of defense; it remains indispensable even after the risk has been eliminated at source.
Reis, sahada sürekli dolaşır; permit kap: The Bosun moves around the site continuously and immediately warns personnel who step outside the scope of the permit, work without PPE or take dangerous shortcuts. A small violation that is tolerated becomes normal and prepares the ground for a major accident. The principle "unsafe behavior that is ignored is unsafe behavior that is approved" applies.
STCW ve MLC 2006, mürettebatın asgari di: STCW and MLC 2006 regulate the minimum hours of rest for the crew: at least 10 hours of rest in any 24 hours and at least 77 hours in any 7 days; rest may be divided into no more than two periods, one of which must be at least 6 hours uninterrupted. The Bosun does not plan work in a way that would breach the team's work/rest hours records.
Yorgunluk, denizdeki kazaların başlıca i: Fatigue is the main human factor in accidents at sea. A rating who has worked long hours during a port/maneuvering period is not given risky work the following morning. By making sure the team actually rests, the Bosun both complies with the regulations and prevents accidents.
Reis; dikkat dağınıklığı, yavaşlama, sin: The Bosun spots signs of fatigue early, such as lack of concentration, slowing down, irritability and increasing errors. In such a case, the pace of work is changed, the team is rotated or the job is postponed. The most valuable quality of an on-site leader is the ability to "read" the team.
Reis, masaya oturup işi izlemez; sahada: The Bosun does not sit at a desk watching the work; the Bosun moves around the site and personally steps in on the technique and safety of the work. On seeing a job start wrongly, the Bosun stops it and shows the correct method. If more than one job is under way at the same time, the Bosun gives the most time to the riskiest one.
Reis, işin ilerlemesini takip eder ve ge: The Bosun follows the progress of the work and informs the Chief Officer in good time when a delay or obstacle arises (shortage of materials, change in the weather, equipment failure). Passing a problem on site to the officer late means a loss of productivity for the whole day.
Limanda yük operasyonu, bunkering, store: In port, cargo operations, bunkering, taking stores and maintenance may all run at the same time. The Bosun ensures that these jobs do not endanger each other — for example, no painting is done underneath a cargo crane while it is working, and no hot work is done during bunkering. Managing overlapping operations is one of the on-site leader's most critical skills.
Gün sonunda Reis, tamamlanan işleri, kul: At the end of the day, the Bosun reports to the Chief Officer on the jobs completed, materials used, jobs left unfinished and observations on site (new rust areas, failed equipment, stock running out). PMS work orders are closed with evidence of completion (photo, measurement).
Bu raporlama yalnızca bürokrasi değildir: This reporting is not just bureaucracy; it is the ship's technical memory. In an inspection, after an accident or when a new team arrives, these records are the only reliable answer to the question "what has been done, and what remains?"
Reis, ucuz atlatılan olayları (near-miss: The Bosun reports near-misses and unsafe conditions with an encouraging attitude. A near-miss culture is the strongest early warning system against major accidents. An instructive rather than punitive approach encourages the team to report.
Ekip disiplini, Reis'in adil ve tutarlı: Team discipline comes from the Bosun being fair and consistent. The same rule is applied equally to everyone; favoritism is what destroys team morale fastest. The Bosun criticizes in private and praises in public; this simple principle protects the team's health for years.
Zor koşullarda (kötü hava, uzun saatler,: In difficult conditions (bad weather, long hours, monotonous work), the Bosun's attitude is reflected in the team. A calm, determined Bosun who stands at the front carries the team; a Bosun who panics or constantly shouts breaks the team apart.
Gemilerde çok uluslu ekipler standarttır: Multinational crews are standard on ships. The Bosun brings ratings of different languages, religions and cultures together in a common safety and work culture. Respect and clear communication are the basic tools. Fairness in mess room arrangements, use of recreation areas and allocation of duties ensures team harmony.
Reis'in günlük yönetimdeki başarısı, \"k: The Bosun's success in daily management lies hidden in trouble-free days that "nobody notices". Well-allocated work, well-supervised safety and a well-motivated team keep the ship both productive and accident-free. As the on-site leader of the deck, the Bosun re-establishes this balance every day.
Çelik gemi gövdesi, deniz suyu, klorür,: A steel ship's hull is under intense attack from seawater, chlorides, oxygen and UV radiation. Once corrosion starts, it accelerates geometrically: a small rust spot can affect hundreds of square meters of surface in 6 months. The Bosun's basic task is to find and remove "small rust spots" before they grow and to maintain the integrity of the protective paint system.
Korozyonun tipleri farklıdır: uniform co: There are different types of corrosion: uniform corrosion (a thin layer over wide surfaces), pitting (localized deep pits — particularly in ballast tanks and in the middle of holds), galvanic corrosion (at joints between dissimilar metals), crevice corrosion (at tight intersections) and stress corrosion cracking (in fatigued areas). Each type requires different measures.
Reis sabah toolbox toplantısından sonra: After the morning toolbox meeting, the Bosun reviews the work orders with the Chief Officer. The work order contains the equipment, the work to be done, the materials list, the PPE required, the risk assessment reference, the estimated duration and the evidence of completion (photo, measurement). When allocating this order to the team, the Bosun combines job competence, team size, weather conditions and the port/at-sea situation.
Yüzey hazırlığı, boyanın ömrünü %60-80 o: Surface preparation determines 60-80% of the life of the paint. ISO 8501-1 defines practical standards for surface cleanliness. There are the levels SA 1 (light brush-off blast), SA 2 (thorough blast), SA 2.5 (very thorough — the industry norm) and SA 3 (white metal — for special applications). For mechanical cleaning, ST 2 (thorough manual cleaning) and ST 3 (very thorough) are used.
Gemide saha şartlarında SA 2.5 zor sağla: On board, under site conditions, SA 2.5 is difficult to achieve; most areas are prepared with hand tools to around ST 2 - ST 3. Using a visual reference (color chart), the Bosun records which standard the area to be painted has achieved; this is critical for the paint warranty period.
Pneumatic chipping hammer, needle scaler: Pneumatic chipping hammers, needle scalers, angle grinders and disc sanders are the most common tools. The Bosun checks the appropriate PPE (goggles, ear protection, mask, gloves, chaps), the daily check of electric/pneumatic tools, hose connections and grounding. Use of a grinder that requires a hot work permit (especially on a tanker deck) needs the approval of the Chief Officer + Master + Chief Engineer.
Tipik bir güverte boya sistemi: primer (: A typical deck paint system: primer (zinc rich epoxy, 75 µm DFT) → intermediate coat (epoxy, 125 µm) → topcoat (polyurethane, 50 µm). Total DFT (Dry Film Thickness) 250-300 µm. On exposed areas such as hatch tops, the main deck and the forecastle, a UV-resistant topcoat is essential.
Underwater hull için anti-fouling sistem: For the underwater hull, the anti-fouling system (usually applied in drydock): anti-corrosion epoxy + tie coat + self-polishing copolymer (SPC) anti-fouling. The exterior of the accommodation is painted with an enamel finish; intumescent (fire-retardant) paint is used in interior spaces.
Boya tatbiki için ortam koşulları kritik: Ambient conditions are critical for applying paint: the surface temperature must be at least 3 °C above the dew point, relative humidity below 85%, air temperature above +5 °C, and there must be no rain or salt spray. The Bosun measures these parameters with a psychrometer and a temperature probe. Paint applied in the wrong conditions comes off within 6 months.
Boya inceltme oranı (genelde max %5-10),: The thinning ratio (usually max 5-10%), mixing time, pot life (4-6 hours for epoxies) and application method (brush, roller, airless spray) are determined according to the product's TDS (Technical Data Sheet).
Modern gemilerde yüksek mukavemetli HMPE: On modern ships, high-strength HMPE (Dyneema) and polyester blend ropes are common. After every voyage, the rope is checked visually for chafe, glazing (heat damage), kinks, broken yarns and UV fading. Under OCIMF MEG4, ropes are kept on record with regard to LDBF (Line Design Break Force), MBL and the use of "tails".
Cargo wire, mooring wire ve crane wire i: Periodic greasing (OEM lubricant), broken wire counts and diameter measurements are carried out on cargo wires, mooring wires and crane wires. According to ISO 4309 and the company standard, >10% broken wires within a lay length, kinks, severe wear or visible bulging are reasons for retirement.
Hatch cover; rubber gasket, compression: The hatch cover consists of rubber gaskets, compression bars, cleats, hydraulic cylinders and drainage channels. Tightness tests (chalk test, hose test, ultrasonic test) are carried out by the Chief Officer + Bosun. Seawater ingress into the hold is a forerunner of major casualties such as the MOL Comfort.
Reis, kapanan hatch çevresinde rubber co: The Bosun checks the rubber compression marks around the closed hatch; if the compression is not even, the gasket or compression bar must be replaced. For the hydraulic system, checking the oil level and hoses and testing the lift/close function are routine.
Cargo crane periyodik load test (yıllık: Cargo cranes require periodic load tests (annual + 5-yearly at 1.25× SWL) under class survey. The Bosun carries out daily checks: oil level, hydraulic leaks, brake test, operation of the limit switches, wire rope condition, hook safety latch.
Windlass ve mooring winch bakımında; bra: In windlass and mooring winch maintenance, brake band wear, gear oil level, the pawl mechanism and brake holding capacity (annual test) are the critical points. Compliance with SOLAS Chapter II-1 and IACS UR A2 is checked.
Anchor ve chain cable, klas survey'inde: The anchor and chain cable are examined closely at the class survey; they are subject to a program under which, every 5 years, the whole cable is ranged out (extracted), inspected and, if necessary, turned end-for-end. Every day, the Bosun checks the chain locker ventilation, drainage of accumulated mud, the chain stopper, the bow stopper and the devil's claw.
Anchor windlass bakımı vinç bakımıyla be: Anchor windlass maintenance is similar to crane maintenance; in addition, the chain compressor (anchor secured at sea) and the riding pawl are tested periodically.
Limanda gürültülü ve toz yapan işler (ch: In port, noisy and dusty jobs (chipping, grinding, painting) take priority, because at sea a large part of the team is keeping watches. Roughly, 30% of port time is allocated to operations, 50% to maintenance and 20% to rest + documentation.
Seyirde havaya bağlı işler yapılamaz; bu: At sea, weather-dependent jobs cannot be done; instead, maintenance inside equipment (crane servicing, hatch hydraulics, workshop jobs), inventory taking and training activities come to the fore. If the weather permits, jobs such as touch-up paint, lashing inspection and lifeboat exterior maintenance are scheduled.
Çalışmalar; risk seviyesine göre permit: Depending on the level of risk, work may require a permit: hot work permit, enclosed space entry permit, working aloft permit, working overside permit, electrical isolation permit. Through supervision on site, the Bosun ensures that the team does not step outside the scope of the permit.
Working aloft (yüksekte çalışma) için ha: For working aloft, the requirements are a harness with double lanyard, a secondary attachment point, a cordon on the deck below, no passage permitted and suitable weather conditions. Working overside starts with a liferaft ready, MOB equipment and communication.
Her sabah Reis, ekibe günün işini, riskl: Every morning, the Bosun holds a toolbox meeting explaining to the team the day's work, the risks, the equipment to be used and the PPE. For important jobs, a job-specific risk assessment (JSA) is completed and the participants sign it. After an accident, this record is evidence of "due diligence".
Klasik bir baş gemi (forecastle) bakım p: A classic forecastle maintenance program: days 1-2 chipping (removing existing rust + flaking paint), days 3-4 finish surface preparation with ST 3 power tools, day 5 primer, day 6 intermediate coat, days 7-8 topcoat. Application is staged according to the weather and the likelihood of sea spray.
Hatch coaming, tuz suya en açık bölgeler: The hatch coaming is one of the areas most exposed to salt water. The Bosun plans periodic washing to remove salt/water accumulated in the drainage recesses. When the onset of rust is seen, a local touch-up is not applied straight away; surface preparation is done first (ST 3), then epoxy primer + topcoat are applied.
Reis sadece denetçi değil, eğitici rolün: The Bosun is not only a supervisor but also a trainer. The Bosun demonstrates in practice basic skills to young ratings, such as preparing ropes, tying knots, rope splicing, chipping and painting, hot work safety and enclosed space discipline. This training is recorded in the "deck training book"; it is an important part of the STCW familiarization requirements.
Güverte bakımı; sadece \"boya atmak\" de: Deck maintenance is not just "slapping on paint". It is a disciplined, systematic and continuous effort to prevent corrosion, extend the service life of equipment, pass inspections with credit and keep the team safe. The Bosun is the on-site leader of this effort; the Bosun's success keeps the ship upright, sound and certified for 10-15 years.
Ambar, bir sonraki yüke uygun temizlik s: The hold must be handed over at a level of cleanliness suitable for the next cargo; otherwise residues of the previous cargo (taint), moisture or odor will damage the new cargo. Independent inspections are carried out for grain cargoes; a failed hold inspection leads to rejection for loading and major delays/costs. The Bosun knows and applies these standards.
Operasyon; süpürme, deniz suyu yıkama, t: The operation consists of sweeping, washing with seawater, rinsing with fresh water (especially for salt/odor), drying and, if necessary, paint touch-up. The Bosun directs the team, sets the sequence and confirms that each stage has been completed. Dryness is critical, especially for grain/steel cargoes.
Hatch coaming, track, bilge well, hold l: Hatch coamings, tracks, bilge wells, hold ladders and light fixtures are cleaned separately; these details often make the difference in an inspection. Cleaning the bilge wells and strainers is important for water drainage and cargo safety.
Tahıl/konsantre hassas ve yüksek temizli: Grain/concentrates are sensitive and require a high level of cleanliness; if ferrous ore is to be loaded after coal, a different standard applies, and "hospital clean" is required for sensitive food cargoes. The Bosun knows which cargo requires which level and directs the team accordingly. Residues of the previous cargo (taint) can contaminate an incompatible next cargo.
Ambar kapalı mekandır; giriş enclosed sp: The hold is an enclosed space; entry is made with an enclosed space entry permit and atmosphere testing. High-pressure washing, slippery surfaces and working at height (hold ladders, edges) are additional risks. The Bosun ensures PPE, supervision and safe working practice.
Hazırlık tamamlanınca Reis, ambarın iste: When preparation is complete, the Bosun checks that the hold is up to the required standard and reports to the Chief Officer. The condition is documented with photos/video; in a cargo dispute, this record is the evidence that the hold was handed over clean.
Cargo hold preparation liderliği, Reisin: Leading cargo hold preparation is an operation in which the Bosun uses technical knowledge, team management and safety awareness together. The correct cleanliness standard, attention to detail points and safe working ensure that the hold is handed over fit to carry the cargo safely and that costly cargo disputes are avoided.
Hatch cover sızdırmazlığı, ambardaki yük: Hatch cover tightness protects the cargo in the hold from seawater and protects the ship's integrity against water ingress. A leaking cover leads to cargo damage (especially grain, steel, sensitive cargo), mold/wetting and large claims. The Bosun knows that the maintenance preserving this tightness is, directly, cargo safety.
Reis; rubber gasket'lerin temiz, esnek v: The Bosun ensures that the rubber gaskets are clean, flexible and undamaged, that the compression bars bear evenly on the gaskets and that the drain channels (water drainage channels) are kept open. A blocked drain lets water leak inside; a crushed/permanently deformed gasket impairs tightness.
Kapağı kapalı tutan cleating/securing me: The cleating/securing mechanism that keeps the cover closed (cleats, wedges, hydraulics) is lubricated and kept in working order. Cleating that does not hold may allow the cover to open in heavy weather and the hold to flood.
Sızdırmazlık; hose test (yüksek basınçlı: Tightness is verified by a hose test (high-pressure water) or an ultrasonic test. The Bosun prepares the covers before the test (gaskets/drains clean, cover correctly seated). The ultrasonic test shows the leak point numerically and provides assurance before loading.
Tank vent head, sounding pipe head ve ma: Deck openings such as tank vent heads, sounding pipe heads and manhole covers are checked periodically; the float/flame screen of the vent head, the sounding pipe cap and the manhole gaskets/bolts ensure watertightness. A defect in these can lead to water entering a tank/void space.
Hatch cover panelleri, coaming ve güvert: Hatch cover panels, coamings and deck openings are monitored for corrosion; advanced corrosion creates both a structural risk and a tightness risk. The Bosun includes corrosion spots in the painting program and reports serious deformation to the Chief Officer.
Hatch cover ve weather deck sızdırmazlık: Hatch cover and weather deck tightness maintenance is one of the Bosun's most concrete tasks in protecting the cargo and the ship from the sea. Clean gaskets, open drains, working cleats and sound deck openings ensure that the holds stay dry even in heavy weather and that the cargo is carried safely.
Deniz ortamı çeliği hızla korozyona uğra: The marine environment corrodes steel quickly; paint is the primary barrier against this corrosion. A well-managed coating extends the life of hull and deck steel by decades, whereas neglected corrosion leads to structural weakness and expensive steel renewal. The Bosun is the on-site leader of this fight.
Boyanın tutması, tümüyle yüzey hazırlığı: Paint adhesion depends entirely on surface preparation.
