The surface is cleaned by chipping, grinding and descaling (removal of scale/rust); loose rust, old paint and salt residues are removed. The Bosun ensures that the preparation level (e.g. Sa 2.5 blast cleanliness) is in line with the plan. On a poorly prepared surface, even the best paint will not hold.
Boya sistemi katmanlıdır: primer (yapışm: The paint system is layered: primer (adhesion/corrosion protection), intermediate (thickness/barrier) and topcoat (outer protection/appearance). The Bosun applies the coat sequence in accordance with the paint scheme, the dry film thickness (DFT) and the overcoating intervals between coats. The wrong sequence or insufficient thickness shortens the protection life.
Boya, hava ve yüzey koşulları uygun oldu: Paint is applied when the air and surface conditions are suitable. The surface temperature should generally be at least 3°C above the dew point; otherwise moisture condenses on the surface and the paint does not hold. Humidity, temperature and wind are measured. The Bosun plans the application according to these conditions.
Reis; boya stoğunu, karışım oranlarını (: The Bosun monitors the paint stock, mixing ratios (two-component paints) and batch number records. The coat applied, area, DFT and conditions are recorded. These records are valuable both for warranty/compliance and for planning the next maintenance.
Chipping/grinding göz/solunum riski, boy: Chipping/grinding carries eye/respiratory risks, and paint carries solvent vapor and fire risks. Suitable PPE (goggles, respirator, gloves), ventilation and distance from ignition sources are essential. Painting in an enclosed space is subject to the enclosed space and atmosphere rules.
Boya programı ve korozyon yönetimi, Reis: The painting program and corrosion management are tasks through which the Bosun contributes directly to the ship's structural life. Good surface preparation, the correct coating system and respect for weather conditions build a lasting defense that protects steel from corrosion and secures the ship's long-term health.
Bağlama operasyonunda halatlar geminin t: In a mooring operation, the lines carry the forces generated by the ship's entire tonnage; when a line is loaded close to its MBL, hundreds of kJ of energy are stored in it. When this line parts, the energy is released like a whip, creating the lethal recoil known as "snap-back". A rotating winch drum, a confined working area, a wet deck and restricted visibility increase the risk.
Reis; istasyondaki tüm tayfaların güvenl: The Bosun ensures that all ratings at the station stand in safe positions, use the correct technique and carry out the bridge's orders in full. The more routine an operation is, the more dangerous it is, because attention drops. The Bosun's task is to keep attention alive.
Reis genelde baş (forward) istasyonunu,: The Bosun usually runs the forward station and the Second Officer the aft station; or, depending on the arrangement, the Bosun is aft. At the station, the Bosun clearly assigns who will tend which line, who will operate the winch and who will act as lookout. The Bosun communicates with the bridge by radio and confirms every order by read-back.
Reis, güvertede kayma/takılma riski yara: The Bosun has anything that creates a slip/trip hazard on deck (oil, heaps of line, tools) cleared away. The snap-back zones are reviewed and the radio/communications are tested. The whole team knows what to do; the report "stations ready forward/aft" is given to the bridge.
Standart bağlama paterni; head line, bre: A standard mooring pattern includes head lines, breast lines and spring lines (forward and aft). The springs restrain longitudinal movement, the breast lines restrain transverse movement and the head/stern lines provide general holding. In coordination with the bridge and the pilot, the Bosun knows which line is to be sent first; usually a spring or a breast line is sent first.
Halat winch drum'a sarılırken \"turn\"la: When the line is wound onto the winch drum, the turns must lie evenly without riding over one another; a riding turn causes the winch to jam and leads to loss of control. The Bosun checks that enough turns (usually 3-4) are on the drum and that the line is able to render.
Bazı gemilerde wire + sentetik tail komb: Some ships use a wire + synthetic tail combination; the tail offsets the stiffness of the wire and absorbs the dynamic load. The Bosun checks that the MBL of the tail is compatible with the wire (usually 125-150% of the wire's MBL) and that the connecting shackle/cow hitch is sound. A worn tail increases the risk of parting.
Mixed mooring (aynı yönde hem tel hem se: Mixed mooring (using both wire and synthetic lines in the same direction) is not recommended by MEG4, because lines of different elasticity do not share the load equally and the stiffer one parts first. The Bosun prevents this error; lines of similar elasticity are used in the same service.
Winch freni, halatın MBL'sinin altında (: The winch brake must be set to render (slip and shed load) below the MBL of the line (usually around 60% of SDBF), so that the brake slips before the line parts and the energy is released in a controlled way. Brake holding capacity is tested periodically. The Bosun knows that this setting must be correct and monitors how tightly the brake is applied.
Aşırı yük altında halat koparmak yerine: Under excessive load, allowing the winch brake to slip in a controlled way (render) rather than letting the line part protects both the equipment and the people. When the Bosun notices that a line is overloaded (water squeezing out, noise, drum vibration), the Bosun intervenes immediately and, if necessary, warns the bridge: "line overloaded".
Manevra sırasında pilot, köprüüstüne kom: During maneuvering, the pilot gives orders to the bridge; the bridge passes them to the station by radio ("heave away forward spring", "slack head line", "make fast", "let go aft"). The Bosun confirms these orders by read-back and carries them out at the station. If an order is not understood, "say again" is used; no action is taken on guesswork.
Reis, sahadan köprüüstüne geri bildirim: The Bosun reports back from the station to the bridge: "forward spring made fast", "one line ashore", "all fast forward", "all gone aft, clear of propeller". The "clear of propeller/thruster" report is especially critical; if a line has fallen into the water, there is a risk of it fouling the propeller, and the engine is not used until the bridge has been warned.
Römorkör kullanılıyorsa Reis, tug line'ı: If tugs are used, the Bosun ensures that the tug line is taken on board safely and made fast to the correct bitt/SPM point, and that the crew keep clear while it is under tension. A parting tug line, or one loaded at the wrong angle, causes serious injuries. Work with the tug is coordinated within the bridge–pilot–tug master triangle.
Sentetik halat esnerken enerji depolar;: A synthetic line stores energy as it stretches; when it parts, this energy is released as snap-back. The modern view is that "the whole deck is a potential snap-back zone", because the danger zone changes as the direction of the line changes. The Bosun teaches the crew to stand out of the line's path and, wherever possible, behind the winch/bitt.
Yeni MEG4 yaklaşımı, sabit \"snap-back z: The new MEG4 approach stresses that fixed "snap-back zone" markings can be misleading, because the line changes direction around the fairlead. Instead of relying blindly on static markings, the Bosun develops the crew's awareness of the hazard as a dynamic one.
Bir halat koparsa Reis derhal \"line par: If a line parts, the Bosun immediately warns "line parted", informs the bridge and checks that the crew are safe. If anyone is injured, first aid and the MOB/medevac procedure are started. Since the load on the remaining lines increases, the operation is reassessed; if necessary, additional lines are put out.
Dar sularda veya akıntılı yanaşmada pilo: In confined waters or when berthing in a current, the pilot may use an anchor to hold the ship's head ("dredging anchor"). The Bosun keeps the windlass ready on the fo'c'sle, handles the chain stopper and brake, and pays out the cable under control on the bridge's order (e.g. "walk back two shackles"). Details of the anchoring equipment are covered in a separate section (task 8).
Baş istasyonu demir/halat ile, kıç istas: The forward station works with the anchor/lines and the aft station with lines, at the same time. The Bosun reports clearly to the bridge what is happening at the Bosun's own station, so that the bridge can manage both ends in step. A breakdown in communication creates dangerous situations, such as one end of the ship coming free while the other end is still made fast.
\"Single up\" komutuyla fazla halatlar t: On the "single up" order, surplus lines are taken in and the ship is held by single lines; on "let go", the last lines are released. The Bosun confirms that the released line has been recovered cleanly from the quay and has not fallen into the water and fouled the propeller ("all gone and clear"). The engine is not used until this confirmation has been given to the bridge.
Halatlar toplandıktan sonra düzgün ranza: After the lines have been taken in, they are stowed neatly on the racks, the fairleads are cleared and the winch is disengaged. The Bosun brings the station to the "secured for sea" condition and reports to the bridge.
Kış ve kutup operasyonlarında halatlar/g: In winter and polar operations, lines and decks ice up, synthetic lines stiffen and decks become more slippery. The Bosun manages the risk by removing ice, providing extra grip (anti-slip) and operating more slowly. A frozen line makes both hand grip and winch control more difficult.
Dünya genelinde mooring snap-back kaynak: Worldwide, deaths caused by mooring snap-back are regularly reported by the MAIB and other authorities. The common factors are: crew standing in the path of a taut line, fatigue, poor lighting and rushed operations. Lesson: no port schedule is more important than the safe positioning of a single crew member.
Bağlama ve manevra, denizciliğin en eski: Mooring and maneuvering is one of the oldest, yet still one of the deadliest, operations at sea. The Bosun's disciplined leadership at the station — clear orders, correct technique, snap-back awareness and an unshakeable "safety first" attitude — keeps the crew alive and the ship safe. At this station, the smallest slackness is paid for at the highest price.
Gemide meydana gelen yaralanmaların önem: A large share of injuries on board is caused by "slip, trip and fall" accidents. Lines left lying about, hand tools left out, spilled oil and paint, loose deck plates and blocked passageways are all low-severity but high-frequency causes of accidents. The Bosun's housekeeping discipline stops these accidents at the source.
Düzen aynı zamanda acil durum hazırlığın: Order is also a precondition for emergency preparedness. Being unable to reach the foam monitor when a fire breaks out, a blocked route to the muster station at the moment of abandon ship, or stowed material blocking access to a liferaft all turn into disaster at moments when seconds save lives.
Endüstriyel 5S yöntemi (Seiri-ayıkla, Se: The industrial 5S method (Seiri – sort, Seiton – set in order, Seiso – clean, Seiketsu – standardize, Shitsuke – sustain) can be applied directly on deck. The Bosun fixes "what belongs where" for each storage area; the places of hand tools are marked with shadow boards, so a missing tool is noticed at once.
Standartlaştırma; bir kişinin değil, eki: Standardization must become a shared habit of the whole team, not of one person. The Bosun ensures that everyone knows "where things go", so that order is kept even when a deckhand is on leave or being relieved.
Açık güvertede yağ, gres, boya, su ve öz: On open deck, oil, grease, paint, water and especially ice are the main causes of slipping. The Bosun gives priority to keeping walkways clean; in cold climates, the Bosun plans anti-slip application, salt spreading and ice breaking. Non-slip paint and anti-slip strips on deck are checked periodically.
Açıkta bırakılmış lashing malzemesi, hor: Lashing material, hoses, cables and line ends left lying about are the most frequent causes of tripping. Hoses and cables laid out temporarily are hung up where possible, or gathered to the side so that they do not obstruct passage; if necessary, they are marked with warning tape/cones.
Açık manhole, ullage port, sounding pipe: Open manholes, ullage ports, sounding pipe caps, hold accesses and missing guard rails are fatal fall hazards. The Bosun ensures that every opening is kept under supervision while open and is closed securely as soon as the work is finished. A manhole left open and unattended can cost a crew member's life in the dark at night.
Guard rail, stanchion, bulwark ve safety: The integrity of guard rails, stanchions, bulwarks and safety chains is checked periodically; missing or loose railings are reported immediately and temporary safety measures (warning, barrier) are taken.
SOLAS Chapter II-2, kaçış yollarının her: SOLAS Chapter II-2 requires escape routes to be kept open and unobstructed at all times. The Bosun checks that no material is stowed in front of corridors, stairways, doors and emergency exits. In a fire, one extra meter along a smoke-filled corridor is the difference between life and death.
Watertight ve fire door'ların serbest ka: Wedges, lashings and stowed items that prevent watertight and fire doors from closing freely are removed. A fire door wedged open "to let the air through" is one of the most common inspection findings and directly endangers the safety of the ship.
Can salları, can filikası, MOB botu, yan: Access to liferafts, the lifeboat, the MOB boat, fire hose boxes, foam monitors, portable fire extinguishers and EEBDs must always be kept clear. The Bosun ensures that nothing is ever stowed around this equipment and that the signage remains visible.
Acil ekipman erişim yolları boyaması (ge: The painted access routes to emergency equipment (usually marked in yellow) and the equipment location signs are checked periodically; faded or covered markings are renewed. The muster station area is always kept clear and accessible.
Bakım sırasında boya kutuları, tiner, ha: During maintenance, materials such as paint tins, thinner, rope reels and lashing material are temporarily kept on deck. The Bosun ensures that they are stowed lashed (so that they cannot shift at sea), without obstructing passage, and, if they are dangerous substances, properly segregated.
Denizde hiçbir gevşek malzeme güvertede: At sea, no loose material is left on deck; even a single drum of paint can be thrown about by rolling and cause injury or be lost overboard. "Sea-fastening" is an integral part of finishing any job.
Boya, tiner, gres, oksijen-asetilen tüpl: Flammable/dangerous materials such as paint, thinner, grease, oxygen-acetylene cylinders and solvents are kept in suitable, ventilated stores away from sparks. On open deck, gas cylinders are secured upright and firmly (with chains/clamps); oxygen and fuel gas cylinders are kept apart.
Paçavra ve solvent emmiş bezler; self-ig: Rags and cloths soaked with solvent are collected in metal bins with lids because of the risk of self-ignition (spontaneous combustion) and are disposed of regularly. This is a simple but vital housekeeping rule.
Güverte üzeri su drenajı (scupper) tıkal: When the deck drains (scuppers) are blocked, water collects on deck; this is both a slip hazard and a cause of damage to cargo/stores. The Bosun checks that the scuppers are kept clean and clear. However, during tanker/cargo operations, scupper plugs are fitted because of the risk of pollution; the balance between these two requirements is managed case by case.
Boya, yağ veya kimyasal döküntüsünün den: Paint, oil or chemical spills getting into the sea is a serious MARPOL violation. During maintenance, the scuppers are plugged (plug + putty), and when the work is finished the deck is cleaned and drained in a controlled way. Save-all trays are kept ready during oil/paint transfers.
MARPOL Annex V kapsamında güverte atıkla: Under MARPOL Annex V, deck waste (plastics, metal, food, operational waste) is collected separately; the Bosun checks that the garbage stations on deck are kept in order and that waste is segregated correctly. Working records are kept on deck for the Garbage Record Book entries.
Liman, denetimlerin (PSC, vetting, klas,: Port is where inspections (PSC, vetting, class, terminal) are most frequent. Before arrival, the Bosun makes the deck ready for inspection: order on the mooring deck, cleanliness of open areas, visibility of markings and access to equipment. After dusty/noisy work in port (chipping, grinding), the area is tidied up immediately.
Seyirde öncelik, denizde gevşek malzeme: At sea, the priority is to leave no loose material on deck and to sea-fasten everything. When bad weather is expected, the Bosun carries out a "secure for sea" check over the whole open deck: lashings, store doors, hose reels, gas cylinders and deck equipment. An object thrown about by rolling causes injury, loss overboard and damage.
Hava uygun olduğunda seyir, rutin temizl: When the weather is suitable, the passage is an opportunity for routine cleaning and tidying; however, the safety constraints (harness, weather window, supervision) are tighter than in port.
Yetersiz aydınlatma, gece operasyonların: Inadequate lighting increases the risk of accidents during night operations and in passageways. The Bosun routinely checks that deck lights, passageway lighting and emergency lighting are working, and reports defective lights. Lighting of the mooring deck, access ways and store entrances has priority.
Tehlike işaretleri, ekipman lokasyon lev: Hazard signs, equipment location signs, mandatory PPE signs and walkway markings are kept legible and visible. Faded, rusted or covered signs are renewed as part of housekeeping. Visible marking is for the safety of both the crew and visitors (pilot, surveyor, stevedores).
Denetçiler güvertede; temizlik, korkuluk: On deck, inspectors look at cleanliness, the integrity of railings, clear escape routes, access to equipment, markings, drainage and the general state of maintenance. The Bosun follows a regular self-inspection routine "through the inspector's eyes"; deficiencies found are reported to the Chief Officer and rectified.
Housekeeping; tek başına bir tutuklama (: Although housekeeping alone is not a reason for detention, a poor general impression puts the inspector into "look deeper" mode and opens the way to other findings. Good housekeeping, on the other hand, sets a positive tone for the inspection.
Reis, haftalık güverte tur kayıtlarını (: The Bosun keeps records of the weekly deck rounds; housekeeping deficiencies found are documented together with the measures taken and photographs showing completion. Under ISM, these records are evidence of "continuous improvement" and show the discipline of the ship's management during inspections.
Reis, güverteyi sorumluluk bölgelerine a: The Bosun divides the deck into areas of responsibility and makes each deckhand responsible for keeping a particular area in order ("zone ownership"). This solves the problem of untidiness being "everybody's job, so nobody's job". A sense of ownership is the foundation of lasting order.
Housekeeping; toolbox meeting'lerin sabi: Housekeeping is a standing agenda item at toolbox meetings. The Bosun praises good examples and treats deficiencies as system issues, not personal ones. When a deckhand reports a hazard (e.g. a loose railing), the report must be welcomed; a reporting culture is the guarantee of order and safety.
Güverte housekeeping; gösteriş için deği: Deck housekeeping is done for life, not for show. A tidy deck means fewer accidents, faster emergency response, cleaner inspections and a more motivated team. The Bosun is both the architect and the guardian of this order; a good Bosun's ship is ready at any moment to receive even an inspector who arrives without notice.
Reis, yük operasyonu öncesi Birinci Zabi: Before a cargo operation, the Bosun receives instructions from the Chief Officer: the loading/discharging sequence, which hold/hatch is to be opened and when, the lashing plan, the required level of hold preparation and the safety restrictions. The Bosun passes these instructions to the team at a toolbox meeting and keeps radio contact with the duty officer throughout the operation.
Sahada bir sapma görülürse (ekipman arız: If a deviation is seen on deck (equipment failure, inadequate lashing, unexpected water ingress, stevedore error), the Bosun informs the Chief Officer immediately. The Bosun is the eyes and ears on deck; if the reporting chain breaks, the safety of the operation is weakened.
Operasyon başlamadan Reis; PPE kontrolü: Before the operation starts, the Bosun reviews PPE (hard hat, safety shoes, gloves, high-visibility vest), lighting, escape routes, the working order of equipment and the points where the crew and stevedores interact. In cargo operations, coordination between the crew and shore workers (stevedores) is a significant factor in accidents.
Folding (katlanır), side-rolling (yana k: Folding, side-rolling, piggy-back and pontoon type hatch covers each require a different operating discipline. Before opening/closing, the Bosun confirms that the cleats have been released, the drainage channels are clean, there are no obstructions on the rails and the hydraulic system is ready.
Hatch cover operasyonu sırasında ezilme: The risk of crushing and falling during hatch cover operations is high. No crew member may be between a moving cover and the fixed structure; a "no-go zone" must be clearly defined and supervised. Nobody stays under or in the path of a cover while it is moving.
Hatch cover'ın weathertight (su geçirmez: A weathertight hatch cover protects the cargo in the hold from seawater. The Bosun checks the condition of the rubber gaskets, compression bars, drainage channels and non-return valves. Water entering a loaded hold is critical, as it damages the cargo and causes stability/strength problems for the ship.
Kapama sonrası compression mark (rubber': After closing, the compression mark (the even impression of the rubber) is checked; uneven compression indicates a gasket or bar adjustment problem. Cleating is done correctly and tightly; a loose cleat at sea means cover damage and water ingress in bad weather.
Her gemi, klas onaylı Cargo Securing Man: Every ship carries a class-approved Cargo Securing Manual (CSM). This manual contains the MSL (Maximum Securing Load) values of the lashing equipment and the approved lashing patterns and methods. The Bosun ensures that the lashing applied on deck complies with this manual; "improvised" lashing causes accidents and cargo loss.
Twist lock, lashing rod, turnbuckle, web: Twist locks, lashing rods, turnbuckles, web/chain lashings, dunnage and shoring are selected according to the type of cargo and applied with the correct torque/tension. The Bosun checks lashing tightness and corrects slack lashings immediately.
Lashing işi, sırt-bel yaralanmaları, par: Lashing work carries a risk of back injuries, crushed fingers and falls from height. The Bosun supervises correct lifting technique, the use of harnesses on lashing bridges, teamwork when carrying heavy lashing rods and the use of the right hand tools. Fall protection is mandatory when working on a lashing cage/platform.
Sefer boyunca lashing rutin olarak kontr: Lashings are checked routinely throughout the voyage; a "lashing inspection" is carried out especially before and after bad weather. Slack lashings are retightened. The Bosun keeps records of these checks and reports to the Chief Officer.
Dökme yük gemilerinde hold hazırlığı; bi: On bulk carriers, hold preparation is graded according to the next cargo and the charter terms: load-ready (swept), shovel-clean, grain-clean, hospital-clean. The Bosun obtains the required level from the Chief Officer and directs the team accordingly.
Hold temizliği; süpürme, deniz suyu yıka: Hold cleaning includes sweeping, seawater washing, freshwater rinsing, drying, deodorizing, paint touch-up and cleaning of the bilge wells. Residues of the previous cargo (taint) can contaminate the next cargo; therefore, the cleaning standard is strict.
Cargo hold, bir enclosed space'tir. Reis: A cargo hold is an enclosed space. Before anyone enters a hold, the Bosun ensures that the requirements for an enclosed space entry permit, atmosphere testing (O2, LEL, H2S, CO), ventilation and a standby person are met. The hold ladder, lighting and escape route are checked.
Yıkama suyu ve kimyasal kullanımı, kayma: The use of washing water and chemicals creates slipping and breathing hazards; suitable PPE and ventilation are essential. After washing, the used water is discharged in compliance with MARPOL rules (especially if it contains cargo residues), in coordination with the Chief Officer.
Reis ve güverte ekibi, ballast/freshwate: The Bosun and the deck team assist with ballast/fresh water/void space soundings and hold bilge measurements. It is important that the sounding pipe heads are clean and open, that the correct sounding tape is used and that the readings are recorded correctly. A wrong sounding corrupts the stability and strength calculations.
Hold bilge sounding'i, hold içine su gir: Hold bilge soundings give early warning of water entering the hold. If regular bilge soundings during operations and on passage show an increase, the Chief Officer and the bridge are warned immediately; this is the early alarm for a hatch seal problem or a hull leak.
Bilge well'ler temiz tutulur; tıkalı str: Bilge wells are kept clean; a blocked strum box or bilge suction prevents water from being pumped out of the hold. The Bosun checks the condition of the bilge well rose boxes and non-return valves. On bulk carriers, a bilge well blocked with cargo residue makes sounding and drainage impossible; this is critical for hold safety.
Güverte üzeri yük (container, boru, proj: Cargo on deck (containers, pipes, project cargo, timber) is directly exposed to sea conditions. On deck, the Bosun checks that the lashing pattern is correct, the dunnage is sufficient and the cargo distribution is in line with the plan. For special cargoes such as timber deck cargo, the requirements of the TDC Code are applied.
On-deck reefer container'ların plug bağl: The plug connections, air circulation and access routes of on-deck reefer containers are checked. Deck cargo must not obstruct escape routes or access to equipment; this is both a safety issue and an inspection issue.
Reis, hava elverdiğinde ve güvenliyse gü: When the weather permits and it is safe to do so, the Bosun periodically checks the lashings of the deck cargo. Going out on deck in bad weather is dangerous; therefore, the checks are made within a weather window, under supervision and with harnesses. Slackened lashings or shifted cargo are reported immediately.
Yük operasyonunda sahil işçileri (steved: During cargo operations, shore workers (stevedores) work on deck. The Bosun watches stevedore movements, manages overlaps between crew and stevedore working areas and monitors compliance with safety rules. Differences in language and practice can create a risk of accidents; clear marking and supervision are important.
Stevedore kaynaklı hasar (hatch cover, k: Damage caused by stevedores (hatch covers, railings, paint, equipment) is common. The Bosun identifies the damage at once, photographs it and reports it to the Chief Officer; if necessary, a stevedore damage report and a Letter of Protest are issued. Damage not documented in time later becomes the responsibility of the ship/company.
Yük operasyonunda bazı işler permit gere: In cargo operations, some jobs require a permit: enclosed space entry (hold), working aloft (upper tier of the lashing bridge), working overside and hot work. Through supervision on deck, the Bosun ensures that the team does not go beyond the scope of the permit, and monitors that the job-specific risk assessment is applied.
Yorgunluk yönetimi de operasyon güvenliğ: Fatigue management is also part of operational safety. During long port operations, MLC rest hours are observed; a tired crew increases the risk of accidents in lashing and hatch operations.
Her vardiya/operasyon öncesi Reis, ekibe: Before each watch/operation, the Bosun holds a toolbox meeting explaining the steps of the job, the risks, the equipment and the emergency procedure. Junior ratings are taught lashing technique, hatch operations and hold safety in practice; this training is recorded in the deck training book.
Yükleme sonrası Reis, ekiple birlikte tü: After loading, the Bosun and the team check the lashing pattern in all bays: are the twist locks locked, are the lashing rods tight, are the turnbuckles tightened? Before a voyage on which bad weather is expected, all lashings are checked twice and records are kept. In mid-voyage, the inspection is repeated during a weather window.
Coal boşaltması sonrası grain yükleme iç: After discharging coal, the hold is prepared for grain loading by sweeping, seawater washing, freshwater rinsing, drying and checking for odor/stains. The Bosun ensures that each hold is entered in line with enclosed space discipline and is ready for the NCB or surveyor inspection.
Yük operasyonunda Reis'in başarısı; plan: In cargo operations, the Bosun's success comes from carrying out the plan on deck completely, safely and on time. The weathertightness of the hatches, the soundness of the lashings and the correct preparation of the holds determine the safety of the cargo, the crew and the ship. A good Bosun never misses even a single slack lashing, because what is left loose at sea is what is lost in bad weather.
Bosun's store, geminin baş tarafında (ge: The Bosun's store is a closed compartment in the forward part of the ship (usually under the forecastle) where rope, wire, paint, chemicals, hand tools, securing gear and small spare parts are stored. For the Bosun, this store is the logistical heart that sets the pace of daily work: if the right material is not at hand at the right time, planned maintenance stops and work orders fall behind.
Store'un bir diğer kritik boyutu emniyet: Another critical aspect of the store is safety. Paints and solvents are flammable, some chemicals give off harmful vapors, and heavy gear (metal shackles, steel wire reels) can shift with the ship's motion and cause injury. The store is therefore not just a "storeroom" but also a controlled hazardous area.
Endüstriyel 5S yaklaşımı (Seiri-ayıkla,: The industrial 5S approach (Seiri – sort, Seiton – set in order, Seiso – clean, Seiketsu – standardize, Shitsuke – sustain) applies directly to the ship's store. The Bosun sorts out unused/expired material, places the rest on labeled shelves, keeps the floor and ventilation clean, sets a labeling standard and keeps it going through watch changes.
Deniz hareketine karşı her ağır kalem la: Every heavy item is secured against the ship's motion with lashings or shelf barriers. Wire reels that could roll are chocked, and paint tins are boxed to stop them toppling over. No heavy object is left loose in the store; it is a risk of both injury and damage.
Modern gemilerde mooring rope olarak HMP: On modern ships, HMPE (Dyneema), polyester, polyamide (nylon) and mixed lines are used as mooring line. Each line has a Line Design Break Force (LDBF) and a certificate; under OCIMF MEG4, lines are entered in the inventory with their type, diameter, length, date of manufacture and MBL. The Bosun tracks the lines in use and the spare lines in the store separately.
Yeni halat tesliminde sertifika (test ce: When a new rope is delivered, its test certificate is checked and filed. Rope reels are kept in the store in a dry area, out of sunlight, away from heat sources and out of contact with chemicals; UV and contact with solvents quickly reduce the strength of synthetic rope.
Reis, store'daki yedek halatları \"first: The Bosun rotates the spare lines in the store on a "first in, first out" (FIFO) basis; synthetic rope that sits on a shelf for years ages even without use. The date of manufacture of the spares is kept visible on the label. When a mooring line reaches its retirement criteria (outer fiber damage exceeds the company threshold, or core damage is seen), a new one is taken from the store, and the old line is tagged and either downgraded for use as a utility rope or put on the disposal list.
Halat kesip iş halatı (heaving line, gan: Cutting rope to make utility lines (heaving lines, gantlines, lashings) is also part of store management. The Bosun does not waste leftover pieces; by heat-sealing or whipping the ends, the Bosun turns them into useful short lengths of rope.
Cargo wire, mooring wire ve crane wire i: For cargo wires, mooring wires and crane wires, the store holds spare wire reels, OEM wire lubricant, wire clips, thimbles and sockets. The Bosun protects the wire reels from moisture; rusted wire loses its strength and flexibility. Spare wire certificates are kept in the same file as the rope certificates.
Tel greasing için kullanılan yağ ve tine: Consumables such as the lubricant and thinner used for wire greasing are classed as hazardous substances; they are kept in the paint/solvent section, in a ventilated and labeled area.
Shackle (kilit), turnbuckle (liftin), pa: Cargo securing gear such as shackles, turnbuckles, pad eyes, chains, lashing bars, twist locks, bottle screws and hooks is stamped with its SWL (Safe Working Load). The Bosun keeps these items in separate boxes according to SWL and size; a mixed box of shackles leads to a part with the wrong SWL being selected during maneuvering, and to accidents.
Her bağlama teçhizatı periyodik görsel k: All securing gear undergoes periodic visual inspection: deformation, cracks, excessive corrosion, damaged threads. A damaged item is removed from the inventory immediately and placed in the "out of service" box, so that it cannot come back into circulation.
Chipping hammer, needle scaler, angle gr: Chipping hammers, needle scalers, angle grinders, disc sanders, hand scrapers, wire brushes, paint brushes, rollers and airless spray guns are part of the store inventory. The Bosun tracks the number and condition of these tools and their spare consumables (grinding discs, scaler needles, brushes). Electric tools undergo periodic electrical safety checks (megger/insulation test); the hoses and connections of pneumatic tools are checked.
Boya, tiner, solvent ve epoxy sertleştir: Paints, thinners, solvents and epoxy hardeners are flammable and are usually kept in a separate paint locker with ventilation and a fire-extinguishing system. The Bosun enforces the ban on smoking/naked flames in this space and checks that the ventilation works and that spillage precautions are in place. Opened paint tins are closed tightly; a mix whose pot life has expired is disposed of, treated not as waste but as a safety risk.
Boya stoğu batch number, üretim/son kull: Paint stock is recorded by batch number, production/expiry date and system (primer/intermediate/topcoat). When a painting program is being planned, the Bosun calculates from the store stock how many liters are needed to reach the target DFT; if there is a shortfall, the Bosun raises a requisition in time.
Her kimyasalın Güvenlik Bilgi Formu (MSD: The Safety Data Sheet (MSDS/SDS) for every chemical must be accessible on board. The Bosun ensures that the labels of the chemicals in the store are legible and undamaged; unlabeled containers are not accepted. Incompatible substances, such as acids and alkalis, or oxidizers and flammables, are kept apart.
Paket halinde tehlikeli madde (IMDG kaps: The difference between dangerous goods in packaged form (within the scope of IMDG) and deck consumable chemicals is important; however, the storage logic is the same: segregation, labeling, ventilation and spill control. Waste chemicals and empty paint tins are collected separately in accordance with MARPOL Annex V.
Reis her ana kalem için bir asgari stok: For each main item, the Bosun sets a minimum stock (min) and maximum stock (max) threshold. When stock approaches the min threshold, a requisition is triggered; the max prevents unnecessary overstocking and clogging of the store. A stock-take is usually done at the end of each month and at the start/end of the voyage; the results are reported to the Chief Officer.
Pek çok gemide envanter, gemi yönetim ya: On many ships, the inventory is kept in the ship management software (PMS/inventory module). The Bosun keeps the physical count reconciled with the digital record; a difference between the record and the shelf points to "unrecorded consumption", theft or a recording error, and is investigated.
Malzeme israfı, hem maliyet hem de denet: Waste of materials is a problem in terms of both cost and inspections. The most common sources of waste are: paint mixed incorrectly and thrown away, epoxy left to dry in the open, cutting unnecessarily long lengths of rope, lost hand tools and undisciplined drawing of consumables. The Bosun records the issue of materials, so that "who took how much" is known.
İsrafın önlenmesi cimrilik değil, doğru: Preventing waste is not stinginess but the discipline of correct use. A painting job left half-done because of insufficient paint stock throws away all the surface preparation already done; this is the most expensive waste of all. The balance lies in planned consumption and timely resupply.
Reis, bakım programını ve stok durumunu: By considering the maintenance program and the stock situation together, the Bosun prepares a requisition for the next supply port. A good requisition includes the item name, technical description (brand/specification/IMPA code), quantity, unit and urgency. Instead of a vague "some paint", it says "brand X epoxy primer, gray, 20 L, 4 units".
IMPA (International Marine Purchasing As: The IMPA (International Marine Purchasing Association) catalog is the common language of ship supply. Using IMPA codes prevents the supplier from sending the wrong part. The Bosun knows these codes for frequently used items or has access to the catalog.
Reisin hazırladığı liste Birinci Zabit t: The list prepared by the Bosun is reviewed by the Chief Officer, combined with the budget and priorities, and sent to the company purchasing department. The Bosun separates recurring needs (paint, consumables) from one-off needs (special equipment that has broken or been used up), so that the approval chain does not get blocked.
İkmal limanına yaklaşırken Reis, tedarik: When approaching a supply port, the Bosun knows that the delivery window is limited; a requisition submitted late is carried over to the next port. Needs are therefore identified in advance and in a planned way, not reactively.
Malzeme gemiye geldiğinde Reis, teslimat: When material arrives on board, the Bosun compares the delivery note with the order list: items, quantities and specifications are checked, and the goods are checked for damage. Missing, wrong or damaged items are written on the delivery note as a "remark" and reported to the Chief Officer; a shortage accepted silently later becomes the ship's problem.
Teslim alınan kalemler vakit kaybetmeden: Items received are put in their places in the store without delay, following FIFO (new items at the back, old ones at the front). Certified items (rope, wire, LSA equipment) are recorded together with their certificates.
Tel makarası, boya fıçısı, demir teçhiza: Heavy items such as wire reels, paint drums and metal fittings are usually lowered into the store with a crane or the provision crane. During this operation, the Bosun checks the SWL of the lifting gear, the slinging points and that nobody stands under the load. For manual handling, correct lifting technique (legs, not back) and suitable PPE are essential.
Bir PSC, SIRE/CDI vetting veya klas dene: When a PSC, SIRE/CDI vetting or class inspector enters the store, the inspector looks at a few things: order, labeling, segregation of dangerous substances, presence of LSA/spare equipment and traceability of certificates. A store that is untidy, unlabeled or has incompatible substances mixed together immediately produces a "housekeeping" finding and gives a negative impression of the ship's general maintenance culture.
Reis, denetimden önce değil, sürekli den: The Bosun keeps the store ready for inspection at all times, not just before an inspection. The "always ready" philosophy removes the last-minute rush and its risks.
Sertifikalı teçhizat (halat, tel, kaldır: For certified equipment (rope, wire, lifting gear, LSA), there must be an immediate answer to the question "what is where, and with which certificate". The Bosun matches the physical tag to the digital record. In an investigation after an accident, traceability is also evidence that the ship exercised "due diligence".
Aşağıdaki liste, düzenli ve denetime haz: The list below summarizes the minimum daily/weekly/per-voyage checks for a tidy, inspection-ready bosun's store. Once the Bosun makes these items routine, the store becomes an asset that speeds up the team's work.
Bosun's store yönetimi, dışarıdan basit: Although managing the bosun's store may look from the outside like a simple "storekeeping job", it is in fact a discipline that directly determines the ship's maintenance capability. Having the right material ready at the right time, safely and traceably, keeps planned maintenance running without interruption, keeps the crew safe and lets the ship pass inspections without problems.
Reis, store'u bir maliyet kalemi değil,: The Bosun sees the store not as a cost item but as a managed asset. A well-kept store reduces waste, makes resupply predictable and becomes one of the most visible signs of the ship's professional maintenance culture.
Pilot ladder, accommodation ladder ve ga: Pilot ladders, accommodation ladders and gangways carry people every day; a defect can lead directly to a fall and death. The Bosun knows that this equipment must actually be safe, not just "look good", and manages its maintenance seriously.
Pilot ladder; basamak çatlağı/eksikliği,: The pilot ladder is checked before every use for cracked/missing steps, worn/rotten ropes, the condition of the spreaders and its overall integrity. It must be certified, undamaged and rigged at the correct height. The Bosun verifies that the combination arrangement (accommodation + pilot ladder) is safe.
Accommodation ladder ve gangway; vinç/ha: Accommodation ladders and gangways are checked for the winch/falls system, the condition of the steps/platforms, the railings (stanchions/ropes) and the safety net. The Bosun ensures that lubrication, wear checks and load tests are carried out. The safety net, which protects against falls, must always be taut and correctly rigged.
Erişim ekipmanı altında safety net ve ya: A safety net is rigged under the access equipment, and a lifebuoy + light + heaving line is kept nearby. These preparations are essential for a quick response if someone falls into the water. The Bosun ensures that these safety arrangements are always in place.
Bosun's chair ile yüksekte (aloft) veya: Working aloft or overside in a bosun's chair is high-risk work; the integrity of the rope/chair, a separate safety line (independent lifeline), a full body harness and a permit to work are mandatory. The Bosun checks these preparations and does not let inexperienced personnel work aloft unsupervised.
Working aloft/overside, permit-to-work v: Working aloft/overside requires a permit to work and a risk assessment; the weather, ship motion and risk of falling are assessed. The Bosun holds a toolbox talk, checks the PPE/harnesses and maintains supervision throughout the work.
Borda iskelesi, merdiven ve erişim ekipm: Maintenance of accommodation ladders, ladders and access equipment is one of the Bosun's most sensitive duties, as it relates directly to the safety of life. Certified equipment, correct rigging, a secondary safety line and constant supervision ensure that every embarkation/disembarkation and every overside job is completed safely.
Yeni katılan tayfa; gemiyi, ekipmanı ve: Newly joined deckhands do not yet fully know the ship, the equipment and the risks. This is why new personnel stand out in accident statistics. The Bosun knows that giving them the right start protects both their lives and the safety of the whole team.
Yeni personel; muster station, can kurta: On their first day on board, new personnel are briefed on the muster station, the locations of life-saving and fire-fighting equipment, escape routes, alarm signals and basic safety rules (familiarization). The Bosun gives the practical familiarization on the deck side and completes the checklist.
Reis; halat işleri, raspa-boya, ekipman: The Bosun teaches rope work, chipping and painting, the use of equipment and deck routines by demonstration. The "watch first, then do it under supervision, then on your own" approach is the most reliable way of building safe competence. New personnel are encouraged to ask questions.
Overside work, working aloft, enclosed s: In high-risk work such as overside work, working aloft, enclosed spaces and mooring, inexperienced personnel are never allowed to work alone. The Bosun pairs them with an experienced team member and supervises them directly. Supervision continues until competence has been proven.
Reis, yeni personeli ekibe katar; görev: The Bosun brings new personnel into the team, introducing them to the distribution of duties, communication within the team and the culture of the ship. A well-integrated deckhand feels safe, shares problems and works more safely. Personnel who are excluded or left on their own become both unhappy and a risk.
Acemilik eğitimi ve yeni personel desteğ: Training newcomers and supporting new personnel is the most valuable investment of the Bosun's leadership; a deckhand taught correctly today is a safe and competent team member tomorrow. Patient training, close supervision and sincere integration protect both the individual's life and the team's safety.
Demir operasyonunda Reis, baş kasara güv: In anchor operations, the Bosun leads the team on the forecastle deck and is the link between the bridge and the station. The Bosun carries out the orders, keeps the team in safe positions, watches the condition of the cable/anchor and reports it to the bridge. In these intense moments, clear communication and composure are vital.
Reis, seyir öncesi demir zincirini kontr: Before sailing, the Bosun checks the anchor cable: link wear, cracks, deformation and the legibility of the markings. If abnormal load, vibration or noise is noticed, the bridge is warned. A weakness in the cable can lead to loss of the anchor or an accident during the operation.
Demir atarken/alırken zincirin yönü (lea: When anchoring/weighing anchor, the lead and tension of the cable are reported to the bridge ("cable leading ahead, moderate strain"). This information is critical for the Master's assessment of the maneuver and of whether the anchor is holding.
Ekip baret, eldiven, çelik burunlu ayakk: The team wears hard hats, gloves, steel-toed shoes and eye protection; goggles are important because of the dust/particles around the cable. Radio communication with the bridge is clear and confirmed. In a noisy environment, hand signals are also agreed in advance.
Demir operasyonlarında ekip liderliği, R: Leading the team in anchor operations is the peak of the Bosun's command on deck; in an intense, noisy and risky environment, the Bosun keeps the team safe while putting the bridge's intentions into effect. Clear communication, safe positioning and the ability to "read" the cable make the anchor operation controlled and safe.
Giriş, Birinci Zabitten alınan Enclosed: Entry is made with an Enclosed Space Entry Permit obtained from the Chief Officer. The Bosun passes the permit conditions on to the team, ensures ventilation, organizes atmosphere testing and makes sure that entry does not begin until every step has been completed. Entry without a permit is strictly prohibited.
Girişten önce ve giriş boyunca atmosfer: The atmosphere is tested before and throughout entry: oxygen (target 20.9%), flammable gas (LEL), H2S and CO. The gas detector must be calibrated, and measurements must be taken at different levels (top/middle/bottom); some gases collect at the bottom, others at the top. The Bosun makes sure that the testing is done correctly.
Giren personel, sürekli okuyan kişisel g: Personnel entering carry a continuously reading personal gas detector; if the atmosphere deteriorates, it gives an alarm and the space is left immediately. Measurement is not a one-off; conditions can change, so monitoring is continuous.
Menhol/kapı başında bir standby kişi sür: A standby person is always present at the manhole/door, keeps in constant communication with the personnel inside and monitors the situation. If there is a problem, the standby person does not rush in, but raises the alarm and calls in the rescue team/SCBA standing by. The rescue line (lifeline) and harness allow the personnel inside to be pulled out.
Atmosferi şüpheli veya solunamaz mekânla: In spaces where the atmosphere is suspect or unbreathable, SCBA (with its own air supply) or SAA (supplied through an air line) is used. The Bosun checks that this equipment is ready, charged and used correctly.
Kapalı mekan girişi hazırlığı, Reisin \": Preparing for enclosed space entry is the Bosun's most serious duty, one where "a single skipped step means death". Full compliance with the permit, continuous atmosphere monitoring, a standby person who does not rush in and a rescue team ready to act bring this invisible hazard under control and ensure that the team comes out alive.
Vardiyayı devralan Üçüncü/Dördüncü Mühen: The Third/Fourth Engineer taking over the watch does not accept the watch on arrival in the engine control room (ECR) without first making a round. The outgoing engineer verbally hands over the main engine load and speed (rpm), the generators put on or taken off load, the service tank levels, the running pump configuration, the status of standby equipment and the alarms/events of the last 4 hours.
Devralan mühendis; manuel/UMS modu, deva: The relieving engineer is briefed on the manual/UMS mode, ongoing maintenance work, isolated equipment (under LOTO), pending work orders and requests from the bridge (e.g. an upcoming maneuver, a request for main engine stand-by). The watch is not taken over until this information has been verified.
Devir tamamlandığında engine room logboo: When the handover is complete, the time of handover and the names of the outgoing and relieving engineers are entered in the engine room logbook. From that moment, responsibility for the safety of the engine room passes to the relieving engineer. If there is any doubt or uncertainty, the relieving engineer delays taking over and informs the Second Engineer.
Manlı (manned) makine dairesinde tur tip: In a manned engine room, rounds are typically made every hour, or at the latest every two hours; in UMS mode, daytime checks + alarm-based response apply. A round follows a systematic route: main engine platform, generator flat, boiler and FO unit, purifier room, pump flat, separator/OWS area, shaft tunnel and steering gear.
Mühendis sadece göstergelere bakmaz; beş: The engineer does not just look at the gauges but uses all five senses. Abnormal noise (knocking, cavitation, bearing hum), vibration, oil/water/fuel leaks, smells (burnt insulation, hot bearing), heat (hot spots) and traces of leakage are detected. Suspect points are measured with a thermometer/IR gun.
Üçüncü/Dördüncü Mühendis bu eğilimleri l: The Third/Fourth Engineer follows these trends through successive entries in the logbook and on the trend screens of the alarm/monitoring system. Early action as a trend approaches its limits prevents a sudden trip and a major breakdown.
Scavenge air pressure, turbocharger rpm: Scavenge air pressure, turbocharger rpm and scavenge temperature show the health of the turbocharger and the air system. A sudden rise in scavenge box temperature is a forerunner of a scavenge fire (ignition of oil deposits) and requires immediate action.
Jacket cooling water, piston cooling oil: Jacket cooling water, piston cooling oil and the cylinder lube oil dosage (feed rate) are monitored. On modern engines, the cylinder oil feed rate is adjusted to the sulfur content of the fuel; overdosing high-BN oil on low-sulfur fuel leaves deposits, while underdosing on high-sulfur fuel leads to corrosion.
Main bearing, crankpin ve thrust bearing: Main bearing, crankpin and thrust bearing temperatures and the sump LO level are monitored. The crankcase oil mist detector (OMD) must be in working order; a high oil mist alarm is a warning of an impending crankcase explosion — the engine is slowed down/stopped immediately, and the crankcase is not opened until it has cooled down sufficiently.
Devredeki jeneratörlerin yükü, exhaust s: The load, exhaust temperatures, LO pressure, jacket water temperature and fuel consumption of the generators on line are monitored. With generators running in parallel, load sharing must be balanced; one set taking noticeably more load than the other points to a governor/AVR setting problem.
On the main switchboard, the bus bar voltage (e.g. 440V), frequency (60 Hz or 50 Hz), megger/insulation condition and the current of major consumers are monitored. It is verified that auto-start of the standby generator is enabled; its automatic start on a sudden load increase or when a set trips prevents a blackout.
Vardiya mühendisi olası blackout senaryo: The watch engineer is prepared for a possible blackout: whether the emergency generator starts automatically, whether there is enough starting air for a dead-ship start, and the restart procedure after a main engine emergency stop are all known. During maneuvering or in restricted waters, a second generator is put on line to provide redundancy.
Auxiliary/exhaust gas boiler için buhar: For the auxiliary/exhaust gas boiler, steam pressure, water level (gauge glass + remote), feed water temperature and burner status are monitored. Water level is the most critical parameter; at low-low level, the boiler shuts off firing automatically (flame failure/low water cut-off). Care is taken to guard against priming/foaming and cascade tank contamination.
Exhaust gas economiser'da soot fire risk: The risk of a soot fire in the exhaust gas economizer is monitored; soot deposits can ignite during standby/low-load periods. Soot blowing is carried out regularly and the outlet gas temperature is monitored.
Starting air kompresörleri ve servis hav: The delivery pressure, temperature and oil level of the starting air compressors and the service air compressor are monitored; main air receiver pressure (typically 25-30 bar) is critical for the main engine's ability to start. If the automatic drain does not work, the receivers are drained manually (accumulated water reduces the number of starts available).
Ballast, bilge, transfer, FO/LO servis p: The discharge pressure, sealing (gland/seal), vibration and bearing temperature of the ballast, bilge, transfer and FO/LO service pumps are checked. It is verified that auto-start of the standby pumps is enabled.
Sea water inlet basıncı ve coolerların g: Sea water inlet pressure and the inlet/outlet temperature difference across the coolers are monitored; a blocked sea chest or an MGPS fault reduces the efficiency of the central cooler. In a central fresh water cooling system, the expansion tank level and system pressure are checked; a fall indicates a leak, and a rise indicates gas/steam ingress.
FO settling/service tank seviyeleri, vis: FO settling/service tank levels, the viscosity control unit (heater outlet viscosity), FO booster pressure and filter ΔP are monitored. On entering an ECA, the timing of the changeover to low-sulfur fuel and the rate of temperature change are controlled; a sudden temperature change causes the fuel pumps to stick.
MARPOL Annex VI kapsamında kullanılan ya: Under MARPOL Annex VI, the sulfur content of the fuel used (BDN), flowmeter readings and the required records are kept. The Third/Fourth Engineer records the changeover in the logbook with the time and position.
Birden çok alarm aynı anda çalarsa kök n: If several alarms sound at the same time, the root cause is sought; for example, after a blackout, dozens of alarms may stem from a single loss of power. The engineer turns to systematic diagnosis, not to panic.
Anormal her durum derhal İkinci Mühendis: Every abnormal situation is reported immediately to the Second Engineer or the Chief Engineer. The Third/Fourth Engineer knows the limits of their authority: jobs they can deal with on their own are kept separate from jobs that need a senior engineer's approval/support. When in doubt, a senior engineer is called — this is not a weakness but correct practice.
Saatlik/vardiya bazlı parametreler engin: Hourly/per-watch parameters are entered in the engine room logbook and the electronic recording system: main engine load/rpm, exhaust temperatures, cooling values, generator loads, tank levels, bunkers/daily consumption and any events. Records must be legible, true and made on time; false/backdated entries are a serious disciplinary offense.
Oil Record Book (Part I) kapsamına giren: Operations covered by the Oil Record Book (Part I) (bilge transfer, OWS discharge, sludge transfer, fuel transfer) are also entered in the ORB. These records serve as evidence for PSC and in court.
Günlük yakıt/yağ tüketimi, sefer raporla: Daily fuel/lube oil consumption is the basic data for voyage reports (noon reports). A deviation from the expected consumption may indicate a decline in engine performance or a measurement/leakage problem. These data are critical for EEXI/CII performance monitoring.
Manevra öncesi \"stand-by main engine\": Before maneuvering, on a "stand-by main engine" request, the engine is put into maneuvering mode: the second generator is on line, the starting air receivers are full, FO heating is correct, the control test (ahead/astern) has been carried out and the telegraph test has been completed. Throughout the maneuver, the Third/Fourth Engineer closely monitors the telegraph orders and the engine's response.
Manevra sırasında ani komut değişiklikle: During maneuvering, the engine room is ready for sudden changes of order, many starts/stops and crash astern maneuvers; starting air consumption and scavenge temperature are watched closely.
Limanda ana makine durur ancak jeneratör: In port, the main engine is stopped, but generator, boiler, cooling, bunkering and cargo (pumps on tankers) operations continue. During bunkering, the engineer monitors tank levels, leaks and the overflow alarm; SOPEP equipment is kept ready against marine pollution.
Makine vardiyası, görünmeyen bir başarı: An engine room watch is an art of invisible success: on a well-kept watch nothing happens, because the engineer has caught problems before any alarm sounds, read the trends and acted in time. The Third/Fourth Engineer's disciplined rounds, honest records and correct reporting reflex are the engine room's first line of defense.
Her yardımcı makine için PMS yazılımında: For each item of auxiliary machinery, a job is defined in the PMS software (AMOS, TM Master, ShipManager); the job is opened when triggered by running hours or by the calendar. The Third/Fourth Engineer allocates open work orders according to the watch schedule, confirms the required spare parts and consumables with a ROB (remaining on board) check and, when the job is finished, closes it in the system with the counter reading + a description of the work done.
PMS kayıtları yalnızca şirket için değil: PMS records are evidence not only for the company but also for class and PSC (Port State Control) inspections. For equipment under CMS (Continuous Machinery Survey), open-up work carried out by the engineers can be reported to class as a "crew survey"; for this reason, photographs, measurements and clearance values before/after the work are recorded.
Hiçbir bakım, ekipman enerjisi izole edi: No maintenance starts until the equipment's energy has been isolated. For a pump/compressor driven by an electric motor, the breaker is set "OFF + LOTO (Lock Out Tag Out)"; in a pressurized system, the suction/discharge valves are closed and the pressure is released by draining. For work involving hot oil or steam lines (boiler, FO purifier heater), the work waits until the system has cooled down.
İş öncesi Risk Assessment (RA) formu dol: Before the work, a Risk Assessment (RA) form is completed; for work that requires a permit to work (PTW) (hot work, enclosed space, electrical work), the relevant permit is submitted to the duty engineer/Chief Engineer for approval. The job is not considered complete until the permit has been closed.
Gemideki SW/FW santrifüj pompalarında en: In the ship's SW/FW centrifugal pumps, the component that fails most often is the mechanical seal. Seal leakage results from dry running, cavitation or excessive axial force. During maintenance, the seal faces are inspected for scratches/wear, the O-rings are replaced, the shaft sleeve is measured and the bearing clearance is checked with a feeler/dial gauge.
Pompa motoru ile pompa arasındaki coupli: The coupling alignment between the pump motor and the pump is checked with a dial gauge or laser; misalignment seriously shortens bearing and seal life. The measurement is interpreted allowing for the difference between the cold and hot (operating) conditions.
Bilge sistemi, gemi su altı bütünlüğünün: The bilge system is the last line of defense for the ship's underwater integrity; the bilge pump is therefore regarded as "critical equipment". For self-priming, the tightness of the air-water separator and the non-return valve (NRV) is critical; if the NRV does not seat, the pump cannot prime. During maintenance, the suction valve is overhauled, the NRV is ground in and the strainer is cleaned.
Bilge well high-level alarm switch'leri: Bilge well high-level alarm switches (float/capacitive) are tested. Under MARPOL Annex I, bilge water may be discharged to sea only through the OWS (Oily Water Separator), below the 15 ppm limit and with OCM (Oil Content Meter) approval; the bilge pump must not be bypassed to pump directly overboard.
Ana makine yol verme havası (starting ai: Main engine starting air is typically around 25–30 bar and is produced by two/three-stage reciprocating compressors. Compressor efficiency depends on the tightness of the suction/discharge valves (reed/plate valves). A leaking valve raises the interstage pressure and the discharge temperature; this creates a risk of carbon build-up and explosion (crankcase/air pipe explosion).
Bakımda valf plakaları, yaylar ve segman: During maintenance, the valve plates, springs and piston rings are inspected for wear, the intercooler/aftercooler is cleaned and the relief valve setting is verified. The air receiver (bullet) is opened periodically, drained and checked for internal corrosion; the air bottle survey is a class requirement.
Service air (kontrol/iş havası) genelde: Service air (control/working air) is usually reduced to 7–8 bar and, for control air, passed through an air dryer; humid air damages control valves and pneumatic equipment. Automatic drain valves (auto-drain) are tested regularly; a blocked drain lets water collect inside the receiver and causes corrosion.
Her starting air receiver üzerinde fusib: Each starting air receiver is fitted with a fusible plug and a relief valve; these are the last safeguards against overpressure and overheating and are covered by survey.
Bowl montajında işaret hizalaması (match: When the bowl is assembled, the matchmarks are aligned and the tightening torque follows the manufacturer's values exactly. Incorrect assembly creates a risk of imbalance (vibration), water leakage or bursting. In these high-speed machines, imbalance is extremely dangerous.
Ağır yakıt (HFO) purifier öncesi buhar/e: Before the purifier, heavy fuel oil (HFO) is heated by a steam/electric heater to ~98 °C; the correct separation temperature depends on viscosity and density. The heater high temperature alarm and trip circuit are tested regularly; overheating leads to fuel degradation and a safety risk.
Sludge tank seviyesi ve sludge pompası,: The sludge tank level and the sludge pump are monitored for the transfer of sludge to the incinerator or to shore reception. All sludge transfers are recorded in the Oil Record Book (ORB) Part I; this record is central to MARPOL inspections.
Yardımcı kazan, limanda ve düşük yük sey: The auxiliary boiler supplies steam (fuel heating, heating, services) in port and at sea at low engine load. Most maintenance is on the burner unit: the nozzle/tip that determines the quality of atomization is cleaned, the electrodes are adjusted, the glass of the photocell (flame eye) is cleaned, and the air-fuel ratio (combustion) is checked by flue gas analysis. Poor atomization causes soot build-up, uptake fires and loss of efficiency.
Su tarafında ise gauge glass, scum/blowd: On the water side, the gauge glass, scum/blowdown valves and water level alarms (low/low-low water level) are tested. Automatic burner shut-off at low water level (flame failure + low water cut-off) is a vital safety function.
Kazan suyu kimyasal olarak şartlandırılı: Boiler water is chemically treated; chloride, phosphate, alkalinity (pH) and condensate hardness tests are carried out regularly. Incorrect water chemistry leads to internal boiler corrosion, scale and carry-over. Test results are entered in the water treatment log.
Emniyet valfleri (safety valve), kazanın: Safety valves are the boiler's last protection against overpressure; the set pressure and the lifting (lift/easing gear) test are verified during survey. Unauthorized tampering with these valves is strictly prohibited.
Yardımcı sistem hatlarındaki valfler (gl: Valves in auxiliary system lines (globe, gate, butterfly, NRV) are overhauled periodically for tightness and function. On a globe valve, the seat/disc is lapped/ground with grinding paste, the gland packing is renewed and the spindle is checked for straightness. NRVs are tested to confirm that they are fitted in the correct direction and move freely; an NRV fitted the wrong way round has disastrous consequences.
Gasket malzemesi akışkan, sıcaklık ve ba: Gasket material is selected according to the fluid, temperature and pressure: CNAF (fiber) for water/oil, spiral-wound or graphite for steam/high temperature, and an oil-resistant type for fuel. The wrong gasket material creates a risk of leakage, fire (fuel/oil) or steam burns.
Yatak arızası, yardımcı makinelerde en s: Bearing failure is the most common cause of unplanned downtime of auxiliary machinery. Noise/vibration is monitored on rolling bearings, and clearance and temperature on plain bearings. Worn bearing clearance is measured with a feeler gauge or lead wire ("bridge gauge"); if it is outside the manufacturer's tolerance, the bearing is replaced.
Titreşim ölçümü ve yatak sıcaklığı trend: Vibration measurement and bearing temperature trend monitoring (condition-based maintenance) catch a failure before it causes unplanned downtime. An abnormal value points to an alignment problem, imbalance or insufficient lubrication.
LO/FO/SW devrelerindeki dubleks (duplex): Duplex filters in LO/FO/SW circuits are cleaned according to the ΔP (pressure drop) gauge. When ΔP rises, the filter is changed over to the clean side and the dirty element is removed and cleaned; on auto-backflush filters, the solenoid and the differential switch are checked.
Filtre üzerindeki metalik partiküller (ö: Metallic particles on a filter (especially an LO filter) can be an early sign of bearing/surface wear; the finding is assessed together with oil analysis and reported to the Chief Engineer.
Üçüncü/Dördüncü Mühendis, basit elektrik: In simple electrical maintenance, the Third/Fourth Engineer works with the electrical engineer/ETO: tightness of motor terminal boxes, megger (insulation resistance) measurement, greasing of motor bearings, checks of contactors/overcurrent relays, and engine room lighting (especially escape route and emergency lighting). All electrical work is done with isolation and LOTO.
Acil jeneratör ve acil yangın pompası gi: Weekly tests of critical electrical equipment such as the emergency generator and the emergency fire pump are recorded; these are among the first items that PSC and class inspections look at.
Mekanik montajda üretici tork değerleri,: In mechanical assembly, the manufacturer's torque values are applied with the correct spanner and a torque wrench; tightening by eye/feel is not accepted on critical connections. When the job is complete, the system is re-energized, a leak test is carried out and the parameters (pressure, temperature, current, vibration) are monitored on the first start.
İş sonrası alan temizlenir, sökülen cont: After the job, the area is cleaned, removed gaskets/waste oil are put into the correct waste stream (MARPOL/garbage management), the spare parts used are deducted in the PMS and the job is closed.
Üçüncü/Dördüncü Mühendis için yardımcı m: For the Third/Fourth Engineer, success in auxiliary machinery maintenance does not come from being able to "take equipment apart and put it back together", but from a discipline that is planned (PMS), isolated (LOTO), measured (clearance/ΔP/vibration) and recorded (ORB/PMS). A bearing noise or a filter ΔP caught early prevents an unplanned blackout or a pollution incident in mid-ocean.
Tipik bir gemide ballast, ayrı bir balla: On a typical ship, ballasting is done with a separate ballast pump (centrifugal) or an eductor (jet pump). The system consists of sea chests (high/low suction), the main ballast line, branch valves and a separate butterfly/remote-controlled valve for each tank. The valves may be hydraulically/pneumatically remote-controlled; their open/closed status is monitored on the mimic panel.
Üçüncü/Dördüncü Mühendis, ballast operas: Before a ballast operation, the Third/Fourth Engineer verifies the line-up: correct suction/discharge selection, sea chest open, status of the overboard valve, and closing of the valves that prevent water from passing into unintended tanks. An incorrect line-up leads to list/trim problems through the wrong tank being flooded or through backflow.
Tank seviyeleri hem otomatik (remote tan: Tank levels are verified both automatically (remote tank gauging) and manually with a sounding tape. If the automatic system and the manual measurement do not agree, a sensor fault or a line leak is suspected. Keeping sounding pipes clear and their self-closing caps in working order is a SOLAS requirement.
Ballast alırken/basarken kademeli soundi: When ballasting/deballasting, changes in trim and list are monitored by soundings at intervals; a sudden change is a sign of a valve fault or a wrong line-up. Operation records (start/finish levels, pump running time, quantity) are kept.
BWM Convention, ballast suyuyla taşınan: The BWM Convention prevents invasive species carried in ballast water from spreading into marine ecosystems. There are two ways of complying: D-1 (ballast water exchange — exchange in the open sea, at least 200 nautical miles offshore and in water at least 200 m deep, with 95% volumetric exchange) and D-2 (ballast water treatment — meeting the biological standard with an approved BWMS). The implementation schedule has been completed; modern ships carry a BWMS for D-2.
D-1 exchange üç yöntemle yapılır: sequen: D-1 exchange is carried out by three methods: sequential (empty and refill), flow-through (pumping through three times the tank volume) and dilution. In the sequential method, stability, strength and the risk of slamming/sloshing while tanks are being emptied are coordinated with the bridge; with some tanks empty, the ship may approach its strength limits.
İki yaygın BWMS tipi vardır: UV (ultravi: There are two common types of BWMS: UV (ultraviolet) systems disinfect with a filter + UV reactor, and electrochlorination (EC) systems disinfect by generating chlorine in situ from seawater. The Third/Fourth Engineer monitors filter backflush, UV lamp/sensor condition, TRO (Total Residual Oxidant) measurement and neutralization (neutralizing the chlorine during discharge) parameters. In EC systems, hydrogen gas ventilation is critical for preventing explosions.
BWMS arızası veya bypass durumunda conti: If the BWMS fails or is bypassed, the contingency procedure is applied; if a bypass has been made, it is entered in the BWRB and reported to the port authority. An unauthorized bypass leads to heavy sanctions in USCG/PSC inspections.
Bilge sistemi, makine dairesi ve hold bi: The bilge system is a safety system that collects oily/dirty water accumulating in the engine room and hold bilge wells. Each bilge well has a high-level alarm; these alarms are tested regularly. A steady rise in the engine room bilge level is an early sign of a leak (seawater, cooling water, oil) and is investigated immediately.
Bilge suyu, bilge primary tank/holding t: Bilge water is collected in the bilge primary tank/holding tank and is discharged to sea only through the OWS, below the 15 ppm limit. In an emergency (flooding), the emergency bilge suction can connect the main SW pump directly to the bilge; this is used only for the safety of the ship and is recorded.
Bilge well ve sludge/bilge holding tank: Bilge well and sludge/bilge holding tank levels are monitored by daily soundings; trend monitoring points to the source of a leak. An abnormal increase in bilge water is entered in the watch report and reported to the Chief Engineer.
OWS, yer çekimi/coalescer prensibiyle bi: The OWS separates oil from bilge water on the gravity/coalescer principle; the oil content at the outlet is measured continuously by the Oil Content Meter (OCM/15 ppm monitor). If the oil content exceeds 15 ppm, the three-way valve automatically diverts the water back to the bilge tank (recirculation), and it cannot be pumped overboard. This automatic stopping device is a MARPOL requirement and must not be disabled.
OWS işletimi öncesi OCM kalibrasyonu, ze: Before the OWS is operated, the OCM calibration, zero/span check and condition of the coalescer element are verified. A cloudy emulsion (bilge water mixed with detergent/chemicals) upsets the OWS and causes constant alarms; for this reason, unnecessary use of detergents in the engine room is avoided.
OWS ile denize basma, bilge transferi, s: Pumping overboard through the OWS, bilge transfers, sludge burning (incinerator) and deliveries to shore reception are entered in ORB Part I with the operation codes, correctly and on time. Entries carry the signature of the crew member concerned and the Master's approval. An inconsistency in the ORB (e.g. the sludge produced not matching the quantity disposed of) is a main red flag in a PSC inspection.
Ballast, bilge, FO/DO/LO ve FW tankların: The levels of ballast, bilge, FO/DO/LO and FW tanks are monitored by daily soundings. Manual measurement is done with a sounding tape + dip paste (to distinguish water from oil) and is cross-checked against automatic gauging (pneumercator, radar, capacitive). A discrepancy indicates a sensor fault or a line/valve leak.
Sounding sonuçları, kalibrasyon tablosu: Sounding results are converted into volume using the calibration table (tank calibration/ullage table), and trim/list corrections are applied. The results are entered in the tank sounding log and feed into bunker/FW/ballast management.
Kısmen dolu (slack) tanklar serbest yüze: Partially filled (slack) tanks create a free surface effect and reduce the ship's effective GM. In ballast operations, tanks are kept either full (pressed up) or empty as far as possible; having many slack tanks at the same time weakens stability. The engine room manages this risk in coordination with the bridge.
Ballast/bilge santrifüj pompaları suctio: Ballast/bilge centrifugal pumps cannot prime when there is air on the suction side; therefore a self-priming arrangement or a priming pump is used. Insufficient NPSH (Net Positive Suction Head) causes cavitation; cavitation produces noise, vibration and impeller erosion. At low tank levels, an eductor (jet pump) is used for stripping (removing the last of the water); the eductor driving water pressure must be sufficient.
Hidrolik/pnömatik uzaktan kumandalı valf: With hydraulically/pneumatically remote-controlled valves, the mimic panel indication may not match the actual valve position (limit switch fault, hydraulic leak). In case of doubt, the valve is checked manually/locally. A wrong valve position leads to a serious list/trim incident through the wrong tank being pumped or through backflow; therefore, during critical operations, the valve position is physically verified.
ABD sularında USCG, type-approved BWMS v: In US waters, the USCG requires a type-approved BWMS and detailed reporting (BWMR — Ballast Water Management Report); states such as California may have additional rules. Australia, New Zealand and some ports also apply their own biosecurity requirements. Before the operation, port information (port agent + company instructions) is checked.
Bazı limanlarda exchange/treatment belir: In some ports, exchange/treatment must be carried out at specified coordinates or at a specified depth; records are kept with GPS position and time stamp. PSC cross-checks the records against the actual situation.
Ballast tanklarında biriken sediment (ça: Sediment (mud) accumulating in ballast tanks may harbor invasive species; periodic sediment removal and disposal are planned under the BWMP. Entry into a tank is made with an enclosed space entry permit; atmosphere testing (O2/LEL/H2S) and standby personnel are mandatory.
Makine dairesine kontrolsüz su girişinde: In the event of uncontrolled water ingress into the engine room (cooler burst, sea valve failure, hull damage), the source is isolated first, then the bilge pumps and, if necessary, the emergency bilge suction are brought into use. The bridge is informed, and if necessary the effect on stability/draft is assessed. This scenario is drilled regularly.
BWMS arızasında contingency planı uygula: If the BWMS fails, the contingency plan is applied (alternative method, adjustment of the voyage plan, port notification). If the OWS fails, bilge water is not pumped overboard; holding tank capacity is managed and shore reception is planned. In both cases, the records (BWRB/ORB) are kept complete and the Chief Engineer/company is informed.
Ballast ve bilge sistemleri, hem geminin: Ballast and bilge systems are zero-tolerance areas, both for the safety of the ship (stability, underwater integrity) and for environmental compliance (BWM and 15 ppm). The Third/Fourth Engineer's work is built on correct line-ups, verified valve positions, working automatic safeguards and complete records. Every shortcut taken here comes back either as a pollution fine or as a flooding incident.
Modern ana makinelerde safety system, pa: On modern main engines, the safety system monitors the parameters and, when a threshold is exceeded, first gives an alarm and, if the condition continues, applies a slowdown or shutdown.
