Some hazards (e.g. low LO pressure, overspeed) are linked directly to a trip, because any delay would wreck the engine. In certain situations, the bridge may temporarily override a shutdown for the safety of maneuvering (e.g. in confined waters); however, this is a conscious acceptance of risk and is recorded.
Üçüncü/Dördüncü Mühendis, her cihazın ha: The Third/Fourth Engineer must know which level (alarm/slowdown/shutdown) each device is linked to, its setpoint and its test method. Tests are usually done without actually stopping the engine, by simulation (imitating the sensor signal) or with an independent test function.
Emniyet testleri PMS'te calendar job ola: Safety tests are defined in the PMS as calendar jobs (weekly/monthly/quarterly). Before a test, the bridge is informed (for trip tests), and the necessary isolation and duty engineer preparations are made. The test result (setpoint, measured value, response time, pass/fail) is entered in the safety test log and the PMS; a faulty device is reported immediately and temporary protective measures are taken.
Bilge well high-level alarmları genellik: Bilge well high-level alarms are usually floater-type or capacitive level switches. The test is done by physically raising the switch (lifting the floater) or with the test button; it is verified that the alarm appears both on the local panel and on the repeater panel on the bridge/CCR (cargo control / engine control room). The automatic start function of the connected bilge pump is also tested.
Bilge alarmları yağ/kir nedeniyle yapışa: Bilge alarms can stick because of oil/dirt; periodic cleaning and function testing are therefore done together. A bilge alarm that does not work allows water to collect silently in the engine room, with the risk that flooding is noticed late.
Bilge seviyesi yönetimi yalnızca emniyet: Bilge level management matters not only for safety but also for pollution prevention. The bilge alarm feeds into bilge holding tank management; OWS operations are planned according to this level. Tests and findings are recorded.
Test, dahili test fonksiyonu (referans/d: The test is carried out with the built-in test function (reference/dummy chamber, optical signal simulation); the cleanliness of the measuring heads and sampling pipes is verified. A dirty/blocked sampling path gives false readings. It is confirmed that the alarm/slowdown signal reaches the bridge.
OMD alarmı asla \"false alarm\" varsayıl: An OMD alarm is never silenced on the assumption that it is a "false alarm". When mist is detected, the engine is slowed down/stopped, and the crankcase doors are kept closed for at least 20–30 minutes (so that the hot spot cools down and a sudden inflow of air does not trigger an explosion) before an inspection is made. This procedure is reinforced through drills.
Ana yatak, krank yatağı, kam mili yatağı: Temperature sensors (Pt100/thermocouple) are fitted to the main bearings, crankpin bearings, camshaft bearings and turbocharger bearings. The test is carried out by applying a simulated value to the sensor input (decade box / test resistor) and verifying that the alarm/slowdown setpoint triggers correctly. In actual operation, bearing temperature is monitored as a trend; a slowly rising trend is a sign of early wear.
Yatak sıcaklık alarmı, OMD ile birlikte: Together with the OMD, the bearing temperature alarm is the second layer of crankcase protection. A sudden jump in temperature indicates loss of lubrication or metal-to-metal contact; in this case, the load is reduced and an inspection is made.
Test sonucu, setpoint değeri ve tetiklen: The test result is recorded with the setpoint value and the level triggered (alarm/slowdown). If sensor drift (deviation from the actual value) is found, calibration or replacement is planned. A bearing temperature alarm that does not work means that a mechanical failure in the bearing is noticed late.
Ana makine ve jeneratörler, devrin tehli: The main engine and the generators are protected by an overspeed trip that prevents the speed from rising to a dangerous level. The mechanical type (spring-loaded bolt/flyweight) trips at a set speed; the electronic type works with a pickup sensor + governor. Overspeed occurs on loss of load (e.g. a generator breaker opening, the propeller coming out of the water) or on governor failure, and can wreck the engine.
Test, kontrollü şekilde (genelde yüksüz,: The test is carried out in a controlled way (usually without load, in coordination with the bridge/Chief Engineer) by raising the speed, or by tripping the mechanism manually/with the test function. The tripping speed (rpm) is measured and compared with the manufacturer's/class value.
Over-speed koruması, governor (devir reg: Overspeed protection is integrated with the governor (speed regulator). A governor fault causes either hunting (speed oscillation) or overspeed through loss of control. On generators, load sharing and frequency control depend on the governor; governor maintenance and the overspeed test are therefore planned together.
Yağlama yağı (LO) basıncının düşmesi, ya: A drop in lubricating oil (LO) pressure means that the bearings run dry and are destroyed within minutes; this is why, on most engines, LO low pressure is linked first to an alarm and then to an automatic shutdown. The test is done by simulating the pressure switch/transmitter input or by reducing the pressure in a controlled way; it is verified that the alarm and trip setpoints trigger correctly.
Aynı test, stand-by LO pompasının otomat: The same test also covers the automatic start function of the standby LO pump: when the pressure of the main LO pump drops, the standby pump must cut in automatically. This auto-start function is vital on UMS ships.
LO basınç düşüşü; tıkalı filtre (yüksek: A drop in LO pressure may be caused by a clogged filter (high ΔP), pump wear, a line leak or air on the suction side (low sump). When a real alarm occurs after the test, the cause is quickly narrowed down by checking the filter ΔP, the sump level and the condition of the pump. The LO low-pressure trip is never disabled for being a "nuisance".
Ağır yakıt (HFO), enjeksiyon için uygun: Heavy fuel oil (HFO) is heated in the FO heater (steam/electric) to bring it to the correct viscosity for injection. Overheating leads to fuel degradation, coking and a safety risk; this is why there is a high-temperature alarm and, where necessary, a heater cut-off. The test verifies, by simulating the temperature sensor, that the alarm/cut-off setpoint works correctly.
Viskozite kontrol sistemi (viscotherm) h: The viscosity control system (viscotherm) adjusts the heater according to fuel viscosity; a sensor/control fault causes overheating or insufficient heating. On electric heaters, there is a risk of dry heating at low fuel flow; the low-flow protection is tested.
Buhar ısıtıcılarda kondensat hattındaki: On steam heaters, the condensate line is checked for traces of oil (internal heater leak); if fuel leaks into the steam side, the boiler becomes contaminated. Tests and checks are recorded together with heater maintenance.
Makine dairesi yangın emniyeti, yakıt/ya: Engine room fire safety includes the quick-closing valves of fuel/oil tanks (which shut off the fuel flow remotely in a fire), the remote emergency stops of pumps, and the ventilation damper/fan stop functions. These devices are tested periodically; it is verified that the fire pump, fuel shut-off and air shut-off can be operated from a single point in a fire. They are covered by SOLAS II-2 and are a focus of PSC inspections.
Alarm monitoring system (AMS) düzenli \": The alarm monitoring system (AMS) is checked regularly with a "lamp test" and for signal integrity. Frequently recurring false alarms (nuisance alarms) either get silenced and ignored, which is dangerous, or their root cause (sensor/cable) is eliminated. The right approach is not to ignore a false alarm but to fix its source.
Emniyet sistemi testleri, \"her şey yolu: Safety system tests are the one layer that "seems unnecessary when everything is fine" but one day saves the engine, the ship and the crew. For the Third/Fourth Engineer, the measure is not having done the test, but having proved and recorded that the device actually works at the correct setpoint and at the correct level (alarm/slowdown/trip). A silenced alarm is an invitation to a future crankcase explosion or bearing seizure.
Sıcak çalışma; açık alev, kıvılcım veya: Hot work covers any operation that involves an open flame or sparks, or that can raise a surface temperature to ignition point: electric arc welding, oxy-acetylene cutting, grinding, drilling, hot chipping. Because of fuel, oil vapor, hot surfaces and limited ventilation, the engine room is by its nature a hazardous environment for such work.
Üçüncü/Dördüncü Mühendis, işin \"rutin\": The Third/Fourth Engineer knows that a job looking "routine" does not make it any less dangerous. Many engine room fires in the past started when sparks from a short grinding job, done without a permit or without supervision, ignited an oil-soaked rag or bilge residue.
Hiçbir sıcak çalışma, geçerli bir Hot Wo: No hot work may start without a valid Hot Work Permit. The permit records the job, its location, the time window, the precautions taken and the approving officer (usually the Chief Engineer and/or the Master). The Third/Fourth Engineer verifies that the permit conditions are actually met on site.
Her sıcak çalışma öncesinde bir risk değ: Before every hot work job, a Risk Assessment or Job Safety Analysis is carried out. The hazards are listed one by one and rated on a likelihood/severity matrix, and a control measure is defined for each hazard. The Third/Fourth Engineer personally helps to complete the form and confirms that it matches the reality on site.
Hiyerarşik kontrol uygulanır: önce işi o: The hierarchy of controls is applied: first eliminate the work (e.g. by taking the part to the workshop/deck and working on it there) or substitute it; if that is not possible, engineering controls (screens, ventilation), administrative controls (permit, fire watch) and finally PPE come into play.
İş başlamadan önce işi yapacak ekip, fir: Before the job starts, the team doing the work, the fire watch and the supervising engineer hold a short toolbox talk: the sequence of work, who does what, who does what in an emergency, where the nearest extinguisher/hose is and what the escape route is. This short talk is the most practical step for preventing most accidents.
Dönen veya enerjili ekipman üzerinde çal: Before work on rotating or energized equipment, all energy sources (electrical, hydraulic, pneumatic, pressurized fluid, potential/gravity) are safely isolated and prevented from being unexpectedly activated. Lock Out is done with a physical lock, and Tag Out with a warning tag.
Üçüncü/Dördüncü Mühendis; breaker'ı açar: The Third/Fourth Engineer opens the breaker, locks it, tags it and, where possible, verifies with a "try-out" (start attempt) that the equipment is actually de-energized. Stop valves are closed and locked, pressure is released, and "stored energy" (accumulators, pressurized lines, springs) is made safe.
En sık görülen hatalar: yalnızca lokal s: The most common errors are: relying only on the local stop without isolating the breaker, not releasing stored energy, not doing a try-out, and the oncoming team not verifying the isolation at the watch change. The Third/Fourth Engineer does not skip these steps; pressure because "we're in a hurry" can never justify relaxing the isolation.
Sintine kuyusu, tank, kofferdam, çift di: Entry into enclosed spaces such as bilge wells, tanks, cofferdams, double bottoms, boilers and the main engine crankcase requires a separate enclosed space entry permit. The atmosphere is tested before and during entry: oxygen (target 20.9%), flammable gas (LEL 0%), toxic gases (H2S, CO). The Third/Fourth Engineer verifies that the gas detector is calibrated and assists with the measurements.
Giriş süresince kapı/menhol başında bir: During entry, a standby person/watchman is present at the door/manhole, continuous communication is maintained and a rescue plan is kept ready. Most enclosed space deaths are caused by low oxygen or toxic gas that comes without warning, and the toll multiplies when a second person goes in unprepared "to help".
Bir tank veya kapalı alanda sıcak çalışm: If hot work is to be done in a tank or enclosed space, the risk multiplies: the atmosphere must be gas-free, and the welding/cutting fumes and gases must be removed by continuous ventilation. It is also verified that adjacent tanks and pipelines have been cleared of flammable residues.
Her sıcak çalışmada, işi yapan kişiden a: For every hot work job, there is a fire watch separate from the person doing the work. The fire watch's task is to keep continuous watch on the area where sparks fall, on hidden voids and on adjacent compartments, and to keep the first-response equipment at hand. The fire watch continues for at least 30-60 minutes (according to company procedure) after the job is finished, because smoldering material can burst into flame later.
İş tamamlanınca ekipman soğutulur, alan: When the job is complete, the equipment is cooled, the area is checked, the fire watch period is completed and the permit is "closed". The Third/Fourth Engineer verifies that the area is clean, that the fire-fighting equipment has been put back in place, and that the LOTO isolation was removed only once the job was completely finished.
Sıcak çalışmada standart KKD; kaynak mas: Standard PPE for hot work includes a welding mask/dark-lens face shield, flame-resistant gloves, a leather apron/coverall, steel-toed shoes, ear protection and, when needed, respiratory protection. For grinding, a face shield and dust mask are mandatory. The PPE is checked every time to make sure it is undamaged and suitable for the job.
Birçok makine dairesi yangını soruşturma: In many engine room fire investigations, the common factor is a short grinding/welding job done without a permit or without a fire watch. The spark ignited unseen bilge residue or oil-soaked insulation, and by the time the flames were noticed, the fire had grown. Lesson: no hot work is "small"; permit, isolation and fire watch are not negotiable.
Üçüncü/Dördüncü Mühendis için sıcak ve i: For the Third/Fourth Engineer, safety in hot work and isolated work is a habit earned through disciplined adherence to procedure. A single skipped step — pressure not released, isolation not verified, a fire watch withdrawn — can cancel out dozens of correct steps.
Engine room logbook (veya elektronik eşd: The engine room logbook (or its electronic equivalent) records the condition of the machinery every watch: main engine speed/load, auxiliary engine loads, temperatures and pressures, tank levels, water production, fuel/oil consumption and any abnormalities observed. The Third/Fourth Engineer enters the data for their own watch completely and legibly.
Kayıt \"gerçek zamanlı ve dürüst\" olmal: Entries must be "real-time and honest". Logs filled in later from memory or padded with "copied" values make failure analysis impossible and destroy trust during inspections.
Engine room logbook, Oil Record Book Par: The engine room logbook must be consistent with the Oil Record Book Part I. Bilge transfers, OWS (Oily Water Separator) operation, oil transfers and sludge operations are also entered in the ORB; the raw data in the logbook supports this statutory record.
PMS, her ekipman için üreticinin önerdiğ: The PMS turns the maintenance intervals recommended by the manufacturer for each item of equipment (based on running hours or the calendar) into work orders. When maintenance is done, the work order is closed with the work done, the parts used, the values measured (clearance, pressure) and the running hours. The Third/Fourth Engineer enters the records of the jobs under their responsibility on time and completely.
Kapatılmayan veya geç kapatılan iş emirl: Work orders that are not closed, or are closed late, fall into the "overdue" list. Too many overdue jobs damage both class CMS compliance and the impression given to PSC; maintenance is therefore recorded as soon as it is done.
Continuous Machinery Survey (CMS) kapsam: Opening-up/measurement records of equipment covered by the Continuous Machinery Survey (CMS) are essential for the class surveyor to give survey credit. Proper PMS records make the survey easier and avoid unnecessary repeat opening-up.
Conta, o-ring, filtre, kayış, yağ, gres,: The use of consumables such as gaskets, O-rings, filters, belts, oil, grease and chemicals is recorded and the stock is updated. This record shows the rate of consumption, identifies items that fall below the minimum stock (ROB – Remaining On Board) and prevents unnecessary over-ordering.
Minimum seviyenin altına düşen veya yakl: Items that fall below or approach the minimum level are reported in good time to the Second Engineer (and, when necessary, to the Chief Engineer). The report includes the part name, the IMPA/maker part number, the current ROB, the quantity required and the urgency. Late reporting means that a critical spare cannot be supplied within the port window.
Makine kayıtları sadece geçmişi belgelem: Engine records do not just document the past; they manage the future. Wrong or invented data leads to wrong maintenance decisions, unexpected breakdowns and loss of trust during inspections. The Third/Fourth Engineer does not fill in a value that could not be measured with an estimate; the value is either measured or noted as "could not be measured".
Modern gemilerde PMS, AMOS, TM Master ve: On modern ships, the PMS is run with AMOS, TM Master or similar software, and the data are synchronized with the shore office. The Third/Fourth Engineer learns to enter work orders against the correct equipment, to update running hours and to verify that the records are complete before synchronization.
Bir yatak sıcaklığındaki kademeli yüksel: If a gradual rise in a bearing temperature is not entered in the logs, the trend can grow unnoticed and eventually lead to bearing damage. A well-kept trend record could have predicted the same failure weeks in advance. Recording discipline is machinery health, directly.
İyi bir mühendisin kayıtları, kendisi va: A good engineer's records describe the machinery even when the engineer is not on watch. For the Third/Fourth Engineer, careful record-keeping is the foundation of both professional discipline and the ship's technical safety.
Bakım üç temel yaklaşımla ele alınır: re: Maintenance follows three basic approaches: reactive (repair when it fails), preventive (planned maintenance based on time/running hours) and predictive/condition-based (according to the actual condition of the equipment). A modern ship uses all three in balance. While carrying out preventive maintenance, the Third/Fourth Engineer also learns to catch failures early from condition data.
Deneyimli bir mühendis, makineyi gözle (: An experienced engineer "listens" to the machinery with the eyes (leaks, color, smoke), the ears (knocking, rubbing), the hands (vibration, temperature) and the nose (burning, smell of fuel). This "human sensor" scan catches changes that even the most expensive monitoring system may miss.
Sıcaklık, basınç, titreşim, yağ analizi: Temperature, pressure, vibration, oil analysis and performance (load/speed/consumption) are the most commonly monitored indicators. The direction and rate of a deviation point to the problem: a slowly rising bearing temperature may mean lubrication problems/wear; a sudden pressure drop, a leak/blockage; increasing vibration, imbalance/bearing damage.
Periyodik yağ numune analizi (viskozite,: Periodic oil sample analysis (viscosity, water, metal particles, TBN) reveals internal wear before it shows from the outside. An increase in metals indicates bearing/piston ring wear, and water/glycol indicates a cooling water leak. The Third/Fourth Engineer assists with taking samples and following up the results.
Filtre tıkanıklığı, gevşek bağlantı, küç: Problems such as a clogged filter, a loose connection, a small gasket leak, bleeding air (priming) or a simple electrical connection are within the authority and competence of a junior engineer. Before intervening, the LOTO and permit rules are followed; the solution and the outcome are recorded.
Belirti kapsamı aşıyorsa, güvenlik riski: If the symptoms go beyond this scope, if there is a safety risk or if the solution is unclear, the work is stopped and a senior engineer is called. Pressing ahead on an unfamiliar system "just to try" can turn a small problem into major damage.
Bir filtreyi sürekli değiştirmek belirti: Changing a filter again and again manages the symptom; finding the source of the contamination that clogs the filter solves the failure. With simple methods such as 5-Why and fishbone, the chain of "why" is traced back to the root cause. The Third/Fourth Engineer contributes to this analysis with observations and data.
Karmaşık arızalar, üst mühendise yapılan: Complex failures are reported to the senior engineer in a structured way: what was observed, when it started, which values changed, what action was taken and what state the equipment is in. Presenting measured data and a timeline instead of a vague "it broke down" speeds up the right decision.
Bazı bakımlar makine durdurularak yapılı: Some maintenance is done with the engine stopped; it is therefore planned in line with the voyage/port schedule. The Third/Fourth Engineer prepares their own jobs for these windows (parts, tools and permits ready), so that downtime is kept to a minimum.
Önleyici bakım ve arıza analizi, genç mü: Preventive maintenance and failure analysis is the area where the junior engineer turns from a "repairer" into a "diagnostician". The engineer who sees the cause rather than the symptom, and catches a small deviation before it grows, is the engine room's most valuable safeguard.
UMS, makine dairesinin belirli periyotla: UMS means that class and the flag State have approved unattended operation of the engine room for certain periods (especially at night); the class notation is often "E0". Approval requires adequate automatic control, a comprehensive alarm system, automatic fire detection, transfer of alarms to the bridge and a duty engineer who can be reached quickly.
UMS, \"makineye bakılmıyor\" demek değil: UMS does not mean "nobody is looking after the machinery"; it means "reliable automation + a duty engineer on call, instead of constant manning". The price of this trust is disciplined preparation before every unmanned period.
Hazırlığın kalbi alarm sistemidir. Tüm k: The heart of the preparation is the alarm system. It is verified that all critical alarm setpoints are correctly set and active; the transfer of alarms to the bridge and the engineers' cabins (extension alarm) is tested. If any alarm is suppressed (inhibit/override), the reason for it and the risk are assessed.
Sintine yüksek seviye alarmı ve high-lev: The bilge high-level alarm and the high-level floater switches are tested, because they are the first to report water ingress during an unmanned period. A bilge alarm that does not work can turn into a serious danger through undetected water ingress.
İnsansız periyot süresince beklenen tüke: The expected consumption during the unmanned period is calculated, and it is verified that the fuel service tank, oil service/storage tanks, settling tank and fresh water tanks are at levels that will comfortably cover the period. Automatic transfer/filling systems must be active and in good order; even so, a manual reserve level is kept.
Standby pompaların (yağ, soğutma suyu, y: The automatic start function of the standby pumps (lube oil, cooling water, fuel) (auto start on low pressure) is tested. It is verified that automatic generator start (blackout/load-dependent) and the auto synchronization system are ready, because during an unmanned period it is the automation that will respond to a pump or generator failure.
İnsansız periyotta nöbetçi (duty) mühend: A duty engineer is designated for the unmanned period; this person must be rested, reachable and able to get down to the engine room quickly when an alarm sounds. The communication channel between the bridge and the engine room, the dead-man alarm and the telephone/radio are tested.
Üçüncü/Dördüncü Mühendis, hazırlığı tama: After completing the preparations, the Third/Fourth Engineer hands over the engine room as "ready for UMS" and records this; the duty engineer and the bridge are informed.
Alarm çaldığında nöbetçi mühendis vakit: When an alarm sounds, the duty engineer goes down to the engine room without delay, assesses the situation and, if necessary, informs the bridge. For a critical alarm such as fire or water ingress, the emergency procedure is put into action. The better the preparation, the fewer and more manageable the night alarms.
UMS hazırlığı, \"yokluğunda makineye bir: UMS preparation is a professional assurance that "nothing will happen to the machinery in your absence". This assurance only becomes real through checks carried out in full before every unmanned period; a single skipped step can turn the night into an emergency.
Bir buhar sıkıştırmalı soğutma çevrimi d: A vapor-compression refrigeration cycle consists of four basic components: the compressor (raises pressure/temperature), the condenser (rejects heat, gas→liquid), the expansion valve (lowers pressure) and the evaporator (takes heat from the space, liquid→gas). Knowing the "normal" pressures and temperatures of this cycle, the Third/Fourth Engineer diagnoses deviations.
Provizyon tesisi genelde tek/çok odalı d: The provision plant is usually a single/multi-room direct-expansion system; each room is kept at the required temperature by a thermostat (e.g. meat −18°C, vegetables +4°C). The HVAC system air-conditions the accommodation. The reefer cargo plant (if fitted) has a much higher capacity and is critical for the integrity of the cargo.
Vardiya sırasında kompresör emiş/basma b: During the watch, compressor suction/discharge pressures, condenser and evaporator temperatures, compressor oil pressure and room temperatures are read and recorded. A deviation from normal is often the first sign of a problem: low suction pressure may mean a shortage of refrigerant/a restriction; high discharge pressure may mean a condenser problem/air in the system.
Sıvı hat sight glass'ında kabarcık görül: Bubbles in the liquid line sight glass usually indicate a low refrigerant charge or a restriction in the line. The Third/Fourth Engineer checks this simple indicator regularly and reports to the Chief Engineer if in doubt.
Kaçak; düşen performans, sık şarj ihtiya: A leak shows itself through falling performance, frequent need for recharging, bubbles in the sight glass, unusual noise or temperature imbalance. Leak points are searched for with an electronic detector or a bubble test. A leak both reduces performance and creates environmental/legal liability.
Refrigerant ilavesi, geri kazanım ve dev: Adding refrigerant, recovering it and opening the circuit usually require expertise and special equipment; the Third/Fourth Engineer detects and reports signs of leaks/faults and carries out any intervention under the supervision of the Chief Engineer. Ignoring a leak brings both loss of food/cargo and legal risk.
Provizyon odalarının doğru sıcaklıkta tu: Keeping the provision rooms at the correct temperature is essential for food safety and crew health. Temperature deviations are monitored in coordination with the cook/steward; if a room fails, quick action (alternative cooling, priority of consumption) is taken to save the food.
HVAC, yaşam mahallini konforlu ve MLC st: The HVAC keeps the accommodation comfortable and in line with MLC standards. Filter cleanliness, fan/damper operation and air quality are monitored. A clogged filter both reduces comfort and increases energy consumption.
Reefer kargo taşıyan gemilerde soğutma a: On ships carrying reefer cargo, a refrigeration failure means direct loss of cargo and large claims. Set temperatures, alarm limits and recording systems are monitored continuously; any deviation is reported immediately. For reefer containers, plug/power and temperature monitoring are carried out in coordination with the deck department.
Soğutma ve klima sistemleri \"görünmez\": Refrigeration and air-conditioning systems go unnoticed while they work "invisibly"; when they fail, food, comfort or cargo is suddenly at risk. The Third/Fourth Engineer's regular, recorded checks ensure the reliability of these silent systems.
Dümen donanımı arızası, geminin yön kont: A steering gear failure means that the ship loses directional control; in confined waters, in traffic or during maneuvering, this can end in disaster. This is why SOLAS requires redundancy (main + auxiliary power unit), regular testing and an emergency steering arrangement for the steering gear.
Çoğu ticari gemide elektro-hidrolik düme: Most merchant ships have electro-hydraulic steering gear: ram type (cylinder-tiller) or rotary vane. Hydraulic pumps (usually variable displacement) move the rams; the gear is controlled from the bridge by telemotor or electric signal. The Third/Fourth Engineer monitors the oil, pressure and mechanical condition of this system.
Günlük kontrolde hidrolik yağ seviyesi (: In the daily check, the hydraulic oil level (tank and replenishing tank), leaks at the ram/cylinder seals, leaks at hose/pipe connections and general cleanliness are checked. A leak from a ram seal means loss of oil and a slip/fire hazard on the floor; it also lets air into the system and reduces performance.
Sistem çalışma basıncı normal aralıkta o: The system working pressure must be within the normal range; if the relief valve opens early or the pressure fluctuates, there may be a pump/valve problem. The filter differential pressure (ΔP) is monitored; a rising ΔP indicates clogging. Dirty hydraulic oil is the most common cause of valve and pump wear.
Acil dümen pompası ve lokal (steering ge: The emergency steering pump and the local (steering gear room) control arrangement are tested; communication (telephone/radio) between the bridge and the steering gear room is verified. It is confirmed that, if one power unit fails, the second unit cuts in, and that the rudder moves from hard over to hard over within the required time.
Acil dümen tatbikatında ekip, lokal kuma: In the emergency steering drill, the team rehearses steering the ship with the local control and communications. The Third/Fourth Engineer takes part in the drill and reports deficiencies, and the tests are entered in the logbook.
Ambar kapakları, krenler ve ırgat/güvert: Hatch covers, cranes and windlasses/deck winches are driven by hydraulic power packs. Oil level, filter ΔP, leaks and pressure are checked regularly. These systems directly affect the safety of the deck crew during cargo operations and anchor/mooring work.
Yavaş dümen yanıtı, anormal ses, aşırı y: Slow steering response, abnormal noise, excessive oil temperature, pressure fluctuation and recurring leaks are the main symptoms. If there is air in the system, it is bled. For a symptom that is beyond the engineer's scope or affects safety, the work is stopped and the bridge and the Chief Engineer are informed; "trial and error" is unacceptable on steering gear.
Steering gear, gemide \"asla arıza verme: Steering gear is one of the foremost systems on board that "must never fail". The Third/Fourth Engineer's disciplined daily checks, serious conduct of the SOLAS tests and clean hydraulic oil keep this critical system running quietly but reliably.
LSA ekipmanları; personal (bireysel), su: LSA equipment is grouped as personal, survival craft, launching appliances and distress/locating equipment. The personal group includes lifejackets, immersion suits, anti-exposure suits, thermal protective aids (TPA) and lifebuoys; the survival craft group includes lifeboats and liferafts; the launching group includes davits, winches and release gear; and the distress group includes pyrotechnics, EPIRB, SART, line-throwing apparatus and two-way VHFs.
Safety Officer, geminin SOLAS Record of: The Safety Officer compares the LSA list in the ship's SOLAS Record of Equipment (Form E/C) item by item with the physical inventory. There must be no difference between the quantity stated in the document (e.g. lifeboats of 100% + 100% capacity, 25% additional liferafts, one immersion suit per person) and the actual number on board.
Modern gemilerde LSA kayıtları hem fizik: On modern ships, LSA records are kept both in a physical logbook and in the electronic PMS (Planned Maintenance System). Each inspection is opened as a job and closed when done; expiry dates are tracked in a separate "expiry tracker" table. The Safety Officer's golden rule: work that has not been done is not recorded, and work that has not been recorded is considered not done.
Kayıt tutarlılığı, denetimin en kırılgan: Consistency of records is the most fragile point in an inspection. If a lifeboat engine has been run, the logbook must show the date, the duration, the person who ran it and the observations. A contradiction between the records and the physical condition (e.g. the logbook says "tested" but the HRU has expired) produces a PSC deficiency directly.
Safety Officer; filika içi inventory'i (: The Safety Officer checks the lifeboat inventory (sea anchor, paddles, hatchet, first-aid kit, rations, water, fishing kit, signaling mirror, whistle, bailer) against the MSC/Circ.1047 list. Missing or expired items (e.g. water tablets, rations) are listed and a resupply request is raised.
Safety Officer ayrıca salın throw-over e: The Safety Officer also checks that there is a clear working area from which the raft can be thrown over, that the lashings can be released freely and that the hydrostatic release unit (HRU) is connected correctly. Painted lashings or a cradle seized with rust prevent the raft from floating free in a real emergency — a common and deadly defect.
HRU değişimi, sal servisine denk getiril: HRU replacement can be timed to coincide with the raft service, but it must also be tracked independently. Incorrect installation (mixing up the weak link and the strong point, attaching the painter to the HRU incorrectly) leads either to the raft not deploying at all or to it being dragged down with the sinking ship.
Her mürettebat üyesi için bir adet can y: There must be one lifejacket for each crew member (in the cabin + spares at the muster station + spares for the bridge/engine room watchkeepers). The Safety Officer checks the light (automatic/manual), whistle, retro-reflective tape, body strap and gas capsule condition. Inflatable lifejackets are subject to periodic servicing.
Can simitleri gemi boyutuna göre belirli: Lifebuoys are provided in a specified number according to the size of the ship and are distributed evenly on the bridge wings and decks. At least half are fitted with self-igniting lights, some with self-activating smoke signals, some with buoyant lifelines, and at least two with a quick-release MOB (man-overboard) marker arrangement.
Safety Officer; light battery expiry'ler: The Safety Officer checks the expiry of the light batteries, the expiry of the smoke signals, the condition of the lines and that the bracket holding the lifebuoy can be released freely. MOB lifebuoys must be releasable from the bridge wing with a single action; the bracket must not be seized with rust.
406 MHz EPIRB (Emergency Position-Indica: The 406 MHz EPIRB (Emergency Position-Indicating Radio Beacon) floats free with its HRU when the ship sinks and transmits the ship's identity + GPS position to the COSPAS-SARSAT satellites. The Safety Officer tracks the EPIRB battery expiry, the HRU expiry, the self-test function (weekly), up-to-date MMSI registration and the requirement for an annual shore-based or onboard test.
SART (Search and Rescue Transponder), 9: The SART (Search and Rescue Transponder) responds to a 9 GHz X-band radar signal and produces a line of 12 dots on the rescue ship's radar. Battery expiry and the self-test are checked. Replacement of the EPIRB battery and HRU is documented with service records.
Pyrotechnics; rocket parachute flare (en: Pyrotechnics consist of rocket parachute flares (at least 12 on the bridge), hand flares and buoyant smoke signals; lifeboats and liferafts also have their own sets. All have an expiry date printed on them (usually manufacture + 3-4 years); expired pyrotechnics cannot be used and produce a PSC finding directly.
Safety Officer, tüm pyrotechnics'in expi: The Safety Officer keeps an expiry list of all pyrotechnics and obtains new stock before they expire. Expired pyrotechnics are not thrown away carelessly; they are disposed of properly (port facility or authorized disposal). These items are stored in easily accessible watertight boxes, protected from moisture.
LSA ekipmanının \"yerinde olması\" yetme: It is not enough for LSA equipment to be "in place"; in a real emergency it must be freely accessible and ready for use. The embarkation deck is kept clean, the area in front of the lifeboat is kept clear and no material is stowed in the davit area. The Safety Officer checks this access during routine safety rounds.
Tüm LSA istasyonları IMO Res. A.760(18): All LSA stations are marked with IMO Res. A.760(18) symbols; the muster station, lifejacket lockers, embarkation points and liferaft positions are shown by illuminated signs. Emergency lighting and photoluminescent escape markings must be in working order.
Operasyonel hazırlık; ekipmanın hem çalı: Operational readiness means that the equipment both works and can be used by the personnel. The Safety Officer periodically tests the integrated operation of the davit motor, winch brake, limit switches, embarkation ladder, emergency lighting and general alarm. Whether a lifeboat can be launched depends not only on its engine running but on the whole davit-brake-falls chain.
PSC ve flag/class survey'de LSA denetimi: In PSC and flag/class surveys, LSA inspection stands on three legs: the physical condition of the equipment, the consistency of the records and the crew's competence in using it. The inspector often picks out an item (e.g. an immersion suit), asks for its expiry/test date and then compares it with the record in the logbook.
En sık deficiency'ler: expired pyrotechn: The most frequent deficiencies are: expired pyrotechnics, overdue liferaft service, expired/missing HRUs, painted lashings, lifeboat engines that do not work, incomplete lifeboat inventory and inconsistencies between "records and physical condition". By tracking these items proactively, the Safety Officer comes through inspections without findings.
Safety Officer'ın LSA yönetimindeki başa: The Safety Officer's success in LSA management remains invisible as long as no abandon ship situation occurs; but in a real abandonment, the lives of the crew depend on exactly this disciplined, recorded and date-tracked routine. Saying "the equipment is in place" is only the beginning; being able to say "it works, it is accessible, it is valid and it is documented" means the task is complete.
Safety Officer, geminin fire control pla: The Safety Officer must know the ship's fire control plan by heart (under SOLAS II-2/15.2.4, it is kept on the bridge, at the entrances to the engine room and the bottle room + in an enclosure outside) and must know the location of every fire station, fixed system, detection zone, fire damper and ventilation stop. The FFE inventory is verified by comparing it with the Record of Equipment (Form E).
Sistem dört katmandan oluşur: passive pr: The system consists of four layers: passive protection (A/B class divisions, fire doors), detection (smoke/heat/flame detectors), containment (fire dampers, watertight/fire doors, ventilation shutdown) and extinction (portable + fixed systems). The Safety Officer monitors the readiness of each layer.
Her FFE kalemi PMS'te bir job ile izleni: Each FFE item is tracked in the PMS with a job: monthly extinguisher checks, quarterly hose/nozzle checks, annual SCBA service, five-yearly extinguisher hydro-test and so on. All checks, maintenance and refills are recorded with the date + the person responsible + the findings. Maintenance without a record is considered "not done" in an inspection.
Safety Officer, her tüpün dolu (tartı/ma: The Safety Officer checks that each extinguisher is full (weighing/pressure gauge), sealed (safety pin + tamper seal), accessible and of the correct class, and that its expiry/service date is valid. The extinguisher bracket must be sound, and the content pressure must be in the green band.
Boşalan veya kullanılan her tüp derhal r: Every extinguisher that has been discharged or used is refilled immediately, and a spare extinguisher is hung at the station in the meantime. CO2 and dry powder extinguishers are weighed annually; a weight loss of more than 10% requires refilling. The shell is subject to a hydrostatic test every 5–10 years according to the manufacturer's/flag requirements. All work is documented with date-stamped labels and records.
Emergency fire pump, ana pompadan bağıms: The emergency fire pump is located in a space separate from the main pump and runs on a separate power source; a weekly/monthly running test is carried out and the pressure is verified. The international shore connection (water connection from ship to ship/shore) is kept accessible near the bridge.
Safety Officer, periyodik olarak en uzak: The Safety Officer periodically verifies that the fire main pressure is sufficient by taking jets simultaneously from the two most remote hydrants. The emergency fire pump is isolated and tested separately. These tests are recorded in the logbook with the pressure value and date.
SCBA, fireman's outfit'in parçasıdır; ya: SCBA is part of the fireman's outfit; it allows the fire team to work in smoky/toxic atmospheres. The Safety Officer checks the cylinder pressure (usually ~300 bar when full), the low-pressure whistle (~50-55 bar), mask tightness, demand valve function and the condition of the harness. The cylinder is refilled after every use.
SCBA tüpleri belirli aralıklarla hydrost: SCBA cylinders are subject to hydrostatic testing at set intervals (composite ~5 years, steel ~10 years — determined by the manufacturer/flag). There must be at least two spare charged cylinders or a compressor on board. The mask and regulator are sent to an authorized service provider annually.
EEBD, yangın/duman durumunda kaçış için: An EEBD is a single-use escape device that provides ~10-15 minutes of air for escape in a fire/smoke situation; unlike an SCBA, it is not used for fire-fighting. EEBDs are located on the accommodation and engine room escape routes, in the numbers marked on the fire control plan. SOLAS II-2/13 sets the minimum numbers.
Safety Officer; her EEBD'nin mühürünün (: The Safety Officer checks that the seal of each EEBD is intact, the pressure gauge is in the green band, the expiry date is valid and the device is visible/accessible on the escape route. An EEBD with a broken seal is regarded as tested and is sent for servicing.
Fireman's outfit; alev geçirmez koruyucu: The fireman's outfit consists of flame-resistant protective clothing, boots/gloves, a helmet, a safety lamp (at least 3 hours), a fire axe and an SCBA. Depending on the type of ship, at least two sets are carried. The Safety Officer checks each set for completeness, the condition of the lamp battery and the soundness of the clothing.
Yangına müdahale eden ekibin lifeline ve: The team responding to a fire must be equipped with a lifeline and fireproof lifeline, and supported by low-location lighting and communications (intrinsically safe portable VHF). A missing or damaged component makes the whole outfit unusable.
Ekipmanın çalışması yeterli değildir; ek: It is not enough for the equipment to work; the team must be able to use it quickly and correctly. The Safety Officer shows newly joined personnel SCBA donning, EEBD activation, laying out hoses and the fire alarm points, observes these skills during fire drills and turns any gaps into training.
Makine dairesi ve kargo mahalleri için f: Fixed CO2 (or foam/water-mist/aerosol) systems are provided for the engine room and cargo spaces. The Safety Officer checks the cylinder pressures, release manifold seals, the alarm-before-release system, the ventilation/fuel shut-off interlocks and the warnings at the bottle room entrance. Before CO2 is released, the sequence of clearing all personnel from the space + alarm + ventilation stop must always be followed.
Fixed CO2 sistemi MSC.1/Circ.1318'e göre: Under MSC.1/Circ.1318, the fixed CO2 system is subject to annual, two-yearly and ten-yearly maintenance: annual visual and alarm test, two-yearly hose/manifold check, ten-yearly cylinder hydro-test. These services are carried out and certified by an authorized company.
Smoke, heat ve flame dedektörleri zone b: Smoke, heat and flame detectors are monitored by zone; alarms and faults are shown on the bridge panel. The Safety Officer periodically tests selected detectors with test smoke/heat, and operates the manual call points (MCP) and the general alarm. Zones that are disabled (isolated) are entered in the logbook and followed up.
FFE, PSC'de en sık deficiency çıkan alan: FFE is one of the areas with the most frequent PSC deficiencies: expired/discharged extinguishers, an emergency fire pump that does not work, missing SCBA cylinders, broken EEBD seals, blocked fire stations and inconsistencies between "records and physical condition" are typical findings. By tracking these items proactively and keeping the records without gaps, the Safety Officer goes into inspections prepared.
Denetçi sıklıkla bir crew üyesine \"Show: The inspector often says to a crew member, "Show me how you start the emergency fire pump" or "Don this SCBA". FFE competence is therefore measured not only by the equipment but also by training; familiarization records must be ready.
Yangın ekipmanı, kullanılmadığı sürece g: Fire-fighting equipment is an insurance that remains invisible as long as it is not used; but in a real fire, the survival of the ship and the crew depends directly on this equipment working and on the team being able to use it. The Safety Officer's task is to keep this chain, from "being there" to "working and usable", intact every day.
Bir yangın söndürücüye veya can salına s: When a fire extinguisher or a liferaft has to be reached within seconds, an obstruction in front of it causes a fatal delay. A blocked escape route means being trapped. That is why safety equipment and routes must always be accessible, working and clear.
Üçüncü Zabit, rondlarında şunları arar:: On rounds, the Third Officer looks for: obstructed fire-hose cabinets/extinguishers, material on escape routes, a deteriorated lifebuoy light, liferaft lashings stuck with paint (release not free), a hydrant box seized with rust and a fire door wedged open.
Yangın kapıları, yangın ve dumanın yayıl: Fire doors must be closed (or self-closing) to prevent fire and smoke from spreading. Holding them open with a wedge completely defeats this protection. The Third Officer corrects this common violation firmly.
Üçüncü Zabit düzenli emniyet rondları ya: The Third Officer carries out regular safety rounds to catch housekeeping defects and corrects them, or has them corrected, immediately. For recurring problems, the Third Officer briefs the team; housekeeping is the continuous responsibility of the whole crew, not of one person.
Safety housekeeping, sadece denetim önce: Safety housekeeping is not a clean-up done before an inspection but a daily habit. The Third Officer spreads awareness of "putting things back in their place" and "not blocking the way" throughout the team. Lasting safety is the sum of these small, correct daily actions.
Housekeeping kusurları PSC'de sık çıkan: Housekeeping defects are frequent PSC findings and create an impression of the ship's general safety culture. A ship that is consistently in good order also inspires confidence during inspections. The Third Officer maintains this order every day.
Safety housekeeping, emniyetin en somut: Safety housekeeping is safety in its most concrete, everyday form: keeping the front of the equipment clear, the routes free and the doors in the right position. The Third Officer's constant rounds and "fix it immediately" discipline ensure that, in a real emergency, every second and every item of equipment can save lives.
Emniyet Komitesi, mürettebatın emniyet k: The Safety Committee is a platform where the crew talk openly about safety matters and share problems and suggestions. The aim is to turn safety into a culture that "everyone owns" rather than one "imposed by management". The Third Officer makes this meeting participatory and productive.
Üçüncü Zabit; gündem hazırlar (önceki ak: The Third Officer prepares the agenda (previous actions, new near-misses, drill evaluations, inspection findings, suggestions), determines the participants and runs the meeting. The meeting is conducted so that everyone can speak, with the focus on solutions rather than blame.
Toplantı tutanağı; kararlar, atanan aksi: The minutes of the meeting are recorded together with the decisions, the assigned actions and the persons responsible, and are forwarded to the DPA (Designated Person Ashore). This allows shore management to keep a finger on the pulse of safety on board and to give the necessary support.
Near-miss (ramak kala), zarara yol açmam: A near-miss is an event that did not cause harm but could have. Every near-miss is a forerunner of an accident that can be prevented in the future. According to the accident pyramid principle, behind a large number of reported near-misses lies a smaller number of serious accidents; by managing near-misses, serious accidents are prevented.
Near-miss kültürünün en büyük düşmanı ko: The greatest enemy of a near-miss culture is fear: the perception that "reporting is punished" kills reporting. The Third Officer stresses that reporting is a tool for learning, not for blame, and builds an environment focused on solutions, not punishment. Open reporting is the sign of a living safety culture.
Her near-miss veya bulgu için kök neden: For each near-miss or finding, the root cause is investigated and corrective and preventive actions are defined. Each action is assigned a responsible person and a deadline and is followed up until it is completed. The Third Officer prevents open actions from being forgotten and left unclosed.
Safety Committee ve near-miss yönetimi,: The Safety Committee and near-miss management only work when they are kept up continuously. By making sure that meetings are regular, minutes are true and actions get closed, the Third Officer keeps the safety culture alive; a committee that becomes a "formality" loses its value.

The Safety Committee and near-miss management are the pulse of the ship's safety culture. The open reporting, serious root-cause analysis and closed actions that the Third Officer keeps alive turn today's small warnings into tomorrow's prevented accidents.
Uyuşturucu veya alkol etkisindeki bir ki: A person under the influence of drugs or alcohol loses attention, judgment and reflexes and becomes a time bomb in terms of safety. This is why ships generally apply a zero-tolerance D&A policy. As the person who applies this policy in practice, the Third Officer protects safety.
Rastgele test programı, testlerin öncede: A random testing program requires tests to be carried out at unpredictable intervals and with impartial selection. Targeting particular people or a predictable schedule undermines the deterrent effect and the fairness of the program. The Third Officer handles these logistics impartially and keeps records.
Alkol genellikle breathalyzer ile, uyuşt: Alcohol is usually measured with a breathalyzer, and drugs with urine/saliva test kits. The Third Officer ensures that the test procedure is applied correctly and that the results are recorded.
Test kitleri ve breathalyzer'ın çalışır,: Test kits and the breathalyzer must be in working order, calibrated and within their expiry dates. An expired kit may give a false result. The Third Officer monitors the kit stock and expiry dates and replenishes any shortages.
Pozitif bir sonuç, gizlilikle ve doğruda: A positive result is reported confidentially and directly to the Master, and then to the company. The process is carried out in a way that protects the person's dignity and does not give rise to gossip. Under company policy, a positive result usually leads to removal from duty and further action.
Numune alımından sonuca kadar gözetim zi: The chain of custody is maintained from sample collection to result: who took the sample, how it was stored and who tested it are recorded. This ensures that the result remains valid against challenges, especially when it is positive. Disposal records are also kept.
Bazı liman devletleri (örn. USCG) veya t: Some port States (e.g. USCG) or terminals may request a D&A inspection. The Third Officer coordinates the process during these inspections and presents the records of the ship's program. A ready and well-organized program gets through these inspections without problems.
D&A test yönetimi, emniyetin en hassas a: D&A test management is one of the most sensitive but most necessary areas of safety; it requires impartial application, confidentiality and a sound chain of custody. The Third Officer's regular and fair program is a deterrent shield that prevents one person under the influence from endangering the whole ship.
Safety Officer, geminin SMS'i ve SOLAS g: Based on the ship's SMS and SOLAS requirements, the Safety Officer sets up a test matrix: which equipment, at what interval, by whom and in which record. Weekly tests are usually done together on a set day (e.g. every Monday); monthly tests are completed before the end of the month. The matrix is approved by the Master and followed up on the bridge.
Her test bir PMS job'ına bağlanır; yapıl: Each test is linked to a PMS job; when it is done, the job is closed by entering the date, the result and the person responsible. A skipped or delayed test appears as "overdue" in the system and goes onto the Safety Officer's follow-up list.
Test sonuçları logbook ve PMS'e işlenir;: Test results are entered in the logbook and the PMS; abnormal findings are also raised separately as defect reports. At the end of the month, the Safety Officer prepares a summary report (tests carried out, defects found, open actions) and submits it to the Master. This report serves as evidence for SMS internal audits and PSC.
Haftalık lifeboat ve launching appliance: In the weekly visual inspection of the lifeboat and launching appliance, the lifeboat and davit are inspected visually, and the condition of the falls, the presence of the release gear and hook connection, and the visual condition of the embarkation ladder and brake are checked. If a deficiency is noticed, it is recorded at once and, if necessary, a defect is raised.
Free-fall filikalarda haftalık kontrol,: For free-fall lifeboats, the weekly inspection includes the visual condition of the simulated launching equipment and of the free-fall system; the interval for an actual free-fall test is different. For a davit-launched liferaft, the davit and release system are also checked.
Motorun ileri/geri kavramaları (eğer güv: The ahead/astern engagement of the engine is tested separately (if it is safe, when the boat has been lowered into the water, not in the davit). The running time, observations and battery condition are entered in the logbook.
Haftalık general alarm testi, tüm gemide: The weekly general alarm test verifies that the alarm can be heard throughout the ship and that it works from the standby power source (battery). The crew are informed in advance, so that it is not mistaken for a real emergency. The PA (public address) system must work intelligibly on every deck and in every space; if dead spots are found, a defect is raised.
Safety Officer, alarm testini emergency: The Safety Officer also verifies the alarm test via the emergency switchboard; it is checked that the alarm is fed from the battery when the main power is cut. The test is recorded with the date and result.
Acil aydınlatma, ana güç kaybında belirl: Emergency lighting must work for a set period after loss of main power (usually 3-36 hours, depending on the space). In the weekly check, the emergency lighting is switched on to verify that the escape routes, muster stations, embarkation deck and engine room escape routes are adequately lit. The charge and visibility of the photoluminescent (low-location lighting) strips are checked.
Tüm yangın istasyonlarını her hafta test: It is not practical to test all fire stations every week; the Safety Officer sets up a rotation and tests a different group of hydrants/hoses/nozzles each week, so that all stations are covered within the month. The hose at the station being tested is pressurized and the jet/spray function of the nozzle is tried.
Emergency fire pump da haftalık/aylık ça: The emergency fire pump is also run weekly/monthly to verify that it can work independently of the main pump. The test pressure, flow observation and station numbers are recorded.
Test sırasında çıkan her kusur (sızdıran: Every defect found during the test (leaking gland, cracked coupling, blocked nozzle) is immediately turned into a defect report; if necessary, the station is marked "out of service" and a compensating measure is decided. After repair, it is retested and the record is updated.
Aylık olarak tüm portatif tüpler görsel: Every month, all portable extinguishers are inspected visually: is the pressure gauge in the green band, are the safety pin and tamper seal in place, is the shell free of corrosion, is the bracket sound, is it at the correct station? The annual weighing dates of CO2 and dry powder extinguishers are tracked separately.
Eksik veya geçersiz tüp anında yedekle d: A missing or invalid extinguisher is replaced with a spare at once; a discharged extinguisher is sent for refilling. All checks are recorded via the checklist and the PMS.
Aylık olarak SCBA tüp basıncı, low-press: Every month, the SCBA cylinder pressure, low-pressure whistle and mask tightness; the EEBD seal, pressure gauge and expiry; and the completeness of the fireman's outfit and the safety lamp battery are checked. Deficiencies found are raised as defects.
Safety Officer, aylık olarak tüm tarihli: Every month, the Safety Officer updates all dated items (pyrotechnics, EPIRB/SART batteries, HRUs, liferaft service, immersion suit seam test, SCBA hydro-test, lifejacket lights) in a single expiry table. For upcoming dates (e.g. 3 months in advance), a resupply/service request is raised, so that no item suddenly becomes invalid.
Inventory güncellemesi; kullanılan, boşa: The inventory update brings the count of used, emptied or replaced items up to date and adds missing items to the replenishment list. This list forms the basis for port call and service planning.
Haftalık ve aylık testler, emniyet siste: Weekly and monthly tests are the "pulse" of the safety system: when they are carried out regularly, the equipment is always ready, the records are continuous and inspections pass without problems. The Safety Officer's disciplined test schedule is the strongest guarantee against the surprise of "it didn't work" in a real emergency.
SOLAS III/8 ve III/37, muster list'in yo: SOLAS III/8 and III/37 require the muster list to be prepared before the voyage and posted in conspicuous places on board (bridge, engine control room, crew accommodation). The list clearly shows the details of the general alarm and abandon ship signals, the action each person is to take when the alarm sounds, the muster stations, the persons assigned to close watertight doors, fire doors and valves, and the persons responsible for preparing the survival craft and fire-fighting equipment.
Muster list, kaptanın yokluğunda kimin y: The muster list also defines who takes charge in the Master's absence and the persons responsible for using the LSA and radio equipment. The Safety Officer continuously checks that the list matches the persons actually on board, one for one; at a crew change the list must be updated immediately, otherwise in an emergency some people end up with "no duty" and others with "two duties".
Muster list (genel) ile bireysel station: The muster list (general) and the individual station card (a personal card posted on the cabin door) complement each other. The station card reminds each crew member of their muster station, their abandon ship duty, the equipment they are to carry and which survival craft they are to board. The Safety Officer checks that every cabin has an up-to-date station card.
Görev kartları kişiye özel ve dilden bağ: Duty cards are prepared for each individual and independent of language (supported by symbols); with a multinational crew, the IMO standard symbols (Res. A.760(18)) and the ship's working language are used. When a new crew member joins the ship, the station card is prepared at once and handed over during safety familiarization.
Abandon ship (gemiyi terk) senaryosunda: In an abandon ship scenario, the muster list assigns every duty individually: lifeboat commander (usually an officer), engine operator, painter/line handler, embarkation ladder and davit operator, the person bringing the portable VHF, the person collecting the EPIRB and SART, the person carrying extra blankets, water and rations, the stretcher party, and the person taking the head count. The Safety Officer makes sure that no link in this chain is left empty.
Kritik ekipmanın taşınması isim isim ata: Carrying critical equipment is assigned by name: the person who will take the EPIRB and SART from their brackets, the person who will bring the portable GMDSS VHFs, and the person who will bring extra pyrotechnics, water and rations are known in advance. In a real abandonment, the answer to "Who took the EPIRB?" must already have been given.
Fire senaryosunda muster list; fire part: In a fire scenario, the muster list defines the fire party leader (usually the Chief Officer or the Safety Officer), the nozzle man, the hose handler, the boundary cooling team, the BA (breathing apparatus) team and the engine room boundary cooling coordinator. The bridge control team manages the ventilation, the fuel valves (quick-closing) and the emergency shut-offs.
Flooding/collision senaryosunda watertig: In a flooding/collision scenario, duties are assigned for closing watertight doors, monitoring draft and list, ballast/bilge pumping and preparing damage control materials (cement box, wooden plugs, shoring). The Safety Officer verifies that these duties are rehearsed in drills and that the related equipment is accessible.
MOB senaryosunda muster list; gözcü (kaz: In a MOB scenario, the muster list assigns the lookout (the person who keeps pointing at the person in the water), the person who releases the MOB marker/lifebuoy, the rescue boat crew (boat commander, engine operator, helmsman), the bridge maneuvering team and the person in charge of communications. Having the rescue boat crew designated and trained in advance is decisive in the golden minutes of the rescue.
General emergency alarm, en az yedi kısa: The general emergency alarm is a signal of seven or more short blasts followed by one long blast on the whistle/bell; it must be audible throughout all accommodation and working spaces of the ship. This signal means "go to your muster station"; the order to abandon ship is given by the Master verbally (PA/radio) and has no separate automatic signal.
Safety Officer, general alarm sisteminin: The Safety Officer periodically tests that the general alarm system can be heard at a sufficient decibel level at all points (cabins, corridors, engine room, open deck). In high-noise areas such as the engine room, a visual (flashing) alarm must be provided in addition to the audible alarm.
Acil durumda emir zinciri ve haberleşme: In an emergency, the chain of command and the communication route are defined in advance: the bridge (Master/OOW) is the command center; communication with the muster stations and the fire party is by portable VHF or talkback. The Safety Officer checks that the portable VHFs are charged, set to the correct channels and sufficient in number (at least one per party).
Her muster station; aydınlatmalı, IMO se: Each muster station must be lit, marked with IMO symbols, freely accessible and large enough. On routine safety rounds, the Safety Officer checks that the escape routes to the muster station are not blocked or obstructed, that the emergency lighting and photoluminescent signs work, and that spare lifejackets are kept at the station.
Embarkation deck (binme güvertesi) özel: The embarkation deck is particularly important: the area in front of the lifeboats and liferafts must be clear, the davit area free of stores, the embarkation ladder ready and the deck safe against slipping. Using these areas as storage leads to fatal delays in a real emergency.
Readiness'ın insan ayağı, her mürettebat: The human side of readiness is that every crew member knows their own station and duty. The Safety Officer keeps this knowledge fresh by asking random people during drills and in daily contact: "Where is your muster station, what is your duty, which lifeboat do you board?" For the head count, an up-to-date crew list and passenger list (if any) are kept at each muster station.
Baş sayımı, terk kararında kimsenin geri: The head count is the critical step that ensures nobody is left behind when the decision to abandon is made. The responsible person ticks off everyone at their station on the list and reports anyone missing to the bridge immediately; search and rescue is directed on the basis of this information.
SOLAS, geminin bir çalışma dili (working: SOLAS requires the ship to establish a working language and the muster list and emergency instructions to be written in that language (and in additional languages where necessary). With a multinational crew, the Safety Officer confirms that the instructions are understood by everyone; where necessary, the language barrier is overcome with IMO standard symbols and illustrated instructions.
Familiarization sırasında dilden kaynakl: Misunderstandings caused by language are identified early during familiarization. It is not enough for a crew member to "appear to read" the instructions; real understanding is verified by the crew member physically showing their station.
Yolcu gemilerinde muster organizasyonu,: On passenger ships, the muster organization also covers directing the passengers: a muster drill is held at the start of the voyage, the passenger lifejacket donning points are marked and marshalling personnel are assigned. The Safety Officer checks that the passenger counting system and the plan for passengers with special needs are ready.
SOLAS III/19 gereği abandon ship ve fire: Under SOLAS III/19, abandon ship and fire drills are held at least once a month; each drill tests the muster list under real conditions. During the drill the Safety Officer times the muster, notes people who are left without a duty or are confused, identifies conflicting duties and revises the muster list based on these findings.
Drill, sadece \"yapıldı\" damgası için d: A drill is held not just to get a "done" stamp but to find the weak link in the organization. A department that musters late, equipment that cannot be found or a duty that nobody knows must be caught in a drill and corrected before a real emergency.
Her drill sonrası debrief'te ortaya çıka: Organizational errors revealed in the debrief after each drill are reflected in a revision of the muster list and station cards. The Safety Officer updates all copies at the same time (the list on the notice board, the cabin cards, the bridge and MCR copies); an old version left on display causes confusion.
PSC ve flag/class survey'de denetçi, mus: In PSC inspections and flag/class surveys, the inspector checks that the muster list is up to date, correctly posted and consistent with the crew on board, then goes out on deck and asks a random crew member: "Where is your muster station, what is your duty, how is the rescue boat engine operated?" If the paperwork is perfect but the people do not know, there will be a finding.
En sık deficiency'ler: güncel olmayan mu: The most common deficiencies: an out-of-date muster list (crew who have left the ship still on the list), conflicting or missing duty assignments, instructions not in the working language, crew without a station card, and inconsistencies between the drill records and the muster list. The Safety Officer checks these points proactively.
Muster list'in başarısı, hiçbir acil dur: The success of the muster list stays invisible as long as no emergency occurs. In a real abandonment, fire or MOB, however, the lives of the crew depend on exactly how this list works on deck: on everyone knowing their station and duty by reflex. The paper on the notice board is only the start; being able to say "everyone knows their station, the equipment is being carried, the head count is complete" means the job is done.
STCW Code A-VI/1, gemiye atanan herkesin: STCW Code A-VI/1 requires everyone assigned to a ship to complete basic safety familiarization before taking up duties: mustering in an emergency, recognizing the alarm signals, the location and donning of lifejackets, how to raise the alarm, and knowing the escape routes. This is the maritime world's "life-saving on day one" training.
ISM Code, şirketin personelin görevlerin: The ISM Code requires the Company to ensure that personnel are familiarized so that they can perform their duties safely. The Safety Officer carries out this responsibility on board: meets the new joiner, shows the critical information, confirms that it has been understood and keeps a signed record. The principle is not "I told them" but "I showed them and confirmed it".
Familiarization katmanlıdır: (1) safety/: Familiarization is layered: (1) safety/emergency familiarization (emergencies, LSA, escape), (2) company/SMS familiarization (procedures, reporting), (3) job/role familiarization (the person's own duties). The Safety Officer is primarily responsible for the safety part; the other parts are carried out by the Chief Officer, the Chief Engineer or the relevant supervisor.
Bridge ve engine room watchkeeper'lar iç: For bridge and engine room watchkeepers, duty-specific familiarization (equipment, alarms, procedures) is also carried out as required by STCW. The Safety Officer ensures that the safety part has been completed and recorded; without this record, a new crew member should not be put on watch.
Yeni mürettebata önce hayat kurtaran tem: A new crew member is first shown the life-saving basics: where their own lifejacket is (cabin + spare at the muster station), how to don it (practical demonstration), where the immersion suit is and how to don it, their muster station, their abandon ship duty and which survival craft they will board. This information is reinforced by the station card.
Alarm sinyalleri tanıtılır: general emer: The alarm signals are explained: the general emergency alarm (≥7 short + 1 long), the fire alarm and other signals, and the fact that abandon ship is ordered verbally by the Master. A new crew member must know by reflex where to go and what to do for each signal.
Yeni personele en yakın fire alarm call: New crew members are shown the nearest fire alarm call points (manual push buttons), the locations and types of portable extinguishers, and the locations of the fire hydrants and hoses. It must be clear how they raise the alarm on discovering a fire (call point, telephone, radio) and to whom they report.
Fire door ve watertight door kullanımı g: The use of fire doors and watertight doors is demonstrated: why they are kept closed, how they are opened and closed, and how the automatic closing system works in an emergency. It is stressed that holding a fire door open with a chock/wedge is prohibited and dangerous.
Yeni mürettebata kendi kamarasından ve ç: New crew members are shown the primary and alternative escape routes from their cabin and work area to the muster station by actually walking them. The photoluminescent escape signs, the emergency lighting, the EEBD (Emergency Escape Breathing Device) locations and the engine room escape trunk are pointed out.
EEBD'nin yangın/duman içinde sadece kaçı: It is explained that the EEBD is used in fire/smoke only for escape (not for firefighting), that its typical duration is 10-15 minutes, and how to don it. The Safety Officer repeats the demonstration until sure that the new crew member can find the escape route in darkness or smoke.
Yeni personele fire door (yangın bölmesi: New crew members are taught the difference between a fire door (fire division) and a watertight door (watertight subdivision), the conditions in which they are kept closed and the emergency closing mechanism. They are shown that power-operated watertight doors can be closed remotely from the bridge and that local controls are also provided.
Door'ların yanındaki uyarı levhaları, ka: The warning signs next to the doors, the risk of trapping fingers or limbs while a door is closing, and the correct way to pass through are taught. It is stressed that these doors are critical barriers protecting the integrity of the ship (fire/flooding containment).
Familiarization, kapıların neden önemli: Familiarization makes clear why the doors matter: a closed fire door delays the spread of a fire for minutes, and a closed watertight door can limit flooding to one compartment. When new crew members understand that these barriers protect the ship and themselves, they internalize compliance with the rules.
Yeni personele kim kime rapor verir, aci: New crew members are told clearly who reports to whom, whom to notify in an emergency and what to do when they see a hazardous situation. Typical chain: seaman → bosun/officer → relevant supervisor → Master. The right to report directly to the bridge (OOW) in an emergency is always stressed.
Near-miss ve unsafe condition raporlaman: The "just culture" approach, in which reporting near misses and unsafe conditions is not punished but encouraged, is passed on from the very beginning. New crew members knowing that they can report without fear is the foundation for keeping the safety culture on board alive.
Familiarization, geminin temel emniyet k: Familiarization also covers the ship's basic safety rules: enclosed space entry permit, hot work permit, working aloft/overside, lockout-tagout (LOTO) and PPE requirements. New crew members learn that starting such work without these permits is prohibited.
Her familiarization, şirket SMS'inde tan: Each familiarization is conducted using a checklist defined in the company SMS; each item is ticked off when it has been shown, and at the end both the new crew member and the person giving the familiarization (Safety Officer) sign. The signature is a statement that "it was shown and I understood"; in an ISM audit, this document is evidence of safe operation.
Checklist, gemiye katılım tarihiyle birl: The checklist is kept, together with the date of joining, in the personnel file and the SMS records. The date must show that the person received familiarization before taking up duties or within 24 hours; late or incomplete records generate a PSC/ISM finding.
SOLAS III/19.3.2 gereği, mürettebatın %2: Under SOLAS III/19.3.2, if more than 25% of the crew have not taken part in drills on board in the previous month, a drill is held within 24 hours of the ship leaving port. The Safety Officer makes sure that new crew members take an active role in their first drill; the knowledge taught in familiarization is reinforced by rehearsing a real scenario.
PSC ve ISM denetiminde denetçi, familiar: In PSC and ISM inspections, the inspector asks for the familiarization records and then goes out on deck, asking a new crew member: "Where is your muster station, where is your lifejacket, where is the fire alarm button?" If the records are complete but the person does not know, it is clear that familiarization was done "on paper" and a finding is raised.
En sık deficiency'ler: imzasız/eksik fam: The most common deficiencies: unsigned or incomplete familiarization checklists, late familiarization, inconsistency with the drill records, and new crew members without basic safety knowledge. While making the record, the Safety Officer also ensures that real learning takes place on board.
Safety familiarization, gemiye yeni katı: Safety familiarization is an investment made in the first few hours after a person joins the ship, but its effect lasts throughout the voyage. A well-conducted familiarization turns a person who "does not know the ship" into someone who "knows what to do" in a real emergency. Signing the record is the start; the job is done when the new crew member can don their lifejacket, walk to their station and recognize the alarm.
SOLAS III/19, her mürettebat üyesinin ay: SOLAS III/19 requires every crew member to take part in at least one abandon ship drill and one fire drill every month. If more than 25% of the crew have not taken part in drills on board in the previous month, an abandon ship drill and a fire drill must be held within 24 hours of the ship leaving port. On ships with a high crew turnover, this rule requires the Safety Officer to build the drill plan around the voyage schedule.
Aylık zorunlu abandon ship ve fire drill: In addition to the mandatory monthly abandon ship and fire drills, enclosed space entry & rescue drills (at least once every 2 months, SOLAS III/19.3.3), man overboard (MOB), collision/grounding, oil spill (SOPEP), steering gear failure, blackout, security (ISPS) and medical emergency drills are also held periodically as required by the SMS. The Safety Officer tracks the schedule of all these drills in a single matrix.
Tanker, gas carrier ve yolcu gemilerinde: On tankers, gas carriers and passenger ships, additional drills apply (cargo emergency, enclosed space, mass rescue). The Safety Officer takes the mandatory drills specific to the ship type from the SMS and the additional flag requirements and enters them in the annual plan; a "due date" table is kept so that no interval is missed.
Muster list (toplanma cetveli), her müre: The muster list shows where each crew member is to go and which duty they will take on in an emergency. Under SOLAS III/8 it must be posted in conspicuous places on the bridge, in the engine control room and in the crew accommodation. The general alarm signal, the abandon ship signal, each person's duty and their substitute are shown on the muster list.
Muster list ve emergency instruction'lar: The muster list and emergency instructions must be in a working language understood by the crew; with multinational crews they are supported by IMO standard symbols (Res. A.760(18) / A.1116(30)). Every cabin must have lifejacket donning instructions and directions to the muster station.
İyi bir drill gerçekçi bir senaryoyla ba: A good drill starts with a realistic scenario: "fire in the engine room purifier room", "unconscious person in an enclosed space in No. 2 cargo hold", "MOB from the bridge wing".
