General, vague "there is a fire" scenarios teach nothing. The Safety Officer shares the scenario in advance with the Master and the Chief Officer and sets the intended learning outcome.
Senaryo, her ay farklı olmalıdır; aynı \: The scenario should be different every month; if the same "lower the lifeboat" routine is repeated, the team memorizes it but does not think. Targeting different skills in turn, such as boundary cooling, re-flash watch, enclosed space rescue and casualty handling, makes the team competent across the whole range of emergencies.
Drill öncesi kullanılacak ekipman çalışı: Before the drill, the equipment to be used must be in working order: full SCBA cylinders, fire pump pressure, fire hoses and nozzles, the rescue boat engine, the davit and the release gear. The Safety Officer plans which equipment will actually be operated during the drill; it is made clear whether the drill will be dry (tabletop) or physical.
The drill itself is the biggest accident risk. In accordance with MSC.1/Circ.1206/Rev.1, in lifeboat launching drills the release gear is tested while no personnel are on the hook, and maintenance pins are managed strictly. Weather and sea state, crew fatigue and the maneuvering area are assessed before the drill; if the risk is high, the drill is postponed.
Drill genel alarm (yedi kısa + bir uzun): The drill starts with the general alarm (seven short + one long) or a signal suited to the scenario. The crew come to the muster station with lifejackets/immersion suits; each station leader takes a head count and reports to the bridge. Anyone missing must be identified at once; in a real emergency, the answer to "who is missing?" must be clear within minutes.
Safety Officer veya atanan gözlemci, mus: The Safety Officer or an appointed observer measures the muster time, how well equipment is donned and how the reporting chain works. Typical target: the whole crew mustered and the head count completed within the set time (usually a few minutes, depending on the ship).
Fire drill'de fire party SCBA donar, hos: In a fire drill, the fire party dons SCBA and runs out hoses, boundary cooling is set up, and the machinery stop/ventilation shut-down procedure is applied. In an abandon ship drill, the lifeboat/liferaft station is prepared, embarkation is explained and the engine is started. In an enclosed space drill, the permit to work, atmosphere testing, rescue and casualty handling are demonstrated.
Gözlemci, her adımda \"doğru prosedür iz: At every step, the observer notes whether the correct procedure was followed: was the SCBA pre-use check done, was the buddy system applied, was communication clear, was the equipment used correctly? These notes form the basis of the debrief and the record; simply saying "drill held" is not enough.
Drill bittiğinde mutlaka debrief yapılır: When the drill is over, a debrief is always held: what went well, what went badly, which equipment was missing or defective, which procedure was slow. A debrief is a learning session, not a blame session; the question is not "who made the mistake?" but "where is the system weak?". Every finding is tied to a concrete action.
Safety Officer, debrief'te ortaya çıkan: The Safety Officer turns equipment defects found in the debrief into work orders, procedural gaps into training/familiarization, and individual skill gaps into targeted coaching. The scenario of the next drill can target the weakest point of this drill.
Debrief'te belirlenen aksiyonlar bir tak: Actions identified in the debrief are entered in a follow-up list and tracked until they are closed. Clear assignments are made, such as "Rescue boat battery to be replaced — responsible: 2/E — date X". An action that has not been closed is carried over to the agenda of the next Safety Committee meeting.
Her drill official log book'a ve ayrıca: Every drill is entered in the official log book and also in a detailed drill record. The record includes the date, drill type, scenario, participants, equipment used, observations, deficiencies and corrective actions. Under SOLAS III/19.5, the dates and details of drills are recorded; if a drill is incomplete or shortened, the reason is also recorded.
Safety Officer'ın altın kuralı LSA bölüm: The Safety Officer's golden rule is the same as for LSA: what is not done is not recorded, and what is not recorded is considered not done. However, "filling in" records without holding a real drill (paper drill) is both an ISM violation and a deception that can be fatal in a real emergency. The record must reflect reality.
Drill kaydı ile mürettebatın gerçek bilg: The drill record and the crew's actual knowledge must be consistent. If the record shows a monthly enclosed space drill, a random crew member must be able to explain the permit to work and atmosphere testing. The Safety Officer maintains this consistency by actually holding the drills and ensuring participation by rotation.
Kayıtlar survey ve PSC için kritik delil: Records are critical evidence for surveys and PSC; however, the real aim is not to pass the inspection but to build a team that is ready for a real emergency. A well-kept drill record based on reality gets the ship through both the inspection and a real crisis.
PSC, drill kaydını okumaktan çok crew'ı: PSC tests the crew rather than just reading the drill record: "Where is your muster station? What is your duty in this fire? How do you start the rescue boat engine? How do you use the EEBD?" If the answers are fluent and correct, the drill regime is real; if they are hesitant or wrong, training is inadequate whatever the record says, and a deficiency is raised.
Safety Officer, denetim öncesi müretteba: Before an inspection, the Safety Officer holds short rehearsals with the crew; new joiners in particular are reminded of their muster station, lifejacket donning and their own emergency duties. This prevents the picture of "good records but unprepared people".
Drill'in başarısı, hiçbir gerçek acil ya: The success of drills stays invisible as long as no real emergency occurs. In a real fire or abandonment, however, the crew's reflexes depend on exactly this disciplined, realistic and recorded drill routine. Saying "the drill was held" is the start; being able to say "the team knows, the equipment works, the gaps are closed and the record reflects reality" means the job is done.
Emniyet ekipmanındaki bir kusur gizlendi: When a defect in safety equipment is concealed, the equipment will not work in a real emergency and the result can be fatal. The Third Officer knows that reporting a defect honestly is both a legal and an ethical obligation; hiding a fault "so that it is not seen in the inspection" is the most dangerous decision.
Üçüncü Zabit, rutin rondlarda emniyet ek: On routine rounds, the Third Officer picks up defects in safety equipment: an SCBA low-pressure whistle that does not work, a weak lifeboat battery, a cracked fire hose coupling, a broken EEBD seal, a leaking hydrant valve gland. Each one is opened as a defect.
Kusur, PMS/defect sisteminde açılır: eki: The defect is opened in the PMS/defect system: the equipment, a description of the defect, the date it was found and a risk assessment are recorded. If the equipment cannot be used safely, it is marked "out of service" and physically tagged so that nobody relies on it by mistake.
Bir emniyet ekipmanı devre dışıyken risk: While a piece of safety equipment is out of service, the risk is compensated for: standby equipment is brought into use, an additional watch or precaution is put in place, or operations are restricted. The Third Officer determines this compensating measure and informs the Master; a gap is unacceptable, especially in fire-fighting and life-saving equipment.
Açılan defect, bir iş emrine (work order: The defect that has been opened is linked to a work order and tracked until the repair is complete. When the work is finished, the work order is closed by recording the work done, the parts used and the test result. The Third Officer prevents open safety defects from piling up on the "overdue" list.
PSC/klas denetiminde, açık ve telafi ted: In a PSC/class inspection, an open defect with a compensating measure is received much better than a concealed fault. Transparent defect management shows that the ship's safety culture is healthy. The Third Officer keeps the defect and work order records ready for inspection.
Defect raporlama ve work order takibi, Ü: Defect reporting and work order tracking are how the Third Officer keeps safety equipment actually working, not just working "on paper". Honest reporting, compensating measures and disciplined follow-up ensure that the equipment works the first time in an emergency.
Gemi; klas sörveyleri, bayrak devleti de: The ship is subject to various inspections, such as class surveys, flag State inspections, PSC and vetting. Each examines LSA/FFE compliance to a different depth. The Third Officer ensures that, as far as safety equipment is concerned, the ship is always ready for inspection.
Denetçi tipik olarak: ekipmanın yerini b: The inspector typically expects you to know where the equipment is, to be able to operate it, to show the logbook/records and to know the expiry and service dates, and expects the crew to be trained. The Third Officer keeps these competences ready, both for themselves and for the team.
Bir kusur varsa, açık defect ve telafi t: If there is a defect, showing it as an open defect with a compensating measure is always better than hiding it. When an inspector finds a concealed fault, trust is completely shaken and the ship is examined more closely.
LSA/FFE sertifikaları, liferaft/lifeboat: LSA/FFE certificates, liferaft/lifeboat/fire extinguisher service reports, drill records and the maintenance log are kept ready for inspection. The Third Officer monitors validity periods and plans renewals; an expired service directly produces a finding.
Denetçi, rastgele bir mürettebata \"must: The inspector may ask a random crew member: "Where is your muster station, how do you use this equipment?" Through regular drills and familiarization, the Third Officer ensures that the team can answer these questions with confidence. Safety is the sum of individual competences.
Denetimde bulgu çıkarsa, düzeltici aksiy: If a finding is raised during the inspection, a corrective action plan is prepared and the finding is closed within the deadline. The Third Officer contributes to the follow-up of safety-related findings and supports a permanent solution that prevents the same finding from recurring.
Survey ve PSC hazırlığı, Üçüncü Zabit iç: For the Third Officer, survey and PSC preparation is not an "exam day" but the natural result of everyday safety discipline. Equipment that is always ready, up-to-date records and a trained crew turn the inspection from a threat into a confirmation of the ship's safety.
Süresi dolan bir işaret fişeği tutuşmaya: An expired distress flare may not ignite, a liferaft whose service is overdue may not inflate correctly, and a flat battery may give no signal. This is why tracking dates is about the equipment "being in working order" as much as "being there". The Third Officer treats this tracking as a priority.
Üçüncü Zabit; roket paraşüt fişeği, el m: The Third Officer tracks rocket parachute flares, hand flares, buoyant smoke signals (pyrotechnics), the HRU (Hydrostatic Release Unit), liferaft service dates, EPIRB/SART/portable radio batteries and immersion suit check/seam test dates. Each has a different validity period and service interval.
Yangın söndürücü servis/yeniden dolum, S: Fire extinguisher service/recharging, SCBA cylinder hydrostatic testing, fire hose/nozzle checks and fixed system (CO2/foam) service dates are also tracked. Pressure vessels such as SCBA cylinders are subject to a statutory test interval.
Tüm tarihler bir takvim/PMS sisteminde t: All dates are kept in a calendar/PMS system, and items coming due give an advance warning. The Third Officer identifies renewal/service needs before the port supply window; if a liferaft service or a flare replenishment is not planned at a suitable port, the date may expire at sea.
Süresi yaklaşan ekipman, uygun limanda y: Equipment approaching its expiry date is renewed at a suitable port or sent for service. The Third Officer reports missing or soon-to-expire items to the Chief Officer and the Master and prepares the requisition. Old pyrotechnics are also disposed of in accordance with the rules (usually ashore).
Tüm servis/yenileme işlemleri kayıt altı: All service and renewal work is recorded and the certificates are kept. These records are presented during inspections and prove that the equipment is kept up to date. The Third Officer ensures that the records are orderly and accessible.
Emniyet stok ve tarih takibi, \"küçük am: Tracking safety stock and dates is a typical example of "small but vital" work. The Third Officer's disciplined schedule and timely replenishment ensure that every liferaft, every flare and every battery works the first time in a real emergency.
Safety Officer, emniyet ekipmanını yönet: Because the Safety Officer is the person who manages the safety equipment, they are a natural on-scene leader in an emergency. According to the station bill, they take on roles such as leading the fire team and coordinating life-saving. This is a role that "directs the response", not one that "keeps records".
Yangında Safety Officer; ileri yangın ek: In a fire, the Safety Officer may lead the attack fire team (fire party), directs the team wearing SCBA and coordinates boundary cooling, that is, cooling the adjacent surfaces to prevent the fire from spreading to neighboring compartments. Team safety (air time, withdrawal signal) is the priority.
MOB durumunda Safety Officer, rescue boa: In a MOB situation, the Safety Officer may coordinate the preparation and launching of the rescue boat and directs the rescue team. A fast and organized response is critical because survival time in cold water is limited. MOB equipment (lifebuoy, light, smoke signal) is thrown overboard quickly.
Abandon ship'te Safety Officer; can fili: In abandon ship, the Safety Officer may coordinate boarding of the lifeboats/liferafts (embarkation), the crew head count and the transfer of distress equipment. Making sure that everyone has been counted, so that nobody is left behind, is the most critical part of this role.
Eksik bir sayım, geride kalmış bir müret: An incomplete head count means a crew member left behind. The Safety Officer verifies against the muster list that everyone is present; if anyone is missing, a search is organized. This verification is the most critical step of abandon ship.
Bu rollerin gerçek bir acilde işe yarama: These roles can only work in a real emergency through realistic and regular drills. The Safety Officer plans drills with a wide variety of scenarios and also rehearses their own role; drills held only on paper turn into panic when it really matters.
Safety Officer'ın acil durum rolü, emniy: The Safety Officer's emergency role is a natural extension of managing the safety equipment: being the person who uses that equipment and leads the team in a crisis. Clear awareness of roles, priority on team safety and realistic drills ensure that this critical duty saves lives in a real emergency.
Lookout görevi; çevredeki tüm gemilerin,: The lookout's duty is to watch for all ships, small craft, buoys, coastlines, ice/debris/floating objects, navigation lights and sound signals in the vicinity and to report them to the OOW at once. The AB does not make decisions; they report what they see, and the decision to maneuver belongs to the OOW. This separation is the basic discipline of the watch: the lookout "reports", the officer "interprets and maneuvers".
Helmsman (dümenci) görevinde AB, OOW vey: As helmsman, the AB keeps the ship on the required course by repeating back the course/helm orders given by the OOW or the pilot and carrying them out correctly. Even when the autopilot is engaged, the helmsman stands by so that a change-over to hand steering can be made immediately in narrow waters, traffic separation schemes and maneuvering situations.
Tek kişi aynı anda hem lookout hem helms: One person cannot be lookout and helmsman at the same time; when steering by hand, the person is focused on the helm and the compass, so a "proper look-out" cannot be kept. For this reason, a separate lookout is posted when hand steering is in use. STCW A-VIII/2 and many accident reports stress that the "sole lookout" arrangement is acceptable only in daylight, in good visibility and low traffic, and after the OOW has assessed all factors.
OOW; kısıtlı görüş (sis, yağmur, kar), g: The OOW calls for additional lookouts when factors such as restricted visibility (fog, rain, snow), darkness, heavy traffic, narrow channels/canals, navigation close to the coast, concentrations of fishing boats or fatigue arise. The AB is called to duty with orders such as "stand by the wheel" or "extra lookout on bridge wing".
STCW dinlenme saatleri (her 24 saatte mi: STCW rest hours (min. 10 hours in any 24-hour period, min. 77 hours in any 7-day period) directly affect lookout effectiveness; a tired lookout is a hazard. If the AB feels too tired to perform their duty, they are obliged to inform the OOW.
Etkili lookout, ufku sistematik tarar: b: An effective lookout scans the horizon systematically: starting from the bow, they check both sides and the stern at regular intervals. 360° awareness, not just looking ahead, is essential; overtaking ships in particular approach from astern. Scanning is done both with the naked eye and with binoculars.
Rapor formatı kerteriz (bearing) + cisim: The report format is bearing + object + range/status. The bearing is given as a "clock" bearing (one o'clock, dead ahead) or as "port/starboard ... degrees". Example reports: "Light dead ahead!", "Vessel two points on the starboard bow!", "Object red one-zero!" (port 10°). If a danger is detected, it is reported immediately, loudly and clearly.
Sabit kerteriz / azalan mesafe (constant: A constant bearing with decreasing range (CBDR) is the classic indicator of risk of collision. If, while watching a ship, the AB notices that the bearing is not changing, they must report it; the OOW confirms this information with a radar plot and decides on the maneuver.
Gece lookout'ta karanlığa adaptasyon (da: On a night lookout, dark adaptation takes 20-30 minutes; this is why bridge lighting is dimmed, white light is not used and red lighting is preferred. Even a phone/tablet screen or the glow of a cigarette spoils night vision. The AB picks out faint lights better by looking slightly to one side (off-center vision) rather than directly at the horizon, because the peripheral part of the eye is more sensitive in low light.
Fener tanıma lookout'un en kritik beceri: Recognizing lights is the lookout's most critical skill: green (starboard) and red (port) sidelights, white masthead/stern lights, the all-round white light of a ship at anchor, and the special light combinations for fishing, towing and restricted in ability to maneuver are defined in COLREG Part C. Although the AB does not have to know the meaning of every light by heart, they must describe what they see correctly and clearly (color, number, arrangement) and pass it on to the OOW.
Sis, yoğun yağmur veya kar gibi kısıtlı: In restricted visibility, such as fog, heavy rain or snow, a visual lookout is not enough and the aural lookout comes to the fore. Under COLREG Rule 35, the fog signals of other ships (prolonged blasts, short-short blasts, the bell/gong of a ship at anchor) are listened for. Listening in the open air on the bridge wing, away from engine/generator noise, is more effective.
Kısıtlı görüşte AB, radar/AIS değerlendi: In restricted visibility, the AB knows that radar/AIS assessment is the OOW's job, but keeps up their own aural and limited visual lookout. Every fog signal heard is reported with an estimated bearing ("fog signal, fine on the port bow").
Komut verildiğinde dümenci komutu birebi: When an order is given, the helmsman repeats it exactly (e.g., OOW: "Starboard ten" — Helmsman: "Starboard ten"), applies the helm and reports when the rudder reaches the ordered angle ("Ten of starboard wheel on"). When the ship is to be steadied on a course, the OOW gives the new course ("Steady on one-two-zero"); once the helmsman has the ship steady on that course by the compass, they confirm "Steady on one-two-zero". This discipline prevents misunderstandings caused by noise, accents or fatigue.
Açık denizde otomatik pilot rotayı tutar: On the open sea, the autopilot keeps the course; however, hand steering is engaged for traffic, maneuvering, narrow waters and system failures. The change-over is a procedure: the OOW says "hand steering", the helmsman switches the mode to manual, checks the compass and confirms "hand steering, on course one-two-zero". SOLAS V/24 requires a helmsman to be ready so that hand steering can be engaged immediately in areas where maneuvering is required.
Otomatik pilot devredeyken dümenci dümen: While the autopilot is engaged, the helmsman may leave the helm, but stays in the "stand by the wheel" position if the OOW so orders. In the event of a steering gear failure, an alarm sounds; the helmsman is immediately ready to change over to an alternative steering mode/emergency steering and alerts the OOW.
Dümenci hem gyro repeater hem manyetik p: The helmsman uses both the gyro repeater and the magnetic compass. The gyrocompass gives the true heading; the magnetic compass is critical as a backup (in case of gyro failure). The difference between the gyro and the magnetic compass is checked periodically; if the error increases, the OOW is informed. At the change of watch, the course and the status of the compasses are handed over.
Steering konsolundaki rate-of-turn göste: The rate-of-turn indicator on the steering console shows the ship's rate of turn (°/min); especially on large ships, the helmsman also monitors the turn with this instrument to prevent over-swinging. The rudder angle indicator confirms the rudder angle; agreement between the ordered angle and the angle on the indicator is monitored continuously.
AB, \"ben gördüm ama önemli değildir\" d: The AB does not filter reports by thinking "I've seen it but it's not important"; every object is reported, including small craft, sailing boats, unlit fishing boats and buoys. In many collisions, the lookout had seen a target but did not report it, assuming that "the officer must have seen it already".
Trafik Ayrım Düzenlerinde (TSS), kanalla: In Traffic Separation Schemes (TSS), canals and straits, the lookout workload increases: there are many targets, fast-developing situations and frequent helm orders. In these conditions, the OOW usually calls for hand steering; the helmsman concentrates on the orders while a separate lookout scans the surroundings. In this high-tempo environment, the AB must repeat back orders even more clearly and must not let their attention wander.
Vardiya değişiminde, görevi devralan AB: At the change of watch, the AB taking over comes to the bridge fit for duty (awake, with night vision adapted). The relieving helmsman takes over and confirms the present course, the steering mode (auto/hand), the compass status and the OOW's special instructions. The handover is not carried out while the ship is maneuvering or during a critical passage; it is postponed to a suitable moment.
Devralan lookout; mevcut trafik durumunu: The relieving lookout takes over the current traffic situation, the targets being watched, the weather/visibility conditions and points requiring special attention (e.g., "group of fishing boats on the starboard bow"). STCW A-VIII/2 provides that relieving personnel are not considered fully on duty until their eyes have fully adjusted to the light conditions.
Çok sayıda çarpışma ve karaya oturma rap: A common factor in many collision and grounding reports is "inadequate look-out": the OOW on a one-man watch being busy with radar/ECDIS/paperwork and not looking outside, night vision discipline breaking down, or the lookout not being called to duty. The AB's presence and effective reporting break this chain.
Yorgunluk (fatigue) lookout etkinliğini: Fatigue is the number one factor that reduces lookout effectiveness. Late at night and on long watches, the risk of micro-sleep increases. The AB must report fatigue or the risk of dozing off to the OOW and use strategies to stay alert, such as standing, moving around or stepping out into the fresh air.
Repeat-back yapılmaması, komut yönünün k: Not repeating back, confusing the direction of the order (port/starboard) and believing that the autopilot has been switched to manual (when it is in fact still in automatic mode) are classic helmsman errors. At every change-over, confirming by the rudder angle indicator and the ship's response that the mode really is correct saves lives.
Usta Gemici'nin köprüüstü vardiyasındaki: The AB's value on the bridge watch comes from disciplined lookout and error-free helmsmanship, which stay invisible "when nothing happens" but are the ship's first line of defense "when a target becomes a danger". A correctly reported bearing, a small helm action taken in time, dark adaptation preserved at night: each of these can prevent a collision. Lookout and helmsman duty may look routine, but it is the most basic safety-of-life duty in seafaring.
Standart mooring düzeninde her halatın g: In a standard mooring arrangement, each line has a different function. The head line and stern line bring the ship in to the berth and limit movement fore and aft; breast lines lead at right angles to the berth and stop the ship's side from moving off; spring lines hold the ship against longitudinal (fore-and-aft) movement. A typical ship sends out lines distributed forward and aft in a 3+2+1 or similar combination.
AB, manevra planında kendi istasyonunun: From the Bosun and the station officer, the AB learns which lines their own station (forward/aft) will send out, and in which order, according to the maneuvering plan. Sending a line in the wrong order (e.g., sending the spring late) can make the ship move out of position; this is why the AB waits for the order and never sends lines on their own initiative.
Halatlar bollard'a (rıhtım babası) \"eye: Lines are put over the shore bollard by the eye; if there are lines from more than one ship on the same bollard, the "dip the eye" technique is used: the eye of the ship arriving later is passed up through the eye of the earlier ship's line from below, so that each ship can let go its own line independently.
Mesafe ve durum köprüüstüne sürekli rapo: Distance and status are reported to the bridge continuously: "Two shackles to go", "All gone forward" (all lines forward have been let go), "Made fast forward" (the forward station is made fast). Without this feedback the bridge carries out the maneuver blind; clear and timely reporting by the AB is the eyes of the maneuver.
Gerilim altındaki bir halat veya tel kop: When a line or wire under tension parts, it releases its stored elastic energy by recoiling like a whip; the area swept by this recoil is called the snap-back zone. Synthetic lines (especially nylon) recoil far more dangerously because of their high elasticity; in less than a second, the parted end moves fast enough to tear a human body apart. This is why most mooring injuries are fatal or involve the loss of limbs.
Snap-back bölgesi sadece halatın doğrult: The snap-back zone is not only along the lead of the line: at every point where the line is bent around a bollard, fairlead or pedestal roller, the direction of recoil can change. MEG4 takes the approach that "the whole deck is a potential snap-back zone when lines are under tension"; the old "painted snap-back zone line" alone is not considered safe.
AB, halat alırken/verirken ayağını asla: When taking in or paying out a line, the AB never puts a foot inside a coil of line or on top of a line running underneath; if the line suddenly comes under tension, the foot is caught and the person is dragged. Hands are kept away from the turns on the bollard, the mouth of the fairlead and the winch drum; "nip points" are the main cause of lost fingers and hands.
Çalışma alanında daima açık bir kaçış yo: An open escape route is always planned in the work area; where to jump clear when the line comes under tension is known in advance. A crowded, slippery or obstructed deck makes escaping snap-back impossible; this is why the deck preparation described in 3.1 is critical.
İşe başlamadan toolbox talk / risk asses: Before starting work, a toolbox talk / risk assessment is held: which lines will go out in which order, the snap-back zones, wind/current conditions and the allocation of duties are discussed. The AB knows their own role and the "stop" signal clearly; if anything is unclear, they ask.
Mooring istasyonunda zorunlu PPE: baret,: Mandatory PPE at the mooring station: safety helmet, steel-toe safety shoes, mooring gloves (a type that gives grip but will not get caught in a roller), coveralls and, for night operations, a reflective vest. The choice of gloves is important; loose or torn gloves increase the risk of being caught by the drum.
Gece veya kötü görüş koşulunda istasyon: At night or in poor visibility, station lighting must be adequate but directed so that it does not spoil the view from the bridge. The AB keeps their radio and whistle at hand; hand signals can also be used in a noisy environment.
Brake (fren) ayarı kritiktir: MEG4'e gör: The brake setting is critical: according to MEG4, the winch brake is set to "render" (slip, relieving the tension) at a specified percentage of the line's MBL (Minimum Breaking Load), so that under excessive tension the brake slips before the line parts. The AB carries out the brake holding (rendering) test and applies the correct brake pressure on the Bosun's instructions.
AB, winch panelindeki mod (manuel/auto),: The AB knows the mode (manual/auto) on the winch panel, the selection between drum and warp end (warping head), and the emergency stop button. Work is not done on the warp end at the same time as a line is on the drum; mechanical confusion is dangerous.
Mooring halatı doğrudan rıhtıma uzanamay: Because the mooring line is too heavy to reach the berth directly, a light heaving line is thrown first; the weight at its end (monkey's fist) carries it ashore, and the mooring gang ashore hauls in this line to bring the eye of the main line onto the berth. The AB coils the heaving line neatly, takes half of it in the throwing hand, aims according to the target and the wind, and throws.
Monkey's fist içine asla metal/ağır cisi: Metal or heavy objects are never put inside the monkey's fist; this can seriously injure the person ashore. MEG4 and COSWP require the weight of a heaving line to be soft and of limited mass. Warning the people on the quay when throwing ("heads up — line coming over") is good practice.
AB, \"make fast\" komutunda halatı doğru: On the order "make fast", the AB makes the line fast at the correct tension; on the order "single up", before departure, the surplus lines are let go one by one to reduce them to the minimum. While letting go, the AB keeps checking which line is under tension; a line under tension is never cast off by hand: the tension is first taken off with the winch.
Yanaşma/kalkmada römorkörler gemiye iter: When berthing and unberthing, tugs push or pull the ship. When making fast a tug, the tug line sent by the tug with a messenger (light line) is usually taken on board and made fast on a suitable bollard or tug bitt, through a Panama lead. When taking the tug line, the AB learns from the Bosun which fairlead the line will pass through and which bollard it will be made fast on; a wrong lead chafes the line against the ship's structure and cuts it.
Tug operasyonu sırasında gemi ile römork: During tug operations, the line between the ship and the tug can come under sudden tension; this is also a source of snap-back. The AB keeps clear of the lead of the tug line and allows for the tug's pulling direction ("ahead/astern"). Coordination between the bridge and the tug is carried out by the pilot/Master; on deck, the AB is responsible for making fast and letting go safely.
Manevra bitince tug çözülür. Gergin tug: When the maneuver is completed, the tug is let go. A tug line under tension is never cast off by hand; the bridge passes "ease the line" to the tug, and once the tension is off, the AB lets go the line under control and returns it to the tug. If a quick-release arrangement is fitted, the AB knows how to use it and in which situations it is to be used.
Windlass çalışırken AB, zincir hareketin: While the windlass is running, the AB stands clear of the moving cable and the gypsy (cable lifter) area; a parting cable, or being caught by the cable, is fatal. Goggles and ear protection are recommended against the dust, sparks and noise generated when the anchor is let go. The ship should not lie at anchor for long without the bow stopper; the whole load must not be left on the windlass brake alone.
Mooring güvenliği büyük ölçüde ekipman d: Mooring safety depends to a large extent on the condition of the equipment. The AB regularly checks lines for wear, cuts, glazing (shine caused by heat) and internal fiber damage, and wires for broken wires, birdcaging, rust and loosening. Damaged lines/wires are reported and taken out of service; the "it will hold a bit longer" mindset produces snap-back accidents.
MEG4, halatların bir Line Management Pla: MEG4 recommends that lines be tracked with a Line Management Plan (retirement criteria, usage records). The AB helps to record at which station and for how long each line has been used; periodically turning the lines end-for-end evens out the wear.
Fairlead ve roller'lar serbest dönmeli;: Fairleads and rollers must turn freely; a seized roller chafes and cuts the line. Stoppers (chain/rope stoppers), bollard welds and Panama leads are checked for cracks and wear. The winch brake is tested periodically, and greasing is carried out according to the greasing schedule. This maintenance is closely linked with the deck maintenance covered under duty no. 3.
Mooring ölümlerinin büyük kısmı, AB'nin: Most mooring deaths result from an AB standing in the recoil zone of a line under tension. In some cases, the person started in the right area, but the direction of recoil changed because the line was bent around a fairlead. Lesson: do not rely on a single "safe line"; treat the whole deck as dangerous while lines are under tension and keep the escape route clear.
Diğer sık hata, çalışma alanının dağınık: Another common error is an untidy or slippery work area that makes escape impossible. Coils of line laid out underfoot, pools of oil or water and an overcrowded station make an accident worse.
Bağlama ve manevra, Usta Gemici'nin en g: Mooring and maneuvering is the AB's most visible but most dangerous duty. A line sent out in the right order, a correctly set winch brake and a disciplined seaman standing outside the recoil zone: each of these saves a limb, a life. Mooring is routine, but carelessness within the routine is fatal; the AB must take every maneuver as seriously as on the first day.
Demirde veya rıhtımda gemi \"park edilmi: At anchor or alongside, the ship may look "parked", but the anchor may drag, a line may part or the surrounding conditions may change suddenly. An anchor/mooring watch is an active watch kept to catch these silent dangers early. The AB knows how serious this watch is.
Usta gemici belirli aralıklarla pozisyon: At set intervals, the AB checks the position (bridge display/transits/landmarks), the weather and sea state, the surrounding traffic and the tension/lead of the anchor cable, and reports to the bridge. Any abnormality (position shifting, sudden jerking of the cable, an approaching ship) is reported immediately.
Demir tarama belirtileri; pozisyonun rüz: Signs of a dragging anchor are the position starting to shift in the direction of the wind/current, the cable alternately coming taut for long periods and then slackening (jerking), and the ship swinging differently from what is expected. The AB recognizes these signs and informs the bridge immediately; delay has irreversible consequences.
Limanda bağlı iken usta gemici halatları: When moored in port, the AB monitors the tension of the lines; the tide and swell can over-tension the lines or let them go slack. Over-tensioned lines are eased/adjusted safely, staying clear of the snap-back zone. Slack lines can allow the ship to move off the berth.
Mooring watch sırasında gangway güvenliğ: During the mooring watch, gangway safety, unauthorized access and the condition of the quay and surroundings are also watched. The AB reports any abnormal situation (chafed line, fire, leak, unauthorized person) to the bridge.
Halat ayarlarken usta gemici gergin hat: When adjusting lines, the AB does not stand on or in front of a taut line; they position themselves clear of the snap-back zone, at a point with an escape route. PPE is worn and care is taken against sudden changes in tension. Rushing with a line under tension can lead to a fatal accident.
Usta gemici, düzenli kontrollerini ve he: The AB reports their regular checks and every abnormality clearly to the bridge. In an emergency (dragging, a parted line, fire, an approaching danger), they raise the alarm. Accurate and timely reporting determines the whole value of the watch.
Anchor ve mooring watch, geminin hareket: Anchor and mooring watches are the guardians of safety during the hours when the ship appears motionless but the danger persists. The AB's regular checks, early detection of signs of dragging and snap-back awareness keep the ship safe at anchor and alongside.
Çelik gemi, tuzlu su, nem, güneş ve meka: A steel ship is under constant attack from salt water, humidity, sun and mechanical wear. Corrosion is not just a cosmetic problem but a safety issue that threatens structural integrity; thinning plates, cracked welds and corroded deck equipment put cargo safety and the safety of life at risk. This is why surface protection (the paint system) and regular maintenance directly affect the ship's class certificate and PSC (port State control) compliance.
Boya sistemi bir kalkandır: önce yüzey h: The paint system is a shield: first the surface is prepared, then the primer, intermediate coat and top coat are applied. When one of these layers breaks down, corrosion advances silently underneath. The AB's job is to keep this shield intact: removing rust early and restoring protection with the right paint.
Reis, hava durumu, liman programı ve mev: The Bosun allocates the daily jobs according to the weather, the port schedule and the current state of corrosion: one group chips on the forecastle while another washes the deck and another greases wire ropes. The AB knows their own job but must also understand the maintenance logic of the whole deck; for example, no painting is done when rain is expected, and nobody walks on fresh paint.
AB, çalışırken fark ettiği kusurları (ça: The AB reports defects noticed while working (cracks, heavy corrosion, loose connections, damaged equipment) to the Bosun. This feedback feeds the PMS; catching a small rust spot before it turns into major plate thinning depends on this reporting.
İyi boyanın sırrı yüzeyde gizlidir: pas,: The secret of a good paint job lies in the surface: paint applied before rust, old loose paint, oil and salt have been removed completely will soon flake off. Chipping is done with a hand hammer/scraper or a pneumatic needle gun; loose rust and blistered paint are removed from the surface. The surface is then roughened and cleaned with a wire brush or a disc grinder (grinding).
Pnömatik ve elektrikli aletler (needle g: Pneumatic and electric tools (needle gun, disc grinder, sandblasting) produce high noise, vibration and flying particles. The AB carries out the pre-use check of the tool (air hose, disc condition, guard), wears the correct PPE and isolates the work area from its surroundings. Disc grinding produces sparks; keep away from flammable materials and paint thinner.
Mekanik temizlik tek başına yetmez; tuz: Mechanical cleaning alone is not enough; salt deposits draw moisture under the paint and cause early breakdown. This is why the prepared surface is washed with fresh water to remove the salt and then left until completely dry. Oil/grease stains are removed with a suitable solvent or detergent; otherwise the paint will not adhere.
Nem ve sıcaklık boyanın yapışmasını doğr: Humidity and temperature directly affect paint adhesion. Painting just above or below the dew point traps moisture on the surface; this is why the Bosun usually does not paint in the morning before the dew has lifted or in the evening once the moisture settles. The AB does not start painting without asking: "Is the surface really dry and clean?"
Boya sistemi katmanlıdır: astar (primer): The paint system is layered: the primer adheres to the steel and forms the first barrier against corrosion; the intermediate coat provides thickness and barrier; the top coat gives UV, abrasion and cosmetic protection. For each coat, the thickness, drying time and overcoating interval given in the manufacturer's technical data sheet (TDS) are followed. Applying the next coat too early spoils the coat underneath.
Uygulama yöntemi fırça, rulo veya airles: The application method may be brush, roller or airless spray. Brushes are used for corners, welds and tight areas, rollers for wide flat surfaces, and spray for large areas and fast application. Spraying carries the risk of overspray and solvent vapor; the wind direction is taken into account and surrounding equipment is protected.
Boya, üreticinin belirttiği sıcaklık ve: Paint is applied within the temperature and humidity range specified by the manufacturer. In very cold weather, drying takes longer and adhesion is poor; in very hot weather, the solvent evaporates too early and the film does not form properly. No painting is done in rain, sea spray or high humidity. During application, the AB keeps the film thickness even by eye, taking care not to leave sags, pinholes or missed spots.
Taze boyalı alan \"WET PAINT\" işareti v: A freshly painted area is protected with a "WET PAINT" sign and a barrier; nobody steps on it and no equipment is placed on it until it is dry. If the overcoating interval is not observed, solvent entrapment and film breakdown occur. Quality work means correct thickness + clean surface + suitable weather + correct waiting time.
Halatın doğru sarılması ve istifi de bak: Correct coiling and stowage of ropes are also part of maintenance; a kinked rope wears quickly and creates a hazard during operations. The AB coils ropes neatly in a figure-of-eight or another suitable coil and stores them where air can circulate.
Çelik tel halatlar (kreyn, vinç, mooring: Steel wire ropes (crane, winch and mooring wires) are greased against corrosion and internal friction; the grease both prevents external corrosion and reduces friction between the wires. Before greasing, the wire is cleaned and inspected for damage (broken wires/birdcaging/crushing). If the limit for the number of broken wires is exceeded, the wire rope is replaced.
Greasing kirli ve kaygan bir iştir; AB e: Greasing is dirty and slippery work; the AB wears gloves, takes care not to slip and does not let grease residue get onto the deck or into the sea. Waste grease and dirty rags are collected as appropriate waste under MARPOL Annex V and are not thrown overboard.
Deniz suyu serpintisi güvertede ve ekipm: Sea spray deposits salt on the deck and equipment; this salt accelerates corrosion and damages paint. Regular fresh water washing removes these deposits. Because washing makes surfaces more slippery, it requires careful walking and suitable footwear; hose pressure and slippery surfaces carry a risk of injury.
Yıkama suyunun ve temizlik kimyasalının: Discharge of wash water and cleaning chemicals into the sea is subject to MARPOL rules; deck water containing oil is not discharged directly overboard, the scuppers (deck drains) are plugged when necessary and the waste is collected appropriately.
Yağ çözücü, pas sökücü, deterjan gibi ki: Chemicals such as degreasers, rust removers and detergents are used in accordance with the Safety Data Sheet (SDS): the rules on correct PPE, ventilation, preventing skin/eye contact and not mixing incompatible chemicals apply. The AB must know the SDS of every chemical they use and must not put chemicals in unlabeled containers.
Her bakım işi öncesi, ekip kısa bir tool: Before each maintenance job, the team holds a short toolbox talk: the steps of the job, the hazards (falls from height, sparks, chemicals, enclosed spaces, slippery surfaces), the control measures and what to do in an emergency are discussed. If the risk is high (work at height, overside work, enclosed space, hot work), a Permit to Work is also issued.
AB, kendi işinin risk değerlendirmesini: The AB does not start a job without understanding its risk assessment and applying the control measures. When a step changes (the weather deteriorates, equipment fails), the job is stopped and the situation is reassessed. "Stop work authority", the authority to stop any job they consider unsafe, is every seafarer's right.
PPE işe göre seçilir: chipping/grinding': PPE is selected according to the job: eye/face protection and a dust mask for chipping/grinding; ear protection for noisy pneumatic tools; suitable gloves and goggles for chemical work; a solvent mask for painting; a safety harness for work at height. A safety helmet, steel-toe shoes and coveralls are the basic outfit on deck.
PPE, doğru takıldığında ve sağlam olduğu: PPE protects only when it is worn correctly and is in good condition. The AB checks their PPE before use (cracked goggles, a worn harness or a clogged filter are not used) and replaces anything damaged. PPE is not an excuse but the last line of defense; the job is first planned to be safe, and PPE is the final layer.
Sık görülen kalite hataları: paslı/ıslak: Common quality errors: painting over rusty, wet or salty surfaces, not observing the overcoating interval, painting in the wrong weather conditions and insufficient film thickness. These cause the paint to flake off within months and corrosion to advance unseen; the job has to be redone from the start, wasting both time and material.
Emniyet hataları daha ağır sonuç doğurur: Safety errors have more serious consequences: skipping PPE (eye, hand and respiratory injuries), doing spark-producing work near flammables, using paint or solvent in an enclosed space without ventilation, and moving carelessly on a slippery wet deck. Each of these is the first link in a serious accident chain.
Disiplinli bir AB; yüzeyi hak ettiği gib: A disciplined AB prepares the surface properly, paints in the right weather with the right coats, wears full PPE, uses chemicals according to the SDS and collects waste in accordance with MARPOL. This way of working keeps the ship's defense against corrosion strong and protects the safety of the AB and the team. Maintenance is valuable not because it is "visible" but because it "extends the ship's life and ensures safety".
Güverte bakımı, denizciliğin \"görünmeye: Deck maintenance is the "unseen heroism" of seafaring: when it is done well, nobody notices, because the ship stays sound, clean and safe; when it is neglected, it comes back as corrosion, accidents and PSC detentions. The hammer, brush and grease gun in the AB's hands are really tools that extend the ship's life and protect the crew. Quality, safe maintenance is possible with patience, the right sequence and disciplined PPE and risk management.
Her yük operasyonu öncesi tool-box talk: Before every cargo operation, a toolbox talk (on-site briefing) is held; the deck officer explains the cargo plan, the sequence, the holds to be opened, the lashing requirements and the hazards. In this briefing, the AB learns clearly their own duty, the equipment to be used and what to do in an emergency. Operations do not start without a briefing.
Görev dağılımında winch/vinç operatörü,: In the allocation of duties, the persons who will operate the winch/crane, operate the hatch cover controls, carry out lashing and handle communications are designated. The AB usually takes on more than one role; however, conflicting duties, such as operating machinery controls and working under a load at the same time, are not given. Communication is maintained by hand-held radio or hand signals.
AB; baret, çelik burunlu bot, eldiven, k: The AB uses a safety helmet, steel-toe boots, gloves, safety goggles and, depending on the task, a high-visibility vest. A dust mask is added for dusty cargoes such as grain or ore, and ear protection in noisy environments. For dangerous cargoes (IMDG/IMSBC classified), additional precautions and special PPE apply; the AB learns these from the Bosun.
İşe başlamadan önce risk değerlendirmesi: Before starting work, the risk assessment is reviewed: falls, crushing, trapping, slipping, parting of equipment under tension and atmosphere risks are assessed. If anyone is to go down into a hold, atmosphere testing and the enclosed space procedure also apply; the AB does not enter a hold or tank without permission.
Modern kuru yük gemilerinde folding (kat: Folding, side-rolling and pontoon (lift-off) type hatch covers are common on modern dry cargo ships. Each type has its own hydraulic/mechanical controls and safety pin system. Before a cover is opened, the AB confirms that the cleats, wedges and safety locks have all been removed; otherwise the hydraulics are overstressed and damage or collision results.
Açma/kapama sırasında kapağın hareket yo: During opening and closing, the path of travel of the cover is cleared; nobody stands under the cover or in its path. On side-rolling covers there must be no chocks or obstructions on the rails, and on pontoon covers the crane/forklift operation must be coordinated. While the cover is moving, the AB acts as lookout, watching for hazards, and if necessary stops the operator with "stop".
Hatch cover'ın su geçirmezliği, geminin: The weathertightness of the hatch covers is a basic element of the ship's seaworthiness; water entering the hold damages the cargo and endangers stability. After closing, the AB checks that the rubber packing, drain channels, compression bars and cleats are correctly seated. Old or crushed rubber, rusty compression bars and clogged drains cause leaks.
Su geçirmezlik kontrolünde tebeşir testi: For the weathertightness check, a chalk test, hose test or ultrasonic test is used; the AB assists with these tests and keeps the rubber and bar surfaces clean. Any defects found are reported to the Bosun/officer and recorded.
Lashing'te lashing rod, turnbuckle (germ: Lashing uses lashing rods, turnbuckles, chains, lashing belts/webbing, shackles, twistlocks and cones (on containers). The AB secures the cargo without exceeding the MSL (Maximum Securing Load) and SWL (Safe Working Load) of the equipment, at the correct angle and symmetrically. Worn, cracked or deformed equipment is not used; it is removed.
Doğru lashing açısı kritiktir: çok dik v: The correct lashing angle is critical: lashings that are too steep or too flat reduce the effectiveness of the equipment. Because turnbuckles can slacken as the cargo settles, they are re-tightened at the start of the voyage and as necessary (re-lashing). During the voyage, the AB checks the lashings according to the Bosun's schedule and tightens any that have slackened.
Her gemi, bayrak devleti/klas onaylı bir: Every ship carries a Cargo Securing Manual approved by the flag State/class; this manual specifies how each cargo is to be secured and with how many lashings. The AB works to this approved plan, not to personal habit. For non-standard or heavy/high cargoes, the officer issues a special lashing plan.
Açık güvertede taşınan yükler (konteyner: Cargo carried on the open deck (containers, timber, pipes, project cargo) is exposed to the high accelerations of the ship's motions at sea (rolling/pitching); it therefore requires extra lashing and regular checks. When bad weather is expected, the Bosun plans an additional lashing round; the AB carries out this round under safe conditions (if going out on deck is risky, only on the officer's decision).
Yeni yük öncesi ambar; önceki yük artıkl: Before a new cargo, the hold is cleaned of residues of the previous cargo, rust, water, oil and bad odors. The cleaning standard depends on the cargo: grain/food cargoes require "grain clean" or "hospital clean", whereas scrap metal can be loaded to a lower standard. The AB learns the required cleanliness level from the Bosun and sweeps, washes and dries accordingly.
Temizlik sonrası ambar kuru ve kokusuz o: After cleaning, the hold must be dry and odor-free; the bilge wells are cleaned, the strum boxes are checked and the bilge pumping is verified to work. Protrusions, sharp surfaces and remains of earlier lashings that could damage the cargo are removed. Any structural damage found (holes, dents, corroded areas) is reported to the officer.
Bazı yüklerde \"kargo terlemesi\" (cargo: With some cargoes, "cargo sweat" and "ship sweat" cause moisture damage; hold ventilation is opened or closed according to the dew point difference. This decision is the officer's; the AB carries out the physical work, such as opening/closing ventilator flaps and running the ventilation fans, and helps with the records.
Draft survey ve yükleme/boşaltma kontrol: For draft surveys and loading/discharging checks, the forward, aft and midship draft marks are read. The AB reads the draft marks at the mean water level between waves and surges, from a boat or the pilot ladder if possible, in a safe position. Readings are taken in meters (m) or feet, according to the arrangement of the marks.
Trim (baş-kıç farkı) ve list (yatıklık): Trim (the difference between the forward and aft drafts) and list are determined from the draft differences; during loading, the drafts are monitored until the required trim is achieved. The AB reports readings clearly and accurately, giving the actual reading and not an estimate, because a poor reading leads to a wrong cargo quantity calculation and stability errors.
Sounding, tank içindeki sıvı yüksekliğin: Sounding measures the height of liquid in a tank (ballast, fuel, fresh water); ullage measures the empty space from the tank top to the liquid surface (common on tankers). The AB takes measurements with a sounding tape (measuring tape + weight) or an electronic gauge, checks the water/fuel interface with "water finding paste" and records the value.
Sounding sırasında tank kapağı/ölçüm boş: When a tank cover or sounding pipe is opened for sounding, there is a risk of flash/gas (especially with fuel and on tankers) and of falling; the AB follows the rules on earthing, anti-static measures and PPE. The measured values are passed to the officer and confirm the accuracy of bilge/ballast operations. A wrong sounding can lead to an overflow or pollution.
Güverte üstünde taşınan konteyner, keres: Containers, timber, pipes, machinery or project cargo carried on deck are tested by the ship's motions, green water and wind loads. At intervals set by the Bosun, the AB makes a lashing round, tightens slack turnbuckles and reports any signs of damage or shifting. In bad weather, if going out on deck is risky, the check is made on the officer's decision, with safety of life as the priority.
Yükün gemi yapısına (deck fitting, lashi: The loads that the cargo imposes on the ship's structure (deck fittings, lashing points) are monitored; points of excessive stress, cracked welds or deformed fittings are reported. Deck cargo must also not block escape routes, bilge channels or access to safety equipment.
Sık görülen hatalar: cleat/wedge sökülme: Common errors: forcing a cover open without removing the cleats/wedges (hydraulic damage), insufficient or asymmetric lashing, not re-lashing during the voyage, and slack turnbuckles. These errors result in loss of cargo, damage to the ship and detention by port State control (PSC).
Konteyner gemilerinde twist-lock'un tam: On container ships, failing to notice that a twistlock was not fully locked has led to container stacks collapsing in bad weather. The AB must physically confirm that every twistlock has engaged and avoid the assumption that "it is probably locked".
Yanlış draft okuması yük miktarı uyuşmaz: A wrong draft reading leads to cargo quantity discrepancies (cargo claims) and stability errors; inadequate hold cleaning leads to cargo contamination and rejection. The AB must report readings honestly and accurately and fully meet the cleaning standard required for the cargo. "Approximate" readings and the assumption that a hold is "clean enough" have expensive consequences.
Yük operasyonlarına destek, AB'nin deniz: Supporting cargo operations is where the AB's seamanship is seen most concretely: a lashing applied at the correct angle, a properly sealed hatch cover, an honestly read draft and a hold cleaned to the required standard ensure that the cargo arrives in port in good condition, the ship remains stable and the crew stay safe. In this work, haste and assumptions are expensive; discipline, checks and honest reporting protect both the cargo and the ship.
Muster List, SOLAS III/8 gereği gemide g: Under SOLAS III/8, the muster list is posted in conspicuous places on board (bridge, engine room, corridors, cabins) and shows who does what for each type of emergency (general emergency, fire, abandon ship, man overboard, pollution). From the card on their cabin door and at the muster station, the AB learns their duty, team and muster station.
Genel acil durum sinyali yedi veya daha: The general emergency signal is given by seven or more short blasts followed by one long blast on the whistle (and the same pattern on the electric bell); the order to abandon ship is given by the Master verbally/over the PA, and the signal itself is not an order to abandon ship. The AB must be able to tell these signals apart by heart and, on hearing the signal, immediately take their lifejacket and go quickly to the muster station.
Sinyali duyan AB önce kendi can güvenliğ: An AB who hears the signal first ensures their own safety (lifejacket, suitable clothing, head covering), then goes to the assigned muster station. Any fire or injured person seen on the way is reported at the muster. The principle is quick, orderly movement in accordance with the procedure, not panic.
SOLAS III/19.3.2, gemiyi terk (abandon s: SOLAS III/19.3.2 requires every crew member to take part in abandon ship and fire drills at least once a month; if more than 25% of the crew have not taken part in drills on board in the previous month, a drill is held within 24 hours of the ship leaving port. Enclosed space entry and rescue drills are held at least once every two months (III/19.3.3) and security (ISPS) drills at least once every three months; man overboard and pollution scenarios are planned according to the company SMS.
Tatbikat gerçek gibi yürütülür: alarm ve: The drill is conducted as if it were real: the alarm is raised, the crew muster, a head count by name is taken and the teams actually carry out their duties (preparing to lower the lifeboat, running out fire hoses, boundary cooling). The AB does not see the drill as "a waste of time"; this is where they acquire the reflexes that will save lives in a real emergency.
Her tatbikat sonrası debrief (değerlendi: After each drill, a debrief is held; points that fell short, late mustering, equipment failures and proposals for improvement are discussed and recorded. The AB reports any problem noticed during the drill (e.g., a blocked escape route, a light that does not work). These records are audited under the ISM Code.
Can yeleği (lifejacket) doğru giyilmeli,: The lifejacket must be donned correctly, with the straps tightened, and its light and whistle must work. The AB must know the lifejacket well enough to don it correctly even with eyes closed; a lifejacket worn incorrectly can turn the wearer face down in the water. On inflatable lifejackets, the automatic/manual inflation mechanism and the CO₂ cartridge are checked.
Soğuk sularda dalış elbisesi (immersion: In cold water, the immersion suit extends survival time by delaying hypothermia; SOLAS requires an immersion suit for every crew member under certain conditions. The AB must be able to don the suit quickly (usually with a target of 1-2 minutes) and check that the zipper and face seal are watertight. Donning time is measured during drills.
Can salı (liferaft) genelde hidrostatik: The liferaft is normally released automatically by the hydrostatic release unit (HRU) and inflates as the ship sinks; the AB must know manual launching (throwing overboard and pulling the painter) and how the HRU works. The lifeboat is lowered by davits; during drills the AB learns about the davit brake, the falls, the embarkation ladder and starting the engine.
Davit-launched ve free-fall filikalarda: On davit-launched and free-fall lifeboats, releasing the safety pins, gripes and brakes in the correct order is critical; the wrong order causes premature release accidents. If the AB is in the lifeboat crew, they must clearly know their own duty (painter, brake, helm, engine) and follow the chain of command.
Yangın drill'inde AB genelde yangın part: In a fire drill, the AB usually serves in the fire party or the support team: duties such as running out the fire hose, holding the nozzle, handling the branch pipe or boundary cooling (cooling the surfaces adjacent to the compartment on fire) are assigned. Boundary cooling prevents the fire from spreading to adjacent spaces and lowers the temperature.
AB, yangın ekipmanının (hortum, nozzle,: The AB must know the location and use of the fire equipment (hoses, nozzles, foam, portable extinguishers) and must select the extinguisher suited to the type of fire (spraying water on an oil or electrical fire is dangerous). The AB follows the chain of command (the fire team leader) and does not attempt heroics alone; a coordinated response as a team is essential.
Yangın/duman ortamına giriş yapacak ekip: The team that will enter a fire or smoke-filled area wears SCBA (Self-Contained Breathing Apparatus, supplied by compressed-air cylinders); if trained, the AB knows how to don the SCBA, check the cylinder pressure and manage the working time. SCBA allows the fire party to make a protected entry; when the low-pressure alarm sounds, the wearer withdraws immediately.
EEBD (Emergency Escape Breathing Device): The EEBD (Emergency Escape Breathing Device) is intended for escape, not for fighting fire or smoke; it is single-use, supplies air for a short time (usually ~10-15 min) and is used to escape from a smoke-filled area. The AB knows where the EEBD is, how to put it on quickly (hood type) and that it is for escape only (NOT for firefighting).
AB, çalıştığı ve yaşadığı tüm bölgelerde: The AB must know at least two escape routes from every area where they work and live, the emergency exit doors, the escape lighting (low-location lighting) and the locations of EEBDs and fire equipment. Escape routes are always kept open, unobstructed and marked; blocking an escape route with stores or cargo is prohibited, and an AB who sees this clears it and reports it.
Duman içinde görüş sıfıra iner; AB karan: In smoke, visibility drops to zero; the AB must know how to get through a dark, smoke-filled corridor by following the wall by hand, keeping low and following the escape lighting. In drills, the escape routes are learned by physically walking them; in a real emergency, memory and reflexes show the way.
Muster station'da isim sayımı (head coun: The head count (roll call) at the muster station is a critical stage; if anyone is missing, a search team is sent. The AB reports their own presence and, if assigned to communications, maintains the flow of information between the bridge and the muster station by radio/PA. A wrong count leads to someone left inside being overlooked.
LSA ve yangın ekipmanı haftalık/aylık/yı: LSA and fire-fighting equipment are checked at weekly, monthly and annual intervals; the AB assists with these checks. Weekly, the lifeboat engine is run and the alarms are tested; monthly, a visual check of the LSA and fire extinguishers is made. Annual and five-yearly services are carried out by an authorized company (renewal of lifeboat falls, liferaft service, SCBA hydrostatic test).
AB; can simidi, can yeleği ışıkları, pyr: The AB checks lifebuoys, lifejacket lights, pyrotechnic (distress flare) expiry dates, the condition of hoses and nozzles, and the emergency lighting, and reports anything missing. Expired pyrotechnics and lights with flat batteries are useless when it really matters; maintenance saves lives.
AB, kontrol sırasında bulduğu her eksik/: The AB immediately reports every deficiency or fault found during checks (an empty extinguisher, a light that does not work, a leaking SCBA, a missing lifejacket) to the Bosun/Safety Officer. A "we'll deal with it later" attitude means equipment that does not work in a real emergency. Records and follow-up are also looked for in ISM audits and PSC inspections.
En tehlikeli hata, tatbikatı \"göstermel: The most dangerous mistake is to hold drills "for show": writing "done" on paper without raising the alarm, and not actually using the equipment. Crew who meet the equipment for the first time in a real emergency panic and are late. The AB must take drills seriously and actually carry out every duty.
Filika indirme kazaları (free-fall erken: Lifeboat launching accidents (premature free-fall release, davit brake failure, parting of falls) account for a significant share of fatal accidents at sea; most are caused by the wrong sequence or poorly maintained equipment. The AB must follow the lifeboat procedure step by step, paying attention to the safety pins and brakes.
Kaçış yolunun malzeme ile kapatılması, k: Blocking escape routes with stores, leaving escape lighting defective and incorrect head counts at muster lead to people left inside being overlooked. The AB must keep escape routes clear, be honest in the head count and report every deficiency they see.
Emniyet ekipmanları ve tatbikatlar, \"hi: Safety equipment and drills are duties that "we hope will never be needed, but which save lives when they are". The AB's value lies in knowing the equipment and internalizing the procedures well enough to respond correctly without thinking in a crisis. Sweat shed in drills means lives saved in a real emergency; this is why no drill is rushed through, no check is skipped and no defect is hidden.
Gemiye erişim; rıhtım yüksekliği, freebo: Access to the ship is provided by a gangway, an accommodation ladder or a combination of the two, depending on the height of the quay, the freeboard and the operation. For pilot transfer, a pilot ladder and, where necessary, a combination arrangement (accommodation ladder + pilot ladder) are used. The AB learns from the Bosun/officer which equipment is to be used in which conditions.
Erişim ekipmanı, güvenli açıyla, sağlam: Access equipment must be rigged at a safe angle, securely fastened, with non-slip steps and adequate lighting. After rigging and before use, the AB and the officer check the equipment; if there are loose fastenings, cracked steps, missing guardrails or insufficient light, it is not used. Access safety is not something to "fix later".
Kurulum öncesi AB; düşme, ezilme, sıkışm: Before rigging, the AB assesses the risks of falling, crushing, trapping, a tensioned line parting and falling overboard. If the job involves work at height or overside, a safety harness, a lifebuoy with lifeline on standby and suitable weather and sea conditions are required. PPE (safety helmet, gloves, non-slip boots and, where required, a lifejacket) is used in full.
Gangway, vinç/davit ile kaldırılıp rıhtı: The gangway is lifted with a crane/davit and landed on the quay/pier at a suitable angle. The AB checks that the lower end of the gangway sits firmly on the quay and will not slip, that the wheels/support leg work properly and that the gangway can move freely (without jamming) as the tide and draft change. The guardrail ropes/chains on both sides must be taut.
Gangway altına ve yanına düşmeyi önleyen: A safety net is rigged under and beside the gangway to prevent falls; the net must be wide enough to cover the gap between the quay and the ship and must be securely fastened. It must not be forgotten that the angle will change with the tide; the gangway is checked and adjusted periodically. An excessively steep or flat angle increases the risk of falling.
Accommodation ladder, geminin bordasına: The accommodation ladder is a ladder mounted on the ship's side, designed so that its steps always remain horizontal. The AB checks that the lower platform of the ladder is at a safe angle, that the steps are non-slip and sound, and that the guardrails are rigged. The SWL (safe working load) is not exceeded; the number of persons allowed on it at one time is observed.
Vinçle indirme/kaldırmada halat, troley: When lowering or hoisting with the winch, it is verified that the hoisting rope, trolley and brakes are working properly; the ladder must never be moved while anyone is on it. When the accommodation ladder and the pilot ladder are used together in a combination arrangement, the safety of the transfer point is particularly important.
Pilot ladder; sağlam yan halatlar (side: The pilot ladder consists of strong side ropes, non-slip steps that remain horizontal and, at set intervals, longer steps that prevent the ladder from twisting (spreader steps). The steps must be equally spaced, free of cracks and unpainted (paint hides cracks). The ladder is rigged securely on the ship's side; man-ropes are rigged when requested.
Pilot ladder'ın su seviyesinden istenen: The pilot ladder must be adjusted to the required height above the water (usually level with the pilot boat's deck); a ladder that is too long or too short is dangerous. If a climb of more than 9 meters is required, a combination arrangement (accommodation ladder + pilot ladder) is mandatory. After rigging, the AB checks the ladder visually; if a step is missing, a rope is broken or a fastening is loose, it is not used.
Combination arrangement'ta pilot ladder,: In a combination arrangement, the pilot ladder is combined with the lower platform of the accommodation ladder; the pilot first climbs the pilot ladder and then steps onto the platform. The transfer point is the most critical area: the platform must be horizontal, fitted with guardrails and level with the pilot ladder, with no gap or difference in height at the transfer. The AB rigs this combination in accordance with the rules.
Bütün düzenek, IMPA/SOLAS posterindeki ş: The whole arrangement must be rigged according to the diagram on the IMPA/SOLAS poster; if the pilot sees an unsafe arrangement, they may refuse the transfer, which delays the ship and/or leads to a report. The AB aims for rigging that matches the diagram exactly, not one that is "roughly right".
Erişim noktasında, ışıklı/dumanlı işaret: At the access point, a lifebuoy with a self-igniting light/smoke signal and a heaving line attached to it are kept ready. If the pilot or anyone else falls into the sea, the AB immediately throws the lifebuoy, keeps the person in sight and raises the alarm. The rescue boat/MOB boat must be ready; for night transfers, a searchlight is ready to illuminate the water.
AB, denize düşme anında ne yapacağını ez: The AB must know by heart what to do if someone falls into the sea: throw the lifebuoy, shout "man overboard", do not lose sight of the person, inform the bridge. Seconds save lives; hesitation and searching ("where is the lifebuoy?") cause delay, which is why the equipment is always kept ready in the same, accessible place.
Gangway, ladder ve pilot transfer noktas: The gangway, ladder and pilot transfer point must be adequately lit at night; however, the lights are positioned so that they do not dazzle the pilot or other persons. When the pilot ladder area is illuminated, the ladder and the water surface must be visible, with no shadows. Backup lighting (portable lamp) is kept ready.
Pilot biniş/inişinde AB; ladder bölgesin: During pilot embarkation/disembarkation, the AB stands at the ladder area, watches the pilot's climb, helps if necessary with the man-ropes and the line for the pilot's bag, and keeps an eye on the safety equipment (lifebuoy, light). Full attention is maintained until the pilot is fully on deck or has climbed down into the pilot boat. The person meeting the pilot escorts them to the bridge by a safe route.
Transfer sırasında gemi hızı, rüzgâr ve: During the transfer, the ship's speed, the wind and the sea state are important; the bridge maneuvers to make a lee for the pilot boat. The AB watches to ensure that the ladder does not slam against the ship's side or get caught, and that nobody gets trapped between the boat and the ship, and warns the bridge/officer of any danger.
Operasyon bitince pilot ladder dikkatlic: When the operation is over, the pilot ladder is recovered carefully and stored in a dry, ventilated place, without tension or crushing; storing it wet or twisted rots the ropes. While recovering the ladder, the AB checks it for damage (broken fibers, cracked steps) and reports any defect found. The gangway/accommodation ladder is brought to its stowed position and secured.
Pilot ladder düzenli görsel ve periyodik: The pilot ladder undergoes regular visual checks and periodic inspections; a worn ladder is taken out of service. The AB helps to keep the ladder clean, unpainted and labeled (manufacture/service information). A poorly maintained pilot ladder is a leading cause of fatal accidents.
Pilot her yıl ladder kaynaklı kazalarda: Every year pilots are injured or killed in ladder-related accidents; the main causes are incorrect securing, missing or broken steps, wrong height, missing combination arrangements and defective or worn ladders. Most of these accidents could have been prevented if the rigging rules had been followed exactly.
IMPA/IMO posterindeki uyarılara rağmen \: Despite the warnings on the IMPA/IMO poster, non-compliant practices such as "securing the steps with shackles", "unsuitable combination arrangements" and "securing with magnetic chocks" have led to accidents. The AB must correct any non-compliance they see or report it to the officer; the pilot has the right to refuse.
Güvenlik ağının eksik gerilmesi, can sim: A safety net that is not properly rigged, no lifebuoy at the access point, failure to monitor tide and draft changes, and inadequate lighting are the main causes of gangway-related falls and drownings. The AB must treat the access point as a fully equipped area that is checked continuously.
Borda iskelesi ve erişim ekipmanlarının: Rigging the accommodation ladder and other access equipment is a task that looks ordinary, but neglecting it can lead directly to death. The AB's discipline is shown in rigging every step of the pilot ladder, every guardrail of the gangway and every lashing of the safety net according to the rules. Whether a pilot, a crew member or a visitor gets on and off the ship safely depends on the AB's approach of rigging "exactly right, not roughly right".
Güvertedeki dağınık halat, takım, hortum: Loose ropes, tools, hoses, spills and unnecessary materials on deck are the main causes of slip, trip and fall accidents. These accidents account for a significant share of lost workdays and injuries at sea. By tidying the area after every job, putting materials back in place and cleaning up spills, the AB eliminates this risk at its source.
Düzen aynı zamanda acil duruma hazırlık: Order also means emergency preparedness: in a fire, flooding or when evacuating, an unobstructed deck allows fast and safe movement. An untidy deck both causes accidents in routine work and hinders escape and response in a crisis. This is why housekeeping is not a "cleaning job" but a continuous safety discipline.
Güvertede bırakılan boya kutusu, takım,: Paint tins, tools, rope reels and equipment left on deck are secured (lashing/securing) so that they do not slide and become dangerous with the ship's motions at sea. Unsecured heavy items cause crushing or impact accidents, or slide overboard, when the ship rolls. The AB puts away or secures every piece of equipment not in use.
İstifleme yaparken kaçış yolları, kapıla: When stowing materials, escape routes, doors, safety equipment and maneuvering stations (mooring stations, fire stations) are kept clear. No material is ever placed in front of a lifebuoy, fire extinguisher, hose box or emergency exit. The AB knows that even material left "temporarily" can turn into a risk.
Kaçış yolları (escape routes), koridorla: Escape routes, corridors, emergency exit doors and stairways are always kept open, unobstructed and marked. The AB immediately removes any material left in an escape route, because in a corridor filled with smoke during a fire, even the smallest obstacle causes a fatal delay. Emergency exit doors are not locked and are never blocked.
Kaçış aydınlatması (escape lighting, low: Escape lighting (low-location lighting) and direction signs must be visible and working; they are not covered with paint or materials. The AB reports defective escape lighting or worn-off signs. During drills, the escape routes are physically checked, and any obstruction found is removed.
Yangın söndürücü, hortum kutusu (fire st: The fronts of fire extinguishers, hose boxes (fire stations), lifebuoys, EEBDs, the first aid cabinet and emergency stop buttons are always kept clear. The AB prevents materials from being stowed in front of these points and removes them if they have been. A piece of safety equipment that cannot be reached is as good as non-existent when it really matters.
Emniyet ekipmanı işaretleri (levha, fosf: Safety equipment signs (plates, photoluminescent direction arrows) are kept visible and clean; they are not covered with paint or dirt. During deck painting and cleaning jobs, the AB takes care not to damage these signs and the equipment, protecting them by masking if necessary.
Scupper'lar (güverte tahliye delikleri): Scuppers (deck drain holes) and drain channels (waterways/gutterways) allow rain, seawater and wash water on deck to drain quickly overboard or to the bilge. The AB clears these channels of leaves, rust, paint residue, ropes and debris. A blocked scupper leads to water collecting on deck and a risk of freezing and slipping.
Yağlı operasyonlarda (yakıt ikmali, maki: During operations involving oil (bunkering, engine work), scupper plugs are fitted so that any spill does not go overboard (MARPOL). When the operation is over and any spill has been cleaned up, the plugs are removed; a plug forgotten in place causes the next rain or sea water to accumulate. The AB manages this cycle carefully.
Freeing port'lar, gemi bordasındaki ment: Freeing ports are hinged flaps at the ship's side; they allow sea water shipped on deck (green water) to be cleared quickly. Water collecting on the well deck adds weight to the ship and endangers stability through free surface effect; freeing ports prevent this.
