The AB checks that the freeing port flaps move freely, are not rusted or jammed, and have not been lashed or closed.
Freeing port'lar kesinlikle bağlanmaz, t: Freeing ports must never be lashed, blocked or permanently closed; otherwise water shipped on deck cannot drain away and the ship is endangered. The AB greases jammed hinges, reports rusted ones and does not block them with materials. These small flaps are the ship's stability safeguard in bad weather.
Yağ, gres, su, buz, gevşek halat ve dökü: Oil, grease, water, ice, loose ropes and spilled materials make the deck slippery and dangerous. The AB cleans up spills immediately, marks wet or oily surfaces and reports worn anti-slip coating where it is needed. An icy deck creates a fatal risk of slipping in winter; salt or sand is spread and the ice is broken up.
Yürüme yolları, geçiş güvertesi (fore-af: Walkways, the fore-and-aft passage, railings and lifelines are kept sound and continuous. The AB immediately marks and reports loose or broken railings, missing lifelines and deck openings left open (manholes, deck openings). An open deck opening is a risk of falling and even of an enclosed space accident.
Yetersiz aydınlatma, gece güverte çalışm: Inadequate lighting increases the risk of accidents during night work and when moving about the deck. The AB reports defective deck lighting, uses a portable lamp for night work and takes visual obstructions (steam, smoke) into account. High-visibility PPE helps the wearer to be noticed by others and increases safety in maneuvering areas.
Güverte temizliği reisin yönettiği günlü: Deck cleaning is carried out according to the daily/weekly program run by the Bosun: washing off salt deposits (especially after a voyage and before painting), cleaning up spills, checking drains and general tidiness. Because sea salt accelerates corrosion, equipment on the open deck is washed with fresh water. The AB follows the program and reports when it is completed.
Temizlik kimyasalları (deterjan, yağ çöz: When cleaning chemicals (detergents, degreasers) are used, the manufacturer's instructions and the Safety Data Sheet (SDS) are followed; suitable gloves and goggles are worn and chemicals are not discharged into the sea. If wash water contains oil or chemicals, it is collected in accordance with MARPOL. The AB considers environmental rules part of the cleaning routine.
Güverte düzeni, geminin Planned Maintena: Deck housekeeping is closely linked with the ship's Planned Maintenance System (PMS) and maintenance program; rust, cracks, broken railings and defective equipment noticed during cleaning are reported into the maintenance system. The AB is not "just a cleaner" but also an observer who detects defects; a small defect reported early prevents large maintenance costs.
En sık hatalar: scupper plug'ın takılı u: The most common errors: forgetting a scupper plug in place (water accumulation), lashing or blocking a freeing port, blocking an escape route with temporary materials, and leaving spills to be "cleaned later". This neglect leads both to routine accidents and to a serious stability/flooding risk in bad weather.
Slip/trip/fall kazalarının çoğu önlenebi: Most slip, trip and fall accidents could have been prevented: cleaning up spilled oil immediately, coiling up a loose rope and marking a wet floor would have been enough. The AB acts in the knowledge that disorder that looks "small" can turn into a real injury.
Emniyet ekipmanı önünün malzeme ile kapa: Blocking access to safety equipment with materials, covering signs with paint or dirt and leaving escape lighting defective cause vital delays in a real emergency. During cleaning and painting work, the AB must protect safety equipment and signs and always keep access clear.
Güverte düzeni ve temizlik, denizciliğin: Deck housekeeping and cleanliness are among the least noticed but most life-saving duties in seafaring. An open escape route, a working scupper, a freely moving freeing port and a clean deck prevent accidents in routine work and make survival possible in a crisis. The AB's value lies in this continuous, quiet discipline, which stays invisible "when all is well" but safeguards the ship and crew in a fire, in a storm or at the moment someone slips.
Kapalı mekan (enclosed space); sınırlı g: An enclosed space is a space with limited means of entry and exit, without continuous ventilation and not designed for continuous occupancy: ballast/fuel/cargo tanks, cofferdams, double bottoms, the chain locker, the pump room, empty holds, waste water tanks, and some cofferdams and void spaces. These spaces may have an oxygen-deficient, toxic or flammable atmosphere.
En tehlikeli yanı, tehlikenin görünmez v: The most dangerous aspect is that the hazard can be invisible and odorless: in a tank where the oxygen level has dropped, a person loses consciousness and collapses within a few breaths and cannot even give a warning. Rust (oxidation), decaying organic cargo, inert gas, welding gases and bilge gases consume oxygen or create a toxic atmosphere. This is why even a space where the air "looks clean" can be fatal.
Standby (attendant / gözcü), girişin dış: The standby (attendant) is the person who stays outside the entrance, maintains continuous communication with the person inside, monitors the atmosphere and the time, and raises the alarm in an emergency. It is a big mistake to think of this duty as "passive waiting"; the standby has the most active safety role in the operation. The AB must not leave the standby post, go off to another job or let their attention wander.
AB standby olarak; giriş izninin (permit: As standby, the AB continuously confirms that the entry permit is valid, that the atmosphere has been tested, that the ventilation is running, and the condition of the person inside. In any uncertainty (loss of communication, the person inside not responding), the AB first raises the alarm and then acts according to the protocol WITHOUT going in.
Kapalı mekana giriş, sorumlu zabit (gene: Entry into an enclosed space is made with an enclosed space entry permit approved by the responsible officer (usually the Chief Officer). The permit states the atmosphere test results, the ventilation status, the entry duration, the job description, the standby and rescue arrangements and the communication method. The permit is time-limited and conditional; it is canceled if conditions change.
AB, izinde kendi rolünü (standby/giren): The AB clearly knows their own role in the permit (standby/entrant) and its conditions; no entry is made without a permit or with an expired permit. The permit is not a "paper formality" but confirmation that all precautions have been taken. A briefing (toolbox talk) is held, and everyone learns by heart what to do in an emergency.
AB, atmosfer ölçüm cihazını (multi-gas d: The AB must know how to use the atmosphere measuring instrument (multi-gas detector / personal monitor), the principles of calibration and bump testing, and the meaning of the alarms. The entrant carries a personal monitor and leaves immediately if the alarm sounds. The standby AB monitors the atmosphere readings and stops the entry at any sign of deterioration. The atmosphere is not something "measured once and forgotten" but a parameter that is monitored continuously.
Standby AB ile giren kişi arasında sürek: Continuous, pre-agreed communication is established between the standby AB and the entrant: radio (intrinsically safe/non-sparking type), lifeline signals or voice confirmation. Communication is confirmed at set intervals (e.g., every 1-2 minutes); no response from the person inside is a sign of an emergency. In an explosive atmosphere, the radio must be suitably (Ex) certified.
AB, iletişimi bir an bile bırakmaz; içer: The AB never lets communication lapse, even for a moment: they do not lose contact with the person inside, do not get involved in other work and do not leave the entrance. If communication is lost, the alarm is raised immediately and the protocol is started. Silence does not mean "all is well"; it means "must be checked".
Giren kişi, mümkünse harness ile bağlı b: Where possible, the entrant wears a harness attached to a lifeline (rescue line); the standby AB holds the line and watches its slack and condition. Rescue equipment stands ready outside the entrance: spare SCBA, a rescue harness, a tripod/winch recovery arrangement (if required), resuscitation equipment and first aid. The AB knows where this equipment is and how to use it.
Standby AB, içeri girmeye uygun ek perso: The standby AB does not attempt a rescue alone without additional personnel fit to enter and without SCBA; their duty is to raise the alarm and direct the rescue team. If the rescue equipment is missing or not ready, the entry is not started; this is part of the permit conditions.
İçerideki kişi yanıt vermez, düşer veya: If the person inside does not respond, collapses or is taken ill, the standby AB's first action is NOT to jump in but to raise the alarm: call the rescue team by general alarm/PA and inform the bridge/officer. Seconds matter, but entering alone and unprepared loses two people instead of saving one. The alarm sets the rescue chain in motion.
Alarm sonrası AB; havalandırmayı artırma: After the alarm, the AB increases ventilation, prepares the rescue equipment and directs the team. Only a trained rescuer wearing SCBA, attached to a lifeline and with their own standby outside goes in. This rule of sequence is one of the strictest safety rules on board.
Kurtarma ekibi geldiğinde: havalandırma: When the rescue team arrives: ventilation is increased to the maximum, the rescuer dons SCBA, has their own standby outside, is attached by lifeline/harness and reaches the casualty. The casualty is lifted out through the vertical/narrow opening using a rescue harness or a tripod/winch arrangement. The recovery plan must have been thought out before entry; getting an unconscious person out through a narrow manhole is very difficult.
Kurban temiz havaya alındığında derhal i: Once the casualty is in fresh air, first aid/CPR is given immediately, oxygen is administered and medical assistance (radio medical advice/MEDEVAC) is requested. The AB must know basic first aid and CPR. In H₂S/CO poisoning, the casualty is kept under observation even if they appear "recovered"; there may be delayed effects.
SOLAS III/19.3.3, kapalı mekan giriş ve: SOLAS III/19.3.3 requires enclosed space entry and rescue drills to be held at least once every two months. In these drills, atmosphere testing, use of the permit, donning SCBA, recovering a casualty with a lifeline and resuscitation are simulated. In these drills, the AB acquires the reflexes to act without thinking in a real emergency.
Tatbikatta kurtarma ekipmanının çalıştığ: During the drill, it is confirmed that the rescue equipment works, the SCBA cylinders are full and the recovery arrangement (tripod/winch) functions. After the drill, deficiencies are reported and rectified. A "drill on paper" is useless in a real emergency; the AB takes every drill seriously.
Gaz dedektörleri düzenli kalibrasyon ve: Gas detectors require regular calibration and a daily bump test (a quick response check with a known gas); otherwise a false "safe" reading can be fatal. Before use, the AB checks the instrument's charge, calibration date and function. SOLAS XI-1/7 requires ships to carry an appropriate atmosphere testing instrument.
Kapalı mekan ölümlerinin ortak nedenleri: The common causes of enclosed space deaths are: atmosphere testing skipped or inadequate, "quick" entry without a permit, inadequate ventilation, neglect of the standby duty and loss of communication. Most cases began with the thought "I was only going in and out for a second" and ended in death.
AB, hiçbir gerekçenin (acele, kısa süre,: The AB must know that no reason (haste, a short duration, 'the air looks clean') justifies skipping precautions. Enclosed space rules are written in blood; every skipped step is a potential death.
Kapalı mekan kazalarının en trajik örünt: The most tragic pattern in enclosed space accidents is that people who jump in unprepared to rescue the first casualty also die; in one case, several people died one after another in a tank, each trying to rescue the one before. The standby AB's discipline of "alarm first, never enter without SCBA" breaks this chain.
Kapalı mekan standby ve kurtarma desteği: Enclosed space standby and rescue support is the most vital duty an AB can take on. A standby who waits attentively outside, never loses communication and, in an emergency, applies the protocol instead of instinctively diving in saves the life of the shipmate inside as well as their own. One lesson sums up everything in this duty: an enclosed space is unforgiving, and heroic rescues kill; alarm first, then entry with preparation. Here, discipline directly means life.
Yüksekte çalışmada (working aloft) temel: In work aloft, the basic hazard is falling: slipping, loss of balance, equipment failure or the roll of the ship can make a person fall. Overside work adds the risk of falling overboard (man overboard); a person who falls into cold water faces hypothermia and drowning, and when the ship is under way there is also the propeller hazard. When these two risks combine, overside work becomes one of the most dangerous operations on board.
Ek tehlikeler: çalışılan ekipmanın enerj: Additional hazards: energy from the equipment being worked on (rotating radar antenna, hot funnel gases, electricity), dropped tools or materials striking people below, fatigue, and weather and sea conditions. The AB assesses all these risks before starting work and never goes aloft or overside until suitable precautions have been taken.
Yüksekte/overside çalışma yalnızca yetki: Work aloft/overside is carried out only by authorized personnel who are physically and psychologically fit; a person who suffers from dizziness or fear of heights, or who is tired, is not given this work. The work is not started without the required permit and suitable weather and sea conditions. If the AB does not feel fit, they are obliged to tell the Bosun/officer.
Permit to Work, yüksek riskli işin tüm ö: The Permit to Work is a written control system that ensures high-risk work does not start until all precautions have been taken. The permit for work aloft/overside contains the job description, location, risks, precautions taken (harness, fall arrest, MOB preparation), energy isolation (switching off radar/antennas, isolating the electrical supply), the appointment of a lookout, the duration and the approving officer.
Permit süreli ve şart bağlıdır; iş bitin: The permit is time-limited and conditional; it is canceled when the job is finished or when conditions change (weather deteriorating, sea getting up). The AB does not start work without a permit or without its conditions being met; the permit is not "paperwork" but confirmation of everyone's safety. In the toolbox talk before the job, everyone learns their role and the emergency arrangements.
Direk veya baca yakınında çalışırken rad: When working near the mast or the funnel, the energy to the radar antenna, radio transmitters, whistle and electrical equipment is switched off, locked out and tagged (lock-out/tag-out). A rotating radar antenna can strike a person, a transmitter emits radiation and a whistle sounding suddenly can cause shock. The AB does not start work until the isolation has been confirmed by the bridge.
Yüksekte/overside çalışmada full body ha: For work aloft/overside, a full body harness is used; a waist belt alone is not sufficient for fall arrest, because in a fall it causes internal organ and spinal injuries. The AB dons the harness correctly: leg and chest straps tight, buckles fastened, the dorsal D-ring centered between the shoulder blades. A loose harness can let the person slip out in a fall.
Harness ve lanyard kullanım öncesi kontr: The harness and lanyard are checked before use: if there is cut or worn webbing, cracked or deformed buckles or karabiners, or rusty snap hooks that do not lock, they are not used. A harness that has been shock-loaded (has arrested a fall) is taken out of service. The equipment must be certified and periodically inspected.
Çift karabinalı (twin/double lanyard) si: The purpose of the twin (double) lanyard system is for the person to stay attached to a secure point by at least one karabiner at all times ("100% tie-off"). When changing position, one karabiner is clipped to the new point, and only then is the other unclipped; in this way the connection is never broken. Climbing with a single karabiner and unclipping from time to time creates a fatal fall window.
Lanyard mümkün olduğunca bel hizası veya: The lanyard is attached, as far as possible, to a fixed point (anchor point) at or above waist level; if the attachment is low, the fall distance increases and a higher impact results. A shock-absorbing lanyard reduces the fall impact to a level that is safe for the body. The AB confirms that the anchor point can really take the load; railings and weak pipes cannot be relied on as anchor points.
Yüksekte/overside erişimde bosun's chair: For access aloft/overside, a bosun's chair, a stage (hanging staging platform) or scaffolding is used. The hoisting line (gantline) and the safety line must be SEPARATE, so that if one parts, the other holds. The AB checks the soundness of the ropes, the connecting knots and shackles, and the blocks and sheaves. If a rope passes over a sharp edge, a chafe guard is fitted.
Bosun's chair'da çalışan kişi ayrıca har: A person working in a bosun's chair also uses a harness + independent fall arrest (attached to a separate safety line); relying on the chair's rope alone is a single-point-of-failure risk. When rigging a stage or scaffolding, an independent lifeline and a harness are also required. The AB always applies the "two independent systems" principle.
Yüksekte kullanılan takım (anahtar, fırç: Tools used aloft (spanners, brushes, paint, removed parts) are tied on (tool lanyard) or carried in a closed bag; a falling object can kill a person below. The work area below is cleared, and a "falling objects" warning and, if necessary, a barrier are put in place. When working above, the AB thinks of the team below; those below wear safety helmets and keep out of the drop zone.
Overside çalışmada, ışıklı can simidi +: During overside work, a lifebuoy with light and line is kept ready right next to the work position; the rescue boat/MOB boat crew is also kept ready. If a person falls into the sea, the lookout immediately throws the lifebuoy, shouts "man overboard", keeps the person in sight and informs the bridge. Overside work is generally not done while the ship is under way; at anchor, in port or other stationary conditions are preferred.
Soğuk sularda düşen kişide hipotermi dak: In cold water, hypothermia sets in within minutes for a person who has fallen in; fast rescue is vital. The AB knows by heart what to do if someone falls overboard and confirms the location of the MOB equipment before starting work. Overside work at night requires additional lighting and stricter precautions.
Yüksekte/overside çalışma yalnızca uygun: Work aloft/overside is done only in suitable weather and sea conditions; increasing wind, precipitation, icing, rolling of the ship or reduced visibility require the work to be stopped immediately. If the AB or the lookout sees that conditions are deteriorating, they stop the job; the "almost done, let's finish" mindset is an invitation to an accident.
Düşme kazalarının ana nedenleri: harness: The main causes of fall accidents: not wearing a harness at all or wearing it loosely, using a single lanyard and unclipping from time to time instead of using a twin lanyard, choosing a weak or unsuitable anchor point, and working with a waist belt instead of a full body harness. Each of these errors means death or serious injury in the event of a fall.
\"Sadece kısa bir iş\" veya \"deneyimliy: Skipping the harness or permit with the thought "it's only a short job" or "I'm experienced, there's no need" has led to accidents in which even experienced seafarers have died. The AB knows that experience is no substitute for precautions; every job aloft or overside is done with full equipment.
Radar/anten enerjisinin kilitlenmemesi,: Failure to lock out the radar/antenna energy, dropped tools injuring people below and MOB equipment not being ready during overside work are among the causes of reported serious accidents. The AB must confirm energy isolation, tie on tools and check MOB preparations before starting work.
Yüksekte ve overside çalışma, AB'nin en: Work aloft and overside is among the AB's highest-risk duties, and no shortcut is forgiven here. A correctly worn harness, a connection that is never broken, a locked-out radar, a tied-on tool and a lifebuoy standing ready make the difference between a seafarer coming home safely from the mast or the ship's side and not coming home at all. The AB's skill is shown in the discipline of "always full equipment, never rush, stop when conditions deteriorate", because falls from height and falls overboard are accidents that give no second chance.
Yük tanklarında hidrokarbon buharı (HC): In cargo tanks, hydrocarbon (HC) vapor forms a flammable/explosive atmosphere; crude oil may also contain substances such as toxic hydrogen sulfide (H₂S) and benzene. Tank cleaning releases this vapor and generates static electricity. If mismanaged, the combination of an ignition source (static spark) + flammable atmosphere + oxygen leads to an explosion.
Bu nedenle tankerlerde temel strateji, y: For this reason, the basic strategy on tankers is to control the "oxygen" side of the fire triangle: inert gas is used to reduce the oxygen content of the tank atmosphere to a level that cannot support combustion (typically below 8% by volume). The AB must understand why work is carried out in an inert atmosphere and that any error that upsets this balance (air ingress, a static spark) can be fatal.
AB; güverte üstü işlemleri (butterworth: The AB carries out deck operations (opening/closing Butterworth machines, connecting hoses, handling tank lids/manholes, earthing, supporting atmosphere measurements) under the instructions and supervision of the responsible officer (Chief Officer). The operation plan, the sequence and approval rest with the officer; the AB carries out the plan and reports any deviation or abnormality immediately.
AB, atmosfer testleri tamamlanıp giriş i: The AB never enters a tank before the atmosphere tests have been completed and an entry permit has been issued; an inerted tank is oxygen-deficient and may contain toxic or flammable gas. Tank cleaning is a job that "cannot be rushed and accepts no shortcuts"; every step is carried out in accordance with ISGOTT and the ship's procedures.
AB, tankın \"inert\", \"gas-free\" veya: The AB must not confuse the "inert", "gas-free" and "non-inert" states of a tank; these states require different precautions. An inerted tank is not entered because it is oxygen-deficient; a gas-free (ventilated and tested) tank may become suitable for entry. The atmosphere status is monitored and recorded continuously.
IGS; oksijen analizörü, basınç göstergel: The IGS is fitted with an oxygen analyzer, pressure gauges, a deck water seal (to prevent backflow) and alarms. The AB helps to monitor the IGS indicators on deck; if the oxygen rises, the pressure drops or an alarm sounds, the operation is stopped and the officer is informed. An IGS failure means a risk of a flammable atmosphere forming; COW/washing is stopped immediately.
COW'da sabit veya taşınabilir yıkama mak: In COW, fixed or portable washing machines spray pressurized crude oil onto the tank surfaces to dissolve the sediment (clingage) and make it pumpable; this both improves discharge efficiency and reduces the quantity of slops (waste) (as required by MARPOL Annex I). COW is carried out only when the tank is inert (low oxygen) and the IGS is working properly.
COW boyunca oksijen seviyesi, IGS basınc: Throughout COW, the oxygen level, IGS pressure, line pressure and leaks are monitored continuously. If the oxygen rises, the IGS fails, there are signs of a leak or fire, or air ingress is suspected, the operation is stopped IMMEDIATELY. When the AB notices an abnormality (pressure drop, smell, noise), they report it without waiting; seconds matter.
COW sonrası tank tortusu azalmış olur; a: After COW, the sediment in the tank is reduced; however, the tank is still inert and contains hydrocarbons, and it cannot be entered. A separate gas-freeing and testing process is required before tank entry. The AB does not consider a tank "clean/safe" just because COW has finished.
AB, statik riskini azaltmak için: tüm il: To reduce the static risk, the AB bonds all conductive equipment (washing machines, hose nozzles, measuring instruments) to the ship's structure, observes the waiting period (relaxation/settling time) for sounding and measurement, and prevents free-falling jets and splashing. Anti-static (conductive) PPE and equipment are used; synthetic clothing or tools that hold a charge are not used.
Tanka indirilen her metal cisim (soundin: Every metal object lowered into a tank (sounding weight, measuring instrument, lamp) is earthed or is of an approved anti-static type; an unearthed conductive object remains "isolated" and becomes a source of static sparks. Mobile phones, cameras, uncertified flashlights and spark-producing tools are prohibited in the hazardous area; only Ex (explosion-proof) certified equipment is used.
Tanka giriş gerekiyorsa (inspeksiyon, on: If tank entry is required (inspection, repair), the tank is first made gas-free: the hydrocarbon vapor is reduced to a safe level by ventilation, the oxygen is brought back to normal (20.9%) and toxic gases (H₂S/benzene) are reduced to safe limits. This transition "from inert to air" is controlled; care is taken that during the intermediate stage (purging), the atmosphere does not pass through the dangerous flammable range. The process is carried out under the officer's control, using fans/eductors.
AB, gas freeing'in fiziksel işlerini (ve: The AB carries out the physical work of gas freeing (opening vents, running fans, handling tank lids), but the authority to declare a tank "gas-free" rests with the responsible officer and is given only on the basis of verified atmosphere tests. Tests are made at different levels, not at a single point; some gases collect at the bottom.
Tank gas-free ve test edilmiş olsa bile,: Even if the tank is gas-free and tested, entry is an enclosed space entry: an entry permit, atmosphere testing (O₂/LEL/toxic), continuous ventilation, a standby outside (lifeline + communication) and rescue arrangements are mandatory. If the AB is to enter, they carry a personal gas monitor; the standby watches from outside and, in an emergency, applies the 'alarm first, then SCBA + team' protocol.
Tank dibinde kalan tortu/slop oksijen tü: Sediment or slops remaining on the tank bottom may continue to consume oxygen or release gas; this is why the atmosphere is monitored throughout the entry. If the readings deteriorate during work, the tank is left immediately. The AB does not fall into the trap of thinking "tested once, so it's safe".
Güvertede scupper tıpaları (scupper plug: Scupper plugs are kept fitted on deck so that any spill does not go overboard; spills are collected with absorbent. Sea and air pollution (including VOC emissions) is prevented, and port/terminal rules are followed. Environmental violations lead to heavy fines and detention of the ship.
Tank temizliği, COW ve giriş işlemleri i: Tank cleaning, COW and entry operations are carried out with the relevant permits (an entry/COW permit even when there is no hot work) and records; the ship-shore safety checklist (at the terminal) and the IG/COW records are kept. The AB knows their own duty within the scope of the permit, keeps in contact with the officer/pump control by radio (Ex-certified) and reports every abnormality.
En ölümcül hatalar: oksijen sınırı doğru: The most fatal errors: starting washing without verifying the oxygen limit, continuing operations after an IGS failure, using equipment without earthing it, and water washing in a tank that is not inert. The major tanker explosions in history (including several VLCCs) resulted from a combination of these errors and led to the introduction of the IG/COW rules.
AB, \"muhtemelen güvenlidir\" varsayımın: The AB knows that the assumption "it's probably safe" is fatal on tankers; every value is measured, every connection is earthed and every doubt stops the operation. In this work, patience and discipline are worth more than speed.
İnert tanka izinsiz baş uzatma, gas-free: Putting one's head into an inerted tank without permission, not monitoring the atmosphere continuously in a tank considered gas-free, and entering without a standby are causes of enclosed space deaths on tankers. Even at the end of tank cleaning, the AB must treat the tank as an enclosed space and apply the entry rules in full.
Tankerde tank temizliği ve butterworth o: Tank cleaning and Butterworth operations on tankers are the least error-tolerant work in seafaring, because here one wrong step can destroy not just one person but the whole ship. The AB's value lies in applying the rules on inert atmosphere, earthing, atmosphere monitoring and entry without exception, and in having the discipline to stop the operation at the slightest abnormality. Skill in this work lies not in speed but in unwavering attention that takes every measurement, every earthing connection and every permit condition seriously.
Her vardiya, bir önceki vardiyadan resmi: Every watch begins with a formal handover from the previous watch. When taking over, the oiler receives verbally and in writing the condition of the machinery, work in progress, the alarm history, expected maneuvers/operations and especially the "points requiring attention". Under STCW A-VIII/2 the handover must be complete; in a doubtful situation, the relieving person does not accept the watch without personally checking the machinery.
Devir-teslimde standby jeneratör durumu,: At the handover, the status of the standby generator, the separators in operation, boiler pressure, bilge and sludge tank levels, ongoing bunkering/transfer operations and the jobs to be done during that watch under the PMS (Planned Maintenance System) are made clear. The oiler includes this information in their own rounds plan.
Modern gemilerin çoğu UMS (Unmanned Mach: Most modern ships are UMS (Unmanned Machinery Space) certified; at night the engine room is left unmanned and the alarms are routed to the bridge and to the cabin of the duty engineer. However, during maneuvering, port operations, passages through narrow waterways and critical maintenance, the engine room is "manned" and the oiler is present on site at all times.
Yağcı, turunu rastgele değil sabit bir g: The oiler makes rounds along a fixed route, not at random, so that no equipment is missed. The general approach is systematic, from top to bottom and from forward to aft: first the upper platforms (purifier room, air compressors, boiler), then the middle platform (generators, upper part of the main engine), and finally the tank top level (lower part of the main engine, bilges, pumps, shaft bearings).
Her durakta beş duyu kullanılır: göz (sı: At every stop, all five senses are used: sight (leaks, levels, color), hearing (abnormal noise, knocking), touch (bearing/casing temperature — the limit that can be felt with the back of the hand is ~60°C), smell (burnt oil, electrical burning, exhaust) and the feel of vibration. This sensory check picks up early signs that no sensor can detect.
Yağcı tur sırasında portatif sıcaklık öl: During rounds, the oiler carries a portable temperature gauge (infrared thermometer), a flashlight and a logbook/tablet. Readings at critical points (exhaust temperatures, bearing temperatures, cooling water outlet temperature) are noted and compared with the previous round. The trend is more important than the instantaneous value; a temperature that rises slowly is a warning of a fault before it reaches the alarm threshold.
Herhangi bir anormallik (yeni sızıntı, s: Any abnormality (a new leak, a change in sound, vibration, a loose connection, spilled oil) is reported immediately to the engineer on watch. The Oiler does not intervene on their own and knows the limits of their authority. However, if the Oiler sees an immediate danger (a fire starting, a high-pressure steam/oil spray), they first ensure safety and raise the alarm.
Ana makinede her silindir için egzoz gaz: On the main engine, the exhaust gas temperature of each cylinder is a critical indicator. A temperature imbalance between cylinders (deviation) indicates a fuel injector fault, a combustion problem or a leaking exhaust valve. Bearing temperatures (main bearing, crankpin, crosshead), cooling water inlet/outlet temperatures and lubricating oil temperature are monitored on every round.
Yardımcı dizel jeneratörlerde yük dağılı: On auxiliary diesel generators, exhaust temperatures, jacket water temperature and oil temperature are monitored in relation to load sharing. A generator that is overloaded or insufficiently cooled may drop off line during harbor/sea changeovers; this is a blackout risk.
Tropik sularda deniz suyu sıcaklığı 32°C: In tropical waters, when the sea water temperature exceeds 32°C the cooling margin narrows; under these conditions the Oiler checks the cooling outlet temperatures more frequently. Clogging of the sea chest strainer (especially in areas with heavy marine growth/weed) causes a sudden temperature rise and requires a changeover between the high and low sea chests.
Yağlama yağı basıncı (LO pressure), maki: Lubricating oil pressure (LO pressure) is the lifeblood of the engine; low oil pressure causes bearing damage within seconds. The inlet oil pressures of the main engine and the generators are verified on every round. Fuel supply pressure (FO supply/booster pressure) affects injection quality and is monitored together with the viscosity control unit (viscotherm).
Çalışma havası (control air, ~7 bar) ve: Control air (~7 bar) and starting air (~25-30 bar) pressures are critical. If the starting air pressure is low, the engine cannot start; for this reason the air compressors and the pressure of the air bottles are monitored continuously. The air bottles are drained daily to remove condensate.
Yağ, yakıt ve hava filtrelerinde diferan: On oil, fuel and air filters, the differential pressure gauge (DP gauge) shows how far the filter is clogged. When the DP rises, the filter is cleaned or replaced; on automatic backwash (auto-backwash) filters, the backflush frequency is monitored. Ignoring a high DP leads to the filter bypass opening and dirty fuel/oil reaching the engine.
Yağcı, filtre değişim sırasında ana hatt: During a filter change, the Oiler turns the duplex filter lever (changeover) without interrupting the main line, so the engine keeps running without interruption. The contents of the removed filter (metal particles, coal-like residue) are examined and any abnormality is reported to the engineer — metal swarf coming from a bearing is an early sign of failure.
Yağcı her turda günlük servis tanklarını: On every round, the Oiler checks the levels of the daily service tanks (FO/DO settling and service tanks), the lubricating oil sump/storage tanks, and the bilge and sludge tanks. A sudden drop in the crankcase (sump) oil level indicates an oil leak, while a sudden rise indicates fuel or water contamination (sump dilution) — the latter is a warning sign of a crankcase explosion risk.
Sludge ve atık yağ tankı seviyeleri MARP: Sludge and waste oil tank levels are critical under MARPOL Annex I; when a tank becomes full, the Oiler informs the engineer, and discharge ashore (shore disposal) or incineration is planned. Tank levels must never be falsified; PSC inspections and ORB (Oil Record Book) checks examine whether the levels are consistent.
Soğutma sistemi genleşme tankı (expansio: The level of the cooling system expansion tank is monitored; a continuous drop means a leak in the cooling circuit. Sight glasses — particularly those on the oil return lines — are used to check the oil flow and its color; foamy or cloudy oil indicates water contamination.
Pompalar, fanlar, kompresörler ve separa: Pumps, fans, compressors and separators have a steady sound and vibration signature. A change in this signature (a new hum, knocking, a screeching sound) is a sign of bearing wear, imbalance, cavitation or a loose connection. Through experience, the Oiler knows "what normal sounds like" and catches deviations early.
Kavitasyon (pompa emişinde basınç düşmes: Cavitation (vapor bubbles forming because of a pressure drop at the pump suction) produces a typical gravel-like rattling sound and wears the pump impeller rapidly. A clogged suction filter or a low tank level is a common cause; the Oiler recognizes the sound and reports it to the engineer.
Ana makinede yeni bir vuruntu (knocking): A new knocking sound in the main engine may indicate a problem with injection timing, a combustion anomaly or a bearing clearance problem; it is reported to the engineer immediately. The color of the smoke from the exhaust funnel also gives information: black smoke (incomplete combustion/overload), blue smoke (burning oil), white smoke (water/fuel problem or cold combustion).
Scavenge space (süpürme havası bölgesi): A fire in the scavenge space (scavenge air space) is a hidden but dangerous event in large two-stroke engines; it shows itself through a local temperature rise and smoke. By monitoring the deposits and the temperature at the scavenge drains, the Oiler can catch the early signs.
Büyük iki zamanlı makinelerde silindir y: On large two-stroke engines, cylinder lubrication is carried out in proportion to load by electronically controlled lubricators (alpha lubricator); the feed rate (g/kWh) is monitored. The Oiler verifies that the lubricator pumps are running, that the oil tank is full and that there is no no-flow alarm.
Manuel yağlama noktaları (greasing point: Manual lubrication points (greasing points) — fan bearings, valve spindles, door hinges, crane/winch bearings — are greased with a grease gun according to the PMS schedule. Over-lubrication is at least as harmful as under-lubrication (strain on seals, dirt sticking). The Oiler uses the correct type of grease (according to temperature/application).
Yağcı, sirkülasyon yağının renk, koku ve: The Oiler observes the color, smell and appearance of the circulating oil. Darkening or thickening, a burnt smell or foam are signs of water/contamination. Periodic oil samples (LO sampling) are taken and sent for laboratory analysis; viscosity, water content, TBN (Total Base Number) and metal content are evaluated.
Sızıntı tespiti, Yağcı'nın en kritik gör: Leak detection is one of the Oiler's most critical duties. Flange weeping, pump gland leaks, valve bonnet leaks, pipe cracks and casing cracks are looked for during the round. When a new leak is found, its source, quantity and risk (proximity to hot surfaces) are reported to the engineer.
Yüksek basınçlı yakıt borularında (HP fu: A leak in high-pressure fuel pipes (HP fuel pipe) is contained by the double-walled pipe (double-walled / sheathed pipe) system; the leak alarm of this system is never disabled. Under SOLAS II-2, shielding of fuel/oil lines near hot surfaces is mandatory.
Sızıntıların toplandığı drip tray ve sav: The drip trays and save-all trays in which leaks collect are emptied regularly and kept clean; accumulated oil creates a slipping hazard and a fire load. By tracing where these accumulations come from, the Oiler identifies hidden/slow leaks. The trays are always emptied into the sludge/waste oil tank and are never mixed into the bilge.
Vardiya verileri makine logbook'una (eng: Watch data are recorded in the engine room logbook (engine room log) at regular intervals: main engine rpm/load, generator loads, temperature and pressure readings, fuel/oil consumption, tank levels and notable events. These records are official evidence both for operational monitoring and for PSC/class/insurance inspections.
Kayıtlar dürüst ve zamanında tutulur; so: Records are kept honestly and on time; filling them in afterwards in bulk (pencil whipping) is prohibited and, if found during an inspection, leads to serious sanctions. Although alarm and data logging on modern ships is done by automation (AMS), the responsibility for manual verification and signature remains.
Bir alarm çaldığında Yağcı önce alarmın: When an alarm sounds, the Oiler first identifies the type of alarm (sensor fault or real fault) and then immediately informs the engineer on watch. Within the limits of their authority, the Oiler may take simple actions (filter changeover, draining, starting the standby pump — if trained and authorized); however, critical interventions are carried out on the engineer's instructions.
Slowdown veya shutdown gibi otomatik kor: If an automatic protection (safety trip) such as slowdown or shutdown is activated, the Oiler observes on site and passes real-time information to the engineer. The locations of the emergency shutdown buttons and the quick-closing valves are known by heart.
Yağcı'nın değeri, otomasyonun göremediği: The Oiler's value lies in seeing what automation cannot see. Disciplined rounds, conscious use of all five senses, trend monitoring and timely reporting are the first line of defense that prevents a small fault in the engine room from turning into a major accident. A good Oiler is the person who notices a problem before the alarm sounds.
Mekanik bakımların büyük çoğunluğu PMS (: Most mechanical maintenance is triggered through the PMS (Planned Maintenance System); jobs such as valve overhauls, opening up pumps and cleaning coolers are planned by running hours or by calendar. The Fitter reads the work order and verifies that the necessary spare parts, gaskets, O-rings, packing and consumables are in stock; if anything is missing, the Fitter informs the engineer.
Plansız (arıza kaynaklı) işlerde de aynı: The same discipline applies to unplanned (breakdown) jobs: first, an effort is made to understand the root cause of the failure, and unnecessary replacement of parts is avoided. Before the job, the manual of the machine/system (the manufacturer's technical manual) is studied; in particular, torque values, tolerance ranges and the assembly sequence are taken from it.
Hiçbir mekanik iş, ekipman emniyetli hal: No mechanical job starts until the equipment has been made safe. With LOTO (Lock-Out / Tag-Out), the electrical supply is isolated, locked and tagged; pressurized systems are isolated and depressurized (de-pressurize); hot systems are allowed to cool down; rotating equipment is verified to be stopped. If these steps are skipped, an unexpected release of energy can be fatal.
Risk değerlendirmesinde sıcak yüzey, bas: The risk assessment identifies hot surfaces, pressurized fluids, heavy parts falling (trapping/crushing), sparks, chemicals and enclosed space risks, and sets out mitigation measures (PPE, crane/slings, ventilation).
Gemide globe, gate, butterfly, check (no: On board there are various types of valve, such as globe, gate, butterfly, check (non-return), safety/relief and quick-closing valves. Before an overhaul, the valve is isolated and the system depressurized. The Fitter removes the bonnet by loosening its bolts gradually (crosswise), takes out the internal parts (disc, seat, spindle, gland packing) and inspects them for wear, gouging and erosion.
Globe ve gate valflerde sızdırmazlık sea: In globe and gate valves, tightness is achieved by the contact surface between the seat and the disc. If there is erosion/pitting, lapping (grinding with lapping compound) is carried out; heavy damage requires replacement of the seat or a new valve. Quick-closing valves (fuel tank quick-closing) are tested as required by SOLAS; a malfunctioning one is a gap in fire safety.
Lapping işleminde uygun grit (kaba→ince): Lapping is done with lapping compound of suitable grit (coarse→fine) using circular/figure-of-eight movements, and continues until the surface is even with a uniform matte-bright finish. Afterwards, all compound is carefully cleaned off — abrasive left in the system will damage the valve again. New gland packing is cut to the correct size and inserted ring by ring, with the joints staggered.
Montaj sonrası valf, hidrostatik veya pn: After assembly, the valve is tested for tightness by a hydrostatic or pneumatic test. Safety/relief valves are adjusted to the set pressure and sealed. All bolts are tightened to the manufacturer's torque values in a crosswise sequence.
Santrifüj pompalarda (deniz suyu, balast: Maintenance of centrifugal pumps (sea water, ballast, fire, general service) covers checking impeller wear, wear ring clearance, shaft condition, bearings and the gland packing/mechanical seal. When the wear ring clearance increases, pump efficiency falls and recirculation increases; the clearance is compared with the manufacturer's limit.
Mekanik salmastra hassas bir parçadır; m: A mechanical seal is a precision part; when it is fitted, the faces must be perfectly clean and free of scratches, and the correct compression must be applied. On pumps with gland packing, a slight drip is normal and provides cooling; tightening the packing until it is completely leak-free burns it.
Vidalı (screw), dişli (gear) ve pistonlu: For screw, gear and piston pumps (fuel, lubrication, hydraulic), clearance and wear checks follow different criteria. In fuel transfer and booster pumps, pressure drops as internal clearances increase; the suction/discharge valves and the safety valve are checked. For bilge pumps, priming capability (removing air from the suction) and check valve tightness are important.
Doğru conta seçimi, sızdırmazlığın temel: Choosing the correct gasket is the basis of tightness. The type of fluid (oil, fuel, water, steam, exhaust), its temperature and its pressure determine the material and thickness. A wrong gasket — for example, a low-temperature gasket on a steam line — soon deforms and leaks. Non-asbestos materials are standard; asbestos is prohibited.
Conta, flanş yüzeyine birebir uyacak şek: The gasket is cut to match the flange face exactly; the bolt holes, inside diameter and outside diameter are marked accurately. Gasket cutting tools (gasket cutter, punch set) and templates are used. The inside diameter of the gasket must not be smaller than the inside diameter of the pipe and must not restrict the flow.
Flanş yüzeyleri eski conta kalıntısından: Flange faces are cleaned completely of old gasket residue, burrs and dirt. The new gasket is fitted dry or with the lubrication recommended by the manufacturer. Bolts are always tightened in a crosswise (star) sequence with the torque applied in stages; applying full torque in one go crushes the gasket and causes leakage. A torque wrench is mandatory on high-pressure/high-temperature joints.
Boru onarımında doğru ölçü almak işin ya: In pipe repairs, taking correct measurements is half the job. The Fitter determines the routing, diameter, wall thickness and material (steel, galvanized, copper-nickel, stainless) of the existing line. The pipe is cut with a pipe cutting machine or a grinder; after cutting, the end is reamed (deburring) to remove burrs and any internal obstruction to flow.
Kaynaklı bağlantı yapılacaksa kaynak ağz: If a welded joint is to be made, a weld bevel is prepared; for a flanged joint, the flange type (slip-on, weld-neck) and the pressure class are selected to match. On threaded joints, threads are cut (threading) and tightness is achieved with suitable flax/Teflon tape plus sealing compound.
Flanş yüzeyleri paralel ve hizalı olmalı: Flange faces must be parallel and aligned; a flange joined out of alignment strains the bolts and leaks. After the gasket has been fitted, the bolts are torqued in a crosswise sequence. Before being put back into service, a repaired pressure line is hydrostatically tested above its working pressure and its tightness is verified.
Geçici onarımlarda (acil sızıntı) boru k: For temporary repairs (an emergency leak), a pipe clamp or a cold repair kit may be used; however, these solutions are temporary and are replaced by a permanent welded/flanged repair at the first opportunity. The class society approves permanent repairs.
Fitter, atölye düzeyinde elektrik ark ka: At workshop level, the Fitter uses electric arc welding (MMA/stick) for tack welding, joining parts and simple repairs. The right electrode (according to material and position), the right current setting (according to electrode diameter) and a clean surface (free of rust/oil/paint) are the conditions for a good-quality weld. A damp electrode causes porosity; electrodes are kept dry.
Basınçlı sistem ve yapısal (structural): Welding on pressure systems and structural welding require an authorized/certified welder and generally class approval; the Fitter knows this limit and does not go beyond their authority. In critical repairs, weld quality may be verified by NDT (non-destructive testing).
Kalın metal kesimi için oksi-asetilen (g: Oxy-acetylene (gas cutting) or plasma cutting is used to cut thick metal. Cylinder pressures (oxygen/acetylene) and the flashback arrestors are checked; the acetylene cylinder is always kept upright. Before cutting, the surrounding area is made safe against fire.
Taşlama (grinding) işlemlerinde doğru di: For grinding work, the correct disc is used (a cutting disc for cutting, a grinding disc for grinding); a disc is never used for the wrong purpose (side grinding with a cutting disc causes the disc to burst). The expiry date of the disc and any cracks are checked, and the guard is never removed.
Torna, gemi atölyesinin en kullanışlı ma: The lathe is the most useful machine in the ship's workshop; it is used for machining shaft bearings, making bolts/studs, refacing gasket surfaces and repairing worn parts. The workpiece is centered correctly in the chuck; the chuck key is always removed after use (a key left in the chuck can be thrown out and kill). Cutting speed and feed are selected according to the material and the cutting tool.
Dönen tezgahta bol giysi, eldiven, krava: Loose clothing, gloves, ties, necklaces and loose sleeves are prohibited at a rotating machine; if they are caught by the workpiece, they can lead to the loss of an arm or fingers. Swarf is cleared with a brush/hook, never by hand; coolant (cutting fluid) is applied.
Matkap tezgahında (drill press) iş parça: On the drill press, the workpiece must always be secured with a vise/clamp; a part held by hand spins when the drill bit grabs it and is flung around like a whip, causing injury. The correct drill bit (HSS, suitable for the material), the correct speed and cooling are used. The machine is stopped to remove the bit.
Sabit taşlama tezgahında (bench grinder): On a bench grinder, the gap between the tool rest and the wheel is kept at ≤3 mm; otherwise the workpiece can jam in the gap. Work is done on the front face of the wheel, not on its side; a workpiece that overheats is cooled. A face shield and goggles are mandatory.
Mekanik bakımın kalitesi doğru ölçümle b: The quality of mechanical maintenance begins with correct measurement. The Fitter uses instruments such as calipers, micrometers, feeler gauges, dial gauges and bore gauges skillfully. Bearing clearances, shaft diameter, ovality (oval wear) and flatness are compared with the manufacturer's tolerances; a part outside the limits is replaced.
Ölçü aletleri hassas ekipmandır; düşürme: Measuring instruments are precision equipment; dropping them, letting them rust or storing them incorrectly spoils their calibration. A micrometer is zeroed before use and stored clean and oiled after use.
Onarılan ekipman devreye alınmadan önce: Repaired equipment is tested before it is put back into service: pumps undergo tightness and pressure tests, valves a tightness test, and welded/flanged lines a hydrostatic test. On first start-up (commissioning), vibration, noise, temperature and leaks are watched; the equipment is stopped immediately if there is any abnormality. Commissioning is carried out under the supervision of an engineer.
İş tamamlandığında kullanılan tüm alet,: When the job is finished, all tools, parts and consumables used are checked; a tool left behind in the work area (foreign object) can be caught by rotating equipment and cause damage or an accident. Cleaning and tidying up are an integral part of the job.
Fitter, kullandığı yedek parça ve sarf m: The Fitter updates the stock records of the spare parts and consumables used; the engineer is informed when items such as gasket sheet, O-ring sets, packing, bolts/studs, electrodes and grinding discs are running low. It is important that critical spares (the minimum spare parts required by class) never run out.
Atölye aletleri temiz, tam ve yerli yeri: Workshop tools are kept clean, complete and in their proper places. Damaged hand tools (a cracked hammer handle, a deformed wrench, a power tool with damaged insulation) are taken out of use; a bad tool is a source of both accidents and poor work.
Düzenli atölye güvenli atölyedir. Yağ/ta: A tidy workshop is a safe workshop. Oil/swarf is not allowed to build up on the floor (slip/fire risk), gas cylinders are secured with chains, electrical cables do not create trip hazards and heavy parts are stowed securely. Lighting must be adequate and ventilation (for welding fumes) must be in working order.
Fitter'ın ustalığı; ölçü disiplini, doğr: The Fitter's craftsmanship comes down to measurement discipline, choosing the right materials, uncompromising compliance with safety rules and clean workmanship. A well-made gasket change or valve overhaul goes unnoticed; a badly made one shows itself through leaks, breakdowns and even fire. That is why, for the Fitter, "correct and safe" always comes before "fast".
Makine dairesi yangınlarının büyük çoğun: Most engine room fires start when a pressurized oil/fuel leak sprays onto a hot surface (>220°C) such as an exhaust manifold, a turbine casing or a steam line. Oil accumulated on the floor and on equipment becomes the fuel for this fire, which then spreads rapidly. A clean engine room removes this fire load.
Aynı şekilde yağlı zemin, kayma-düşme ka: Likewise, an oily floor is the main cause of slip-and-fall accidents; slipping on ladders and platforms leads to serious injuries. By cleaning up oil deposits immediately, the Wiper reduces both the fire risk and the accident risk. For this reason, the Wiper's job is low in rank but of high importance for safety.
Silici; zeminler (floor plates), ekipman: The Wiper is responsible for a wide area covering floors (floor plates), equipment surfaces, handrails, ladders, platforms, drip trays, save-all trays and bilge wells. The Wiper also keeps track of the stock of cleaning materials and helps with waste oil/sludge management.
Bu görevler, vardiya turlarıyla iç içe y: These tasks are carried out together with the watch rounds; while cleaning, the Wiper also looks out for leaks, loose connections and abnormalities, and reports anything noticed to the engineer or the Oiler. In this way, cleaning is also an early-warning activity.
Çelik ızgara zeminler (floor plates) ve: Steel grating floors (floor plates) and platforms are degreased regularly. The oil is dissolved using hot water, detergent/degreaser and a brush, and the surface is rinsed so that it does not become slippery. Deposits that fall between the gratings are also cleaned out; otherwise oil is carried down into the bilge below.
Kullanılan temizlik malzemesi (degreaser: The cleaning agent (degreaser) is chosen correctly; some aggressive chemicals damage paint/seals/metal surfaces and pose a respiratory hazard. When chemicals are used, the MSDS is read, gloves and eye protection are worn and ventilation is provided.
Makine, pompa ve boru yüzeyleri temiz tu: When machinery, pump and pipe surfaces are kept clean, a new leak (weeping) is noticed immediately; clean equipment is therefore also a diagnostic tool. During cleaning, electrical panels, cable connections and hot surfaces are not exposed to water/chemicals.
Boru hatları renk koduyla işaretlidir (y: Pipelines are marked with a color code (fire line red, sea water green, etc.); cleaning helps keep these markings readable. If a loose bolt, cracked insulation or corrosion is noticed on a surface being wiped, it is reported to the engineer.
Sintine kuyuları (bilge wells), makine d: Bilge wells are the places at the lowest point of the engine room where leaking water, oil and dirt collect. If they are not cleaned regularly, an oil-water mixture builds up, causes odors and makes the bilge alarms/sensors malfunction. The Wiper cleans the well strainers and collects the deposits properly.
Sintinedeki yüzen yağ, sintine pompası ç: Oil floating in the bilge risks getting into the sea when the bilge pump runs; oily bilge contents must therefore first be passed through the oil separator (OWS — Oily Water Separator) or transferred to the sludge tank. The Wiper collects leaks at their source so that excess oil is not carried into the bilge.
Makine, pompa ve filtre altlarındaki dri: The drip trays and save-all trays under machinery, pumps and filters are designed to collect leaking oil; however, when they become full, they overflow and stop doing their job. The Wiper empties these trays regularly and keeps them clean. The oil removed is always transferred to the sludge/waste oil tank and is never mixed into the bilge or the sea.
Tepsideki birikinti, gizli bir sızıntını: Deposits in a tray are a clue to a hidden leak; their origin is traced and the source is reported to the engineer. A tray that keeps filling up points to a leak that needs to be fixed.
Makine dairesi merdivenleri dik ve metal: Engine room ladders are steep and made of metal; a film of oil on them leads to serious falls. The Wiper gives priority to keeping ladder steps, handrails and walkways clean and dry, and checks that anti-slip surfaces remain effective.
Geçiş yollarında engel (hortum, kablo, a: No obstacles (hoses, cables, tools, parts) are left on walkways; tripping accidents are at least as common as slipping. Good housekeeping means both cleanliness and order.
Gemi yalpa/baş-kıç vururken kayma riski: When the ship is rolling/pitching, the risk of slipping multiplies; in bad weather the Wiper gives cleaning priority to the walkways and works on the principle of "one hand always on a handhold". A wet/oily floor may be marked with a warning sign, but the real solution is to dry the floor quickly.
Separatör (purifier) sludge'ı, drip tray: Separator (purifier) sludge, drip tray deposits, filter oil and oil from the oily bilge are collected in the sludge/waste oil tank. The Wiper directs these flows to the correct tank and helps monitor the tank levels. When the tank is full, the engineer is informed; delivery ashore or burning in the ship's incinerator is planned.
MARPOL Annex I, tüm bu işlemlerin Oil Re: MARPOL Annex I requires all these operations to be recorded in the Oil Record Book (ORB Part I); the quantities delivered/incinerated, the tank levels and the dates must be consistent. The Wiper provides observation and on-site support for these operations; the accuracy of the records is the engineer's responsibility.
İnsineratör (incinerator) ile atık yağ/s: When waste oil/sludge is burned in the incinerator, the Wiper provides feeding and cleaning support under the engineer's supervision. During delivery ashore (shore disposal), the Wiper helps with anti-pollution measures such as hose connections, drip trays and plugging the scuppers. The receipt (waste receipt) issued for each delivery is kept.
Silici, temizlik malzemelerinin (degreas: The Wiper keeps track of the stock of cleaning materials (degreaser, detergent, rags, absorbent pads, brushes, gloves, garbage bags) and informs the engineer when stocks run low, so that nothing is missing from the port supply order (requisition). Chemicals are stored in their original/labeled containers, with their MSDSs kept accessible.
Kimyasalların depolanması güvenlik kural: The storage of chemicals is subject to safety rules; flammable solvents are kept in a ventilated place away from heat/sparks. Incompatible chemicals are stored separately. Empty containers are disposed of properly.
Temizlikte kullanılan PPE (kimyasal eldi: The stock of PPE used for cleaning (chemical gloves, goggles, a mask where necessary) is also monitored; worn/damaged PPE is replaced. The right job is done with the right materials — for example, near an electrical panel a dry method is preferred instead of wet cleaning.
Silici, temizlik yaparken güvenlik ayakk: When cleaning, the Wiper wears safety shoes, gloves, goggles and, where necessary, ear protection (engine room noise). The Wiper keeps clear of hot surfaces, moving/rotating equipment and electrical systems; cleaning these points may require the equipment to be stopped or isolated.
Dar/kapalı alanda (bilge, tank top altı): If cleaning is to be done in a confined/enclosed space (bilge, below the tank top), the enclosed space procedure is applied — no entry without gas measurement, a permit and standby personnel. The Wiper knows the limits of their authority and consults the engineer when in doubt.
Temizlikten doğan atık (yağlı su, kimyas: Waste from cleaning (oily water, chemical residue, oily rags) is never thrown into the sea or onto the open deck; it is segregated in accordance with the ship's waste management plan (Garbage Management Plan, MARPOL Annex V) and the oily waste procedure. Even with a small act, the Wiper can protect or damage the ship's pollution record.
Silici'nin işi rütbece mütevazı olsa da: Although the Wiper's job is modest in rank, it is critical for safety; a clean and tidy engine room directly reduces the risk of fire and accidents, allows faults to be noticed early and is the first indicator of the ship's professionalism during inspections. A good Wiper is someone who sees cleaning as a safety duty.
Yakıt ve yağ sistemlerine kontaminasyon: Contamination enters fuel and oil systems in three ways: from outside (solids/water received during bunkering, air intake), from inside (wear metal, gasket remnants, rust) and from chemical breakdown (oxidation, thermal degradation). If these particles are not caught by filters, they lead to costly failures such as injector nozzle wear, bearing scoring, pump impeller erosion and sticking valves.
Gemi makine dairesinde duplex (çift koll: The engine room has duplex (twin, allowing uninterrupted changeover), simplex (single), automatic backwash (auto-backwash), self-cleaning and magnetic filters. Duplex filters are standard on the main fuel/oil lines; while one side is being cleaned, the other remains in service and the engine does not stop.
Filtreler genelde pompa basma tarafında: Filters are generally installed in two stages: on the pump discharge side (fine filter) and on the suction side (suction strainer / coarse filter). The Oiler must know by heart the location of each filter, its mesh size, the direction of the changeover lever and the drain/vent valves.
Her ana filtrede bir diferansiyel basınç: Every main filter has a differential pressure (DP) gauge, which shows the difference between the filter inlet and outlet pressures. On a clean filter the DP is low; as particles accumulate, the DP rises. When the threshold set by the manufacturer (e.g. 0.8-1.5 bar) is exceeded, the filter is cleaned or replaced.
Yağcı, DP değerini her turda not eder ve: The Oiler notes the DP value on every round and monitors its trend. A sudden jump in DP (within hours) is usually a sign of dirty fuel after bunkering or of an in-line fault; a slow rise is normal build-up. When the bypass valve opens, the filter is taken out of action and dirty fluid goes to the engine — this is never regarded as normal.
Changeover, makineyi durdurmadan yapılan: Changeover is a critical operation carried out without stopping the engine. First, the side that is not to be cleaned (the new side) is vented to remove air and slowly equalized with the line; then the changeover lever is turned to direct the flow to the new side. The dirty side is isolated, its pressure is drained and the cover is opened.
Kapak açılırken sıcak yakıt/yağ fışkırma: There is a risk of hot fuel/oil spraying out when the cover is opened; it is therefore verified that the pressure has been fully released, a drip tray is placed and suitable PPE (gloves, goggles) is worn. The cartridge is removed and its contents are examined (metal swarf, water or unusual residue is reported to the engineer), a new/clean cartridge is fitted, the O-ring is checked and the lever is left in the "standby" position.
Ağır yakıt (HFO/RMG) yüksek viskoziteli: Heavy fuel oil (HFO/RMG) has a high viscosity and carries a heavy load of contaminants; it contains cat fines (aluminum-silicon particles), water, sludge and asphaltenes. For this reason, HFO systems are protected by a combination of purifier + booster + fine filter. When dismantling an HFO filter, the Oiler knows that the fuel is heated (60-90°C) and viscous, and that it will solidify as it cools.
Cat fines özellikle tehlikelidir; enjeks: Cat fines are particularly dangerous; they wear the surfaces of the injection pump and nozzle like sandpaper. If the Al+Si value in the bunker specification is close to the ISO 8217 limit (60 mg/kg), purifier and filter maintenance is carried out more frequently. If shiny, sand-like particles are seen in the filter contents, the engineer must always be informed.
Yağlama sisteminde full-flow filtre tüm: In the lubricating oil system, the full-flow filter filters the entire oil flow, while the bypass (partial-flow) filter keeps the oil clean by continuously passing a small portion of it through a fine filter. Auto-backwash filters discharge the dirt they have caught to the sludge side during backflushing; if the backflush frequency is increasing, oil contamination has increased.
LO kartuş değişiminde changeover yapılır: When an LO cartridge is changed, a changeover is made and the old cartridge is examined. Particles of bearing metal (white metal/babbitt, bronze, steel) are a sign of early bearing wear and are cross-checked against the OMD/oil analysis. The Oiler photographs the finding and passes it on to the engineer.
Büyük iki zamanlı makinelerde sistem yağ: In large two-stroke engines, the system oil is generally not changed completely; it is cleaned continuously by the purifier and refreshed by topping up. The oil properties (TBN, viscosity, water) are monitored by analysis; if they go outside the limits, a partial or complete change is planned. In four-stroke auxiliary engines, however, the oil is changed completely more often (according to PMS running hours).
Yağ değişimi planlanırken eski yağın boş: When an oil change is planned, the old oil is drained, the system is flushed, new oil of the correct grade and quantity is filled and the level is verified. The drained oil never goes to the bilge; it is transferred to the waste oil/sludge tank and entered in the ORB.
Yağ analizi ancak doğru alınmış numune k: Oil analysis is only as reliable as the sample taken. The sample is taken while the engine is running and the oil is hot, from a representative point of the system (usually a dedicated sampling cock on the circulation line). First, the line is flushed for a few seconds (stagnant oil is discarded), then the clean sample bottle is filled.
Numune şişesi temiz, kuru ve doğru etike: The sample bottle must be clean, dry and correctly labeled: ship's name, engine, date, running hours, oil grade, last top-up information. A sample exposed to contamination (dirty funnel, wet bottle) gives a wrong result and causes unnecessary alarm/cost.
Onboard hızlı test kitleri (su tespiti i: Onboard quick test kits (crackle test/hot plate for detecting water, a titration kit for TBN, a Karl Fischer-type kit for water) allow an immediate assessment, while laboratory analysis gives the definitive result. The two are used together.
Türboşarjer (T/C) emiş tarafındaki hava: The air filter/silencer (air filter silencer) on the intake side of the turbocharger (T/C) protects the compressor blades from dust and engine room contamination. A dirty filter reduces the air flow; this lowers the scavenge pressure, raises exhaust temperatures and impairs fuel efficiency. The filter panel is washed or replaced periodically.
Yağcı, T/C filtresinin yağ banyolu (oil-: The Oiler knows whether the T/C filter is of the oil-bath or dry type; on the oil-bath type, the oil level and cleanliness are checked. When the filter is cleaned, the greatest care is taken that no foreign object falls into the compressor inlet.
Kontrol havası (control air) ve start ha: The control air and starting air systems have air dryers and filters, which remove moisture and oil vapor. Damp control air leads to valve and actuator failures, and to corrosion in the starting air bottles. The air bottles are drained daily to remove condensate.
Purifier (santrifüj separatör), filtrede: The purifier (centrifugal separator) is the main cleaning stage that comes before the filter; it separates water and solid particles from the fuel/oil by centrifugal force. Filters catch the remaining dirt that the purifier misses. If purifier efficiency falls, the load on the filter increases and the DP rises quickly; the two are therefore assessed together.
Yağcı, purifier'ın desludging (çamur atm: The Oiler monitors the purifier's desludging (sludge discharge) timing, the feed temperature (~98°C for HFO), the gravity disc (dam ring) selection and the operating water system. Detailed separator maintenance is a separate task; here the Oiler provides operational support and daily monitoring.
Filtre temizliği, purifier desludging, d: Waste from filter cleaning, purifier desludging, emptying of drip trays and oil changes is collected in the sludge/waste oil tank. Under MARPOL Annex I, these fluids are classified as "oily residue (sludge)" and must not be discharged into the sea; they are disposed of by delivery to a shore facility (shore disposal) or by burning in the ship's incinerator (incineration).
Yağcı, her transfer ve bertaraf işlemini: The Oiler reports every transfer and disposal operation to the engineer so that it is entered in Oil Record Book Part I with the correct codes; tank levels, transferred quantities and operation times are recorded. ORB inconsistencies are among the most frequent PSC findings and lead to detention of the ship.
Kullanılmış yağ/yakıt filtre kartuşları: Used oil/fuel filter cartridges are oil-soaked waste and must not be thrown into the garbage at random. The oil is drained off (into the sludge tank), and the cartridge is suitably packaged and landed ashore under garbage/oily rag management. Oily rags and gloves are also kept in a closed metal container — there is a risk of spontaneous combustion.
En yaygın hata, changeover sırasında yen: The most common mistake is putting the new side into service during a changeover without venting it; an air pocket lowers the oil/fuel pressure and puts the engine at risk. The second common mistake is closing the cover without renewing the O-ring/gasket; this creates a risk of hot oil leakage and fire. The third is using oil of the wrong grade or a filter with the wrong mesh.
Numune alırken hattı flush etmemek, kirl: Not flushing the line when taking a sample, using a dirty bottle or filling in the label wrongly spoils the analysis result and leads to wrong decisions. Accidentally mixing drained oil into the bilge is a direct violation of MARPOL.
Bir gemide bunker sonrası purifier verim: On one ship, purifier efficiency dropped after bunkering; the Oiler noticed shiny, sand-like particles in the LO/FO filter contents and informed the engineer. A fuel analysis showed a high Al+Si value (cat fines); purifier maintenance was made more frequent, the filter changeover interval was shortened and the injection equipment was protected from premature wear. Had this not been detected, nozzle and pump erosion would have been unavoidable.
Filtre ve yağ işleri tekrarlayan ama asl: Filter and oil jobs are repetitive, but they must never be treated as mere routine. Disciplined changeovers, correct sampling, careful examination of filter contents and meticulous waste management protect both the engine and the environment. A good Oiler is not someone who simply changes a filter, but someone who reads what comes out of it and diagnoses the health of the engine.
Makine dairesinde tehlikeler katmanlıdır: Hazards in the engine room come in layers: physical (noise, vibration, temperature, pressure), mechanical (rotating shafts, belts, couplings, rotating machine tools), chemical (fuel vapor, oil, coolant, cleaning chemicals, battery acid), electrical (high-voltage panels) and atmospheric (O₂ deficiency in enclosed spaces, toxic/flammable gas). Each type requires its own control method.
Sıcak yüzeyler (egzoz manifoldu, türbin: Hot surfaces (exhaust manifold, turbine casing, steam line) exceed 200°C; in contact with a flammable liquid, they become the source of engine room fires (the most frequent type of fire). Noise in most engine rooms is in the range of 85-110 dB(A) and carries a risk of permanent hearing loss. The Oiler keeps this layout in mind and assesses the relevant hazards before starting any job.
Riskler bir öncelik sırasıyla kontrol ed: Risks are controlled in order of priority: first removing the hazard (elimination), then substitution, engineering controls (guarding, ventilation, isolation), administrative controls (procedures, training, permits) and finally PPE. PPE is the weakest defense because it depends on the individual and can fail; it is therefore regarded as the "last line of defense".
Pratikte Yağcı, bir işe başlamadan \"bu: In practice, before starting a job the Oiler asks: "how can I control this hazard at the highest level?" For example, isolating and cooling down a hot line (engineering) is always better than relying on PPE. PPE covers the risk that remains after the higher controls have been applied.
Permit to Work (PTW), yüksek riskli işle: Permit to Work (PTW) is a formal system that ensures high-risk work is carried out in a controlled and authorized manner. Separate permits are issued for hot work, enclosed space entry, electrical isolation, working at height and overside work. The permit documents the hazards, the precautions taken, the persons responsible and the period of validity.
Yağcı/Fitter, PTW kapsamındaki bir işe i: The Oiler/Fitter does not start a job covered by the PTW before the permit has been signed. The permit is usually issued by the responsible engineer; the person doing the work reads, understands and applies the precautions in the permit. When the job is finished, the permit is closed (sign-off); a permit is not left open without the area having been made safe.
Her yüksek riskli iş öncesi toolbox meet: A toolbox meeting (on-site briefing) is held before every high-risk job; the steps of the job, the hazards, the precautions, the allocation of tasks and the emergency plan are discussed with the participants. The risk assessment form documents the hazards and controls in writing; the question "what can go wrong, and how do I prevent it?" is answered systematically.
Yağcı, toolbox meeting'te aktif rol alır: The Oiler takes an active part in the toolbox meeting and, drawing on experience, raises hazards that may have been overlooked (e.g. a hot surface on an adjacent line, difficulty of escape from a confined space). A good briefing turns the risk assessment on paper into real safety.
Lock-Out/Tag-Out (LOTO), bir ekipman üze: Lock-Out/Tag-Out (LOTO) is the procedure that prevents equipment from starting or becoming energized unexpectedly while work is being done on it. The electrical supply is isolated, valves are closed and pressure is released; these isolation points are then secured with a lock, and a tag with the warning "work in progress, do not operate!" is attached. The key of the lock stays with the person doing the work.
Enerji sadece elektrik değildir: hidroli: Energy is not only electrical: hydraulic/pneumatic pressure, steam, spring tension, heat and gravity (a suspended load) are also "stored energy". Before dismantling a pump, the Oiler both isolates/locks out its electrical supply and closes the suction/discharge valves and drains the line; otherwise back pressure or an inadvertent start can cause serious injury.
İzolasyon yapıldıktan sonra \"sıfır ener: After isolation, "zero energy" is verified: the start button is pressed to test that the equipment really does not start (try-out), the pressure gauge reads zero and rotating parts have stopped. If this step is skipped, someone may put their hands on equipment that appears to be isolated but is in fact energized.
Makine dairesinde temel PPE her zaman gi: Basic PPE is always worn in the engine room: steel-toe safety shoes (non-slip soles), coveralls (non-flammable/cotton, not loose-fitting), a safety helmet (falling objects/impact) and, in the engine room, hearing protection. Job-specific PPE is added on top: a face shield and leather apron for welding/grinding, chemical gloves for chemicals, heat-resistant gloves for hot work.
PPE doğru seçilmeli, doğru takılmalı ve: PPE must be correctly selected, correctly worn and in good condition. Worn-out PPE, or PPE of the wrong size or class, gives no protection. The Oiler checks PPE before use (cracked goggles, torn gloves or a defective mask are not used) and selects the correct type.
İşitme koruması (kulak tıkacı veya manşo: Hearing protection (earplugs or earmuffs) is mandatory in the engine room when noise is above 85 dB(A), and it is worn continuously in the main engine area. As the exposure time increases or the level rises, a higher attenuation rating (SNR) is required. Hearing loss is insidious; by the time it is noticed, it is permanent.
Göz koruması kıvılcım, sıçrayan sıvı ve: Eye protection is used against sparks, splashing liquids and dust, and respiratory protection against dust, fumes and chemical vapors. Respiratory protection is selected according to the MSDS/risk assessment; a dust mask does not stop gas — for gas, a mask with a suitable filter or an air-supplied system is needed. In an enclosed space, only SCBA/SAA is safe.
Kaynak, kesme (oksi-asetilen, plazma), t: Hot work such as welding, cutting (oxy-acetylene, plasma), grinding and open flames is the work with the highest risk of fire and explosion. The hot work permit documents that the area has been cleared of combustible materials, that a gas test has been carried out (especially around tanks/fuel), that firefighting equipment is ready and that a fire watch has been assigned.
Yağcı/Fitter, sıcak çalışma yapacağı ala: The Oiler/Fitter prepares the area where the hot work is to be done: removes combustible materials, cleans up oil/fuel leaks, checks adjacent compartments (sparks can pass through openings), sets up a fire blanket/curtain and keeps an extinguisher and a hose at hand. In a confined/enclosed space, ventilation is essential, as welding gases can accumulate.
Yangın gözcüsü (fire watch), sıcak çalış: The fire watch is the person who watches the area during and after the hot work.
