The fire watch's duty is to detect at an early stage any hidden fire caused by sparks/heat, to be ready to use the extinguisher and to raise the alarm if necessary. The fire watch is not occupied with any other work; their only task is to keep watch.
Sıcak çalışma bittikten sonra gözetim he: Monitoring does not stop as soon as the hot work is finished; the area continues to be watched for half an hour to several hours (depending on the risk), because heat can remain hidden and cause delayed ignition. The back face of the welded metal, adjacent compartments and the area under insulation are checked in particular.
Yağcı, \"sadece bir bakayım\" diyerek iz: The Oiler never enters an enclosed space without a permit just to "take a quick look". Many deaths in the past have occurred when a second or third person rushing to rescue someone who had entered without a permit suffocated in the same atmosphere. Ventilation is kept running continuously and measurements are repeated throughout the entry.
Her kapalı alan girişinde dışarıda bir s: For every enclosed space entry, there is a standby person outside who keeps in continuous communication with the person inside, tends the lifeline and, in an emergency, raises the alarm and starts the rescue. The rescue plan is prepared in advance: rescue equipment (tripod, winch, harness, SCBA) is ready and the rescue route is kept clear.
Torna, matkap, taşlama tezgahı ve dönen: Loose clothing, gloves (gloves can be caught on a rotating tool), jewelry and long hair are dangerous near lathes, drills, grinders and rotating shafts/couplings; they can get caught and tear off a limb. Guards are never removed; the workpiece is clamped securely.
Yağcı, döner tezgahta çalışırken talaş i: When working at a rotating machine, the Oiler uses a face shield/goggles against swarf, never takes measurements or cleans without stopping the machine, and knows where the emergency stop button is. Checking the grinding wheel for cracks/wear and using it at the correct speed prevents the risk of it bursting.
Makine dairesinde yüksek gerilim panolar: There are high-voltage panels and circuits in the engine room. The Oiler/Fitter does not undertake electrical work for which they are not authorized; electrical work is done by an authorized person after isolation, locking and testing (LOTO + voltage test). Using power tools on a wet floor, damaged cables and unearthed equipment carry a risk of electric shock.
Yorgunluk, dikkat ve refleksi düşürerek: Fatigue increases the risk of accidents by reducing attention and reflexes. STCW A-VIII/1 and MLC 2006 make minimum hours of rest mandatory (at least 10 hours in any 24 hours, at least 77 hours in any 7 days). When fatigued, the Oiler does not start critical/high-risk work and reports the situation to the engineer.
Her gemiadamının, güvensiz bir durum gör: Every seafarer has the right (and the duty) to stop work when they see an unsafe situation. When a job becomes unsafe (missing permit, defective PPE, an unexpected hazard), the Oiler stops the job and informs the engineer; this is not "cowardice" but professionalism. No commercial/time pressure overrides this right.
Makine dairesinde tipik yaralanmalar: ya: Typical injuries in the engine room are burns (hot surfaces/steam/fluids), cuts/crushing (tools, rotating equipment), eye injuries (swarf/chemical splashes), chemical contact and electric shock. The Oiler knows where the nearest first-aid cabinet, eye wash and emergency shower are.
Kimyasal göz/cilt temasında derhal bol s: In case of chemical contact with the eyes/skin, the area is washed immediately with plenty of water (eye wash/shower), the first-aid instructions in the MSDS are followed and the person in charge of medical care is informed. In a serious injury, the scene is first made safe (energy isolation) and only then is the casualty attended to; a second victim must not be created.
Her kaza, yaralanma ve ramak kala (near-: Every accident, injury and near-miss is reported. A near-miss is an "it almost happened" situation and a free warning of a future accident. The Oiler reports without fear any dangerous situation seen or near-miss experienced; the aim is a learning culture, not a blame culture.
İş güvenliği, bir prosedür dosyası değil: Occupational safety is not a file of procedures but a working culture. The safety of the Oiler/Fitter depends on recognizing hazards, complying with the permit system, isolating energy, using the correct PPE and the "stop and ask" discipline. The safest job in the engine room is one that is never rushed, is covered by a permit, is isolated and has someone keeping watch. Getting home safe and sound is the one priority ahead of every task.
Muster list (station bill), her acil dur: The muster list (station bill) sets out where each person goes and what they do in each type of emergency (fire, flooding, abandon ship, man overboard). The duties of the Oiler/Fitter are generally engine-room-focused, such as fire party membership, boundary cooling, operating the emergency generator/pump or closing shut-off valves.
Yağcı, kendi muster station'ını, görev r: The Oiler knows by heart their own muster station, their role, the equipment they are to carry (e.g. nozzle, hose, SCBA) and their alternative duty (if the person originally assigned is absent). The muster list is posted on the board, but real readiness means being able to carry out one's duty without looking at the paper.
Genel acil durum alarmı (general emergen: The general emergency alarm is a signal of seven short blasts plus one long blast on the whistle/bells; it calls everyone to the muster station. The fire alarm, the abandon ship signal and other signals are defined in the SMS. To be sure of noticing an alarm in the high noise of the engine room, the Oiler also watches the visual alarm beacons and follows telephone/UHF communication.
Acil durumda iletişim disiplinlidir: köp: Communication in an emergency is disciplined: the bridge (command), the engine control room and the teams on scene coordinate by UHF/internal telephone. The Oiler reports observations (location of the fire, spread, smoke) clearly and briefly and does not give vague messages that could cause panic.
Makine dairesi yangınlarının çoğunluğu,: Most engine room fires start when a pressurized fuel/oil leak sprays onto a hot surface (exhaust manifold, turbine casing >220°C). Fuel sprayed as a fine mist ignites instantly. By catching leaks early (routine rounds), the Oiler prevents a fire before it starts; this is the first defense.
Yangın çıktığında ilk adımlar: alarmı ve: When a fire breaks out, the first steps are: raise the alarm, report the location of the fire, cut off the fuel source if possible (quick-closing valve, stop the pump) and make a first attack with a portable extinguisher (if trained and if it is safe). If the fire grows, the engine room is evacuated so that the fixed system can be used.
İlk müdahalede doğru söndürücü seçilir:: For the first response, the correct extinguisher is selected: for oil/fuel fires (class B), foam or dry chemical powder; for electrical fires (C/E), CO₂ or dry powder; water is not sprayed directly onto a liquid fuel fire (it spreads the flames). The Oiler knows the types of extinguisher, their range and how to use them (PASS: pull-aim-squeeze-sweep).
Yangın büyükse yangın hortumuyla müdahal: If the fire is large, it is attacked with a fire hose; the fog setting gives both protection and extinguishing. The fire party advances in pairs, the retreat route is kept open and the team withdraws when heat/smoke increases. No one enters a smoke-filled space without SCBA.
Makine dairesi yangını kontrol edilemezs: If an engine room fire cannot be controlled, the fixed CO₂ total flooding system is activated. This system extinguishes the fire by smothering it of oxygen; however, CO₂ is lethal to people. For this reason, before release, the engine room is completely evacuated, a head count is made and all openings (ventilation flaps, doors) are closed.
CO₂ salımı iki kademeli güvenlik kontrol: CO₂ release requires a two-stage safety control (first alarm/time delay, then release); the authorized person (usually with the approval of the Chief Engineer/Master) gives the order. After release, the engine room is kept closed for a certain time (to prevent re-ignition) and is entered only with SCBA and after a gas test.
Modern gemilerde su sisi (water mist) ve: On modern ships, water mist and local application foam systems tackle a fire around the ME/AE/incinerator without the engine room having to be evacuated. Water mist works through both cooling and oxygen dilution and is less hazardous than CO₂. The Oiler knows the manual release points of these systems and the areas they cover.
Yangın bir bölmede kontrol altına alınma: While a fire in one compartment is being brought under control, the boundary bulkheads and decks of the adjacent compartments heat up; this heat can cause the fire to spread and combustible materials in the adjacent space to ignite. Boundary cooling is the task of cooling the surfaces surrounding the compartment on fire by spraying them with water.
Yangının kontrol edildiği veya yayıldığı: Whether the fire is being controlled or is spreading is assessed continuously. If a boundary bulkhead is too hot to touch by hand, the fire is at risk of spreading to the adjacent space; cooling is intensified or the area is evacuated. The boundary cooling team works in coordination with the main fire team and reports the situation to the command center.
Makine dairesi tahliye/CO₂ salımı öncesi: Before the engine room is evacuated and CO₂ released, the remotely operated emergency shutdowns are activated: the quick-closing valves of the fuel service/settling tanks are closed (cutting off the fuel supply), the fuel transfer/booster pumps, ventilation fans and purifiers are stopped remotely, and the ventilation flaps/dampers are closed. These are generally operated from a panel/box outside the engine room.
Yağcı, bu acil kapatma noktalarının (eme: The Oiler knows by heart where these emergency shutdown points (emergency stop and QCV control boxes) are and can find them in the dark/in smoke. These shutdowns cut the fire off from fuel and air, so that the fixed system can be effective.
Makine dairesinin en az iki ayrı kaçış y: The engine room has at least two separate means of escape, at least one of which is protected (escape trunk). The Oiler knows by heart the normal and alternative escape routes, the locations of the EEBDs (Emergency Escape Breathing Device) and the emergency lighting. An EEBD provides ~10-15 minutes of breathing for escape from a smoke-filled space; it is used for escape, not for firefighting.
Tahliye sırasında panik değil disiplin e: When evacuating, discipline, not panic, is essential: the space is left by the shortest safe route, it is verified that no one has been left behind (head count) and doors are closed behind. By keeping the escape route free of obstacles (housekeeping) in normal times, the Oiler makes this moment easier in advance.
Blackout, tüm jeneratörlerin devre dışı: A blackout is the loss of the ship's electrical power when all generators drop off line; the main engine stops, the steering gear and pumps do not work, and the ship loses navigational control. This is a very dangerous situation, especially in confined waters/during maneuvering. The emergency generator starts automatically and supplies the critical consumers (steering gear, emergency lighting, communications).
Yağcı, blackout anında sahada gözlem yap: At the moment of a blackout, the Oiler observes on site and gives the engineer real-time information: which generator tripped, what the alarm is, the state of fuel/oil pressure. The Oiler verifies that the emergency generator has started and that the emergency switchboard is energized.
Blackout recovery, jeneratörleri ve ana: Blackout recovery is the process of bringing the generators and the main engine back into service step by step. The engineer starts the standby generator, energizes the busbar and loads the consumers in sequence; the main engine is restarted. The Oiler provides on-site support in re-establishing pumps, lubrication and cooling, monitors fuel/starting air pressure and carries out the engineer's instructions.
Recovery sırasında start havası tüplerin: During recovery, the adequacy of the starting air bottles is critical; repeated start attempts use up starting air. The Oiler monitors the air compressors and the air pressure. During recovery, each action is taken in sequence and on the engineer's order.
Makine dairesine su girişi; deniz suyu h: Water may enter the engine room as a result of a burst sea water line, a sea chest/valve failure, hull damage, a crack in a cooling line or back-flooding. The bilge high-level alarm gives early warning. When the Oiler notices water ingress, they immediately raise the alarm, try to identify the source (which valve/line) and isolate it if possible.
İlk müdahale: kaynağı kes/izole et (valf: First response: cut off/isolate the source (close the valve), start the bilge/ballast pumps and, if necessary, use the emergency bilge suction (the main sea water pump drawing directly from the bilge). The aim is to bring the water level under control before it reaches electrical panels/machinery.
Su basması hem makine kaybı hem stabilit: Flooding is a risk of both loss of machinery and loss of stability; the free surface reduces GM and can capsize the ship. Flooding is therefore managed at the same time as a technical matter (pumping out water) and as a stability matter (coordination with the bridge). The Oiler continuously reports the water level and the pumping rate to the engineer.
Makine dairesi yangınında ana yangın pom: In an engine room fire, the main fire pump may be unusable; in that case the emergency fire pump, located outside the engine room and with its own power source, is started and pressurizes the fire main. The Oiler knows the location of the emergency fire pump, its starting procedure and its suction line.
Dümen sistemi arızasında emergency steer: In the event of a steering system failure, the emergency steering procedure is applied; steering is controlled from the steering gear room by manual/local control, in coordination with the bridge by telephone/signals. The Oiler knows their duty at this position and the emergency steering drills.
Terk gemi (abandon ship) durumunda Yağcı: In an abandon ship situation, the Oiler, according to their role in the muster list, helps with preparing the lifeboats/liferafts, carrying portable equipment or the head count. In a man overboard situation, the engine is kept ready for maneuvering; the Oiler carries out their maneuvering support duty in the engine room.
Yağcı, her drill'i kendi görevini gerçek: The Oiler sees every drill as an opportunity to rehearse their own duty as if it were a real emergency: time taken to find the equipment, donning SCBA, closing valves, the escape route. Deficiencies identified in the debrief after the drill (equipment failure, unclear duties) are reported and corrected.
Acil durumda kullanılacak ekipmanın yeri: The location and use of the equipment needed in an emergency are learned in normal times: SCBA, EEBD, portable extinguishers, fire stations, emergency stop and QCV boxes, escape routes, emergency generator/pump. A newly joined Oiler learns these points by walking round them at the first opportunity after joining the ship (familiarization), and this is recorded.
Acil durumda Yağcı/Fitter'ın değeri, pan: In an emergency, the value of the Oiler/Fitter lies in relying on procedure, not on panic. Cutting off the fuel source, choosing the right extinguisher, evacuating with discipline and giving the engineer a clear report stop a small incident before it turns into a disaster. The best emergency response is the routine round that prevents a fire before it starts; the best way out is an escape route kept clear in normal times. Preparedness is gained long before the moment of crisis, not during it.
Makine dairesinde kullanılan başlıca kal: The main lifting equipment used in the engine room comprises chain blocks / lever hoists, overhead travelling cranes and monorails (overhead crane above the ME), wire rope slings, chain slings, textile/web slings (polyester webbing slings), shackles, eye bolts and trolleys. Each has its own SWL, limits of use and inspection criteria.
Bu ekipmanlar bir \"kaldırma planı\" çer: This equipment is used together within a "lifting plan": the load is attached with the correct sling and shackle, lifted with a chain block or crane, and moved with a trolley. The weakest link in the chain determines the strength of the whole system; each component must therefore be sound in its own right.
SWL (Safe Working Load) veya WLL (Workin: SWL (Safe Working Load) or WLL (Working Load Limit) is the maximum load that a piece of equipment can lift safely, and it is marked/labeled on the equipment. This value is obtained by dividing the breaking load of the equipment by a safety factor (usually 4:1, 5:1, or 7:1 for textile slings). The SWL is never exceeded.
Sling'lerde efektif SWL, kullanım açısın: For slings, the effective SWL decreases with the sling angle; as the slings move away from the vertical (as the angle increases), the load in each leg increases. In multi-leg slinging, the Oiler allows for the angle factor; a wide angle (>120°) is very dangerous. If the SWL label cannot be read, the equipment is not used.
Çelik tel sapanlar zamanla yorulur ve ha: Wire rope slings fatigue and become damaged over time. Defects looked for during inspection: broken wires, kinks (permanent bends/loops), bird-caging (wires opening out like a cage), excessive wear, corrosion (rust), heat damage (discoloration) and damage at the eye/termination area (ferrule/splice). A specified number of broken wires (ISO 4309 criteria) takes the equipment out of service.
Yağcı, sapanı boylu boyunca elle (eldive: The Oiler checks the sling along its full length by hand (wearing gloves) and by eye; broken wires prick, and kinks can be felt by hand. If an oily rag is run along the full length of the sling, broken wires snag on the rag — a practical way of checking. The eye and the pressed ferrule area are the most critical inspection points.
Çelik sapan keskin köşelerden geçerken y: If no softeners (softener/packing) are used where a wire sling passes over sharp edges, the wire is crushed and breaks. A sling is not knotted or kinked and is not bent under load. When not in use, it is stored dry, hung up and protected from corrosion; it is not dragged along the floor.
Tekstil/web sling'ler hafif ve yüzeyi ko: Textile/web slings are light and protect the surface of the load, but they are sensitive to cuts, abrasion, chemical damage and UV degradation. Inspection looks for: tears/cuts, worn webbing, chemical burns (oil/acid stains and stiffening), heat damage (melting/glazing), broken stitching and fading. The label (SWL, material, date of manufacture/test) must be legible; a sling without a label is not used.
Tekstil sling'lerde renk kodu kapasiteyi: On textile slings, the color code indicates capacity (e.g. violet = 1 t, green = 2 t, yellow = 3 t — a standard convention); however, the SWL is always confirmed from the label. If no protection is used at a sharp edge, the sling is cut instantly. A damaged sling is not repaired; it is discarded.
Zincir sapanlar yüksek sıcaklık ve aşınm: Chain slings are resistant to high temperature and wear and are often used in the engine room. Inspection looks for: link wear (reduced diameter), stretching/elongation (stretch — the links look elongated), cracks, nicks, deformation, damage to welds/joints and the condition of the master link/hook. The safety latch on the hook must work.
Zincir halkalarındaki uzama, aşırı yükün: Elongation of chain links is a sign of overloading; it is detected by measurement (with a gauge). When wear exceeds a specified percentage, the chain is scrapped. The Oiler checks the chain link by link along its full length; a single damaged link takes the whole chain out of service.
Shackle (D veya bow tipi), sapan ile yük: A shackle (D or bow type) connects the sling to the load/lifting point. Inspection looks for: SWL marking on the shackle and its pin, deformation (opening/bending), wear, cracks and the condition of the pin thread. The pin must be fully seated, and the correct shackle pin must be used (a wrong/improvised pin is lethal). The pin is not rigged in a position where it can turn/work loose under load.
Shackle'ın gövdesine yan (transverse) yü: No side (transverse) load is applied to a shackle; it is loaded only along the axis for which it was designed. A shackle with an unsuitable item such as a screw/nail fitted in place of its pin must never be used. A shackle without an SWL marking, or one that is deformed, is out of service.
Eye bolt (mapa), ekipmana vidalanan kald: An eye bolt is a lifting point screwed into a piece of equipment (e.g. a pump casing, a motor). A plain eye bolt is suitable only for axial (vertical) loads; if it is loaded at an angle, it breaks — collar/swivel eye bolts are used for angled loads. The eye bolt must be screwed fully home (shoulder in contact) and its threads must be in good condition.
Ekipman üreticisinin belirlediği kaldırm: The lifting points specified by the equipment manufacturer (lifting points / pad-eyes) are used; lifting is never done from a random pipe or a weak flange. The Oiler checks the lifting diagram in the equipment manual.
Chain block (zincir palanga), makine dai: The chain block is the most widely used lifting device in the engine room. Inspection looks for: wear/elongation/cracks in the load chain, smooth operation of the hand chain, the brake mechanism (load holding — the block must not slip when it takes the load), the hook and safety latch, and deformation of the housing. The SWL plate must be legible.
Fren testi kritiktir: yük kaldırıldığınd: The brake test is critical: when the load has been lifted and the hand chain is released, the load must stay where it is and must not slip. A slipping brake is lethal. A chain block is pulled straight; pulling it at a side angle jams the chain and damages the device.
ME üstündeki tavan vinci (overhead trave: The overhead travelling crane above the ME and the monorail are fixed equipment designed for lifting heavy engine parts; their SWL is marked on their rails/girders. Inspection looks for: rail condition, trolley movement, limit switches, brake, hook and hoist wire/chain, and operation of the control pendant. Periodic load testing and certification are required.
Yağcı, crane'i kullanmadan önce hareket: Before using the crane, the Oiler checks the path of travel (that no one is under the load), the limit switches and the brakes. A load above the SWL of the crane is never lifted; a lifting plan and a risk assessment are made before a heavy lift.
Tüm kaldırma ekipmanları bir \"register: All lifting equipment is recorded in a "register of lifting appliances and cargo gear"; the SWL, last test date, certificate and inspection history of each item are kept in this register. Periodic (usually annual) inspection and inspection with load testing by an authorized person/company are mandatory; the validity of certificates is tracked.
Yağcı, kullandığı ekipmanın sertifikasın: The Oiler verifies that the certificate of the equipment being used is current (date on the tag/in the register). Equipment that is out of date is not used, even if it looks sound; this is a finding both for safety and in class/PSC inspections.
Birçok gemi, muayene durumunu görsel tak: Many ships use a color coding system to track inspection status visually; equipment fitted with the colored tag/tape for the current inspection period is fit for use. If the color is out of date or there is no tag, the equipment is set aside. Damaged equipment is clearly marked with an "out of service" tag and physically removed from use (collected/locked away) so that it is not used by mistake.
Yağcı, kullandığı ve kontrol ettiği ekip: The Oiler records the condition of the equipment used and checked and the lifting operations carried out; the maintenance records must be available for the PMS and for class inspections. The decision to take equipment out of service is made without hesitation.
Her ağır kaldırma öncesi plan yapılır: y: A plan is made before every heavy lift: the weight and center of gravity of the load, the equipment to be used and its SWL, the lifting points, the sling angle, the route of travel and the allocation of tasks are determined. The load is slung so that it is balanced; if the center of gravity is misjudged, the load rotates or slips. Soft edge protectors (softeners) are used.
Sapanlamada açı kontrol edilir, bacak yü: When slinging, the angle is checked, the leg loads are balanced and correct seating on the hook is ensured. The lift starts slowly and under control; as soon as the load leaves the ground (a few cm), the lift is stopped to check the balance and the seating of the slings, and only then continued.
Kaldırma sırasında tek bir yönlendirici: During the lift, a single signaller (banksman/signaller) directs the operation with clear hand/verbal signals; mixed orders are dangerous. Absolute rule: no one stands under a suspended load or in its path. If a taut rope/chain parts, the snap-back is lethal.
Yağcı, kaldırma sırasında geri çekilme a: During the lift, the Oiler keeps a clear area to withdraw to, wears gloves and keeps their hands away from pinch points. If the ship is rolling, the load can swing freely; in bad weather/when rolling, heavy lifts are postponed or carried out with extra safety measures.
En yaygın hatalar: SWL aşımı (yükü hafif: The most common mistakes are: exceeding the SWL (underestimating the load), a wrong sling angle (excessive leg loads at a wide angle), using unlabeled/uncertified equipment, slings without protection at sharp edges, side-loaded shackles/eye bolts and using a chain block without testing its brake. Another is using damaged equipment with an "it's a short job, it'll do" mentality.
Gemi hareketinin (roll/pitch) yükü dinam: It is often forgotten that the ship's motion (roll/pitch) increases the load dynamically; a static SWL calculation may be inadequate when the ship is rolling. The Oiler leaves a safety margin, allowing for the sea state.
Bir gemide silindir kapağı kaldırılırken: On one ship, while a cylinder cover was being lifted, the load started to slip slowly because the brake of the chain block in use was worn; the Oiler noticed this early, immediately lowered the load onto a secure support and moved personnel out of the line of the load. The investigation revealed that the periodic inspection date of the block had passed; the equipment was taken out of service. A few seconds of attention prevented a serious crushing accident.
Kaldırma ekipmanı kuru, temiz ve korozyo: Lifting equipment is stored dry, clean and protected from corrosion; slings are kept hanging (not dragged along the floor), and chain blocks are lubricated and stored covered. Equipment left carelessly in a damp/oily environment deteriorates and is unsafe at its next use. Maintenance is included in the PMS program.
Hasarlı ekipman onarılmaya çalışılmaz (ö: No attempt is made to repair damaged equipment (especially slings and shackles); the standard is to discard the damaged item and replace it with a new certified one. An attempt to "repair it and use it" leaves an invisible weakness.
Güvenli kaldırma, eğitim gerektiren bir: Safe lifting is a skill that requires training: sling angles, center of gravity, equipment selection and signaling have to be learned. Inexperienced personnel work under the supervision of a competent person. Over time, the Oiler/Fitter masters this skill and passes correct practice on to newcomers.
Kaldırma ve taşıma ekipmanı güvenliği, m: Lifting and handling equipment safety prevents the most fatal accidents in the engine room. Meticulous checking of every sling, every shackle and every brake, correct slinging and the discipline of "never go under a suspended load" make working with heavy parts safe. A good Fitter is someone who lifts even the heaviest part in the safest way, does not use any equipment they have doubts about and keeps complete records. There is no shortcut here; there is only the right way.
Bunker, transfer ve bilge operasyonları: Bunkering, transfer and bilge operations involve oily liquids and are therefore the jobs with the highest risk of marine pollution. MARPOL Annex I prohibits oil pollution from the engine room under strict rules; the oil content of bilge water that may be discharged into the sea must not exceed 15 ppm (parts per million), and such discharge is only possible through an approved separator + 15 ppm alarm.
Yağcı, bu operasyonlarda \"sıfır kirlili: In these operations, the Oiler works to a "zero pollution" target: every flange, every hose and every valve is a potential leak point. Drip trays, scupper plugs and SOPEP material are prepared in advance. Even a small overflow or leak is reported immediately and cleaned up; it is never concealed.
Tüm yağ ile ilgili işlemler (bunker alım: All oil-related operations (bunkering, internal transfer, bilge discharge, sludge disposal, incineration) are recorded in the Oil Record Book (ORB) Part I with the standard codes, promptly and correctly. The ORB is the document most frequently examined in PSC and flag State inspections; tank levels, quantities and times must be consistent.
Yağcı, kayıtları bizzat tutmasa da opera: Although the Oiler does not keep the records personally, they observe the operational data (start/finish times, quantity received, tank levels, alarm events) accurately and pass them to the engineer; these data are entered in the ORB. An ORB that is incorrect or filled in afterwards in bulk is regarded as falsification.
Bunker öncesi kapsamlı hazırlık yapılır:: Thorough preparation is made before bunkering: the bunker plan (how much into which tank, sequence), verification of tank levels and available capacity (ullage), checking that the air vent pipes are clear, checking the manifold connections, plugging the scuppers, placing drip trays and having the SOPEP material ready. The Ship-Shore (or ship-barge) Safety Checklist is completed and the communication/emergency stop signal is agreed.
Yağcı, scupper tıkaçlarının (deck scuppe: The Oiler verifies that the scupper plugs (deck scupper plugs) are fitted; these plugs prevent a possible deck spill from going into the sea. Drip trays are placed around the manifold, and absorbent material and shovels/rags are made ready. The no-smoking/no-naked-flame rule for bunkering is applied and the "B flag" (Bravo) is hoisted.
SOPEP (Shipboard Oil Pollution Emergency: The SOPEP (Shipboard Oil Pollution Emergency Plan) locker contains absorbent pads/pillows, shovels, rags, plastic bags, dispersant (if appropriate) and warning material. Before bunkering, this material is moved close to the manifold. If a spill occurs, the plan is activated immediately: stop the source, limit the spread, collect and report (Master, terminal, port authority).
Bunker başlarken düşük debiyle (slow rat: Bunkering starts at a slow rate; the rate is increased after the tightness of the connections and flow to the correct tank have been verified. The Oiler stands at the manifold and continuously watches the flange, hose and valve connections, reporting even the slightest weeping/leak. A separate person monitors the tank levels (sounding/ullage or level gauge).
Tank dolmaya yaklaştığında \"topping off: As a tank approaches full, the rate is reduced in the "topping off" stage; the risk of overflow is highest at this moment. Fuel spraying from the air vent pipes is a sign of overflow and requires an immediate stop. Filling stops when the tank is 90-95% full (manufacturer/company limit), and the next tank is started.
Bunker sırasında, MARPOL Annex VI ve şir: During bunkering, a representative fuel sample is taken (usually with a continuous drip sampler at the manifold) as required by MARPOL Annex VI and company procedure. This sealed sample (MARPOL sample) is kept and, if necessary, sent for laboratory analysis in the event of a dispute. It is recorded together with the Bunker Delivery Note (BDN).
İç transfer; storage tanktan settling ta: Internal transfer is the transfer of fuel from a storage tank to a settling tank, from a settling tank to a service tank, or between tanks. On the engineer's instructions, the Oiler opens/closes the correct valves (line-up), starts the transfer pump and watches the levels of both the tank being emptied and the tank being filled. A wrong valve line-up can cause a transfer to the wrong tank or an overflow.
Transfer boyunca tank seviyeleri sürekli: Tank levels are monitored continuously throughout the transfer; the transfer is stopped as the target level is approached. Settling and service tanks generally have high/low-level alarms; action is taken when an alarm sounds. The tank being emptied is not allowed to run completely dry, which would make the pump run dry (draw air).
Farklı bunker partileri (özellikle farkl: When different bunker batches (especially from different suppliers/of different types) are mixed, incompatibility can cause sludge precipitation and clogging of purifiers/filters. Where possible, batches are kept in separate tanks; if mixing is unavoidable, a compatibility test is carried out. Low-sulfur fuel for ECA areas is kept ready in a separate service tank.
Makine dairesinde biriken yağlı sintine: Oily bilge water accumulated in the engine room must not be discharged directly into the sea; it is first processed by the Oily Water Separator (OWS / 15 ppm bilge separator). The OWS separates the water from the oil, and the Oil Content Monitor (OCM / 15 ppm alarm) continuously measures the oil content of the water leaving it. If 15 ppm is exceeded, the three-way valve automatically redirects the discharge back to the bilge tank (not to the sea).
Yağcı, OWS başında bekleyerek operasyonu: The Oiler stays at the OWS and monitors the operation, verifying that the separator is working correctly, that the 15 ppm alarm is active and not bypassed, and that the three-way valve is in the correct position. The separated oil goes to the sludge/waste oil tank. The operation is carried out only under permitted conditions (outside special areas, en route).
Sintine kuyuları, holding/bilge tankına: The contents of the bilge wells are transferred to the holding/bilge tank; from there they are processed by the OWS or delivered to a shore facility. Sludge (purifier sludge, waste oil) is collected in a separate tank and burned in the incinerator or delivered to a shore reception facility. Every transfer is entered in the ORB; tank levels must be consistent.
Yağcı, bilge ve sludge seviyelerini izle: The Oiler monitors the bilge and sludge levels, informs the engineer before the tanks become full and provides on-site support for OWS/incinerator operation. Non-oil waste (detergent, chemicals) mixing with the bilge water impairs OWS performance; chemicals are therefore prevented from being poured into the bilge.
Güverte tahliye delikleri (scupper), nor: Deck drain holes (scuppers) normally discharge rain/sea water overboard; however, during bunkering/transfer they are plugged (scupper plugs) to prevent a possible spill from going into the sea. The plugs remain fitted throughout the operation and any accumulated liquid is monitored; when rainwater collects, the clean water is drained off in a controlled manner.
Drip tray (damlama tepsisi), manifold ve: Drip trays are placed under the manifold and connection points to catch small leaks. The Oiler checks the drip trays regularly and empties their contents into the sludge/waste tank (never into the sea/bilge).
Güverteye dökülme olursa: önce kaynağı d: If there is a spill on deck: first stop the source (emergency stop), then limit the spread (absorbent kit, verify that the scuppers are plugged), clean up and report. Even the smallest amount of oil reaching the sea is managed by activating the SOPEP and informing the port authority. Procedure, not panic, is what counts.
Yağcı, yakıt buharı kokusu veya gaz alar: In the event of a smell of fuel vapor or a gas alarm, the Oiler reports immediately. Gas accumulation in pump rooms and enclosed transfer areas is dangerous; entry into these spaces requires a gas test and ventilation.
Akan yakıt statik elektrik üretir; uygun: Flowing fuel generates static electricity; if this is not handled properly, there is a risk of sparks and ignition. At hose connections, the insulating flange/bonding practice is applied in accordance with company procedure, and a low rate at the start reduces static build-up. The Oiler watches that these precautions are applied.
Bunker Delivery Note (BDN), alınan yakıt: The Bunker Delivery Note (BDN) documents the quantity, type and sulfur content of the fuel received; it is kept on board as required by MARPOL Annex VI. The ORB Part I records all oil operations. Tank levels, quantities received/transferred and discharge records must be consistent with each other; in an inspection, a contradiction is regarded as a "suspicious record".
Yağcı, gözlemlediği operasyon verilerini: By reporting the operational data observed accurately, the Oiler ensures that the records reflect reality. False/inconsistent records are among the most serious PSC findings and can lead to detention of the ship.
OWS deşarjları, 15 ppm alarm olayları ve: Records of OWS discharges, 15 ppm alarm events and OCM calibration are kept; PSC inspects this system closely. The operability of the OWS, the alarm being active, the correct functioning of the three-way valve and tightness are checked. Signs of a bypass (hidden hose/flange) are the main finding looked for.
En yaygın hatalar: scupper'ı tıkamayı un: The most common mistakes are: forgetting to plug the scuppers, reducing the rate too late when topping off, setting up the valve line-up wrongly (wrong tank/overflow), emptying the drip tray too late and bypassing the OWS alarm in the belief that it is a "fault". Another is not reporting a small spill and trying to conceal it — this turns a small incident into a serious offense.
İletişim kopukluğu da tehlikelidir; mani: A breakdown in communication is also dangerous; without clear and continuous communication between the manifold and the control room/terminal, an emergency stop is delayed. The Oiler keeps a communication device (UHF) with them and knows the signals by heart.
İyi bir operasyon: kapsamlı hazırlık (ch: A good operation means thorough preparation (checklist, scuppers, drip trays, SOPEP), starting at a low rate, a constant watch, care when topping off, honest records and immediate reporting of every deviation. "Do not rush, do not look away, do not conceal" are the three basic principles.
Bunker, transfer ve sintine operasyonlar: Bunkering, transfer and bilge operations are jobs in which attention must not slacken even for a moment. Correct preparation, a constant watch, honest records and the discipline of "zero pollution" protect both the ship from heavy fines and the sea from pollution. A good Oiler is someone who does not forget the scupper plugs, does not take their eyes off the manifold when topping off and never bypasses an alarm. There is no hiding anything here; there is only doing it right and recording it right.
Separatör bowl'u (kovan) çok yüksek devi: The separator bowl rotates at a very high speed (usually around 6000-10000 rpm); this rotation forces the denser water and solid particles outward and the less dense clean fuel/oil inward. The disc stack makes the liquid flow in thin layers, which increases the separation surface and the efficiency. Clean fuel/oil leaves at the top, while water and sludge collect at the outside.
Separatör iki modda çalışabilir: purifie: A separator can operate in two modes: purifier (separating water + solids, with a water seal) and clarifier (separating solids only, if there is no water ingress). For HFO, purifier mode is generally used because both water and cat fines must be removed. The Oiler knows which mode the separator is in and why it is in that mode.
Ayrım verimi büyük ölçüde besleme sıcakl: Separation efficiency depends largely on the feed temperature; as the temperature rises, the viscosity of the fuel/oil falls and water/solids separate more easily. For HFO, the typical separator feed temperature is raised to ~98°C (without reaching boiling point); the preheater provides this temperature. For LO, lower values (~90-95°C) are used.
Debi (flow rate) düşük tutuldukça ayrım: The lower the flow rate, the longer the separation time and the higher the efficiency; better separation is therefore achieved by running the separator below its nominal capacity (e.g. at the rate recommended by the manufacturer). The Oiler monitors the feed temperature and the flow rate; a low temperature or a high flow rate means poor separation.
Purifier modunda, su ile yakıt arasındak: In purifier mode, keeping the dividing line between water and fuel (interface) in the correct position depends on the diameter of the gravity disc (dam ring / regulating ring). The higher the density of the fuel, the smaller the diameter of the gravity disc selected. Selecting the wrong disc results in the interface shifting, the water seal breaking and either fuel mixing into the water or water mixing into the fuel.
Yüksek yoğunluklu yakıtlarda gravity dis: Because the gravity disc is inadequate for high-density fuels, manufacturers have developed systems without a gravity disc that monitor the interface automatically by means of a water sensor/conductivity. When these systems detect water, they trigger automatic water draining or a desludge. The Oiler knows which generation the ship's separator belongs to and the daily check points that go with it.
Separatör çalıştıkça dış çeperde (bowl p: As the separator runs, sludge and water accumulate at the outer wall (bowl periphery); at set intervals this accumulation is discharged (desludge / sludge discharge). In modern separators this is done automatically by a timer; the moving part at the bottom of the bowl (sliding bowl bottom) moves down by means of the operating water, opening the sludge ports so that the sludge is thrown out by centrifugal force, and then closes again.
Desludge aralığı, yakıt kirliliğine ve y: The desludge interval is set according to fuel contamination and load: frequent for very dirty fuel, less frequent for clean fuel. If the interval is too long, the bowl clogs and separation deteriorates; if it is too short, there is unnecessary loss of fuel/oil and consumption of operating water. The Oiler verifies that the desludge takes place completely and properly (sound, vibration, observation of the discharge).
Desludge düzgün olmazsa (partial dischar: If the desludge does not take place properly (partial discharge / no discharge), sludge accumulates in the bowl; this leads to imbalance (vibration), loss of separation and eventually clogging of the bowl. Signs: increasing vibration, the housing getting hot, a drop in the quantity of water/sludge separated and a loss of quality at the clean fuel outlet. The Oiler recognizes these signs and reports them to the engineer.
Operating water (kumanda suyu), separatö: Operating water drives the hydraulic mechanism of the separator: it opens and closes the sliding bowl bottom (desludge) and holds the bowl in the closed position. Clean fresh water (at the appropriate pressure and flow) is generally used; dirty operating water or operating water at insufficient pressure leads to incomplete desludging or to the bowl not closing properly.
Yağcı, operating water basıncını, debisi: The Oiler monitors the pressure, flow and cleanliness of the operating water and checks the operating water filter/strainer. A fault in the operating water system (low pressure, clogged nozzle) translates directly into desludge failure.
Yağcı, separatör start ve her desludge s: The Oiler watches that the water seal has been established at separator start-up and after every desludge (clean water coming from the water outlet, no fuel escaping). Water at the fuel outlet or fuel at the water outlet indicates a seal/gravity disc problem and is reported.
Otomatik desludge'a rağmen bowl ve disc: Despite automatic desludging, the bowl and disc stack become coated over time with sticky sludge, asphaltenes and scale; periodically (according to the PMS interval), the separator is stopped and the bowl is dismantled and cleaned by hand. Before dismantling, the separator is stopped and allowed to cool down, and LOTO/energy isolation is applied; the high-speed bowl is not opened until it has come to a complete stop.
Bowl bileşenleri (bowl hood, sliding bow: The bowl components (bowl hood, sliding bowl bottom, disc stack, top disc, distributor) are dismantled in sequence; since each part is marked/numbered, it is refitted in the same sequence. The discs are cleaned one by one (with a suitable solvent/brush) without being scratched or deformed. The number and sequence of the discs in the stack are critical; a missing disc or a wrong sequence impairs separation.
Geri montajda parçalar doğru sırada, doğ: On reassembly, the parts are fitted in the correct sequence, in the correct orientation and to the manufacturer's tightening torque (particularly the lock ring / large nut). Incorrect assembly can lead to imbalance (vibration) and even to a disaster with the bowl flying apart. The alignment marks of the lock ring are lined up; over- or under-tightening is dangerous.
O-ring ve seal ring'ler her açımda kontr: O-rings and seal rings are checked every time the bowl is opened and renewed if necessary. An old/hardened O-ring leaks and impairs the seal. The Oiler inspects all the seals removed and replaces any that are worn.
Separatör performansı sürekli izlenir: b: Separator performance is monitored continuously: the feed temperature, the quality of the clean fuel/oil outlet, the water drainage and the sludge discharge are observed. A dark sludge discharge is normal; however, clean fuel/oil escaping into the water (oil loss) or fuel appearing at the water outlet indicates a seal/disc problem. The Oiler makes these observations every watch.
Backwash/operating water sıcaklığı ve di: The backwash/operating water temperature and the discharge temperature are monitored; an abnormal change in temperature points to a preheater or separation problem. A drop in performance (rising filter DP, water/dirt reaching the engine) is indirect evidence of separator inefficiency.
Separatör, filtreden önceki ana temizlem: The separator is the main cleaning stage before the filter; if its efficiency falls, the load on the filter increases and the DP rises quickly. Cat fines (Al+Si) are a particular target of the separator; a well-functioning purifier removes most of the cat fines. If the Oiler sees sand-like particles in the filter contents, they question the separator's efficiency.
FO separatörü ağır/kirli yakıtı işler; y: The FO separator processes heavy/dirty fuel; it focuses on high temperature, frequent desludging and the removal of cat fines/water. The LO separator, on the other hand, cleans the system oil continuously (bypass purification); it works with a cleaner feed and removes water and wear metals. The feed temperature, flow rate and desludge frequency of the two are different and must not be confused.
Yağcı, hangi separatörün hangi sisteme h: The Oiler knows which separator serves which system, the condition of the standby separator and the procedure for putting it into service. When a separator is taken out for maintenance, the standby one is put into service, so the supply to the engine is not interrupted.
Bazı gemilerde sludge'ı daha da konsantr: Some ships have a separate sludge separator/decanter that concentrates the sludge further; by reducing the oil content of the liquid discharged, it reduces the volume to be disposed of. The separated sludge goes to the sludge tank under MARPOL Annex I and is burned in the incinerator or delivered ashore. Under no circumstances is it discharged into the sea.
En sık görülen sorunlar: water seal kayb: The most frequent problems are: loss of the water seal (wrong gravity disc, low feed/sealing water), oil loss (broken seal, excessive flow rate), vibration (sludge build-up in the bowl, incorrect assembly, bearing wear), incomplete desludge (operating water pressure/clogging problem) and water/dirt reaching the engine (general drop in efficiency). The root cause of each symptom is looked for systematically.
Düşük besleme sıcaklığı ayrımı bozar; pr: A low feed temperature impairs separation; a preheater or thermostat fault is a typical cause. High vibration is always taken seriously and the separator is stopped. The Oiler carries out simple checks (temperature, pressure, operating water) and passes on to the engineer whatever cannot be solved.
Bir gemide separatör su çıkışından yakıt: On one ship, the Oiler noticed fuel coming from the separator's water outlet (oil loss); the investigation revealed that the gravity disc had not been changed although the bunker density had changed. When the correct disc was fitted, the water seal was re-established, the fuel loss stopped and water was prevented from reaching the engine. Daily observation prevented both fuel waste and risk to the engine.
Separatör hem çok sıcaktır (~98°C beslem: The separator is both very hot (~98°C feed, heater, hot fuel) and a mass rotating at very high speed; both carry a risk of serious injury. Contact with hot surfaces, leaking hot fuel and the rotating bowl are the main hazards. Maintenance is done only on equipment that has been stopped, has cooled down and has been energy-isolated.
Yağcı, separatör çalışırken muhafazaları: While the separator is running, the Oiler does not remove guards, does not approach the rotating part and wears gloves against hot surfaces. If leaking fuel meets a hot surface, there is a fire risk; for this reason, cleanliness of the separator room and leak checks are critical.
Separatör bakımı ve desludge'dan çıkan t: All oily waste from separator maintenance and desludging goes to the sludge tank; fuel/oil spilled during maintenance is collected and is not mixed into the bilge. Sludge transfers and disposal are entered in the ORB. By directing maintenance waste correctly, the Oiler maintains MARPOL compliance.
Separatör bakımı, makineyi cat fines ve: Separator maintenance is an invisible shield that protects the engine from cat fines and water. The correct temperature, the correct gravity disc, a sound water seal, proper desludging and meticulous periodic cleaning both prevent fuel/oil loss and protect the injection equipment and the bearings. A good Oiler/Fitter is someone who checks the separator's water and clean outlets every watch, takes vibration seriously and touches the bowl only when it has come to a complete stop. Clean fuel means a sound engine.
